Uniform Title: Śāktapramoda Author: Devanandanasiṃha Description: A ritual manual for the worship of primarily Śākta deities, comprising seventeen individual tantras.
Reprint of the edition published in 1892. Notes: Data entered by the staff of Muktabodha under the supervision of Mark S. G. Dyczkowski.
Revision 0, February 9, 2009.
Publisher: Śrīveṅkaṭeśvara Press Year of Publication: 1949 City of Publication: Bombay
Country of publication: India.
Śrīḥ Śāktapramodaḥ.
It consists of the ten great vidyā-tantras beginning with Kālī,
is adorned with the tantras of the deities of the five āyatanas beginning with Kumārī,
and is presided over by the sovereign kings of the capital city of Śiva-Hara.
Compiled and composed by the illustrious King Rājadeva Nandana Siṃhabahādura; the printer and publisher is as follows.
Khemarāja Śrīkṛṣṇadāsa, Managing Director, Śrī Veṅkaṭeśvara Press,
Khemarāja Śrīkṛṣṇadāsa Mārg, Bombay-400 004.
Edited in the year 1892, Samvat 1949.
Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa. Now begins the Śāktapramoda.
Having bowed to Kālī, whose limbs are moist with compassion, whose beautiful body is soft and removes the impurities of the Kali age,
I compose this *Śāktapramoda*, which bestows merit and excellent intelligence, and is auspicious for the virtuous.
Herein has been described the ritual worship and other rites for the Śaktis along with their mantras and ten states;
likewise, [the rites] for the five deities who shatter all the doubts of those of evil intellect.

Now, the meditation on Śrī Kālī: [One should meditate upon] the auspicious goddess, mounted upon a corpse, of most terrifying form, with formidable fangs and a laughing face, possessing four arms, holding a sword and a severed head, and displaying the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness. (1)
One should thus meditate upon Kālī, who dwells in the abode of the cremation ground, wearing a garland of severed heads, with a lolling tongue, and naked.
(p. 4) Now, the extraction of the yantra: Having first drawn a triangle, one should draw another triangle outside of that.
Then the practitioner of mantra should indeed draw three excellent triangles. (1)
Then, having drawn a circle, one should draw an eight-petalled lotus;
then, having drawn another circle according to the rule, one should draw a single square enclosure.
Now follows the extraction of the mantra: Having first uttered the three seed-syllables of Kālī, then the two seed-syllables of Lajjā, then two *hūṃ* syllables, and after that, "Dakṣiṇe Kālike. (1)

From that [seed-syllable], one should recite the three seed-syllables of Kālī, followed by the two seed-syllables of Lajjā (the Goddess of Modesty), and finally two *hūṃ* syllables ending with *svāhā*; this is declared to be the mantra of Kālī. || 2 ||
Now the mantra: Krīṃ krīṃ krīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hūṃ, O Dakṣiṇakālikā, krīṃ 3 hrīṃ 2 hūṃ 2 svāhā.
Now, the ritual manual for the worship of Śrī Dakṣiṇakālī: first, having gone to a pure place adorned with five-colored powders,
standing outside the altar of worship, one should bow to the Guru, bow to the chosen deity (iṣṭadevatā), and [bow to] the guardians of the directions.
Having prostrated and sipped water (ācamana), one should then, with kuśa grass in hand and observing silence, recite two verses for the purpose of pacifying evil. They are as follows:
"O Goddess, my mind, which was originally pure, has become overcome by sin."
May my mind be liberated from that evil; hūṃ phaṭ! And homage to you! || 1 ||
The sun, the moon, Yama, Time, and the five great elements.

Having recited, "These nine are the witnesses here of one's auspicious and inauspicious karma," and having offered prayers, he should enter his home. Remaining silent, having performed the ritual rinsing of the mouth (*ācamana*) with the *mūla-mantra*,
and having taken water while reciting "O Vajrodake hūṃ phaṭ svāhā," he should place it in his hand while reciting "Hūṃ svāhā."

Having taken [water], one should wash the feet with the mantra: "Oṃ hrīṃ, purify all sins, pacify, remove all conceptual constructions, hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Then, having sipped water again with "Oṃ hrīṃ svāhā," one should offer salutations with:
"Aiṃ, obeisance to Kālikā; aiṃ, obeisance to Kapālinī; aiṃ, obeisance to Kullā."

Having sipped water three times, then having washed both hands with the root mantra, and having wiped the lips twice with the ten fingers of the hands while reciting "Oṃ, obeisance to Kālikā; Oṃ, obeisance to Kapālinī," and having washed the hand while reciting "Oṃ,
obeisance to Kullā," [one should wash them] with the root mantra.

With the fingers contracted, one should touch the face with the index finger and thumb, the nose at its base with the ring finger and thumb, the ears with the thumb and little finger, the navel with the palm, the heart with all the fingers, and the head and arms [with the palms].

Then, one should apply a tilaka-mark with kuṅkuma, sandalwood paste, and so forth, upon twelve locations: the forehead, the belly, the heart, the throat, the right side, the shoulder, the back of the neck, the upper spine, the two arms, and the head. Then...
One should inscribe the seed-syllable of Kālī on the forehead with the divine weapon-mantra, and then [inscribe it] in the heart.
Having placed the Śakti in the center, the wise one should install the Kūrca seeds;
thereafter, he should perform the installation of the general arghya vessel.

For example: having drawn the maṇḍala consisting of a triangle, a circle, and a square on one's own left, then, having worshipped it with flowers, unbroken rice, and so forth, saying "Oṃ, obeisance to the foundational powers (ādhāraśakti)," and having said "Oṃ haḥ,
I prepare the water for the door-offering (dvārārghya)," it is washed with "Phaṭ."
Having placed the conch or other vessel upon a tripod stand and filled it with water while reciting "Namaḥ," one should say:
"O Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Godāvarī, Sarasvatī,
Narmadā, Sindhu, and Kāverī, please manifest your presence in this water."
Having invoked the holy water from the solar disc into that water with this mantra and the goad mudrā (aṅkuśamudrā),
having offered scents and other offerings with the syllable Om (praṇava), and having displayed the cow and fish mudrās,
one should consecrate the door by empowering it eighteen times with the syllable Om and sprinkling it with the mantra "phaṭ."

One should bind the topknot with the mantra: *oṃ maṇidhariṇi vajriṇi śikhariṇi sarvalokavaśaṅkari hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. Then one should worship the deities of the doorway: *gaṃ gaṇeśāya namaḥ*, *baṃ baṭukāya namaḥ*, *kṣaṃ kṣetreśāya namaḥ*, *yaṃ yoginībhyo namaḥ*.
Thus, one should worship in the four directions— above, to the left, to the right, and below— with the mantras: "Oṃ Gaṅgāyai namaḥ" and "Oṃ Yamunāyai namaḥ" on the two sides of the branches,
and "Oṃ Laṃ Lakṣmyai namaḥ" and "Oṃ Saṃ Sarasvatyai namaḥ."
Thus, one should worship [the deities] both above and below.

Having worshipped with sandalwood paste, flowers, and other offerings at the threshold with the mantra "Oṃ, obeisance to the eight Mothers beginning with Brahmāṇī," one should then enter within the maṇḍala, contracting the right limb and placing the right foot forward, without touching the left branch.

Having gone there, one should sprinkle water while reciting "Oṃ rakṣa rakṣa hūṃ phaṭ svāhā," consecrate it with "Oṃ pavitravajrabhūme hūṃ phaṭ svāhā," and worship the seat with "Hrīṃ ādhāraśaktikamalāsanāya namaḥ" upon the triangle.

Having drawn the vajra-lines with "Ā Ū REKHE VAJRA-REKHE HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ," and having drawn the *pretabīja* (seed-syllable of the corpse) "HASAUṂ" therein, one should worship the seat with "HRĪṂ ĀDHĀRAŚAKTI-KAMALĀSANĀYA NAMAḤ.
Then: "OṂ ANANTĀYA NAMAḤ; VIMALĀSANĀYA NAMAḤ."
Having spread out *kuśa* grass with the mantra "Salutation to the lotus-seat" (*padmāsanāya namaḥ*), one should prepare either a tiger skin, a black antelope skin, or a woolen blanket as a seat.
In the absence of these, however, one should prepare a seat made of twenty-five *kuśa* blades or a corpse-like form.
Having worshipped with the mantra "Hsauṃ, obeisance to the Great Preta seated upon a lotus throne," one should sit upon that seat with the mantra of the self,
placing the right foot upon the left thigh and assuming the bound hero's posture (vīrāsana).
Placing the right thigh upon the left foot, or in the reverse position, and assuming a seat facing either east or north, one should recite the mantra.

For the seat-mantra (*āsana-mantra*), Meru-pṛṣṭha is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Sutala is the meter (*chandaḥ*), Kūrma is the deity (*devatā*), and its application (*viniyoga*) is in the formal acceptance of the seat. "Oṃ! O Earth, the worlds are supported by you; O Goddess, you are supported by Viṣṇu.
Therefore, support me always and make this seat pure. Thus: "Oṃ..."

Having worshipped in the southwest with "Salutation to Vāstupuruṣa; Oṃ, salutation to Brahmā," and having worshipped in the cardinal directions with "Oṃ, salutation to Dharma; Oṃ, salutation to Jñāna; Oṃ, salutation to Vairāgya;
Oṃ, salutation to Aiśvarya," [and] "Oṃ, salutation to Adharma; Oṃ..."
One should worship in the intermediate directions with "Oṃ, obeisance to Avairāgya" and "Oṃ, obeisance to Anaiśvarya. Then,
having performed the purification of body, speech, and mind with either the mantra "Oṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā" or the mantra "Oṃ hrīṃ svāhā," [one recites] "Protect, protect, hūṃ phaṭ svāhā."

Thus one should protect oneself: "Oṃ śatābhiṣeke śatābhiṣekapade hūḥ phaṭ svāhā! Oṃ, Puṣpaketu, King Arhat! In the flower, in the flower, in the great flower, in the beautiful flower, in that which arises from the flower!"

One should consecrate the flowers with the mantra: *puṣpacayāvakīrṇe hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. All other articles of worship should be sprinkled with the general *arghya* water, and one should display the *dhenumudrā* and the *matsyamudrā*.

One should visualize the flowers as pure. Having sprinkled a stream of water with the syllable *vaṃ*, and having meditated upon a fire-rampart with the seed-syllable of fire (*raṃ*), one should drive away all obstacles by gazing in the four directions with a wrathful look while reciting the mantra *hūṃ phaṭ*. It is as follows:

Having looked upward with the mantra "Sarvavighnānutsāraya hūṃ phaṭ svāhā," he should dispel the divine obstacles by scattering water in the four directions, and the terrestrial obstacles by striking the ground three times with the left heel.
Taking any one of the following—parched grain, sandalwood, white mustard seeds, sesame, curd, dūrvā grass, or unbroken rice—and reciting: "Oṃ, may those spirits depart who dwell upon the earth;
and those here who create obstacles, may they perish by the command of Śiva," one should scatter them in the four directions.

Then, one should prostrate, saying: "Oṃ, obeisance to the Gurus" on the left; "Oṃ, obeisance to the Parama-gurus"; "Oṃ, obeisance to the Parātpara-gurus"; "Oṃ, obeisance to the Parameṣṭhi-gurus"; "Oṃ, obeisance to Gaṇeśa" on the right; and "Oṃ, obeisance to Dakṣiṇakālikā" in front. Then...

One should perform the purification of the hands (*karaśuddhi*). As follows: taking flowers smeared with sandalwood paste with the fingertips while reciting the mantra "HŪṂ," one should rub them between both hands with the mantra "HAUṂ," wipe them with the right hand using the seed-syllable "KLĪṂ," and [conclude] with "OṂ TATSAT."

Having smelled [the flower] with the left hand while reciting this mantra, one should cast the flower in the northeastern direction while reciting the mantra "Hauṃ," [and say]: "Oṃ! May all those who harm me, the violent ones—death, disease, fear, and anger—dissolve away and fall upon the head of my enemy."
One should release [the breath] with this mantra; and the release is performed with the nārāca-mudrā.
Now, the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*):

In the head: *namaḥ* to Bhairava, the seer (*ṛṣi*). In the mouth: *namaḥ* to the *uṣṇih* meter (*chandas*). In the heart: *oṃ namaḥ* to Dakṣiṇakālikā. In the secret place: *namaḥ* to the seed-syllable *krīṃ*. In the feet: *hūṃ*.
Salutation to Śakti. Salutation to Krīṃ, the Kilaka, on all limbs.
(p. 8) Now, the ritual placement of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*):
With the mantra *krāṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ*, one should touch the heart with the index, middle, and ring fingers extended. With *krīṃ śirase svāhā*, [one should touch the head].
With the index and middle fingers, one should touch the head with the mantra: *Kraṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*.
With the fist closed, one should touch the topknot (*śikhā*) with the thumb while reciting: *Kraiṃ kavacāya hūṃ*.
With the two hands spread apart, one should touch all the limbs while reciting: *Krauṃ netratrayāya vauṣaṭ*.

One should touch the two eyes with the index and ring fingers, and the space between the eyebrows with the middle finger; thus one should touch the three eyes. With the mantra "Kraḥ astrāya phaṭ," one should perform the binding of the directions with a snap of the fingers. Thus is the *karanyāsa*: "Krāṃ..."
Namaḥ to the two thumbs; svāhā to the two index fingers with *krīṃ*;
vaṣaṭ to the two middle fingers with *krūṃ*; hūṃ to the two ring fingers with *kraiṃ*;
vauṣaṭ to the two little fingers with *krauṃ*; phaṭ to the palms and backs of the hands with *kraḥ*.
Having thus performed the placement of the hands (karanyāsa), one should perform the pervasive placement (vyāpakanyāsa) with the root mantra tenfold, sevenfold, or fivefold.
Then, one should perform the three breath-controls (prāṇāyāma) according to the previously mentioned sequence. It is as follows:
Blocking the right nostril with the thumb of the right hand,
one should slowly draw in the vital air called *prāṇa* through the left nostril while reciting the root mantra sixteen times, and then hold it in the head at the *sahasrāra*.

The inhalation (*pūraka*): Having blocked both nostrils with the ring finger, index finger, and thumb of the right hand, one should perform the retention (*kumbhaka*) while reciting the root mantra sixty-four times.
Then, having released the blockage of the right nostril with the thumb, [one should recite the root mantra] thirty-two times.
One should slowly exhale that breath through the five-colored [nostril petals]; this constitutes three rounds of prāṇāyāma.

If one desires purification (*vicchodhana*), it should be performed right here. Its procedure is as follows: "Oṃ, [I worship] Bhairavī, who is rich in accomplishments, the consort of Śiva, whose hands shine with the noose and goad, who grants boons to her devotees, who is highly skillful, and who severs the bonds of saṃsāra."

"Having meditated thus: 'I meditate upon the supreme Suvijayā, who deludes the world, whose playful movements are like the essence produced from churning the ocean of nectar, and whose sandals are worshipped by heroes,' [one should recite]: 'Oṃ, O you who are born of Brahman, daughter of Brahman, eternally sinless! For the sake of the fulfillment of the bliss of bearing [the burden]...'"

"May you always be the purifier. *Oṃ*, obeisance to Brāhmaṇī, Svāhā! *Oṃ*, O Goddess Siddhamūlakriyā, awakener of those with deficient understanding; O subduer of kings and subjects, O destroyer of the throats of enemies!
*Aiṃ*, obeisance to Kṣatriyā, Svāhā! *Oṃ*... [p. 9]

O you whose form is the fire of knowledge, blazing with the fuel of ignorance; O Mother, grant me the joy of the scriptures and perfect knowledge for the sake of victory over the three worlds. *Hrīṃ vaiśyāyai namaḥ svāhā*. "Oṃ, I bow, I bow to you, O revealer of the path of Yoga! O Mother, [grant] victory over the three worlds."

Having purified [the vessel] with these mantras: *samādhiphaladābhava klīṃ śūdrāyai namaḥ svāhā*, and then [with]: *oṃ amṛte amṛtodbhave amṛtavarṣiṇi amṛtamākarṣaya ākarṣaya siddhiṃ dehi sarvaṃ me vaśamānaya svāhā*.

One should consecrate [the object] with the mantra. Then, having consecrated it with the Aghora mantra— "Oṃ hrīṃ hlīṃ lūṃ aḥ aṃḍaṃ eṃ mahāghoreśāya namaḥ"— and having recited the root mantra seven times, one should invoke the venerable chosen deity and display the Dhenu-mudrā and the Yoni-mudrā.

Having performed the binding of the directions (*digbandhana*) with finger-snaps (*choṭikā*) and made three *tāla* gestures, one should worship the venerable *iṣṭadevī* there with mental offerings (*mānasopacāra*). Then, with the mantra "Ai! Obeisance to the sandals of the Guru," one should satisfy the venerable Guru three times at the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*).
With the root mantra, one should satisfy the beloved deity within the heart-lotus five times. Then follows the formal acceptance: "Aiṃ!
By means of the principle of the self (ātmatattva), I purify the principle of the self, svāhā! Aiṃ! By means of the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva), I purify the principle of knowledge, svāhā!"
"Oṃ aiṃ, by means of the Śiva-tattva, I purify the Śiva-tattva, svāhā! Reciting the root mantra:
"By means of the Sarva-tattva, I purify the Sarva-tattva, svāhā! "Aiṃ! Speak, speak, O Goddess of Speech! Be firm upon the tip of my tongue, O subduer of all beings!"
One should offer [the oblation] into the digestive fire with the face [uttering] "Svāhā," and drink everything while reciting the root mantra. Then, one should praise [Her]:
"O Goddess, Thou art all-knowing, most venerable, composed of the gunas, the destroyer of the darkness of illusion, delusion, and pride."
She who brings about the pacification [of suffering] and uproots the threefold affliction.

Salutations to the embodiment of realized wisdom, who is victorious through the perfection of discernment born of the knowledge of Brahman, and who is the illuminating lamp of awakening, finding sole delight in the lotus-face of the Goddess of Speech. || 1 ||
Between the two, the knower and the ignorant, the knower of the gods is superior.
"O destroyer of fear, you who are renowned as Nirgandhā and who produce delightful fragrance.

Having thus offered praise, and having prostrated before the venerable Guru and the venerable *iṣṭadevatā*, one should perform the assignment of the seers (*ṛṣinyāsa*) and so forth, the six-limbed assignment (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*), and the assignment of the hands (*karanyāsa*). It is as follows:

*Śirasibhairavāya ṛṣaye namaḥ* (Salutation to Bhairava, the Seer, on the head); *mukhe uṣṇikchandase namaḥ* (Salutation to the Uṣṇih meter, on the mouth); *hṛdaye oṃ dakṣiṇākālikāyai namaḥ* (Salutation to Dakṣiṇakālikā, on the heart); *guhye krīṃ bījāya namaḥ* (Salutation to the seed-syllable Krīṃ, on the private parts); *pādayoḥ hūṃ śaktaye namaḥ* (Salutation to the power Hūṃ, on the feet); *sarvāṅge krīṃ kīlakāya namaḥ* (Salutation to the pin Krīṃ, on all limbs). Now follows the six-limbed assignment (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*).
*krāṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ*; *krīṃ* to the head, *svāhā*; *krūṃ* to the tuft of hair (*śikhā*), *vaṣaṭ*; *kraiṃ* to the armor (*kavaca*), *hum*;
*krauṃ* to the three eyes, *vauṣaṭ*; *kraḥ* to the weapon (*astra*), *phaṭ*. Thus is the ritual placement on the hands (*karanyāsa*). *krāṃ*—
Namaḥ to the two thumbs; svāhā to the two index fingers with *krīṃ*;
vaṣaṭ to the two middle fingers with *krūṃ*; hum to the two ring fingers with *kraiṃ*; vauṣaṭ to the two little fingers with *krauṃ*; phaṭ to the palms and backs of the hands with *kraḥ*.
Having thus performed the ritual placement on the hands (karanyāsa), one should perform the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi).
Having placed [the kuṇḍalinī] face upwards in his lap with a steady mind, he awakens the kuṇḍalinī with the mantra "So 'ham" and leads her from the mūlādhāra through the path of the suṣumnā,
sequentially into the svādhiṣṭhāna, maṇipūra, and anāhata [cakras], and there—
One should contemplate the *jīva* (life-principle) situated there in the form of a lamp-flame and project it into its [the heart's] opening;
then, it is brought to the *jñānacakra* known as Viśuddha;
from there, it is led to the thousand-spoked wheel (*sahasrāracakra*) located at the head, which faces downward and is all-pervasive, shining like snow and possessing all colors.
A lotus with a thousand petals, adorned with three lines and three marks (*ālaka*), and marked with the syllable *uṣitākakhāditrirekhāsu*, is visualized.

Having brought the Guru there, one should unite him with the Supreme Śiva residing in its pericarp by means of the mantra "ahaṃsaḥ. Then, from the feet to the knees, a square of golden luster is visualized with the syllable "laṃ."

One should meditate upon the Brahmā [element] as the earth-maṇḍala conjoined with its seed-syllable and the vajra, together with the faculty of the feet for the purpose of movement, the faculty of smell together with odors, and conjoined with the *nivṛtti-kalā*, as well as the *samāna* wind.
Then, from the knees to the navel, there is the water-maṇḍala, shaped like a half-moon, white in luster, joined with the seed-syllable "vaṃ," marked with two lotuses,
and therein established the organ of the hand together with the activity of grasping, the organ of the tongue together with taste, and the kalā of the foundation (pratiṣṭhā).

One should meditate upon Śrī Viṣṇu, Udāna, and Vāyu. Then, from the navel to the heart, there is a red triangle joined with the seed-syllable "Raṃ," containing a svastika and a circle of fire (tejo-maṇḍala). Within that—
One should contemplate the anal faculty together with the act of emission, the visual faculty in the form of Śiva accompanied by Vidyā and Kalā, and the Vyāna breath. || 3 ||

Then, from the heart up to the midpoint between the eyebrows, there is a circular wind-maṇḍala, smoke-colored, joined with the seed-syllable ‘Yam’ and marked with six dots; therein is the organ of generation (upasthendriya) together with the functions of bliss.

One should contemplate the tactile sense organ accompanied by the element of touch; likewise, one should contemplate Īśāna accompanied by the Śānti-kalā and the apāna-vāyu. Then, from the space between the eyebrows up to the brahmarandhra, one should visualize a clear, circular sphere as "I" (Ahaṃ).

p.11) One should meditate upon the sphere of space (*ākāśamaṇḍala*) conjoined with its seed-syllable; therein, one should meditate upon the organ of speech together with its function, the organ of hearing together with sound, Sadāśiva together with the *kalā* called Śāntyatītā, and the vital breath (*prāṇavāyu*). Then—

One should meditate upon the Supreme Brahman, which consists of all consciousness, within the thousand-spoked void. Then, one should dissolve the earthly sphere along with its retinue into the watery sphere; that into the fiery sphere; that into the airy sphere; that into the ethereal sphere; that into the ego-principle (ahaṃkāra); and that into the Great Principle (mahat-tattva). And that...
One should contemplate those [elements] as dissolved into Prakṛti, and that [Prakṛti] as dissolved into Brahman;
thereafter, one should contemplate everything as empty.
Then, in the right side of the belly, [one should visualize] a dark-colored figure the size of a thumb, whose head is the murder of a Brahmin, whose arms are the theft of gold,
whose heart is the drinking of liquor, whose hips are the violation of the Guru’s bed, and whose two feet are association with such sinners, and minor offenses (*upapātaka*).

Having visualized the sinful person wearing a goat-skin and facing downwards, one should dry up his body along with that [sin] by means of the seed-syllable *yam*, which has been recited ten times according to the *pūraka* (inhalation) method while meditating on the sky; then,
by means of the syllable *ram*, which has been recited sixty-four times according to the *kumbhaka* (retention) method.
Having meditated on the seed-syllable *vaṃ* within a fire-mandala at the base of the penis,
and having visualized the red-colored *māyā* at the navel, one should burn it with the fire arising therefrom by means of the exhaling breath (*recaka*), while reciting [the mantra] thirty-two times.

Having meditated upon the seed-syllable *kālī* (the seed of Kālī) arising from the Corpse-Man (*pāpapuruṣa*), which originates from the seed-syllable *yam*, as yellow in color within the heart, one should expel it with the wind produced therefrom. Then, by the method of inhalation (*pūraka*), one should [expel it] with the Varuṇa-seed-syllable *vam*, recited sixteen times.
Having meditated on the *ghaṇṭikā* located in the heart, one should visualize that [fire] as ash upon the forehead, appearing like frost;
then, having bathed it with the nectar arising from that [ash] by means of the *kumbhaka* method while reciting "Alam" sixty-four times, [one should proceed].
Having meditated on the earth-maṇḍala with the seed-syllable *iti*, one should condense that ash; then, by means of the exhalation (*recaka*) method,
having purified the limbs while reciting the seed-syllable *haṃ* thirty-two times, which is situated in the sky-maṇḍala.
Having meditated upon the body as being free from sin and merit and as consisting of Śambhu, one should produce the elements from that which is composed of consciousness (*cinmaya*).
For example: having produced *prakṛti* from that which is composed of consciousness by means of the mantra "So 'haṃ, haṃsaḥ," [one proceeds].

From *prakṛti* one should produce the principle of *mahat*; from *mahat*, the *ahaṅkāra*; from *ahaṅkāra*, space (*nabhaḥ*); from space, air (*vāyu*); from air, fire (*agni*); from fire, water (*apaḥ*); and from that, earth (*pṛthvī*). With that same mantra, one should cause the *kuṇḍalinī*, who consists of consciousness, to drink the nectar situated within the lunar orb.

Sprinkling [the disciple] with the rain of nectar contained within her own pair of feet sequentially through the six cakras, bringing [that nectar] back to those [cakras], enlivening them, and separating [it from them], she should establish it in the heart; then,
she should place that [nectar] upon the self-arisen liṅga (svayambhū-liṅga) in the mūlādhāra.
Thus, one should meditate upon the Self as consisting of the deities. This concludes the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*).

Then, one should perform the installation of the life-force (*jīva*) with the *prāṇa-mantra*. The procedure for this is as follows: "Oṃ, of this mantra for the installation of the life-force, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara are the seers (*ṛṣis*)."
The *Ṛg*, *Yajur*, and *Sāma* Vedas are the meters (*chandas*); the deity is the power of consciousness (*caitanya-rūpa-prāṇa-śakti*);
the application (*viniyoga*) is for the installation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*). [One should recite: "Salutation to the sages Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara on the head;
salutation to the meters *Ṛk*, *Yajuḥ*, and *Sāman* in the mouth."

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) thus: "Oṃ, obeisance to the deity Prāṇaśakti in the heart; Āṃ, obeisance to the seed-syllable (*bīja*) in the secret place; Hrīṃ, obeisance to the power (*śakti*) in the two feet; Krauṃ, obeisance to the pin (*kīlaka*) in all limbs," one should then perform the placement of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*). [Then]: Ṅaṃ Kaṃ Khaṃ Gaṃ Ghaṃ...
To the heart, which is the essence of ether, air, fire, water, and earth, *namaḥ*.
To the head, which is the essence of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell, represented by *ñaṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ*, *svāhā*.
To the crest-lock (*śikhā*), which is the essence of the ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose, represented by *ṇaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ*, [*vaṣaṭ*].
Ṣaṭ | Naṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ vaṃ vāk-pāṇi-pāda-pāyu-upasthātmane ekavacāya huṃ | Maṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ vaktavya-ādāna-gamana-visarga-ānandātmane netratrayāya vauṣaṭ |

*Śaṃ yaṃ raṃ vaṃ laṃ haṃ ṣaṃ kṣaṃ saṃ laṃ manobuddhyahaṅkāracittātmane astrāya phaṭ.* Thus is the ritual placement on the hands (*karanyāsa*). It is performed as follows: beginning from the navel and ending at the feet, one should place *āṃ*; then *ṅaṃ kaṃ khaṃ ghaṃ gaṃ*.

To the self of ether, air, fire, water, and earth, salutation with the two thumbs (aṅguṣṭhābhyām namaḥ); to the selves of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell, svāhā with the two index fingers (tarjanībhyām svāhā), [represented by] ñaṃ caṃ chaṃ jhaṃ jaṃ;
to the selves of hearing, skin, eyes, tongue, and nose, [salutation with the middle fingers], [represented by] ṇaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍhaṃ ḍaṃ.
To the self of speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals: *vaṣaṭ* with the two middle fingers;
*hūṃ* with the two ring fingers, [to the self of] *naṃ taṃ thaṃ dhaṃ daṃ*.
To the self consisting of speech, grasping, movement, excretion, and pleasure: *maṃ paṃ phaṃ bhaṃ baṃ*—to the little fingers, *vauṣaṭ*.
To the self consisting of mind, intellect, ego, and consciousness: *śaṃ yaṃ raṃ vaṃ laṃ haṃ ṣaṃ kṣaṃ saṃ laṃ*.

And with *phaṭ* from the palms and the backs of the hands; then one should place *hrīṃ* from the navel to the heart, and *kroṃ* from the heart to the crown of the head. Then, one should assign: *yaṃ tvagātmane namaḥ* at the heart;
*raṃ asṛgātmane namaḥ* on the right shoulder; and *laṃ māṃsātmane namaḥ* at the back of the neck (*kakud*).

*Vaṃ*—salutation to the self consisting of fat, on the left shoulder; *Śaṃ*—salutation to the self consisting of bone, from the heart to the tip of the right arm; *Ṣaṃ*—salutation to the self consisting of marrow, from the heart to the tip of the left arm; *Saṃ*—salutation to the self consisting of semen.
From the heart to the tip of the right foot: *hauṃ oja-ātmane namaḥ*;
from the heart to the tip of the left foot: *haṃ ghrāṇātmane namaḥ*; from the heart to the navel: *saṃ jīvātmane*.
Saying "Namaḥ," one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpakanyāsa*) seven or five times with the *prāṇamantra* from the heart to the top of the head. Then, one should meditate as follows:
[She] is seated upon a lotus as red as the sun rising over the ocean of blood, holding a noose, a goad, a bow, arrows, a sword, and [additional] shafts.
"I bow to the Goddess who holds a trident and a skull in her lotus-like hands, and who has red feet and three eyes.
Then, touching his heart with the *lelihāna-mudrā* (the licking gesture) to be described hereafter, he should recite the *prāṇamantra* eleven times. And the mantra is:

Āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ hoṃ oṃ kṣaṃ saṃ haṃ saḥ hrīṃ oṃ haṃ saḥ. O Śrī Dakṣiṇakālikā, [my] vital breaths are here, my vital breaths are here. Āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ hoṃ.
Oṃ kṣaṃ śaṃ saṃ haṃ saḥ hrīṃ oṃ haṃ saḥ. Oṃ kṣaṃ saṃ haṃ saḥ. The life-force (jīva) of Śrī Dakṣiṇakālikā is established here: āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ hoṃ oṃ kṣaṃ saṃ haṃ saḥ.
All the sense organs of Śrī Dakṣiṇakālikā are stationed here:
Āṃ Hrīṃ Kroṃ Yaṃ Raṃ Laṃ Vaṃ Śaṃ Ṣaṃ Saṃ Hoṃ Oṃ Kṣaṃ Saṃ Haṃ Saḥ Hrīṃ Oṃ Haṃ Saḥ, [belonging] to Śrī Dakṣiṇakālikā.
Speech, mind, skin, eyes, ears, nose, and breath, having come here, may they remain happily; svāhā! Oṃ kṣaṃ saṃ haṃ saḥ hrīṃ oṃ āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ śrī Dakṣiṇakālikāyāḥ prāṇā iha prāṇāḥ.
ĀṂ HRĪṂ KROṂ ŚRĪ DAKṢIṆAKĀLIKĀYĀ JĪVA IHA STHITAḤ;
ĀṂ HRĪṂ KROṂ ŚRĪ DAKṢIṆAKĀLIKĀYĀḤ SARVENDRIYĀṆI;
ĀṂ HRĪṂ KROṂ ŚRĪ DAKṢIṆAKĀLIKĀYĀḤ...
"Speech, mind, skin, eyes, ears, nose, and breath, having come here, may you dwell happily;
svāhā! Then, having meditated upon oneself in the form of the deity, one should perform the *ṛṣyādi-nyāsa* and the *ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa* for the *prāṇāyāma*.

Having performed the *akaranyāsa*, one should perform the *mātṛkānyāsa*. In this regard: "Oṃ, for this Mātṛkā-mantra, Brahmā is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the meter (*chandas*), Mātṛkā-Sarasvatī is the deity (*devatā*), the consonants (*hal*) are the seeds (*bīja*), the vowels (*svara*) are the powers (*śakti*), and both together constitute the bolt (*kīlaka*)."

The application [of the breath] for the sake of accomplishing one's desired goal is as follows: the *prāṇāyāma* is performed by filling [the breath] through the *iḍā* [nāḍī] with the vowels *a, i, u, ṛ, ḷ, e, ai, o, au*; holding it [within] (*kumbhaka*) with the five consonants *ka, ca, ṭa, ta, pa*; and exhaling (*recaka*) with these eight consonants: *ya, ra, la, va, śa, ṣa, sa, ha*.
The ritual placement (nyāsa) of the seers and so forth is as follows:

"Obeisance to Brahmā, the seer," at the head; "Obeisance to Gāyatrī, the meter," at the mouth; "Obeisance to Mātṛkā-Sarasvatī," at the heart; "Obeisance to the seeds of the limbs," at the genitals; [and] at the feet.
Salutation to the Śaktis from the vowels; salutation to this Kīlaka for both [the body and the mantra] in all its limbs.
Now, the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) is as follows: *aṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ āṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ*; *iṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ īṃ śirase svāhā*;
*uṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ ūṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*.
Eṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ aiṃ kavacāya huṃ;
oṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ auṃ netratrayāya vauṣaṭ;
aṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ aḥ astrāya phaṭ.
The ritual placement of the hands (*karanyāsa*) is as follows: *aṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ āṃ*—*namaḥ* to both thumbs;
*iṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ īṃ*—*svāhā* to both index fingers; *uṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ*—[to both middle fingers].
Ūṃ to the middle fingers, vaṣaṭ; aiṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ—aiṃ to the ring fingers, hum; oṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ—auṃ to the little fingers, vauṣaṭ.
Aṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ aḥ phaṭ with both palms and backs of the hands. Now, the meditation (dhyāna):
"With His chest, waist, arms, and face adorned by the fifty letters [of the alphabet], and His radiant crown..."
The Goddess of Speech,
who possesses three eyes and radiant white luster, holds in her lotus-like hands a crescent moon, full and high breasts, a rosary of beads, a jar brimming with nectar, and a book.
In the stomach.

Now, the internal placement of the Mātṛkās (antarmātṛkānyāsa): One should place [the syllables] *aṃ iṃ uṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ eṃ aiṃ oṃ auṃ* with the mantra *namaḥ* upon the sixteen-petaled [lotus] at the throat, which has a smoky luster.
Then, one should place *kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ* with the mantra *namaḥ* upon the twelve[-petaled lotus].
In the heart, which resembles a fresh sprout,
is the ten-petaled lotus above the navel, similar to a dark blue cloud, filled with jewels, and marked with the syllables *ḍaṃ, ḍhaṃ, ṇaṃ, taṃ, thaṃ, daṃ, dhaṃ, naṃ, paṃ, phaṃ*.

In the Svādhiṣṭhāna, below the navel, is a six-petaled lotus with the syllables *baṃ maṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ namaḥ*, resembling lightning; in the Mūlādhāra, at the base, is a four-petaled lotus with the syllables *vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ namaḥ*, resembling gold; and in the space between the eyebrows is a two-petaled lotus with the syllables *haṃ kṣaṃ namaḥ*, resembling the moon.
One should place [it] in the *ājñācakra*: "In the thousand-spoked [wheel], resembling snow in luster, adorned with all colors."

On the three lines that have not been consumed and adorned with the three *ālaka*s, one should place the mantra "Oṃ namas para-bindubhyaḥ. Having meditated upon the Bindu, whose nature is consciousness (*cid-ātman*), extending from the *mūlādhāra* to the aperture of Brahmā (*brahma-randhra*), one should satisfy the *mātṛkā*s with the streams of nectar flowing from it.
[One should apply: *aṃ namaḥ* on the forehead; *āṃ namaḥ* on the circumference of the mouth; [and] on the right eye...
*Īṃ namaḥ* to the left eye; *īṃ namaḥ* to the right ear; *uṃ namaḥ* to the left ear;
*ūṃ namaḥ* to the right nostril; *ṛṃ namaḥ* to the left nostril; *ṝṃ namaḥ* to the right cheek; *ḷṃ namaḥ* to the left cheek; *eṃ namaḥ* to the upper lip.

*Aiṃ namaḥ* on the lower lip; *Oṃ namaḥ* on the upper row of teeth; *Auṃ namaḥ* on the lower row of teeth; *Aṃ namaḥ* on the head; *Aḥ namaḥ* on the mouth. However, in the *Vīracūḍāmaṇi*, it is stated:
*Aṃ namaḥ* on the tip of the tongue; *Aḥ namaḥ* at the region of the throat; *Kaṃ namaḥ* at the root of the right arm.
At the elbow: *khaṃ namaḥ*; at the wrist: *gaṃ namaḥ*; at the base of the fingers: *ghaṃ namaḥ*;
at the tips of the fingers: *ṅaṃ namaḥ*; at the root of the left arm: *caṃ namaḥ*; at the elbow: *chaṃ namaḥ*; at the wrist: *jaṃ namaḥ*.
*Jhaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the fingers; *ñaṃ namaḥ* at the tips of the fingers;
*ṭaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the right thigh; *ṭhaṃ namaḥ* at the knee; *ḍaṃ namaḥ* at the ankle;
*ḍhaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the [left] fingers; *ṇaṃ namaḥ* at the tips of the fingers; *taṃ namaḥ* at the base of the left thigh; at the knee...
*Thaṃ namaḥ* at the ankles; *daṃ namaḥ* at the calves; *dhaṃ namaḥ* at the bases of the toes;
*naṃ namaḥ* at the tips of the toes; *paṃ namaḥ* on the right side; *phaṃ namaḥ* on the left side;
*baṃ namaḥ* on the back; *bhaṃ namaḥ* at the navel; *maṃ namaḥ* on the abdomen; [and] at the heart.

"Yaṃ, obeisance to the self of skin; raṃ, obeisance to the self of blood on the right shoulder; laṃ, obeisance to the self of flesh on the crown of the head; vaṃ, obeisance to the self of fat on the left shoulder;
śaṃ, obeisance to the self of bone from the heart to the tip of the right arm."
From the heart to the tip of the left arm: *ṣaṃ majjātmane namaḥ*; from the heart to the tip of the right foot: *śukrātmane namaḥ*;
from the heart to the tip of the left foot: *haṃ ātmane namaḥ*.
From the heart to the top of the head: "Laṃ, obeisance to the Supreme Self (Paramātman). This is the external Mātṛkā-nyāsa.

Now follows the sequence of emanation (*sṛṣṭikrama*). In that regard, [the mantra] should be worshipped as accompanied by the *visarga*, enclosed within the *praṇava* (Oṃ), preceded by the seeds of Vāmā, Māyā, and Lakṣmī, or else preceded by the *Vāgbhava* seed-mantra, or any other [appropriate form].
Among these, the one preceded by the *Vāgbhava* is as follows: at the tip of the tongue—*aiṃ aṃ namaḥ*; from the region of the throat—*aiṃ aḥ*.

*Namaḥ*; at the base of the right arm—*aiṃ kaṃ namaḥ*; at the elbow—*aiṃ khaṃ namaḥ*; at the wrist—*aiṃ gaṃ namaḥ*; at the base of the fingers—*aiṃ ghaṃ namaḥ*; at the tips of the fingers—*aiṃ ṅaṃ namaḥ*; at the base of the left arm—*aiṃ caṃ namaḥ*; at the elbow—
Aiṃ chaṃ namaḥ; at the wrist—Aiṃ jaṃ namaḥ; at the base of the fingers—Aiṃ jhaṃ namaḥ;
at the tips of the fingers—Aiṃ ñaṃ namaḥ; at the base of the right thigh—Aiṃ ṭaṃ namaḥ; at the knee—Aiṃ ṭhaṃ namaḥ; at the ankle—Aiṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ; at the base of the toes—Aiṃ ḍhaṃ namaḥ.
Aiṃ Ṇaṃ namaḥ on the tip of the finger; Aiṃ Taṃ namaḥ at the base of the left thigh;
Aiṃ Thaṃ namaḥ on the knee; Aiṃ Daṃ namaḥ on the ankle; Aiṃ Dhaṃ namaḥ at the base of the fingers;
Aiṃ Naṃ namaḥ on the tip of the fingers; Aiṃ Paṃ namaḥ on the right side; [Aiṃ Phaṃ namaḥ] on the left side.
Aiṃ phaṃ namaḥ on the back; aiṃ baṃ namaḥ on the navel; aiṃ bhaṃ namaḥ on the abdomen;

aiṃ maṃ namaḥ on the heart; aiṃ paṃ namaḥ to the self of the skin on the right shoulder; aiṃ raṃ namaḥ to the self of the blood on the hump; aiṃ laṃ namaḥ to the self of the flesh on the left shoulder.

Aiṃ vaṃ me ātmane namaḥ, from the heart to the tip of the right arm: Aiṃ śaṃ asthyātmane namaḥ; from the heart to the tip of the left arm: Aiṃ ṣaṃ majjātmane namaḥ; from the heart to the tip of the right foot.

Aiṃ saṃ, obeisance to the individual self (ātman); from the heart to the tips of the left feet: Aiṃ haṃ, obeisance to the individual self; from the heart to the crown of the head: Aiṃ laṃ, obeisance to the supreme self (paramātman).

(p.16) Now follows the sequence of the [deities'] abiding forms. Therein is the first dhyāna: as follows—[she who is] with three eyes, adorned with black ornaments, and possessing the luster of vermilion.
Holding a rosary of vidyā-beads and a young deer.

One should meditate upon the Goddess standing at one’s side, golden-bodied, holding a book and a rosary in her lotus-like hands. Having meditated thus, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: *ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ* on the forehead; *ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ* on the circumference of the mouth; *ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ* on the right eye.
Ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ to the right eye; ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ to the left eye; ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ to the right ear; ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ to the left ear; ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ to the right nostril;
ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ to the left nostril; ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ to the right cheek.
Ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ, on the left cheek; ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ, on the upper lip;
ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ, on the lower lip; ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ, on the upper row of teeth; ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ, on the lower row of teeth.
Ṭaṃṭhaṃḍaṃ namaḥ on the head; ṭaṃṭhaṃḍaṃ namaḥ on the face; ṭaṃṭhaṃḍaṃ namaḥ on the tip of the tongue; ṭaṃṭhaṃḍaṃ namaḥ at the region of the throat;
ṭaṃṭhaṃḍaṃ namaḥ at the base of the right arm; [ṭaṃṭhaṃḍaṃ namaḥ] at the elbow.
Ṭaṃṭhaṃḍaṃ namaḥ; at the wrist, ṭaṃṭhaṃḍaṃ namaḥ; at the base of the fingers, ṭaṃṭhaṃḍaṃ namaḥ; at the tips of the fingers, ṭaṃṭhaṃḍaṃ namaḥ; at the base of the left arm, ṭaṃṭhaṃḍaṃ namaḥ;
at the elbow, ṭaṃṭhaṃḍaṃ namaḥ; at the wrist...
Ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ, at the base of the fingers; ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ, at the base of the right thigh; ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ, at the knee;
ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ, at the ankle; ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ, at the base of the [left] fingers; at the tips of the fingers.

Ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ, at the root of the left thigh; ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ, at the knee; ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ, at the ankle; ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ, at the base of the fingers; ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ, at the tips of the fingers; on the right side.
Ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ on the left side; ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ on the back; ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ on the belly; ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ on the heart;
ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ on the right shoulder; ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ on the nape of the neck.
Ṭaṃṭhaṃḍaṃ namaḥ on the left shoulder; Ṭaṃṭhaṃḍaṃ namaḥ from the heart to the tip of the right arm;
Ṭaṃṭhaṃḍaṃ namaḥ from the heart to the tip of the left arm.
From the heart to the tips of the right foot: *ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*; from the heart to the tips of the left foot: *ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*; from the heart to the top of the head: *ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*.
Thus is the sequence of maintenance (*sthiti*).
Now, as for the sequence of withdrawal (*saṃhāra*), the meditation therein is as follows: "The rosary, the young deer, the mudrā, and the adze..."
Bow down to the Mistress of the Letters (Varṇeśvarī), who is incessantly bestowed by the masters of knowledge, who possesses three eyes,
whose head is adorned with the crescent moon, who dwells within the lotus,
and who is weary from the weight of her breasts.

p. 17) || The sequence therein is as follows: *kṣaṃ namaḥ* on the forehead; *haṃ namaḥ* on the circumference of the mouth; *saṃ namaḥ* on the right eye; *ṣaṃ namaḥ* on the left eye; *śaṃ namaḥ* on the right ear; *vaṃ namaḥ* on the left ear; *laṃ namaḥ* on the right nostril; [and] on the left nostril...
*Raṃ namaḥ* on the right cheek; *yaṃ namaḥ* on the left cheek; *maṃ namaḥ* on the upper lip;
*bhaṃ namaḥ* on the lower lip; *phaṃ namaḥ* on the upper row of teeth;
*paṃ namaḥ* on the lower row of teeth; *naṃ namaḥ* on the head; [and] on the mouth.
*Dhaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the right arm; *daṃ namaḥ* at the elbow; *thaṃ namaḥ* at the wrist; *taṃ namaḥ* at the base of the fingers; *ṇaṃ namaḥ* at the tips of the fingers;
*ḍhaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the left arm; *ḍaṃ namaḥ* at the elbow; *ṭhaṃ namaḥ* at the wrist.

Ṭaṃ namaḥ at the base of the fingers; ñaṃ namaḥ at the tips of the fingers; jhaṃ namaḥ at the base of the right thigh; jaṃ namaḥ at the knee; chaṃ namaḥ at the ankle; caṃ namaḥ at the base of the [left] fingers;
ṅaṃ namaḥ at the tips of the [left] fingers; ghaṃ namaḥ at the base of the left thigh.
Gaṃ namaḥ to the knees; khaṃ namaḥ to the ankles; kaṃ namaḥ to the bases of the toes; aḥ namaḥ to the tips of the toes; auṃ namaḥ to the right side; oṃ namaḥ to the left side;
aiṃ namaḥ to the back; eṃ namaḥ to the navel; ḹṃ namaḥ to the abdomen; [aṃ namaḥ] to the heart.
Ḷṃ namaḥ, on the right shoulder; Ṛṃ namaḥ, on the crown of the head; Ṝṃ namaḥ, on the left shoulder;
Ūṃ namaḥ, from the heart to the tip of the right arm—uṃ asthyātmane namaḥ;
from the heart to the tip of the left arm—īṃ majjātmane namaḥ.
From the heart to the tips of the right foot: *iṃ śukrātmane namaḥ*; from the heart to the tips of the left foot: *āṃ ātmane namaḥ*; from the heart to the crown of the head:
*aṃ paramātmane namaḥ*. This is the sequence of withdrawal (*saṃhārakrama*). Now follows the *Śrīkaṇṭha* nyāsa.
In that regard, meditative absorption (*dhyāna*) is as follows: "The one who is exceedingly dark, three-eyed, and elevated by the latent impressions (*vāsanā*) of the rays of the Sun."
She bore various ornaments and was surrounded by ten Śivas in the four directions.

"I worship the Lord who is half-woman, who has three eyes, who shines with the luster of red gold, and whose head is adorned by the cool-rayed moon; he holds in his hands a noose, a goad, a boon-granting gesture, and a rosary. The meditation on the Śaktis is as follows:
"These [Śaktis] reside upon the seats that are the limbs of Rudra; their bodies are as crimson as vermilion, and they hold red lotuses."
"One whose lotus-like hands are adorned with two skull-cups"—thus should the meditation be performed during the Rudra-nyāsa.
For this Śrīkaṇṭhādi-nyāsa,
Dakṣiṇāmūrti is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandas), Ardhanārīśvara is the deity (devatā),
and its application (viniyoga) is in the Śrīkaṇṭhādi-nyāsa. [On] the forehead.
*Āṃ*, salutation to Aṃśu-kaṇṭha and Pūrṇodarī on the circumference of the face; *Āṃ*, salutation to Ananna and Vīryā on the mouth;
*Iṃ*, salutation to Sūkṣmeśa and Śālmali on the right eye; [on] the left eye... (p. 18).

*Īm trimūrtaye lolākṣyai namaḥ* (Salutation to the three-formed one with tremulous eyes), on the right ear; *Um amareśāya vartulākṣyai namaḥ* (Salutation to Amareśa with round eyes), on the left ear; *Ūm ardhaṃśāya dīrghaghoṇāyai namaḥ* (Salutation to Ardhaṃśa with a long nose), on the right nostril.
Ṛṃ, salutation to Ṛmārambhubhūti, the long-faced one, on the left nostril;
Ṛṃ, salutation to Ṛtithīśa, the cow-faced one, on the right nostril; Ḷṃ, salutation to Ḷsthārādhīśa, the long-tongued one, on the right cheek; [on the] left cheek...
*Ḷṃ* to Hararāja-Kuṇḍodarī, *Namaḥ*; on the upper lip, *Eṃ* to Jhiṇīśa-Urddhvakeśī, *Namaḥ*; on the lower lip, *Aiṃ* to Bhauktika-Vikṛtamukhī, *Namaḥ*;
on the upper row of teeth, *Oṃ* to Sadyojāta-Jvālāmukhī, *Namaḥ*.
On the lower row of teeth: *oṃ anugraheśāya ulkāmukhyai namaḥ*; on the head: *aṃ akrūrāya śrīmukhyai namaḥ*; on the mouth: *aḥ mahāsenāya vidyāmukhyai namaḥ*;
at the base of the right arm: *kaṃ krodhīśāya mahākālyai namaḥ*; at the elbow [kūrpara].
Khaṃ, obeisance to Caṇḍīśāya-Sarasvatī; at the wrist, Gaṃ, obeisance to Pañcāntakāya-Gaurī; at the base of the fingers, Ghaṃ, obeisance to Śivonnamāya-Trailokyavidyā; at the tips of the fingers, Ṅaṃ—

*Ekārudrāyamantraśaktaye namaḥ* (Salutation to the mantra-power of Ekārudra), at the root of the left arm; *Caṃ Kūrmeśāya Ātmaśaktaye namaḥ* (Salutation to Kūrmeśa and the Self-power), at the elbow; *Chaṃ Ekanetrāya Bhūtimātṛye namaḥ* (Salutation to Ekanetra and the Mother Bhūti), at the wrist; *Jaṃ Caturānanāya Lambodarīye namaḥ* (Salutation to Caturānana and Lambodarī), at the base of the fingers; *Jhaṃ*... at the tips of the fingers.
*Oṃ* Ajeśāya Drāviṇyai *namaḥ*, on the tips of the fingers; *Ñaṃ* Sarveśāya Nāgaryai *namaḥ*, on the root of the right thigh;
*Ṭaṃ* Someśāya Khecaryai *namaḥ*, on the knee;
*Ṭhaṃ* Lāṅgalīśāya Mañjaryai *namaḥ*, on the ankle.

Oṃ *ḍaṃ* to the one whose hair is like a staff, to the Formless One, *namaḥ*; at the base of the fingers, *ḍhaṃ* to the Half-Woman Lord, to the Heroine, *namaḥ*; at the tips of the fingers, *ṇaṃ* to the Beloved of Umā, to the Serpent-Belly Woman, *namaḥ*; at the base of the left thigh, *taṃ*.

*Āṣāḍhine pūtanāyai namaḥ* (Salutation to Āṣāḍhin and Pūtanā), at the knees; *Thaṃ daṇḍine bhadrakālyai namaḥ* (Salutation to Daṇḍin and Bhadrakālī), at the ankles; *Daṃ atrīśāya yoginyai namaḥ* (Salutation to Atrīśa and Yoginī), at the roots of the toes;
*Dhaṃ mīneśāya śaṅkhinyai namaḥ* (Salutation to Mīneśa and Śaṅkhinī), at the tips of the toes.
*Naṃ* to Naṃmeṣeśa and Garjinī, on the right side;
*paṃ* to Lohitāya and Kālarātri, on the left side;
*phaṃ* to Śikhīśa and Vakūrdinī, on the back.
*Baṃ* to Bañcagaṇḍāyakapardinī, *namaḥ* at the navel;
*Bhaṃ* to Dviraṇḍeśa-Vajrā, *namaḥ* at the abdomen;
*Maṃ* to Mahākāla-Jayā, *namaḥ* at the heart.
Or: *yaṃ vāṇīśāya sumukhaisvaryai namaḥ* on the right shoulder;
*raṃ bhujaṅgāya revatyai namaḥ* on the hump; *laṃ pinākine mādhavyai namaḥ* on the left shoulder.
*Vaṃ* to Vaṃśaṅgīśa-Vāruṇī, *namaḥ*, from the heart to the tip of the right arm;
*Śaṃ* to Śambukeśa-Vāyavyā, *namaḥ*, from the heart to the tip of the left arm; *Ṣaṃ* to Śvetā-Rakṣovidāriṇī, *namaḥ*, from the heart to the tip of the right foot.
*Saṃ bhṛgu-veśa-hā-jāyai namaḥ* [from the heart to the tip of the left foot];
*Haṃ nakulīśāya lakṣmyai namaḥ* [from the heart to the crown of the head];
*Kṣaṃ sa-varttakāya mahāmāyāyai namaḥ* [from the heart to the crown of the head]. Thus ends the Rudra-nyāsa.

Now, the sixfold placement (*ṣoḍhā-nyāsa*) should be performed according to the method taught in the *Kālītantra*. First is the placement of the Mother-letters (*mātṛkā-nyāsa*): *aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namo hṛdi*; *eṃ aiṃ oṃ auṃ aṃ aḥ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ*.
In the right arm: ṄAṂ CAṂ CHAṂ JAṂ JHAṂ ÑAṂ; in the left arm: ṬAṂ ṬHAṂ ḌAṂ ḌHAṂ; in the right foot: ṆAṂ TAṂ THAṂ DAṂ DHAṂ NAṂ PAṂ PHAṂ BAṂ BHAṂ;
[in the left foot: MAṂ YAṂ RAṂ LAṂ VAṂ ŚAṂ ṢAṂ SAṂ HAṂ LAṂ KṢAṂ.
Thus one should place [the letters] on the left foot. Thus ends the first [section], the Mātṛkā-nyāsa.
Now the second [set]:
on the forehead, *śrīṃ aṃ śrīṃ aṃ śrīṃ aṃ namaḥ*; on the perimeter of the face, *śrīṃ āṃ śrīṃ āṃ śrīṃ āṃ namaḥ*; on the right eye, *śrīṃ iṃ śrīṃ iṃ śrīṃ*.
Iṃ namaḥ, to the left eye; Śrīṃ īṃ śrīṃ īṃ śrīṃ īṃ namaḥ, to the right ear;
Śrīṃ uṃ śrīṃ uṃ śrīṃ uṃ namaḥ, to the left ear; Śrīṃ ūṃ śrīṃ ūṃ śrīṃ ūṃ namaḥ, to the right nostril; Śrīṃ ṛṃ śrīṃ ṛṃ śrīṃ ṛṃ [namaḥ], to the left nostril.
*Namaḥ*, to the left nostril: *śrīṃ ṛṃ śrīṃ ṛṃ śrīṃ ṛṃ namaḥ*;
to the right cheek: *śrīṃ ḷṃ śrīṃ ḷṃ śrīṃ ḷṃ namaḥ*; to the left cheek:
*śrīṃ ḹṃ śrīṃ ḹṃ śrīṃ ḹṃ namaḥ*; to the upper lip: *śrīṃ eṃ śrīṃ eṃ*.
Śrīṃ Eṃ Namaḥ; on the lower lip, Śrīṃ Aiṃ Śrīṃ Aiṃ Śrīṃ Aiṃ Namaḥ;
on the upper row of teeth, Śrīṃ Oṃ Śrīṃ Oṃ Śrīṃ Oṃ Namaḥ;
on the lower row of teeth, Śrīṃ Auṃ Śrīṃ Auṃ Śrīṃ Auṃ Namaḥ; on the head, Śrīṃ.
Aṃ Śrīṃ Aṃ Śrīṃ Aṃ Namaḥ; on the face, Śrīṃ Aḥ Śrīṃ Aḥ Śrīṃ Aḥ Namaḥ; at the base of the right arm, Śrīṃ Kaṃ Śrīṃ Kaṃ Śrīṃ Kaṃ Namaḥ;
at the elbow, Śrīṃ Khaṃ Śrīṃ Khaṃ Śrīṃ Khaṃ Namaḥ; at the wrist, Śrīṃ...
Gaṃ Śrīṃ Gaṃ Śrīṃ Gaṃ Namaḥ, at the base of the fingers; Śrīṃ Ghaṃ Śrīṃ Ghaṃ Śrīṃ Ghaṃ Namaḥ, at the tips of the fingers;
Śrīṃ Ṅaṃ Śrīṃ Ṅaṃ Śrīṃ Ṅaṃ Namaḥ, at the base of the left arm.
At the elbow: *śrīṃ chaṃ śrīṃ chaṃ śrīṃ chaṃ namaḥ*; at the wrist: *śrīṃ jaṃ śrīṃ jaṃ śrīṃ jaṃ namaḥ*; at the base of the fingers:
*śrīṃ jhaṃ śrīṃ jhaṃ śrīṃ jhaṃ namaḥ*; at the tips of the fingers: *śrīṃ ñaṃ śrīṃ ñaṃ śrīṃ ñaṃ*.
*namaḥ*, at the root of the right thigh: *śrīṃ ṭaṃ śrīṃ ṭaṃ śrīṃ ṭaṃ namaḥ*; at the knee:
*śrīṃ ṭhaṃ śrīṃ ṭhaṃ śrīṃ ṭhaṃ namaḥ*; at the ankle: *śrīṃ ḍaṃ śrīṃ*.
Ḍaṃ Śrīṃ Ḍaṃ Namaḥ; at the base of the fingers, Śrīṃ Ḍhaṃ Śrīṃ Ḍhaṃ Śrīṃ Ḍhaṃ Namaḥ; at the tips of the fingers, Śrīṃ Ṇaṃ Śrīṃ Ṇaṃ Śrīṃ Ṇaṃ Namaḥ;
at the base of the left thigh, Śrīṃ Taṃ Śrīṃ Taṃ Śrīṃ Taṃ Namaḥ; at the knee, Śrīṃ Thaṃ.
*Śrīṃ thaṃ śrīṃ thaṃ namaḥ*, at the ankles; *śrīṃ daṃ śrīṃ daṃ śrīṃ daṃ namaḥ*, at the bases of the fingers; *śrīṃ dhaṃ śrīṃ dhaṃ śrīṃ dhaṃ namaḥ*, at the tips of the fingers;
*śrīṃ naṃ śrīṃ naṃ śrīṃ naṃ namaḥ*, on the right side.
Śrīṃ Paṃ Śrīṃ Paṃ Śrīṃ Paṃ Namaḥ on the left side; Śrīṃ Phaṃ Śrīṃ Phaṃ Śrīṃ Phaṃ Namaḥ on the back; Śrīṃ Baṃ Śrīṃ Baṃ Śrīṃ Baṃ Namaḥ at the navel; Śrīṃ Bhaṃ Śrīṃ Bhaṃ Śrīṃ Bhaṃ Namaḥ on the abdomen.

Śrīṃ maṃ śrīṃ maṃ śrīṃ maṃ namaḥ; in the heart, Śrīṃ yaṃ śrīṃ yaṃ śrīṃ yaṃ, obeisance to the self of the skin (tvagātman); on the right shoulder, Śrīṃ raṃ śrīṃ raṃ śrīṃ raṃ, obeisance to the self of blood (asṛgātman); at the crown of the head, Śrīṃ laṃ śrīṃ laṃ śrīṃ laṃ.
*Śrīṃ vaṃ śrīṃ vaṃ śrīṃ vaṃ*, obeisance to the self consisting of flesh on the left shoulder;
*Śrīṃ śaṃ śrīṃ śaṃ śrīṃ śaṃ*, obeisance to the self consisting of bone from the heart to the tip of the right arm; *Śrīṃ ṣaṃ* [from the heart to the tip of the left arm].
Śrīṃ ṣaṃ śrīṃ ṣaṃ, salutation to the marrow-self (majjātman), from the heart to the tips of the right foot;
Śrīṃ saṃ śrīṃ saṃ śrīṃ saṃ, salutation to the semen-self (śukrātman), from the heart to the tips of the left foot; Śrīṃ haṃ śrīṃ haṃ śrīṃ haṃ, salutation to the self (ātman).
*Namaḥ*, from the heart to the crown of the head: *śrīṃ kṣaṃ śrīṃ kṣaṃ śrīṃ kṣaṃ paramātmane namaḥ*. Thus is the second [mantra].
Now the third [mantra]: *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ* on the forehead; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ* on the face; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ* on the right eye.
*Śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ* *namaḥ* on the left eye; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ* *namaḥ* on the right ear;
*klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ* *namaḥ* on the left ear; *klīṃ śrīṃ* [on] the right nostril.
*klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ* on the left nostril;
*klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ* on the right cheek; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ* on the left cheek.
*Śrīṃ* namaḥ; on the upper lip, *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*;
on the lower lip, *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*;
on the upper row of teeth, *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*.
On the lower row of teeth: *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*; on the head:
*klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*; on the mouth: *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*; at the base of the right arm: *klīṃ śrīṃ*.

*p. 21) *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ* *namaḥ* [to the heart]; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ* *namaḥ* to the elbow; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ* *namaḥ* to the wrist; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ* *namaḥ* to the base of the fingers.
*klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ* on the tip of the finger; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ* at the base of the left arm;
*klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ* at the elbow; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ* at the wrist.
*Śrīṃ* namaḥ; at the base of the fingers, *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ* namaḥ;
at the tips of the fingers, *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ* namaḥ; at the base of the right thigh, *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ* namaḥ; at the knee, *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ*.
Śrīṃ Klīṃ Śrīṃ Namaḥ at the ankles; Klīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ Śrīṃ Namaḥ at the base of the fingers;
Klīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ Śrīṃ Namaḥ at the tips of the fingers; [and] at the base of the left thigh.
*klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ* *namaḥ* at the knees; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ* *namaḥ* at the ankles;
*klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ* *namaḥ* at the bases of the fingers.
On the tip of the finger: *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*; on the right side:
*klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*; on the left side: *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*; on the back: *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ*.
*Śrīṃ* *namaḥ*, at the navel; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*, in the belly;
*klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*, in the heart; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ*, on the right shoulder.
Śrīṃ namaḥ; on the crown of the head, klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ;
on the left shoulder, klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ;
from the heart to the tip of the right arm, klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ.

*Namaḥ*, from the heart to the tip of the left arm: *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*; from the heart to the tip of the right foot: *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*; from the heart to the tip of the left foot: *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ*.
Śrīṃ namaḥ; from the heart to the head: Klīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ Śrīṃ Namaḥ. Thus ends the third [section].
Now the fourth [section]:
*hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ* on the forehead; *hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ* on the face-circle; *hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ* on the right eye.
Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Namaḥ; at the left eye, Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Namaḥ;
at the right ear, Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Namaḥ. (p. 22)
In the left ear: *hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*; in the right nostril: *hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*;
in the left nostril: *hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*.
On the right cheek: *hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*; on the left cheek:
*hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*; on the upper lip: *hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*; on the lower lip: *hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, salutation to the upper row of teeth; Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, salutation to the lower row of teeth; Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, salutation to the head; Hrīṃ [Śrīṃ] to the mouth.
Śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ, at the base of the right arm; hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ, at the elbow; hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ, at the wrist;
hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ, [at the hand].
At the base of the fingers: *hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*; at the tips of the fingers:
*hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*; at the base of the left arm: *hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*; at the elbow: *hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance; at the wrist, Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance; at the base of the fingers, Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance;
at the tips of the fingers, Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance; at the base of the right thigh.
*Hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ* at the knees; *hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ* at the ankles; *hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ* at the bases of the fingers.

*Hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ* on the tip of the finger; *hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ* at the base of the left thigh; *hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ* at the knee; *hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ* at the ankle.
*Namaḥ*, at the base of the fingers: *hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*;
at the tips of the fingers: *hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*; on the right side:
*hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*; on the left side: *hrīṃ śrīṃ*.
Hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance on the back; hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance at the navel;
hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance at the abdomen; hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ [śrīṃ], obeisance at the heart.

Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Namaḥ on the right shoulder; Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Namaḥ on the back of the neck; Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Namaḥ on the left shoulder; Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Namaḥ on the left shoulder.

From the heart to the tip of the right arm: *hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*; from the heart to the tip of the left arm: *hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*; from the heart to the tip of the left foot: *hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Namaḥ, from the heart to the head; Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Namaḥ. Thus ends the fourth [section].
(p. 23) Now the fifth [application]:
at the forehead, the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*; on the circumference of the face, the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*; in the right eye, the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ*.
Ṛṃ klūṃ namaḥ, on the left eye; the root mantra hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ, on the right ear; the root mantra hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ, on the left ear;
the root mantra hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ, on the right nostril.
The root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ* on the left nostril; the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ* on the right cheek; the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ* on the left cheek.
*Namaḥ*, on the upper lip: the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*; on the lower lip: the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*;
on the upper row of teeth: the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*.
On the row of lower teeth: the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*; on the head:
the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*; on the mouth: the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*; at the base of the right arm: the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ*.
*klūṃ* namaḥ; at the elbow, the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ* namaḥ;
at the wrist, the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ* namaḥ; at the base of the fingers, the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ* namaḥ; at the tips of the fingers, the root mantra *hrāṃ*...
*Hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*, at the base of the left arm; *mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*, at the elbow; *mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*, at the wrist;
*mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*, at the base of the fingers.

The root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ* at the base; the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ* on the tips of the fingers; the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ* at the base of the right thigh; the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ* at the knee.
At the ankle: the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*; at the base of the fingers:
the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*; at the tips of the fingers: the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*; at the base of the left thigh: the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ*.
*Namaḥ*, at the knee: the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*; at the ankle: the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*; at the base of the fingers:
the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*; at the tips of the fingers: the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ*.
*klūṃ namaḥ* on the right side; *mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ* on the left side; *mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ* on the back; *mūlaṃ hrāṃ* at the navel.
*Hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*, on the belly; *mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*, on the heart; *mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*, on the right shoulder; *mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ*, on the back of the neck.
*Ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*, on the left shoulder; *mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*, from the heart to the tip of the right foot; *mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*.

From the heart to the tip of the left arm: the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*. From the heart to the tip of the right foot: the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*. From the heart to the tip of the left foot: the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ*.
*klūṃ namaḥ*, from the heart to the crown of the head; the root mantra *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ klūṃ namaḥ*. Thus ends the fifth [section].
Now the sixth [section]:
*mūlaṃ namaḥ* on the forehead; *mūlaṃ namaḥ* on the circumference of the face; *mūlaṃ namaḥ* on the right eye; *mūlaṃ namaḥ* on the left eye; *mūlaṃ namaḥ* on the right ear.

At the left ear: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*; at the right nostril: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*; at the left nostril: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*; at the right cheek: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*; at the left cheek: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*; at the upper lip: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*; at the lower lip: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*.
*Mūlaṃ namaḥ* on the upper row of teeth; *mūlaṃ namaḥ* on the lower row of teeth;
*mūlaṃ namaḥ* on the head; *mūlaṃ namaḥ* on the mouth; *mūlaṃ namaḥ* at the root of the right arm; *mūlaṃ namaḥ* at the elbow; *mūlaṃ namaḥ* at the wrist.

At the base of the fingers: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*; at the tips of the fingers: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*; at the base of the left arm: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*; at the elbow: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*; at the wrist: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*; at the base of the fingers: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*; at the tips of the fingers: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*; at the base of the right thigh: [mūlaṃ namaḥ].

*Mūlam namaḥ* at the root [of the right leg]; *mūlam namaḥ* at the knee; *mūlam namaḥ* at the ankle; *mūlam namaḥ* at the base of the toes; *mūlam namaḥ* at the tips of the toes; *mūlam namaḥ* at the root of the left thigh;
*mūlam namaḥ* at the knee; *mūlam namaḥ* at the ankle; *mūlam namaḥ* at the base of the toes.

*Oṃ [Mūla-mantra] Namaḥ* on the tip of the finger; *Oṃ [Mūla-mantra] Namaḥ* on the right side; *Oṃ [Mūla-mantra] Namaḥ* on the left side; *Oṃ [Mūla-mantra] Namaḥ* on the back; *Oṃ [Mūla-mantra] Namaḥ* on the navel;
*Oṃ [Mūla-mantra] Namaḥ* on the abdomen; *Oṃ [Mūla-mantra] Namaḥ* on the heart; *Oṃ [Mūla-mantra] Namaḥ* on the right shoulder; *Oṃ [Mūla-mantra] Namaḥ* on the crown of the head.
*Mūlaṃ namaḥ* on the left shoulder; *mūlaṃ namaḥ* from the heart to the tip of the right arm;
*mūlaṃ namaḥ* from the heart to the tip of the left arm; *mūlaṃ namaḥ* from the heart to the tip of the right foot; [and] from the heart to the tip of the left foot.
The root mantra, *namaḥ*, from the heart to the top of the head; the root mantra, *namaḥ*.
Thus is the *anuloma* [sequence].
Now, the *viloma*:
from the heart to the top of the head, "Root-mantra, *namaḥ*"; from the heart to the tip of the left foot.

*Mūlaṃ namaḥ* from the heart to the tips of the right feet; *mūlaṃ namaḥ* from the heart to the tips of the left arms; *mūlaṃ namaḥ* from the heart to the tips of the right arms; *mūlaṃ namaḥ* on the left shoulder; *mūlaṃ namaḥ* on the crown of the head.
Mūla-mantra, salutation to the right shoulder; Mūla-mantra, salutation to the heart; Mūla-mantra, salutation to the abdomen;

Mūla-mantra, salutation to the navel; Mūla-mantra, salutation to the back; Mūla-mantra, salutation to the left side; Mūla-mantra, salutation to the right side; Mūla-mantra, salutation to the tips of the fingers.
At the base of the fingers: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*; at the ankle: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*; at the knee: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*;
at the root of the left thigh: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*; at the tips of the fingers: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*; at the base of the fingers: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*; at the ankle: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*; at the knee: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*.
At the root of the right thigh: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*; at the tips of the fingers: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*; at the base of the fingers: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*; at the wrist: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*; at the elbow: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*;
at the root of the left arm: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*; at the tips of the fingers: *mūlaṃ namaḥ*; at the base of the fingers.
Mūlaṃ namaḥ at the wrists; Mūlaṃ namaḥ at the elbows; Mūlaṃ namaḥ at the base of the right arm; Mūlaṃ namaḥ at the mouth; Mūlaṃ namaḥ at the head;
Mūlaṃ namaḥ at the lower row of teeth; Mūlaṃ namaḥ at the upper row of teeth.

*Mūlaṃ namaḥ* on the lower lip; *mūlaṃ namaḥ* on the upper lip; *mūlaṃ namaḥ* on the left cheek; *mūlaṃ namaḥ* on the right cheek; *mūlaṃ namaḥ* on the left nostril; *mūlaṃ namaḥ* on the right nostril; [and] on the left ear.

*Mūlaṃ namaḥ* on the right ear; *mūlaṃ namaḥ* on the left eye; *mūlaṃ namaḥ* on the right eye; *mūlaṃ namaḥ* on the circumference of the mouth; *mūlaṃ namaḥ* on the forehead. Thus is the reverse order (*viloma*). [Perform this] one hundred and eight times with the root mantra (*mūla*).
One should perform the pervasive placement (vyāpakanyāsa); this is the sixth [chapter].
Now, the placement of the principles (*tattvanyāsa*):
namely—*krīṃ krīṃ krīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hūṃ oṃ*, [recited] from the feet up to the navel, *ātmatattvāya namaḥ*; from the navel up to the heart on the right, *oṃ kālike*.
Salutation to the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva);
from the heart up to the head: *krīṃ krīṃ krīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hūṃ svāhā*; salutation to the principle of Śiva (*oṃ śivatattvāya namaḥ*).
Now, the ritual placement of the seed-syllables (*bījanyāsa*) is as follows: *krīṃ namaḥ* at the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*), *krīṃ namaḥ* between the eyebrows,
*krīṃ namaḥ* on the forehead, *hrīṃ namaḥ* at the navel, *hrīṃ namaḥ* in the secret place, and [the same] on the face.

"Hūṃ namaḥ; hūṃ namaḥ on the limbs of the Guru"—these are the two *nyāsas*. Then, with the seed-syllable of the Vidyā: "Krīṃ krīṃ krīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hūṃ, O Dakṣiṇakālikā, krīṃ krīṃ krīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hūṃ svāhā," and then nine or seven times with the root mantra (*mūla*).
One should perform the fivefold placement of the pervasive [mantras]. Then one should perform meditation as follows:
[one should meditate upon] Kālikā, the divine Dakṣiṇā, who has a terrifying face, is fierce, has loose hair, possesses four arms, and is adorned with a garland of severed heads.
Her left upper and lower lotus-hands hold a sword with a freshly severed head.
And her right hands, the lower and the upper, display the gestures of granting fearlessness and bestowing boons.
She is dark like the luster of a great cloud,
naked, with a garland of severed heads hanging from her neck, smeared with dripping blood.
Terrifying with a pair of corpses used as earrings for her ears,
with a mouth made formidable by terrible fangs, and possessing full, elevated breasts.
She wears a girdle fashioned from a multitude of corpses as sprouts, her face is smiling,
and her countenance is made radiant by streams of blood trickling from both corners of her mouth.
She who utters a terrible roar, who is exceedingly fierce, who dwells in the abode of the cremation ground,
who has protruding teeth, and whose mass of hair hangs down and spreads toward the south.
She is seated upon the heart of Mahādeva in the form of a Śava,
surrounded on the four sides by Śivās of terrible appearance.
And likewise, one should meditate upon the Goddess as being equal to Mahākāla, yet afflicted by the passion for perverse union, for the sake of accomplishing all desires and goals.

Then, having contemplated oneself as free from all impurities and possessing a stainless body, one should visualize oneself in the form of the Goddess. Next, one should visualize the seat (pīṭha) within the body of the deity of the seat. It is as follows:
"Salutation to Maṇḍūka at the Ādhāra; salutation to Kālāgnirudra at the Svādhiṣṭhāna."

At the navel: *namaḥ* to Kacchapa; at the heart: *oṃ namaḥ* to Ādhāraśakti, *namaḥ* to Kūrma, *namaḥ* to Dharā, *namaḥ* to Sudhāsamudra, *namaḥ* to Kalpavṛkṣa, *namaḥ* to Maṇiharmya, *namaḥ* to Hemapīṭha.
Thus one should place [it] in the heart.
p. 27) On the right arm: *namaḥ* to Dharma; on the left: *namaḥ* to Jñāna;
on the left thigh: *namaḥ* to Vairāgya; on the right thigh: *namaḥ* to Aiśvarya; on the face: *namaḥ* to Adharma; on the left side: *namaḥ* to Ajñāna; at the navel: *namaḥ* to Avairāgya.

On the right side: *anaiśvaryāya namaḥ*; in the heart: *saṃsattvāya namaḥ*, *raṃ rajasena namaḥ*, *taṃ tamasena namaḥ*, *tapinyādikalābhyo namaḥ*, *amṛtādikalābhyo namaḥ*, *dhūmrārcikalābhyo namaḥ*, *āṃ ātmane namaḥ*.

Aṃ, obeisance to the inner self (antarātman); Paṃ, obeisance to the supreme self (paramātman); Hrīṃ, obeisance to the self of knowledge (jñānātman); Maṃ, obeisance to the principle of illusion (māyātattva);
Kaṃ, obeisance to the principle of kalā; Viṃ, obeisance to the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva); Paṃ, obeisance to the supreme principle (paratattva).

Homage to the cemetery; homage to the sages and the gods; homage to the jackals who delight in much flesh and bone; homage to the corpses, skulls, funeral pyres, and embers; Oṃ, homage to Jayā; Oṃ, homage to Vijayā.
Oṃ, obeisance to Jitā; Oṃ, obeisance to Aparājitā; Oṃ, obeisance to Nityā;
Oṃ, obeisance to Vilāsinī; Oṃ, obeisance to Dogdhī; Oṃ, obeisance to Aghorā;
Oṃ, obeisance to Maṅgalā. Then: Hsauṃ, obeisance to the Great Preta Lotus Throne.

Having thus visualized the body as the *pīṭha*, and having performed the rising of Kuṇḍalinī and so forth according to the method described in the *Prātaḥkṛtya* (morning rites), one should meditate upon the Goddess, display the respective mudrās, and worship her with mental offerings (*mānasopacāra*). It is as follows: in the *mūlādhāra*, below the penis and above the anus...

One should meditate upon [the goddess] who encircles the self-manifested liṅga (svayambhūliṅga), having the form of a sleeping serpent, upon a bamboo staff joined with four red leaves and the syllables *vaṃ* and *ṣaṃ*. It is as follows:
One should meditate upon the subtle Kuṇḍalinī residing in the Mūlādhāra,
shaped like a sleeping serpent and resembling a mass of lightning.
She is the form of one’s chosen deity (iṣṭadevatā), endowed with three and a half coils,
possessing the brilliance of ten million lightning flashes, and encircling the self-manifested linga (svayambhūliṅga).
Having raised that Great Goddess with the *haṃsa* mantra, the practitioner,
seated firmly, should [visualize her] shining like the light of the rising sun.
With a mind long composed for the sake of pacifying all misfortune without exception,
one should also contemplate one's own body as pervaded by the mass of its radiance.

One should unite this [individual soul] with the Supreme Brahman by means of the path of Suṣumṇā; having brought it into union there with the Supreme Brahman, one should then drink the stream of nectar situated within the lunar orb and, by that—

One should bring [the self] back to the mūlādhāra, as it becomes liquefied, consisting of consciousness, and flowing through the expanse of the universe with floods of nectar trickling from between the two feet— one's own self being composed of pure consciousness and bliss.

One should visualize the form of the deity. Then, having raised Kuṇḍalinī from the *mūlādhāra* by means of the *haṃsa*-mantra, she proceeds to the twelve-petaled heart-lotus, which is marked with six dots and accompanied by the letters from *ka* to *cha*; there, she takes the form of the individual soul (*jīva*), appearing like the flame of a lamp.

Having drawn out the second lamp-flame and cast it into her own mouth, one should unite it with the Supreme Brahman; then, bringing it back to the region of the heart, one should extract the lamp-flame from that mouth and establish it in the *mūlādhāra*.
One should meditate on those lamp-flames as having the form of deities. It is as follows:
She has cloud-like limbs, is naked, and has three eyes;

she utters the howls of jackals and corpses, wears a pair of hair-locks hanging down to her ears which inspire fear, and is garlanded with a string of severed heads. In her left upper and lower lotus-hands, she holds a human head and a sword.
I always pay homage to Kālikā, who holds the gestures of generosity and fearlessness in her right and left hands, and whose mass of hair is disheveled.

Having meditated thus and displayed the respective mudrās, one should worship with mental offerings. Therein, one should pray with this mantra: "Oṃ, welcome, O Goddess of the gods! Be present here, O Kālikā!"

"Accept this mental worship as it has been described according to its true meaning. Then, one should perform the recitation (*japa*) with a rosary (*mālā*) consisting of one hundred and eight beads. Thus concludes the procedure for mental worship (*mānasapūjāvidhi*).
Now, as for the external worship (*bahiḥpūjā*), one should perform the breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*), and so forth. It is as follows:
*krāṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ*; *krīṃ* to the head, *svāhā*; *krūṃ* to the crest-lock, *vaṣaṭ*; *kraiṃ* to the armor, *hum*; *krauṃ* to the three eyes, *vauṣaṭ*; *kraḥ* to the weapon, *phaṭ*.
With these, one should perform the binding of the directions (*digbandhana*) by snapping the fingers. Thus is the ritual placement on the hands (*karanyāsa*).
*krāṃ* to the two thumbs, *namaḥ*; *krīṃ* to the two index fingers, *svāhā*;
*krūṃ* to the two middle fingers, *vauṣaṭ*; *kraiṃ* to the two ring fingers, *hum*; *krauṃ* to the two little fingers, *vauṣaṭ*; *kraḥ* to the palms and backs of the hands, *phaṭ*.
Having thus performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) and so forth, one should [draw] with saffron, vermilion, and the like, using this mantra— *āḥ surekhā vajrarekhā huṃ phaṭ svāhā*—
upon a vessel made of gold, silver, copper, crystal, coral, or any other such material.

One should draw the yantra consisting of a hexagon, a triangle, an eight-petaled lotus, and a square enclosure. As it is stated in the Rudrayāmala: "Then, the yantra for yogis should be prepared with saffron and vermilion."

"The Goddess should be worshipped by the best of men on wheels made of gold, silver, copper, crystal, or likewise wood, according to the prescribed ritual. Also, in the *Sārasaṅgraha*: "In copper [the worship lasts] for twelve years;
in crystal and so forth, however, it is always [effective]. Among these, the crystal [wheel]..."

"It shall become the bestower of all accomplishments," and so forth. Also in another Tantra: "As long as one lives [the benefit] is in gold; in silver, O Dear One, for twenty-two years; in copper, for twelve years; and half of that in birch-bark. [The weight] may be one tola, two tolas, three tolas, or four tolas."
"A man who performs [the rite] according to his own whim incurs sin. Thus ends the external worship (bahiḥpūjā).
Now, the procedure for establishing the *arghya* (offering water) is as follows:
having fashioned a mandala consisting of a triangle, a circle, a hexagon, and a square between oneself and the yantra, and having inscribed the syllable *īṃ*, [one should proceed].
Having worshipped the triangle with three segments of the root mantra, and having worshipped the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga) in the six corners, one should worship in the square:
"Oṃ, namaḥ to the seat of Pūrṇagiri" in the east;
"Oṃ, namaḥ to the seat of Uḍḍīyāna" in the south; and "Oṃ, namaḥ to the seat of Kāmarūpa" [in the west].

Having thus worshipped in the west with "Oṃ, salutation to Jālandharapīṭha," and in the north with "Oṃ, salutation [to Uḍḍiyānapīṭha]," and having worshipped in the center with "Oṃ, salutation to Ādhāraśakti," one should install the Yoni, which is adorned with a triangle within a triangle and a hexagon,
using the root mantra, saying "Salutation."
Having sprinkled [the vessel] with water from the general *argha* vessel, one should worship it with:

"Oṃ vāṃ vīṃ vuṃ ha sa kṣa ma la va ra yūṃ, obeisance to the support of the *arghya* vessel for Kālikā, whose nature is the circle of fire (*vahnimaṇḍala*) of Dharma. Then: "Yaṃ, obeisance to Dhūmrārciṣī; Raṃ..."
Oṃ ūṣmāyai namaḥ; oṃ laṃ jvalinyai namaḥ; oṃ vaṃ jvālinyai namaḥ;
oṃ śaṃ visphuliṅginyai namaḥ; oṃ ṣaṃ suśriyai namaḥ; oṃ saṃ surūpāyai namaḥ;
oṃ haṃ kapilāyai namaḥ; oṃ laṃ havyavāhāyai namaḥ; oṃ kṣaṃ kavyavāhāyai namaḥ.
Having thus worshipped the ten kalās of Bahirdaśa, and having worshipped the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga) in the six corners,

and having worshipped the Goddess in the center with the root mantra, one should recite: "Oṃ śrīkālikā-śrīpātraṃ sthāpayāmi namaḥ," and [place] upon it a vessel made of gold, silver, copper, or coconut.

Alternatively, having washed the vessel with "phaṭ" and placed it down, one should worship it with: "Obeisance to the solar orb consisting of twelve digits beginning with Tapinī, such as Vasupradā, whose essence is *hrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hasakṣamalavarayūṃ*, for the sake of the *arghya* vessel of Śrī Dakṣiṇakālī. Thus, one should complete the worship.
One should worship the *kalās* in clockwise order starting from the east as follows:
"Oṃ *kaṃ bhaṃ* to Tāpinī, obeisance; *khaṃ baṃ* to Tāpanī, obeisance;
*gaṃ phaṃ* to Dhūmrā, obeisance; *ghaṃ paṃ* to Marīcī, obeisance. (p. 30)
Ṅaṃ ṇaṃ, obeisance to Jvālinī; caṃ dhaṃ, obeisance to Ruci; chaṃ daṃ, obeisance to Suṣumnā; jaṃ thaṃ, obeisance to Bhogadā;
jhaṃ taṃ, obeisance to Viśvā; ñaṃ ṇaṃ, obeisance to Bodhinī.
Having worshipped with "Ṭaṃ Ḍhaṃ Dhāriṇyai namaḥ" and "Ṭhaṃ Ḍaṃ Kṣamāyai namaḥ," one should draw a triangle,
a hexagon, and a circle within that vessel using the root mantra (mūla).
Having worshipped the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga) and worshipped the triangle with the root mantra, [one should worship] by means of the reverse alphabet (vilomamātṛkā).

Having recited [the mantra] ten times over milk, water, honey, clarified butter, or other substances, and having filled a triangular vessel with it, one should perform the drying, burning, and flooding of defects by means of the syllables *yaṃ raṃ vaṃ*. Then, [one should worship] the sixteen-fold essence consisting of the digits of nectar that bestows desires, beginning with *saṃ sīṃ sūṃ saha kṣa ma la va ra yūṃ*.

Having worshipped the moon-maṇḍala with the mantra: "Obeisance to the nectar of the *arghya* offering of Śrī Dakṣiṇakālī," one should worship the *kalās* (energetic digits) as follows: "Aṃ, obeisance to Amṛtā; Āṃ, obeisance to Mānadā;
Iṃ, obeisance to Pūṣā; Īṃ, obeisance to Tuṣṭi; Uṃ, obeisance to Puṣṭi."
Ūṃ, obeisance to Vṛtti; Ṛṃ, obeisance to Dhṛti; Ṝṃ, obeisance to Śaśinī; Ḷṃ, obeisance to Candrikā; Ḹṃ, obeisance to Kānti; Eṃ, obeisance to Jyotsnā;
