Tarūṇī, Śāmbhavī, Chinnabhālā, Bhadratāriṇī, Ugrā, Ugraprabhā, Nīlā, Kṛṣṇā, and Nīlasarasvatī. || 3 ||
The second is Śobhanā, Nityā, Navīnā, and Nityanūtanā;
she is Caṇḍikā, Vijayārādhyā, and the goddess Gaganavāhinī. || 4 ||
She who possesses the loud laugh, the terrifying face, and the moving mouth; she who is worshipped by Aditi;
she who possesses qualities and is to be propitiated by those with qualities; she who is worshipped by Hari, Indra, and the gods. || 5 ||
She who loves red, she with red eyes, adorned with a mouth of blood;
she who loves offerings, delights in offerings, difficult to restrain, powerful, and strong.
She who is dear to Bala, who delights in strength, who is worshipped by Balarāma;
she who is the Mistress of half-her hair, whose hair is adorned with Keśava.
Padmamālā, Padmākṣī, Kāmākhyā, Girinandinī, Dakṣiṇā, Dakṣā, Dakṣajā, and Dakṣiṇeratā. || 8 ||
She who loves the *vajra*-flower, who loves the red [lotus], adorned with flowers;
she belongs to Maheśvara, is beloved by Mahādeva, and is adorned with the five [ornaments]. || 9 ||
Iḍā and Piṅgalā, as well as Suṣumnā who is the form of the vital breath (prāṇa),
and Gāndhārī as the fifth, are worshipped by the five-faced one and others.
She is true knowledge, of true form, following the true path;
she is the nature of reality, fond of reality, consisting of the knowledge of reality, and sinless.
She is satisfied by the practice of the tāṇḍava dance, she causes the beloved tāṇḍava to be performed,
she delights in keeping time with rhythm, she is fierce and scorching, and her splendor is like that of the sun.
Endowed with modesty yet free from shame, she is gratified and brings satisfaction;
content with the state of youth, she is devoted to and full of affection for Śakti. || 13 ||
She was attached to Śiva, delighted in Śiva, and devoted solely to the worship of Śiva;
she possessed the luster of copper, a copper-like passion, and subsisted on the light from copper vessels.
She is devoted to the love of Balabhadra, she who provides offerings for the strength of the gods;
she is the form of Rāma, the power of Rāma, and the one who imitates the form of Rāma. || 15 ||
Thus, O Goddess, this most wonderful secret has been told;
by hearing it, one attains liberation through the grace of the Goddess Tārā. (16)
Whoever recites this hymn, the secret praise of Tārā, shall wander upon the circle of the earth endowed with all spiritual accomplishments (siddhis). 17.
For him alone shall there be success in mantra; my own unsurpassed success shall surely come to pass, O Mahāmāyā. This is the truth, the absolute truth; there is no doubt. 18.
Whoever recites this at night on a Monday or a Tuesday while lying down, for him alone there shall be the perfection of mantra; he shall attain the status of a leader of the Gaṇas. || 19 ||
Whether with faith or even without faith, one who recites the *Tārārahasyaka* shall,
in a very short time, become liberated while living and attain the state of Śiva.
O Goddess, by reciting [this] a thousand times, one obtains the fruit of the preliminary rite (*puraścaryā*).
Thus, those who, being constantly disciplined, worship you while meditating [upon you], [attain the goal].
O Great Goddess, they have achieved their purpose regarding the path of death and worldly existence.
Thus ends the hymn of the one hundred names of Tāraṇī from the Svarṇamālā Tantra.
Then Vasiṣṭha spoke the *Sahasranāma* of Śrī Tārā, beginning with the letter *Ta*: "The thousand names of Tārā have emerged from her lotus-like mouth."
O Grandfather, tell me that which has been proclaimed as bringing about the accomplishment of mantras.
Brahmā said:
Listen, my child, I shall proclaim the secret that bestows all perfections;
by the mere instruction of which, you will attain success.
At the beginning of the time of the great dissolution, when all moving and stationary beings had perished, he— having heard of the Great Form— out of compassion withdrew his body.
By that name she became known as Mahātārā, possessing the form of Brahmā;
having fashioned three great tridents, she remained there all alone.
Furthermore, there arose a desire for creation known as the Divine Empire;
its thousand names, beginning with the letter 'ta', were remembered by me.
By her power, O twice-born one, the vast and very firm cosmic egg was fashioned;
we appeared there within its mechanisms from of old.
Just as we were wandering there, seeking our own purpose, she, out of compassion, instructed us and became the cause of our creation. (7)
O best of Brahmins, by her grace the three lords of the universe and all other hosts of gods are her servants at her feet.
Through recitation and retention, I am the creator and Hari is the protector;
through the instruction on the syllables of reality, Śaṅkara himself is the destroyer.
(136) Meditation on the seers, meters, and so forth is proclaimed as being like the root;
likewise, the application [of mantras] is for the accomplishment of mere worldly tasks and for the four aims of human life. 10.

Tārā consists of five syllables beginning with *tāra*; another Tārā is born from the potency of the Vedas; she is the syllable devoid of *tāra* and *tāra*; she begins with *tāra* and has *tāra* as her form.
Born from the Night of Stars (Tārārātri), striving during the Night of Stars,
intent on the recitation of the Night of Stars, she is the very embodiment of the Night of Stars.
Tārārājñī is ever-contented, Tārārājñī is the bestower of boons; she is the very embodiment of Tārārājñī and the giver of the success of Tārārājñī. (13)
Tārā is the abode within the lotus-heart; Tārā is beyond the lotus-heart;
Tārā is the support of the lotus-heart; and likewise, Tārā is the lotus-heart itself. || 14 ||
She is the Mistress of the Stars (Tāreśvarī), possessing the luster of stars, and her very nature is that of the host of stars;
she is surrounded by the host of stars and attended by the host of stars.

Tārā, accompanied by Tārās, Tārā adorned with jewel-encrusted ornaments; Tārā who is near to the sound of the host of stars (tārāgaṇa), and Tārā worshipped through the performance of the rite of Tārā. || 16 ||

She whose food is provided by the hosts of stars, she whose refuge is provided by the hosts of stars, she whose dwelling is provided by the hosts of stars, she who is devoted to the hosts of stars. || 17 ||
She is strewn with a multitude of the qualities of stars; she bestows a multitude of the qualities of stars;
she is attached to a multitude of the qualities of stars; she is the abode of a multitude of the qualities of stars. || 18 ||
Tāreśvarī, she who is worshipped by Tāra, she whose mantra is Tāra, she who delivers;
she who is foremost among those called Tāra, she who is named Tārā, she who is skillful with the Tāra-mantra, and Tāriṇī. || 19 ||
She who is accessible through the stars, she who abides in the stars, she who is the immortal river of the stars;
she who is worthy of being reached by the stars, she whose essence is the stars, and she who is the savior through the stars. || 20 ||
She who dwells within the stars, whose ornament is the multitude of stars,
who is enriched by the beauty of a necklace of stars, and whose courtyard is surrounded by stars.
She is strewn with stars like swans and crows; she is adorned with ornaments made of stars;
her limbs are beautified by armlets of stars; and her bracelets are set with stars.
She whose girdle is adorned with stars, whose eating is accompanied by stars, who wears garments variegated with stars, and whose seat is a circle of stars. || 23 ||
Her crown is strewn with stars; her earrings rest upon stars;
and the regions of her cheeks shine with a pair of star-adorned earrings.
She whose lotus feet rest upon stars, she who grants boons to the stars, she whose heart was given by the stars, and she whose arrows are adorned with stars. || 25 ||
Skilled in the ritual placement of the stars (tārakā-nyāsa), her very form is the ritual placement of the stars;
she is satisfied by the ritual placement of the stars and bestows the perfection of the ritual placement of the stars.

She whose abode is the placement of the stars (tārakā-nyāsa), she who is worshipped through the placement of the stars, she who is delighted by the placement of the stars, and she who bestows the perfection of the placement of the stars. || 27 ||

(137) She is immersed in the deposition of the stars (tārakānyāsa), she dwells within the deposition of the stars, and she bestows the accomplishment of mantras that are complete through the deposition of the stars. || 28 ||

She whose life-breath is the Tāraka devotee, she who is dear to the Tāraka devotee, she who cannot be attained by those other than the Tāraka devotee, and she who grants the desired objects to the Tāraka devotees. (29)
She is devoted to the Tārakopāsaka, she seeks the Tārakopāsaka, she honors the Tārakopāsaka, and she takes refuge in the Tārakopāsaka. || 30 ||
She who is satisfied by the demon Tāraka, she who is worshipped by the demon Tāraka, she who is the creator of the manifestation of the demon Tāraka, and she who is saluted by Tāraka. || 31 ||
She is honored by the demon Tāraka, she bestows pride upon the demon Tāraka,
she is perfected through the demon Tāraka, and she is the deity of the demon Tāraka.
She who dwells within the body of the demon Tāraka, she who grants heaven to the demon Tāraka, she who is united with the demon Tāraka, and she who bestows pride upon the demon Tāraka. (33)
She is the destroyer of the demon Tāraka, the crusher of the demon Tāraka;
she is the dancer in the battle with the demon Tāraka and the remover of the stars.
She who waged war against the demon Tāraka, she who bore the slayer of Tāraka, and she who was saluted by the multitude of headless trunks in the battle with the demon Tāraka. || 35 ||
She is the mother of the enemy of Tāraka’s enemies, yet she is the enemy of Kārika;
she is the captivator of the mind of the enemy of Tāraka, and she is the instructor in garments and ornaments.
She is the performer of the act of saving, the creator, and she is served by those who perform the act of saving;
she is pleased by the words of those who perform the act of saving, and she is well-instructed by those who perform the act of saving. || 37 ||
She who is perfectly satisfied by the enemy of Tāraka, adorned by the enemy of Tāraka, whose lap is occupied by the enemy of Tāraka, and who bestows great joy upon the enemy of Tāraka. 38.
With all her limbs filled with darkness, her body smeared with darkness, she clings to places pervaded by darkness, resembling a mass of gloom. (39)
She is the destroyer of darkness, the creator of darkness, the one who causes movement within darkness;
she whose limbs are dark, the giver of darkness, the vessel of darkness, and the remover of darkness.

She who is filled with masses of darkness, she who destroys the masses of darkness, she who effects the destruction of the masses of darkness, and she who causes fear to the masses of darkness. || 41 ||
Her face is radiant with the quality of tamas; she bestows the perfect accomplishment of the quality of tamas;
she stands upon the path taught by the quality of tamas; she is resplendent with the quality of tamas. || 42 ||

Devoted to the praise of the quality of darkness (tamas), increasing the quality of darkness, intent on those who have taken refuge in the quality of darkness, and yet destroying that very quality of darkness. || 43 ||
She who causes the destruction of the quality of darkness (tamas), whose body consists of the quality of darkness,
who is pleased by the annihilation of the quality of darkness, and who is established on the far shore of darkness.
Delighting in the existence born of darkness, fond of the existence born of darkness, lacking faith in the existence born of darkness, and taking refuge in the existence born of darkness. || 45 ||
Her life-force arises from the state of darkness; she is worshipped by those whose existence arises from darkness;
she stands upon the site of the *kumbha* (pitcher), embraced by the love of those whose existence arises from darkness. (46)

She who is satisfied by the multitude of ascetics, she who bestows nourishment upon the multitude of ascetics, she who is praised by the multitude of ascetics, and she who is saluted by the multitude of ascetics. || 47 ||
She is endowed with multitudes of ascetics, she bestows joy upon multitudes of ascetics, she is worshipped by multitudes of ascetics, and she is adorned by multitudes of ascetics. || 48 ||
She dwells upon the surface of the ascetics' minds, she moves within the hearts of the ascetics;
she is worthy of being contemplated by the minds of the ascetics, and she captivates the hearts of the ascetics. || 49 ||
She is the radiance of the creeper of the ascetics' resolve, the wish-fulfilling tree for the ascetics,
the cow of plenty for the ascetics, and the one who fulfills the desires of the ascetics.
Devoted to the protection of ascetics, she resides in the homes of ascetics;
she is the glory of the king of ascetics' dwellings and the bestower of sovereignty upon ascetics.

She who is to be propitiated by the minds of ascetics, she who bestows honor upon ascetics, she who removes the suffering of ascetics, and she who brings peace to the afflictions of ascetics. || 52 ||
She is the accomplishment of knowledge for ascetics and the bringer of success through the mantras of ascetics;
she is the sovereign of the mantras and tantras of ascetics and possesses the very form of the mantras of ascetics.
Skilled in the mantras of ascetics, performing the duties of ascetics, born from the deeds of ascetics, and a witness to the deeds of ascetics. || 54 ||
She is to be served through austerity, she is to be realized through austerity, she is to be manifested through austerity;
she is the ascetic woman, she is mastered by austerity, she is accessible through austerity, and she dwells in the abode of austerity. || 55 ||
She is blessed with austerity, honored for her austerity, a maiden of austerity, and enveloped by austerity;
she is truth itself as austerity, protected by austerity, recited as austerity, and made real through austerity.
She whose essence is austerity, who is attained through austerity, who is honored by austerity, and who consists of austerity;
she who is the twilight of austerity, who is never lacking in austerity, and who brings about the presence of austerity. || 57 ||
She is to be meditated upon through austerity, sung of through austerity, one who has practiced austerity, and whose strength is austerity;
she is to be approached through austerity, the giver of austerity, and the bestower of the fruit that is the reality of austerity.
She is the destroyer of the foremost obstacles to penance, the annihilator of obstacles to penance;
she is the one who shatters the mass of obstacles to penance and the one who strikes fear into those obstacles to penance. || 59 ||

She is the life-force of the boon-granting regions of austerity, praised by the lords of those regions of austerity, meditated upon by the lords of those regions of austerity, and she bestows what is desired by the lords of those regions of austerity. 60.
She who dwells as a deer in the penance grove, she who destroys the penance grove, she who delights in moving through the penance grove, and she who sports in the penance grove. || 61 ||
She is attached to the fruits of the penance grove, she bestows the fruits of the penance grove;
she is easily accomplished through the penance grove, and she grants the perfect success of the penance grove.
She is to be well-served by those in penance groves, she dwells in penance groves;
she is to be well-served by those whose wealth is austerity, and she is perfectly accomplished through those whose wealth is austerity.
She is well-reposed in those whose wealth is austerity; she consists of the minds of those whose wealth is austerity;
she is the salutation of those whose wealth is austerity; she is the bestower of liberation upon those whose wealth is austerity. (64)

She who cannot be attained except through the wealth of asceticism, whose very self is the wealth of asceticism, who is to be propitiated by the wealth of asceticism, and who bestows the fruit of asceticism. (65)
She is enriched by the wealth of asceticism, the sovereign of the wealth of asceticism,
delighted by the wealth of asceticism, and the abode of the wealth of asceticism.

Crowded with people whose wealth is asceticism, a refuge for people whose wealth is asceticism, worthy of worship by people whose wealth is asceticism, and the mother of people whose wealth is asceticism. || 67 ||
She is the life-breath of those whose wealth is austerity, she bestows what is desired by those whose wealth is austerity,
she is unattainable by those whose wealth is austerity, and she is the sovereign of those whose wealth is austerity.
Afflicted by the drinking of fresh blood, satiated with fresh blood, dwelling in an ocean of fresh blood, she bestows joy through fresh blood. (69)
She is well-satisfied by fresh blood, smeared with fresh blood,
her life-breath is the river of fresh blood, and she is adorned with fresh blood.

She who delights in the offerings of young deer, she who is fond of the offerings of young deer, she whose life-breath is the offering of young deer, and she who grants the desired objects of the offerings of young deer. (71)

She who is pleased by the oblation of the young goat, she who is dear to the oblation of the young goat, she who smells the oblation of the young goat, she who is the consumer of the oblation of the young goat. 72.
Resembling the rising sun, having the form of the rising sun, radiant as the rising sun, and as pure as the rising sun. || 73 ||
She whose abode is the rising sun, whose orb is the rising sun;
she who is as lovely as the rising sun, and who wears earrings like the rising sun.
Her moonlight is like the rising sun; her radiance is like the rising sun;
her appearance is like the rising sun; she is nourished by the rising sun. || 75 ||
She is young, with young eyes;
she is young, with young glances; she is young, with young pupils; she is young, with young ornaments. || 76 ||

She who has received the secret appointment from young women, she who has been adorned by young women, she who is delighted by the company of young women, she who is the jewel among young women. || 77 ||

She is to be served by the jewels of young women, she is worshipped by the jewels of young women, she is satisfied by the jewels of young women, and she is honored by the jewels of young women. || 78 ||
She is the one whose speech is the delight of the assembly of young women, she who is worshipped by the assembly of young women,
she who is praised by the assembly of young women, and she who bestows honor upon the assembly of young women.
Standing in the midst of a multitude of young women, surrounded by a multitude of young women, delighted by a multitude of young women, and adorned by a multitude of young women. || 80 ||
She is perfected through the recitation of the Taruṇī mantra; she bestows liberation through the recitation of the Taruṇī mantra;
she is intent upon those who worship the Taruṇī; she is the seeker of those who worship the Taruṇī. || 81 ||
She bestows fortune upon those who worship young women; she removes the suffering of those who worship young women;
she is the life-breath of those who worship young women; and she inflicts pain upon those who revile young women. (82)
She dwells within ten million young women; she has the form of ten million young women;
she stands in the midst of ten million young women; she is surrounded by ten million young women. || 83 ||

She who is difficult for millions of young women to attain, whose form consists of millions of young women, who is as beautiful as millions of young women, and who is the youthful mistress of all young women. 84.
Richly adorned with necklaces of young gems, wearing earrings of young gems, satisfied by young gems, and embellished with young gems. || 85 ||
Delighting in the path of young women, devoted to the path of young women, abiding on the path of young women, and finding pleasure in the path of young women. || 86 ||
She is the bestower of glory upon the orb of the sun, the sovereign of the orb of the sun, the faith within the orb of the sun, and she who abides in the orb of the sun. || 87 ||
She is enriched by the worship of the solar orb, she is adored by the solar orb, she is meditated upon as the solar orb, and she is the boat across the ocean of existence. 88.

She who is intent upon the cause of crossing over, she who is worshipped by the carpenters who cross over, she who bestows the glory of crossing over upon the carpenters, and she who is the seeker of those who cross over and the carpenters. || 89 ||

She whose nature is to cross over, she who causes the crossing by means of the boat, she who is to be known through the crossing by means of the boat, and she who effects the crossing by means of the boat. || 90 ||
She is tree-formed, situated upon trees, consisting of trees and creepers;
she is tree-formed, resides in trees, and dwells within the midst of trees.
She dwells in a house of molten gold, upon a floor of molten gold, within walls of molten gold, and wearing sandals of molten gold. || 92 ||
Her limbs radiant like molten gold, resembling molten gold,
her body fair as molten gold, she rests upon a couch of molten gold.
Richly adorned with garments of molten gold, possessing a form of molten gold,
situated in the midst of molten gold, she is the creator of molten gold.
Worshipping with molten gold, eating from a vessel of molten gold,
dwelling upon a mountain of molten gold, and wearing earrings of molten gold— 95.
Rich with constellations like molten gold, holding a staff of molten gold,
adorned with ornaments of molten gold, she is the giver of gifts of molten gold.
She is the sovereign of the land of molten gold, bearing a bow of molten gold;
she is enriched with quivers of molten gold and carries arrows of molten gold.
She is the ordainer of Talātala and the fashioner of Talātala;
she is the sovereign mistress of the very nature of Talātala and the one who sports in Talātala. || 98 ||

She who is unattainable by the inhabitants of Talātala, the sovereign of the inhabitants of Talātala, she who is worshipped by the inhabitants of Talātala, and the bestower of wealth upon the inhabitants of Talātala. 99.
She who possesses the victory over Talātala, she who is restless with the joy of Talātala, she who is enriched by the jewels of Talātala, and she who is the deity of Talātala. (100)
She delights in the sites along the river; she dwells upon the riverbanks.
She is the river itself, she moves along the river's shore, and she is beloved by the river.
Delighting in bathing in the river, intent upon bathing in the river, praiseworthy for bathing in the river, she bestows the fruits of bathing in the river. 102.
Taṭalāsthā, Taṭasthānā, Taṭeśī, Taṭavāsinī, Taṭapūjyā, Taṭārādhyā, and Taṭaromamukhārtthinī. || 103 ||
Born on the bank, having the form of the bank, standing on the bank, flickering on the bank;
dwelling in a house near the bank, accompanied [by others], and reclining on the bank. || 104 ||
She has waves, she possesses the appearance of waves, and her eyes are as long as waves;
she is as difficult to overcome as a wave and as fickle as a wave. || 105 ||
Her limbs were as long as waves, she grew like the waves, her increase was like the waves, and she was as pure as the waves. || 106 ||
Dwelling in the midst of a lake, born from the center of a lake,
praiseworthy for her arrangement of necklaces, she is intent on the creation of a lake.
She who is fragrant with the lotuses of the pond, the mistress of the pond, the one possessing a pond;
she who has bathed in the waterless pond, and she who is as pure as the waters of the pond.
She whose abode is the lotus of the pond, whose dwelling is the lotus of the pond, who resides within the lotus of the pond, and who arises from the lotus of the pond. 109.
She whose body was like a lotus in a pond, whose face was like a lotus in a pond, whose life-breath was like a lotus in a pond, and whose eyes were like lotuses in a pond. || 110 ||
She who dwells upon red lotuses in a pond, she who moves among white lotuses in a pond, she who has the luster of blue lotuses in a pond, and she who bears blue lotuses from a pond. (111)
She who has entered the body, she who is slender, she whose limbs are delicate, she who assumes a subtle form;
she whose nature is subtle, she who has entered the subtle, she who sustains the subtle, and she whose form is the subtle. || 112 ||
She whose limbs are slender, whose waist is thin, whose auspicious body is delicate, who is to be served by her own body, who is born of the body, and who originates from the body. (113)
Born from the body of the embodied one, she bestows a subtle body and makes that body exceedingly thin;
she is the destroyer of the body of the embodied one and the cause of its movement.
She is truthful in speech, truthful in word, one who acts truthfully, and a speaker of truth;
she maintains truth, her conduct is truthful, and she follows the true Dharma.
She who experiences reality, whose gait is reality, who bestows boons through true devotion;
she who is the sovereign of the base reality, whose mind and conduct are reality, and who grants swift accomplishment. 116.
She whose nature is both conceivable and inconceivable, who bestows reasoning and performs reasoning;
she who presides over the teaching of reasoning and brings about the teaching of reasoning. || 117 ||
She is satisfied by the teaching of logic, she is embodied as the teaching of logic;
she is devoted to the practice of teaching logic, and she is propounded through the meaning of logic. (118)
She is satisfied by the teaching of logic, she expounds the meaning of logic, her words rest upon logical arguments, and she increases the discourse of logic. || 119 ||
She is uniquely skilled in the art of logic, she who moves within the sphere of logical discourse;
her limbs are dark like the leaf of the *tāla* tree, and she wears a garland of *tāla* leaves.
She whose secret rendezvous is in the Tamāla forest, who is worshipped with Tamāla flowers;
she who dwells in Tagara, who is propitiated by Tagara, and whose sandals are honored with Tagara. || 121 ||
She is satisfied by garlands of *tagara*, she is adorned with garlands of *tagara*, she is pleased by offerings of *tagara*, and she bestows fame through offerings of *tagara*. 122.
She is perfected by offerings of *tagara* incense and bestows honor through those same offerings;
she has the form of a flash of lightning and eyes as flickering as lightning.
She is the streak of lightning, she whose body is lightning, she who is radiant with lightning, she whose splendor is lightning;
she is of that form, the mistress of its true nature, composed of it, and having the essence of reality as her form.
She is intent on bestowing that station, the giver of the fruits of those actions;
she is the creator of reality, the giver of reality, reality itself, the knower of reality, and the one who satisfies with reality.
She is worshipped through the principles, she is the worship of the principles, she is the offering of water (arghya) according to the principles, and she is the embodiment of the principles.
She is the sovereign bestower of the knowledge of reality, and she grants the excellent liberation of the knowledge of reality.
Tvaritā, she who is pleased by speed, the destroyer of swift affliction;
Tvaritā, she who is satisfied by the essence of speed, Tvaritā, she who grants swift gratification. || 127 ||
Clad in bark, wearing bark as her garment, she was tremulous with restless eyes;
she wore the skin of a hyena as her dress and was adorned with the hide of a hyena.
She whose life-force is that of a hyena, who moves upon the back of a hyena, who is stationed upon the back of a hyena, and who dwells upon the back of a hyena. || 129 ||
Her thirst for libations has been quenched by the waters; her mind is intent on offering libations;
her heart rejoices in the bliss of libation; she is the praise of the Lord of Libations. || 130 ||

She consists of the three Vedas, she is served by the three Vedas, she is worshipped by the three Vedas, she is the discourse of the three Vedas; she is the essence of the three Vedas, she is to be contemplated through the three Vedas, she is the goal of the three Vedas, and she is united with the three Vedas. || 131 ||
She who consists of three syllables, the sovereign of the three-syllabled mantra, the mistress of the three-syllabled mantra who grants swift accomplishment;
she who is the ruler of the three syllables, who abides in the three syllables, and who removes the suffering of those composed of the three syllables.
She is Tapanā, Tapaneṣṭā, and Tapastapanakanyakā;
she is as unbearable as the rays of the sun and possesses the splendor of ten million suns.
She who is of refined gold, she who has ascended to the surface of the couch,
she who provides the couch, she who is fashioned from the couch, she who dwells upon the couch, she who bestows the couch, and she who takes refuge in the surface of the couch.
Her surface is like molten gold, she longs for the rays of molten gold;
she is heated by the gift of molten gold and resides upon the mountain of molten gold. (135)
She who dwells on the couch, she who gives the couch, she who is seated upon the couch, she who is dear to the couch;
she who loves the couch, she who is devoted to the couch, and she who is the creator of the couch.
She who is intent on worshiping with speed, she who bestows boons with speed, she who confers success with speed, and she who grants liberation with speed. || 137 ||
She is the female ascetic, the one to be propitiated by ascetics, the destroyer of the afflictions of ascetics;
she is the distressed ascetic, the glory of ascetics, and the one who speaks kindly to ascetics. || 138 ||
Her heart is filled with joy for the ascetics; she bestows joy upon the ascetics;
her lotus feet are resorted to by the ascetics; and her mind is devoted to the ascetics. || 139 ||
Tāmasī is worshipped by those of a tamasic nature; she is eager for the affection of the tamasic;
Tāmasī is Sītā herself; Tāmasī bestows swift accomplishment. || 140 ||
She who is the mistress of rhythm, she who enjoys rhythm, she who bestows rhythm, she whose breasts resemble palm trees;
she who dwells in the palmyra tree, she who is born from the palmyra tree, she whose form is that of the palmyra tree. || 141 ||
She who is Tārkkṣā, mounted upon Tārkkṣa, the Mistress of Tārkkṣa, worshipped by Tārkkṣa;
the Sovereign of Tārkkṣa, the Mother of Tārkkṣa, and the Bestower of boons through the Lord of Tārkkṣa. || 142 ||
She is Tāpī, Tapinī, the destroyer of ascetics (tāpasa), the dispeller of heat, the giver of heat, the creator of heat, and the one who brings about the destruction of all suffering. || 143 ||
She who causes terror, she who bestows fear, she who removes terror, and she who destroys it;
she who is herself terrified, she who is free from fear, and she who acts as the uprooter of terror.

She who provides protection, who is devoted to protecting, who seeks to protect, who bestows protection; she who delights in the song of protection, who effects protection, and who sings of protection. 145.
She is filled with the nectar of youth, an ocean of the nectar of youth;
she is satisfied by the nectar of youth and satiated by the nectar of youth.
Her limbs are filled with the nectar of youth; her very form is the embodiment of the nectar of youth;
she is endowed with the virtues of youth; and she is skilled in the expression of youthful sentiments. || 147 ||
She is the mistress of betel, intent upon chewing betel,
her mouth filled with betel, and her lips reddened by betel.
Renowned for her jeweled earrings, adorned with jeweled earrings, situated between two jeweled earrings, and decorated with a pair of earrings. 149.
She is the mistress of the lunar days (tithi), she is to be worshipped by the lunar days, she dwells in the lunar days, and she has the form of the lunar days;
she resides in the three lunar days, she is to be served, and she is the bestower of boons upon the lords of the lunar days.

She who is worshipped by Tilottamā and others, she who possesses the splendor of Tilottamā and others, Tilottamā, she who is sprinkled with sesame seeds, she who is worshipped by sesame seeds, and she who is honored by sesame seeds. || 151 ||
She who eats sesame, she who bestows sesame, she who is satisfied by sesame, she whose abode is sesame;
she who grants the ground, she who resembles sesame, and she who provides sesame oil. || 152 ||
Her limbs are anointed with sesame oil, and she is fragrant with the scent of sesame oil;
she is satisfied by oblations of sesame and clarified butter, and she bestows the success of oblations of sesame and clarified butter. (153)

She who is pleased by an offering of sesame flowers, she who is fond of an offering of sesame flowers, she who is most excellent with an offering of sesame flowers, and she who destroys the splendor of the sesame flower. 154.
She whose vermilion rests upon her forehead mark, whose sandalwood paste is marked by the tilaka, whose musk is drawn out by the tilaka, and who is enchanted by the fragrance of the tilaka. || 155 ||

She whose form consists of the three qualities, who possesses a body endowed with the three qualities, who is renowned for her threefold nature, she is the triple-formed one whose essence is the three qualities. || 156 ||
Triśirā, Tripureśānī, Tripurā, Tripureśvarī, Tripureśī, Trilokasthā, Tripurī, and Tripurāmbikā. || 157 ||
She who is to be propitiated by Tripurāri, she who bestows boons upon Tripurāri;
she who is the crest-ornament of Tripurāri’s head, she who bestows boons upon Tripurāri. 158.
She who bestows the welfare of the enemy of Tripura, she who is the tutelary deity of the enemy of Tripura;
she whose half-body was fashioned by the enemy of Tripura, she who sports with the enemy of Tripura. 159.
She is the destroyer of the demon Tripura, the crusher of the demon Tripura,
the one served by the demon Tripura, and she who is honored by the foremost among the demons of Tripura.
She who possesses the three peaks, she who is worshipped by the three peaks, she whose form is adored at the three peaks;
she who dwells in the midst of the Trikūṭa mountain, she who resides upon the Trikūṭa mountain. || 161 ||
Born from the Trikūṭa mountain, emerged from the Trikūṭa mountain;
she who has three matted locks, the sovereign of those with three matted locks, the bestower of boons upon those with three matted locks. || 162 ||
The mistress of the three eyes, the three-eyed one, and the excellent consort of the three-eyed Lord;
she who possesses the three folds [of the waist], is endowed with the three folds, and is the bearer of the excellent trident. || 163 ||
She who possesses the Lord of the Trident, she who is the Mistress of the Trident-bearer, the bearer of the trident, and the possessor of the trident;
she who is to be worshipped by the three Manūs, she who is the sovereign of the worshippers of the three Manūs. 164.
She is pleased by the three types of humans, she grants swift accomplishment to the three types of men;
she is delighted by the worship of the three mantras and bestows liberation through meditation on the three mantras. || 165 ||
She is the threefold, threefold devotion; she is honored by the three, the sovereign of the three honors;
she abides in the three states, the mistress of the three states, completely filled with the three states.
She whose self is the three principles, the mistress of the three principles, the knower of the three principles, the upholder of the three principles;
she who is pleased by the sipping of water (ācamana) consisting of the three principles, and who grants the desired fruits of that three-principled ācamana.
She who resides in the triangle, she who is the mistress of the triangle, she who dwells within the wheel of the triangle;
she who stands in the center of the wheel of the triangle, she whose form is the bindu of the triangle. || 168 ||

Established within the triangular yantra, having the form of the triangular yantra, she is to be worshipped with the triangular yantra and is the bestower of the siddhis of the triangular yantra. (169)
She is enriched by the three letters, the sovereign of the three letters, and her form is the worship of the three letters;
she abides in the three letters, is enriched by the three letters, and bestows boons through the three letters. || 170 ||
She whose beginning consists of the three letters, she who is worshipped by the three letters, she who bestows the fruits of the three aims of life;
she who is enriched by the three aims, she who is the mistress of the three aims, and she who grants the first fruits of the three aims. || 171 ||
She is worshipped at the three junctions of the day, she is the Mistress of the three junctions, and she grants the desired fruits through worship at the three junctions;
she is satisfied by the worship at the three junctions, and she bestows liberation through the recitation performed at the three junctions.
She whose feet are worshipped by the three Vedas, she who consists of the three steps, the sovereign of the three steps;
she who is the mistress of that which cannot be reached even by the three steps, she who is the three steps themselves, and she who brings about their realization. || 173 ||
She is the triple power (triśakti) and the mistress of the triple power; she bestows the desired fruits of the triple power.
She is beloved by the triple power, she is cherished by the triple power, and she is completely surrounded by the triple power.
She is Triveṇī, the woman who is Triveṇī, worshipped by Mādhava at Triveṇī;
she is satisfied by the waters of Triveṇī and bestows the merit of bathing in Triveṇī. || 175 ||
She is bathed in the waters of the Triveṇī, she is the very form of the Triveṇī water;
her limbs are purified by the waters of the Triveṇī, and she is worshipped with the waters of the Triveṇī.
Abiding in the three channels, having the three channels as her nature, she moves within the middle of the three channels;
she is most auspicious at the junctions of the three channels, and she possesses the three channels and the three points.

She consists of fifty-three lines, she moves along the path of the three powers, she abides on the triple path, she is the sovereign of the three worlds, and she bestows liberation upon the three crores of families. 178.
She who delights in the three Rāmas, she who is worshipped by the three Rāmas, she who bestows boons upon the three Rāmas;
she whose lotus feet are resorted to by the thirty gods, she who is more radiant than the abode of the thirty gods.
She is the thirty-three [gods], she is sought after by the thirty-three, she is the swift bestower of boons upon the thirty-three;
she is endowed with the sovereignty of the thirty-three and is served by the Lord of the thirty-three. || 180 ||
She who is to be worshipped during the three watches of the night, the Mistress of the Three Watches, the bestower of infinite accomplishments during the three watches;
she whose moonlight exceeds that of the Mistress of the Three Watches, and whose face surpasses that of the Mistress of the Three Watches.

Gentle like the Lord of the Three Nights (the Moon), adorned by the Lord of the Three Nights, possessing the loveliness of the Lord of the Three Nights, her face endowed with ten million jewels. || 182 ||
Abiding in the three times, knowing the three times, she who brings about the knowledge of the three times;
the mistress of the three times, worshipped in the three times, she who bestows the knowledge of the three times. || 183 ||
She dwells on the bank, she goes to the bank, she is the river of the bank, she resides on the bank;
she is born in the land of Tīrabhukti and established in the land of Tīrabhukti. || 184 ||
Resembling the sharp and the unsharp rays [of the sun], she dwells within the lap of the Sharp-rayed One (the Sun);
her limbs are radiant as ten million rays of the Sharp-rayed One, and her form consists of ten million rays of the Sharp-rayed One. (185)
She is sharp, sharper still, the crusher of the fierce demon Mahiṣāsura;
her hand glitters with a sharp sickle, and she wields a sharp sword. || 186 ||
Fierce, with a fierce gait, she is the destroyer of the fierce hosts of asuras;
she has fierce ornaments of the eight nāgas and fierce adornments of severed heads.
She whose nature is the sacred ford, who consists of the sacred ford, the mistress of the sacred ford, worshipped by the sacred ford;
the sovereign lady of the king of sacred fords, the bestower of the fruit of the sacred ford, and the giver of the gift of the sacred ford. 188.
She is tumultuous, possessed of tumultuous wisdom, the destroyer of tumultuous asuras;
she delights in tumultuous blood and moves within the tumultuous courtyard.
She is the female horse-rider, mounted upon a horse, moving on the back of a steed;
she delights in the gait of a horse and moves with the speed of a horse. || 190 ||
The fourth is comparison; it is equal, its conduct is equal, and it acts with equality.
It is the mistress of weighing, the sign of Libra, and the one who knows the subtle within the sign of Libra.
Tumbikā, she who eats from the vessel of a gourd, she who desires the gourd;
Tulasī, the most excellent Tulasī, born of Tulaja, the sovereign of Tulaja. || 192 ||
She is satisfied by the vow of the fire of chaff;
she is made from a heap of chaff by the fire of chaff; her limbs are cool as the moon; she fulfills the desires of the moon. || 193 ||
Tuṣārādri, Tuṣārādrisutā, Tuhinadīdhiti, Tuhinācalakanyā, and Tuhinācalavāsinī. (194)
She is the sovereign of the group of musical instruments, the bestower of the group of musical instruments, and the giver of the four Vedas;
she is the essence of the most excellent among musical instruments, possessing the nature of the Lord of the supreme musical instruments.

She is the giver of contentment, the creator of contentment, and contentment itself; she carries two quivers upon her back, is fully satisfied by the knowledge of Tumburu, and bestows the attainment of fulfilled perfection.

She is the swift bestower of kingdoms, the swift giver of stammering eloquence, the swift giver of lotuses, the swift bestower of scholarship, and the swift giver of previously incomplete strength. || 197 ||
She who is the third, the mistress of the third, worshipped on the third lunar day;
she whose crest-jewel is the moon on the third day, adorned with the moon as her third ornament. || 198 ||
Satisfaction, the cause of satisfaction, the satisfied one; thirst, the increaser of thirst;
the fulfiller of thirst, the destroyer of thirst, the thirsty one, and thirst itself. (199)
Accomplished in the Tretā age, she is the Tretā herself, bestowing the fruits of the Tretā Yuga;
she is the worship of the three worlds, the giver of the three worlds, and the bestower of the perfections of the three worlds. || 200 ||

She who bestows the lordship of the three worlds, the Supreme Sovereign of the three worlds, the Mistress of the Enchantment of the three worlds, and the Giver of the sovereignty of the three worlds. || 201 ||
The Mistress of the thirty-three branches, she who possesses thirty-three branches, the bestower of discernment regarding the three;
she dwells in a house adorned with arches, her mind fixed upon the arches. (202)
She who fastens golden bracelets upon the arms of the Tola, she whose armlets are made of gold weighing a Tula;
she who has the form of the *tomara* weapon, and she who wields the *tomara* weapon. || 203 ||
She is the sovereign of the triple arts (tauryatrika), the master of the threefold art, and she who is eager for the triple arts;
she is subtle like a thread and the essence of the sacred threads, mantras, and sounds.

She who is to be worshipped through the Tantras, the Mistress of Tantra, esteemed by the Tantras; she who knows the Tantras, who understands the Tantras, who is to be accomplished through the Tantras, and whose very nature is the Tantras. || 205 ||
Established in the Tantra, born of the Tantra, the lute-player, the bearer of the Tantra, the giver of the Tantric mantra;
the source of the Tantra, moving within the Tantra, the mistress of the Tantra, worshipped by the Tantra, she who bestows the accomplishments (siddhis) found therein. || 206 ||
Thus has been told to you this divine [hymn], which bestows the fruit of ten million sacrifices;
it is the thousand names of Tārā, beginning with the letter 'Ta', and is well-guarded as a secret. (207)
Charity, sacrifice, austerity, pilgrimage, vows, fasting, and so forth—each of these names has been declared by me as equal in merit to the performance of the Sandhyā prayers. || 208 ||
Only he whose mind is unwavering toward the Guru, the Deity, and likewise the Mantra, shall possess the qualification for this recitation of the hymn. || 209 ||
The mantra-practitioner, whose body is marked by the sixfold [deities] undivided from the Great Cīna-krama and who is endowed with the Krama initiation, should recite this; it is not otherwise.
Having worshipped Tārā according to the rules with the five types of substances beginning with perfumes and flowers, the twice-born one, with undistracted mind, should recite this.
On the eighth and fourteenth lunar days, during the sun's transit (saṅkrānti), on Sundays, on Saturdays and Tuesdays, at night, and during eclipses of the moon and the sun. || 212 ||
Especially on the night of the stars, the night of Time (Kālarātri), and the night of delusion (Moharātri),
through recitation there shall be the attainment of mantra-perfection, and omniscience arises.
One should perform the recitation of the hymn in a cremation ground, a delightful wilderness, especially in an empty house, or likewise in a temple or on a mountain. (214)

The killing of a Brahmin, the drinking of liquor, theft, sexual intercourse with women [of forbidden classes], and likewise other sins such as violating the teacher’s bed—these are certainly destroyed. (215)
If the practitioner, situated in the midst of a creeper, should worship with faith,
then he may summon Rambhā, Menā, and likewise Urvaśī.
At the time of battle, a hero, by chanting the glory of Tārā’s sovereignty, shall conquer the fourfold army and become the possessor of the entire empire. || 217 ||
At midnight and at the conclusion of the worship, one should perform the worship according to each individual name,
using single blossoms of karavīra and the like, as well as blue lotuses.
(148) His speech, consisting of both prose and verse, flows like a river of royal bounty;
he possesses mastery over all sciences, and a disputant trembles at the mere sight of him. (219)
With these names, beginning with Tārā and ending with the wife of Vahni (Svāhā), one achieves entry into the bodies of others among all kings for a kṣatriya. 220.
Invisibility, the power of moving through the air, the manifestation of many bodies, as well as the pill (guṭikā), the sandal (pādukā), Padmāvatī, and Madhumatī. || 221 ||
All elixirs of taste and all supernatural accomplishments are present;
[one should perform the rite] with water mixed with camphor, agallochum, musk, and sandalwood. || 222 ||
One should worship the root [mantra] with each name joined together in a *sampuṭa* (enclosed) form:
the Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Gandharvas, Vidyādharas, and Mahoragas. (223)
The spirits, ghosts, piśācas, and others; the hosts of ḍākinīs and śākinīs; the wicked bhairavas and vetālas; the kūṣmāṇḍas and the hosts of kinnarīs. (224)
Terrified by the power of the practitioner, they flee;
once knowledge of the mantra has arisen, one should investigate it by means of its counter-name.
By means of this very mantra-encasement, his peace shall certainly be attained;
Lalitā comes under one's control, and kings become submissive servants. 226.
The fires become cool through the recitation of the Japāka;
by a single repetition alone, fear of kings is averted. || 227 ||
By merely revolving [the wheel] once, an increase in livestock is produced;
by ten revolutions, there is the acquisition of wealth; and by twenty, one shall obtain a kingdom. || 228 ||
By reciting [this] a hundred times in his house, even a fickle woman becomes steady;
her speech arises like the flow of the Gaṅgā, even from mere idle chatter. 229.
Accompanied by sons and grandsons, the practitioner of the mantra shall live long like a god;
by reciting it two hundred times, he is honored by people as if he were a deity. (130)
By repeating it five hundred times, he becomes equal to Bhairava;
by repeating it a thousand times, the mantra grants him its own supernatural powers (siddhis).
In that [state], every accomplishment proceeds, fulfilling all aims:
the magical sandals, gold, the vetāla, the underworld, the sky, and so forth.
Various accomplishments of the yakṣiṇīs and the accomplishment of speech arise for him;
likewise, the drying up of oceans, the holding of rain-showers, and wandering [through the air]. || 233 ||
He shall become capable of creating an entirely new creation;
by merely revolving [the mantra] ten thousand times, he beholds Tārā with his own eyes.
By merely performing one hundred thousand recitations, one becomes equal to the Lord of the Stars (the Moon);
for such a person, nothing on earth is difficult to obtain, as they are indeed liberated while living.
After that, at the end of a kalpa, one shall attain union with Tārā;
for there is no vidyā equal to Tārā, who possesses the form of youth. (236)
And even with thousands of millions of mouths and hundreds of millions of tongues, such a hymn as this would not exist within the entire sphere of the universe. (237)

It is not possible for me to describe the fruit [of such actions] even in hundreds of eons, [if one acts] toward a kisser, a slanderer, a wicked person, a backbiter, or a killer of living beings. (238)
This hymn is to be kept secret; it should not be revealed to anyone except through direct vision [of the deity].
One may give away one's kingdom, one may give away wealth, or even one's head. (239)
This excellent hymn, though more powerful than even mantras, should not be given away;
it should be enclosed by the root mantra both in direct and reverse order.
Having written it on birch bark or similar material with the eight fragrant substances as the foremost ingredients,
one should wear it on the right arm, or likewise on the neck or the left arm.
For him, all purposes shall be accomplished; he is never burned by fire, nor is his body ever pierced by multitudes of weapons. (242)
O son, he shall wander upon the circle of the earth like Bhairava;
even a barren woman obtains a son, and a destitute man shall obtain wealth.
He obtains, without obstacle, knowledge such as logic, grammar, and so forth. || 243 ||
Thus has been recited this thousand names of hers, known as the Divine Sovereignty,
which is the source of the granting of boons and is uniquely capable of bestowing power upon Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the rest.
This is to be recited during the ritual procedure for the Equal One (Samavidhi) by those known as the Kālitārās. || 244 ||
Thus ends the *Sahasranāmastotra* of Tārā, beginning with the letter *Ta*, from the *Śrī Brahmayāmala*.
Thus ends the Tārātantra within the Śrīśāktapramoda.
Composed and compiled by the sovereign King Śrī Rājādeva-nandana Siṃha Bahādura, the lord of the capital of Śiva-Hara and the possessor of glory.
The third Tantra, the Ṣoḍaśī, contained within the Śāktapramoda.
This has been edited by the learned Paṇḍita Śrī Raghurāja Dubejī, a descendant of the aforementioned royal preceptor.
Printed and published by Śrī Kṛṣṇadāsātmaja Khemarāja at his own Śrī Veṅkaṭeśvara Press.
*Bombai*, p. 153): *Śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ*.
Now begins the *Śāktapramoda*.
Now, the Sixteenfold Tantra:
the meditation on the Sixteenfold [Goddess],
who has the luster of the orb of the rising sun, four arms, and three eyes.
I worship Śivā, who holds a noose, a goad, arrows, and a bow.
(p. 154) Now, the extraction of the yantra:

A dot, a triangle, an eight-cornered figure, two sets of ten, eight, sixteen petals joined with eight petals, three circles, and three abodes of the earth—this is the Śrīcakra-rāja, proclaimed as belonging to the Supreme Deity.
Now follows the extraction of the mantra:
First, having uttered *lajjā* (the seed-syllable hrīṃ), then *ka-e-ī-la*;
again, having uttered *lajjā*, then *hasakahala*. (1)
Then, having uttered "Lajjām" once more, followed by "Lajjāntam" and "Sakalam," this sixteen-syllable mantra of Ṣoḍaśī is proclaimed. || 2 ||
This beautiful lore is difficult even for the gods to obtain;
it should be guarded with great effort and is considered to bestow all prosperity.
Now the mantra:
Hrīṃ ka-e-īla-hrīṃ, ha-saka-hala-hrīṃ, sa-kala-hrīṃ.
Now, the procedure for worship:
having risen during the *brāhma-muhūrta* and remaining upon the bed itself, one should meditate on the venerable Guru within the great thousand-petaled lotus at the crown of the head:
The Guru has two eyes and two arms, is peaceful, and is seated in the lotus posture.
Seated comfortably according to his color, liberated, and possessing a radiant form.
He who displays the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, and whose form embodies Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śaṅkara.
Having meditated upon her as being joined with Śakti, who holds a blue lotus in her left hand and rests upon her left side,
[one should contemplate] that which pervades the entire universe of moving and non-moving beings in the form of an unbroken circle.
Salutations to that venerable Guru, by whom that state has been revealed.
For one blinded by the darkness of ignorance, with the collyrium-stick of knowledge...
Salutation to that glorious Guru by whom the eye was opened.
Homage be to that Guru, who is the very embodiment of one's chosen deity.
Whose nectar-like speech destroys the poison-filled turmoil of cyclic existence.
Having paid homage to the immediate self and the guru, one should perform the internal meditation;
one should recite the root mantra one hundred and eight times.
O Goddess whose girdle is the ocean, whose breasts are the mountain ranges!

Reciting, "O Consort of Viṣṇu, salutations to you; forgive my touch upon your feet," one should touch the ground, beginning with the left foot. Therein is the mantra: *lasaha hrīṃ e klīṃ sa*. Having remembered this, one should spread a seat there and sit down.
One should contemplate the Root-Vidyā from the base (mūla) up to the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra),
resembling the rising sun and possessing a radiance equal to ten million flashes of lightning.
One should contemplate well the body pervaded by the mass of its radiance.
One should perform the piercing of the six cakras as follows:
between the anus and the genitals is the Mūlādhāra, which has four petals marked with the syllables *vaṃ*, *śaṃ*, *ṣaṃ*, and *saṃ*, and is yellow in color.
Here the deity is Ḍākinī, and Gaṇeśa, who has four tusks; [the triangle] in its center is the color of lightning.

With the syllable *HŪṂ*, [one should contemplate] the power Kuṇḍalinī, who is like a spider's thread, resembling a coiled serpent, endowed with three and a half folds, having the form of a sleeping snake, and possessing the nature of the Moon, Sun, and Fire.
Having struck and raised [the disciple] with the mental staff, one should mutter "Ha-sa. || 1 ||
At the base of the linga is the red Svādhiṣṭhāna, consisting of the syllables BAṂ BHAṂ MAṂ RAṂ LAṂ; there resides the goddess Ḍākinī and the deity Brahmā. || 2 ||
At the navel, the blue Maṇipūra consists of the syllables ḍaṃ, ḍhaṃ, ṇaṃ, taṃ, thaṃ, daṃ, dhaṃ, naṃ, paṃ, and phaṃ; there resides the goddess Lākinī and Viṣṇu. (3)
In the heart is the twelve-petaled Anāhata-cakra, smoke-colored, with the syllables *kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ*; there resides the goddess Kākinī and Rudra. (4)

At the throat is the Viśuddha-cakra, having sixteen petals and a tawny (piṅgala) color, with the syllables aṃ, āṃ, iṃ, īṃ, uṃ, ūṃ, ṛṃ, ṝṃ, ḷṃ, ḹṃ, eṃ, aiṃ, oṃ, auṃ, aṃ, and aḥ; there resides the goddess Śākinī, whose nature is Śiva. || 5 ||
Between the eyebrows is the Ājñā-cakra, consisting of two petals and marked with "haṃ" and "laṃ"; there resides the goddess Hākinī and the Supreme Self (parātmā).

Having thus pierced the six chakras and united [the self] with Paramaśiva in the form of the bindu situated within the pericarp of the thousand-petaled lotus, one should satiate Kuṇḍalinī with the nectar of Lakṣmī, Abhaya, and Ramā.
Furthermore, one should lead [the breath] through Ājñā, Viśuddha, Anāhata, Tripurā, Svādhiṣṭhāna, and Mūlādhāra.

Thus is the meditation; having meditated upon the Goddess, worshipped her with mental offerings, performed recitation (japa), offered praise, and prostrated, one should perform the necessary purifications and so forth, and take up the tooth-stick.

(156) One should perform the cleansing of the teeth with the mantra: *klīṃ sarvajanapriyāyai ratikāmasvarūpāyai namaḥ*. Then, having rinsed the mouth with the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*), one should go to a body of water at the appropriate time and, facing the sun, submerge oneself once like a pestle.

Having prepared a square measuring four cubits in front [of oneself], and having drawn a triangle in its center, one should bring the sacred water (tīrtha) from the solar orb by means of the goad mudrā (aṅkuśamudrā). [Recite:
"Oṃ, O Gaṅgā, O Yamunā, O Godāvarī, O Sarasvatī..."
O Narmadā, Sindhu, and Kāverī, take up your residence in these waters!
Having displayed the *dhenumudrā* while uttering "vaṃ," one should recite the root mantra eight times.
One should sprinkle [the water] on the head seven times with the root mantra while forming the *kalaśa-mudrā*.
Having blocked the seven apertures, one should immerse oneself three times.
Then, having performed the sprinkling for the removal of sins, one should perform the twilight devotions (*sandhyā*).

Having performed three breath-retentions (prāṇāyāma), one should transform the water into nectar with the syllable "Vam" using the cow-mudrā (dhenumudrā). Having sprinkled it over the head three times with the root mantra,
and having sipped water nine times, one should place that water in the right hand and recite the mantra of the five elements— "Laṃ Vaṃ Raṃ Yaṃ Haṃ"— eight times.

One should recite the root mantra ten times. By snapping the ring finger and thumb of the left hand, one should sprinkle water three times over the head. Imagining that the remaining water has entered through the *iḍā* channel in the left hand, one should contemplate that all impurities have been completely incinerated by it; then, one should visualize [the water] exiting through the *piṅgalā* channel.

Having placed that *jālinda* in the right hand, one should visualize the personification of sin (*pāpapuruṣa*) therein; then, having meditated upon a diamond-stone (*vajraśilā*) on the ground to the left and having cast the personification of sin there, one should contemplate it being pulverized—this is the *aghamarṣaṇa*. Thereafter, [one should worship] the deities and others according to the ritual procedure.
Having satisfied [them]: *Oṃ*, I satisfy Gaṇeśa; I satisfy Baṭuka; I satisfy the Yoginīs;
I satisfy all the hosts of gods; I satisfy all the hosts of ancestors;
I satisfy all the hosts of mothers; I satisfy all the hosts of humans.

Having recited the root mantra of the Inner Controller (*sarvāntaryāmī*) and offered libations three times with the formula, "I satiate Śrī Mahātripurasundarī; *namaḥ*," one should then recite: *aiṃ ātmatattvaṃ śodhayāmi*, *klīṃ vidyātattvaṃ śodhayāmi*, *sauṃ śivatattvaṃ śodhayāmi*, *aiṃ klīṃ sauṃ sarvatattvaṃ*.

I purify. Then, rising from the water, having put on two washed garments, having made a *tilaka* with the root mantra, and having prepared the *arghya* offering with perfumes, flowers, and unbroken rice grains, [one recites]: *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kulamārtaṇḍabhairavāya*.

Having offered the *arghya* to the Sun with the mantra, "To the one endowed with the power that illuminates the lunar days (*tithi*), the weekdays (*vāra*), the asterisms (*nakṣatra*), the conjunctions (*yoga*), and the lunar phases (*karaṇa*), this *arghya* is offered;
obeisance," one should recite the *Devatā-gāyatrī* according to one's ability.
"Klīṃ! We know Kāmeśvarī; we meditate upon Vāgīśvarī; may she, Klinnā, impel us.
Having offered the moon-water libation at night.
O you who were born from the Ocean of Milk, O you who arose from the lineage of Atri!
O Lord, O God, together with Rohiṇī, accept this arghya offering.
Thus one should offer the *arghya* to the Moon. One should perform this likewise during all three periods of twilight (*sandhyā*).

Then, having paid homage to the lords of the directions and arrived at the door of the worship chamber, one should wash the hands and feet, perform the ritual sipping of water (*ācamana*), and, having consecrated the door with the mantra "Astrāya phaṭ namaḥ," one should worship it.
On the left branch: *Gaṃ Gaṇeśāya namaḥ*; on the right: *Kṣaṃ Kṣetrapālāya namaḥ*;
above: *Dvāṃ Dvāraśriyai namaḥ*.
In the middle of the threshold: *dehalyai namaḥ*;
on the left side: *klīṃ kāmadevāya namaḥ*, *raṃ ratyai namaḥ*, *vāṃ vasantāya namaḥ*, *prīṃ prītyai namaḥ*.
Oṃ, obeisance to Śaṅkhanidhi; on the right side, obeisance to Padmanidhi,
obeisance to Sarasvatī, obeisance to Śrī, obeisance to Māyā, obeisance to Durgā, obeisance to Bhadrakālī, obeisance to Svāhā, obeisance to Śubhakārī, obeisance to Gaurī.

"Salutation to Lokadhātrī; salutation to Vāgīśvarī. Contracting his limbs, beginning with the right foot, he should enter the interior of the house; then he should offer [the oblation] within the house.
One should worship in the northeast: "Oṃ, obeisance to Vāstupuruṣa; Oṃ, obeisance to Brahmā."
Therefore, let those beings depart who dwell upon the earth.
May those beings who create obstacles perish by the command of Śiva.
Thus, one should scatter rice-grains in the four directions; this is the expulsion of the elemental spirits (bhūta-apasāraṇa).
Having raised the hands three times higher and higher, one should dispel the three obstacles by striking with the left foot three times.
Then, having spread out a seat made of tiger skin, red woolen cloth, or the like, and having taken his place upon that seat, he should recite [the mantra].
Of this mantra for the seat, Merupṛṣṭha is the seer (ṛṣi), Sutala is the meter (chandas), Kūrma is the deity (devatā),
and its application (viniyoga) is in sitting upon the seat.
Oṃ! O Earth, by you the worlds are supported; O Goddess, you are supported by Viṣṇu.
And you, hold me constantly and make my seat pure.
Then one should perform worship: *Kūṃ kūrmāsanāya namaḥ*,
*Ādhāraśaktikamalāsanāya namaḥ*, *Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ sarvaśaktikamalāsanāya namaḥ*, *Oṃ pṛthivyai namaḥ*.

Then, having sat down in the *svastika* or other [auspicious] postures, one should perform the assignment of mantras (*nyāsa*) as follows: with "Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to the one whose nature is the ocean of nectar," on the two feet; with "Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to the seat of the white lotus," on the two knees;
and with "Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to the seat of the Goddess," on the two sides.
Reciting "Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to the Cakrāsana," one should worship at the secret place (guhya). One should worship at the four corners of the seat:
"Oṃ, obeisance to Gaṇapati; obeisance to Durgā; obeisance to Baṭuka Bhairava;
obeisance to Kṣetrapāla," starting from the northwest (vāyavya) and ending at the southwest (nairṛtya). Then: "Hrīṃ Ka-E-Ila Hrīṃ."

*Hasakaha-lhrīṃ sakalahrīṃ*, obeisance to Gaṇapati; on the back, obeisance to Kṣetrapāla; in front, obeisance to Śrī Mahātripurasundarī. Now, the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*): placing the hands palms-upward upon one's own body with the mantra *so'haṃ*.
Having struck the Kuṇḍalinī, whose form is as previously described, at the Mūlādhāra with the syllable *HŪṂ* by means of the mind-made staff,
one should raise her up together with the individual soul (*jīvātman*), which has come under its own control and is like the flame of a lamp in the Maṇipūra and Anāhata [cakras].
Having dissolved the wheel known as Viśuddha and having united [the self] with Paramaśiva in the form of the bindu situated within the thousand-petaled lotus,
one should contemplate the body as empty and meditate upon the Person of Sin (pāpapuruṣa) in the belly.
In his left side stands the Personification of Sin, with the luster of black collyrium.
The head [of the corpse] represents the murder of a Brahmin, and the two arms represent the theft of gold.
The heart is joined with the drinking of liquor, and the two hips with violating the teacher's bed.
The pair of feet of that yogi causes the downfall of [all] limbs and minor members.
His body hair was like that of a minor sinner, and his beard and eyes were red.
It is insentient, resembling a tree with its roots above and its top downward that has been burnt.
One should visualize him as cruel, bearing a sword and shield, and having a belly like that of a dog.

Having meditated thus, one should perform the drying and other rites together with that [wind]. Reciting the wind-seed syllable *yaṃ*, which is smoke-colored, sixteen times through the left nostril, one should draw up the wind, fix it at the navel in the ten-petalled lotus, and completely dry the entire body along with the personification of sin (*pāpapuruṣa*). [Then] the two nostrils...
Holding the seed-syllable *ram*, which is red in color, and reciting it sixty-four times through the practice of breath-retention (*kumbhaka*),
one should reduce the body to ashes along with it. Then, having raised the vital air and fixed it in the heart at the twelve-petaled lotus,
one should recite the white-colored Varuṇa-seed-syllable *vam* thirty-two times.
Having caused a stream of nectar to fall while reciting the lunar seed-syllable *caṃ* sixty-four times,
and having flooded [the body] through the yoga of breath-retention (*kumbhaka*) by means of that shower of nectar,
one should fix the yellow-colored earth-seed-syllable *laṃ* upon the earth-mandala at the root-center (*mūlādhāra*).

Furthermore, strengthening the entire body so that it becomes fit for the worship of the deity, one should lead the individual soul (*jīvātman*) to the heart-center (*hṛdayacakra*) with the mantra "Haṃsa," and lead Kuṇḍalinī to the root-center (*mūlacakra*).
Thus ends the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi).
Then, having placed the hand upon the heart, one should perform the consecration of the vital breath (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*).
For this *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* mantra, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara are the seers (*ṛṣis*);
the *Ṛg*, *Yajur*, and *Sāma* Vedas are the meters (*chandāṃsi*); and the Supreme Self (*paramātman*) is the deity (*devatā*), who is the power of consciousness (*caitanyaśakti*).
The application is for the Prāṇapratiṣṭhā (the ritual installation of the vital breaths). Ā Hrīṃ Krīṃ Ya Ra La Va Śa Ṣa Sa Ha La Kṣa Ha Saḥ. My vital breaths are here;
my life-force is established here. May all my senses be here. My [vitality is here].
Speech, mind, eye, ear, nose, skin, tongue, and breath—having come here, may they dwell happily; svāhā!
Now, the breath control (prāṇāyāma).

Holding the left nostril closed, while reciting *ka-e-ī-la-hrīṃ* sixteen times, one should slowly fill [the lungs] with air; this is *pūraka* (inhalation). Holding both nostrils closed, while reciting *ha-sa-ka-ha-la-hrīṃ* sixty-four times, one should retain the air; this is *kumbhaka* (retention).
Reciting the seed-syllable *sakalahrīm* thirty-two times, one should slowly exhale the breath through the right nostril.
This is exhalation (*recaka*). In this manner, one should perform three such breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*). [Now, the Mātṛkā-nyāsa:
Of this venerable Mātṛkā-nyāsa mantra, the seer is Brahmarṣi, the meter is Gāyatrī, and the deity is the Mother of the Letters (*varṇajananī*).
The Mātṛkā-deities are the seed-syllables *hal*, the vowels are the powers (*śakti*), and the application is for the perfection of ritual action.
Salutation to the Brahman-sages, on the head;
salutation to the Gāyatrī metre, on the face; salutation to the deity Mātṛkā, the mother of all letters, on the heart.
Salutation to the half-syllables at the secret place;
salutation to the vowels and the Śaktis at the anus;
the application for the perfection of action is at the feet.
One should meditate upon the Mātṛkā:
her middle chest divided by the fifty letters,
her forehead adorned with a crescent moon shining from her bound crown, and her breasts full and tawny.
I take refuge in the Goddess of Speech, who holds a rosary of beads and a jar brimming with nectar, who bears knowledge in her beautiful lotus-hand, and whose three eyes possess pure radiance.

Aṃ *namaḥ* on the forehead; Āṃ *namaḥ* on the face; Iṃ *namaḥ* on the right eye; Īṃ *namaḥ* on the left eye; Uṃ *namaḥ* on the right ear; Ūṃ *namaḥ* on the left ear; Ṛṃ *namaḥ* on the right nostril; Ṝṃ *namaḥ* on the left nostril; Ḷṃ *namaḥ* on the right cheek.

Ḷṃ namaḥ to the left cheek; eṃ namaḥ to the upper lip; aiṃ namaḥ to the lower lip; oṃ namaḥ to the upper row of teeth; auṃ namaḥ to the lower row of teeth; aṃ namaḥ to the head; aḥ namaḥ to the mouth.
At the tips of the five joints of the right arm:
ka namaḥ, kha namaḥ, ga namaḥ, gha namaḥ, ṅa namaḥ.
At the tips of the five joints of the left arm: [the same].
*Ca*—salutation; *cha*—salutation; *ja*—salutation; *jha*—salutation; *ña*—salutation.
On the five joints of the tips of the right foot: *ṭa*—salutation; *ṭha*—salutation; *ḍa*—salutation; *ḍha*—salutation; *ṇa*—salutation.
At the tips of the five joints of the left foot:
*ta* namaḥ, *tha* namaḥ, *da* namaḥ, *dha* namaḥ, *na* namaḥ. On the right side—
*Pa* / *namaḥ* / *pha* / *namaḥ* on the left side;
*ba* / *namaḥ* on the back; *bha* / *namaḥ* at the navel; *ma* / *namaḥ* on the belly; *ya* / *namaḥ*.

*Ra*: Homage to the heart. *La*: Homage to the right shoulder. *Va*: Homage to the crown of the head. *Śa*: Homage to the left shoulder. *Ṣa*: Homage from the heart to the right hand. *Sa*: Homage from the heart to the left hand. *Ha*: Homage from the heart to the right foot. *La*: Homage from the heart to the left foot. *Kṣa*: Homage from the heart to the [entire body].
*Udare* (in the belly); *kṣaṃ namaḥ* (salutation) from the heart to the mouth. Thus is the Mātṛkā-nyāsa.

[Now, the internal placement of the Mātṛkās (antarmātṛkānyāsa): One should place the sixteen vowels, red in color, at the throat; the letters from *ka* to *ṭha*, vermilion-colored, at the heart; the letters from *ḍa* to *pha*, blue in color, at the navel; the letters from *ba* to *la*, the color of lightning, at the generative organ;
the letters from *va* to *sa*, red in color, at the anus; and [the remaining letters] between the eyebrows.

One should place the fifty letters from *a* to *kṣa*, which have the color of lac-dye, upon the thousand-spoked, thousand-petalled [lotus]. Following this sequence, one should perform the placement a thousand times, repeating it twice and then up to twenty times during the third round.

Beginning from the *mūlādhāra* up to the thousand-petalled lotus (*sahasradala*), one should place the root mantra (*mūlamantra*) everywhere upon all the petals. One should contemplate the recitation of one hundred and twenty-one repetitions with each breath, through the coming and going of the *kuṇḍalinī* upon every petal, every lotus, and every wheel (*cakra*); this is the *ajapā*.
And the internal nyāsa of the Mātṛkās should always be performed with constant vigilance.

Thus ends the internal Mātṛkā-nyāsa. Now, the Kulukā-nyāsa: *Aiṃ Klīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Bhagavati Mahātripurasundari Svāhā*. With this, one places the Kulukā on the head; *Oṃ* at the heart; the Setu at the throat; the Mahāsetu at the thousand-petalled lotus (*sahasrāra*); and *Oṃ Śrīṃ A-Ā-E-Klīṃ*.

Sauṃ Aiṃ A Ā I Ī U Ū Ṛ Ṝ Ḷ Ḹ E AI O AU A AḤ Ka Kha Ga Gha Ṅa Ca Cha Ja Jha Ña Ṭa Ṭha Ḍa Ḍha Ṇa Ta Tha Da Dha Na Pa Pha Ba Bha Ma Ya Ra La Va Śa Ṣa Sa Ha La Kṣa— thus [is the mantra] at the navel of Nirvāṇa; the seed-syllable of desire (Kāma-bīja) is at the *liṅga*.

Having meditated upon the root-vidyā on the tongue, one should recite it according to one's capacity. This is the *itikulukānyāsa*. [Now, the *pīṭhanyāsa*: On the forehead, *a*, salutation to the sacred seat (*pīṭha*) of Kāmarūpa; [this applies] everywhere.
On the circumference of the mouth, *ā*, salutation to the sacred seat of Vārāṇasī; in the right eye, *i*, salutation to the sacred seat of Nepāla.
To the left eye, *īṃ* for the Pīṭha of Pauṇḍravardhana; to the right ear, *u* for the Pīṭha of Purastira;
to the left ear, *ū* for the Pīṭha of Kālikubji; to the right nostril, *ṛ* for the Pīṭha of Pūrṇaśaila; to the left nasal cavity, *ṝ* for the Pīṭha of Arbuda; to the right cheek, *ḷ*—
To the seat of Āmrātakeśvara on the left cheek; to the seat of Ekāmra on the [left] lip;
to the seat of Trisrotas on the lower lip; to the seat of Kāmakoṭa on the upper row of teeth;
to the seat of Kedāra on the lower row of teeth; to the seat of Guptanagara on the head.

To the Candrapura-pīṭha, at the mouth: AḤ; to the Śrī-pīṭha; on the five joints of the right hand: KA—to the Oṃkāra-pīṭha; KHA—to the Jālandhara-pīṭha; GA—to the Mālava-pīṭha; GHA—to the Bhadrakoṭa-pīṭha; ṄA—to the Devīkoṭa-pīṭha.
And on the tips of the five fingers of the left hand: *cha* for Gokarṇa-pīṭha, *ja* for Māruteśvara-pīṭha, *jha* for Maṅgalakoṭa-pīṭha, *ña* for Aṭṭahāsa-pīṭha, and *ña* for Viraja-pīṭha.

At the tips of the five joints of the right foot: *Ṭaṃ* to the seat of Rājagṛha, *Ṭhaṃ* to the seat of Mahāpatha, *Ḍaṃ* to the seat of Koṇagiri, *Ḍhaṃ* to the seat of Ailāpura, and *Ṇaṃ* to the seat of Rāmeśvara. At the tips of the five joints of the left foot:

To the *taṃ* of the Tañjapīṭha, to the *thaṃ* of the Ujjayinīpīṭha, to the *daṃ* of the Caritrīpīṭha, to the *dhaṃ* of the Kṣīrikāpīṭha, and to the *naṃ* of the Hastināpurapīṭha. On the right side, *paṃ* to the Uḍḍīśapīṭha; on the left side, *pha* to the Prayāgapīṭha; and on the back—
To the pīṭha of Baṅgaṣaṣṭhīśa at the navel; to the pīṭha of Bharmāyāpura at the belly;
to the pīṭha of Maṅnirjana at the heart; to the pīṭha of Yaṃmalaya at the right shoulder;
to the pīṭha of Raṃśrīśaila at the back of the neck; to the pīṭha of Laṃmahāmeru at the left shoulder.
To Vaṃgiripīṭha; from the heart to the end of the right hand, to Śaṃmahendrapīṭha;
from the heart to the end of the left hand, to Ṣaṃrasenapīṭha.
From the heart to the right foot, *saṃ* to the Saṃbharī-pīṭha;
from the heart to the left foot, *haṃ* to the Mahālakṣmīpura-pīṭha; from the heart to the abdomen, *laṃ* to the Uḍḍīyānapura-pīṭha; from the heart to the mouth...

Salutation to Kṣaṃsaumyapīṭha. Then, in the Mūlādhāra: salutation to Dhyānapīṭha; in the Svādhiṣṭhāna: salutation to Kāmapīṭha; in the Maṇipūra: salutation to Jñānapīṭha; in the Anāhata: salutation to Videhapīṭha; in the Viśuddhi: salutation to Nandinīpīṭha; in the Ājñā—
To Nandāpīṭha; then, upon the thousand petals: to Kṣīranidhipīṭha, to Kalpavanapīṭha, to Cintāmaṇipīṭha, to Paryaṅkapīṭha, to Śivāsanapīṭha, and to Mūrttimayapīṭha.
To the Pīṭha that pervades all: thus is the Pīṭha-nyāsa. [Now, the Rahasya-nyāsa:
Of this Śrī Rahasya-nyāsa mantra, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara are the seers (ṛṣis);
the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāma Vedas are the meters (chandāṃsi); and the deity is Caitanyaśakti Mahātripurasundarī.
The application (viniyoga) is for the sake of accomplishing the perfection of the nyāsa that has been performed and remains to be performed.
Salutation to the sages Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara on the head;
salutation to the meters Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman on the mouth;
salutation to the deity Cid-Śakti Mahātripurasundarī on the heart.

The application (*viniyoga*) for the feet is for the sake of accomplishing the perfection of the nyāsa performed and yet to be performed: *aiṃ klīṃ sauṃ klīṃ aiṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ sadāśivāsanāyai mahātripurasundaryai namaḥ*—thus at the *mūlādhāra*. (1)
Aiṃ klīṃ sauṃ sauṃ klīṃ aiṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ, obeisance to Ratipriyā Mahātripurasundarī; thus, in the Svādhiṣṭhāna. || 2 ||
Aiṃ klīṃ sauṃ sauṃ klīṃ aiṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ so'haṃ jñānasvarūpāyai mahātripurasundaryai namaḥ—thus [one should worship] in the Maṇipūra. 3.
Aiṃ klīṃ sauṃ sauṃ klīṃ aiṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ so'haṃ dhyānasvarūpāyai mahātripurasundaryai namaḥ—thus, in the Anāhata [cakra]. (4)
Aiṃ klīṃ sauṃ sauṃ klīṃ aiṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ viśuddhasvarūpāyai mahātripurasundaryai namaḥ—thus [one should worship] in the Viśuddhi [cakra]. || 5 ||
Aiṃ klīṃ sauṃ sauṃ klīṃ aiṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ, salutation to Mahātripurasundarī, whose essential nature is independent; thus [it is] in the Ājñā [cakra]. || 6 ||
One should place [the mantra] at the thousand-petaled lotus (*sahasrāra*): *aiṃ klīṃ sauṃ sauṃ klīṃ aiṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ ānandasvarūpāyai mahāsundaryai namaḥ*.
Thus ends the Secret Nyāsa. [Now, the Kāma-nyāsa: Hrīṃ, obeisance to Kāma;
Klīṃ, obeisance to Manmatha; Aiṃ, obeisance to Kandarpa; Klūṃ, obeisance to Makaradhvaja; Strīṃ, obeisance to Mīnaketu. Then: Aiṃ, obeisance to the Heart; Klīṃ, Svāhā to the Head; Sauṃ...

*Śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*, *aiṃ kavacāya huṃ*, *klīṃ netratrayāya vauṣaṭ*, *sauṃ astrāya phaṭ*. Having repeated this mantra twice, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) upon the two hands. This is the *Kāma-nyāsa*. [Now, the *Ratyādi-nyāsa*: *Aiṃ ratyai namaḥ* on the *liṅga*; *klīṃ prītyai namaḥ* in the heart; [and] in the middle of the eyebrows—

*Sauṃ* to *Manobhavā* at the center of the eyebrows; *sauṃ* to *Amṛtāśā* at the heart; *klīṃ* to *Yoginī* at the *liṅga*; *aiṃ* to *Viśvayoni*, salutations. This is the *Atinyāsa*. [Now, the *Manobhava-nyāsa*:
On the head, *hsauṃ* to *Īśāna-Manobhava*, salutations; on the face...

Hsauṃ, salutation to Tatpuruṣa, the one whose banner is the sea-monster (Makaradhvaja), at the heart; Shrūṃ, salutation to Aghora Kumāra, the god of desire (Kandarpa), at the secret place; Hsrīṃ, salutation to Vāmadeva, the god of love (Manmatha), at the feet;
Hsrūṃ, salutation to Sadyojāta, the god of desire (Kāmadeva), at the two feet; Hsrauṃ, [salutation] at the upper face on the head.

To Īśāna, the Mind-born (Manobhava) [at the eastern face]; on the forehead at the eastern face: *hsrauṃ* to Tatpuruṣa, the Dolphin-bannered (Makaradhvaja); at the southern face and right ear: *hsrūṃ* to Aghora-kumāra, Kandarpa;
at the northern face and left ear: *hsrīṃ* to Vāmadeva, Manmatha.
In the western face, below the crest-jewel: *hsrūṃ sadyojātāya kāmadevāya namaḥ*.
Thus ends the placement of the mind-born [arrows]. [Now, the placement of the arrows: *hrāḥ*—salutation to the agitating arrow;
*hrīṃ*—to the intoxicating arrow; *klīṃ*—to the attracting arrow; *klūṃ*—to the deluding arrow; *saḥ*—salutation to the maddening arrow. Thus.
One should place [the fingers] on the hands from the thumb to the little finger. This is the Bāṇanyāsa.

[Now, the Svatantranyāsa: Of this venerable Svatantranyāsa of Mahātripurasundarī, Ānandabhairava is the seer (ṛṣi), the divine Gāyatrī is the meter (chandas), and the venerable Mahātripurasundarī is the deity (devatā).
