Thus ends the *Tripurasundarīṣoḍaśītantra* in the *Śrīśāktapramoda*. Śrī! [This was composed by] Siṃha, the son of the illustrious Rājādeva, the lord of the capital city of Śivahara.
The Fourth [Chapter] within the Śāktapramoda, composed and compiled by the noble lord Bahādur Narādhipa.
The Bhuvaneśvarī Tantra,
edited by Paṇḍita Śrī Raghurāja Dube Jī, a descendant of the aforementioned royal preceptors.
This [work] was printed by Khemarāja, son of Śrī Kṛṣṇadāsa,
at his own "Śrī Veṅkaṭeśvara" Press.
Having been printed and published at Bombay.
Salutations to the illustrious Gaṇeśa.
Now, the Śāktapramoda:
the Bhuvaneśvarī Tantra;
now, the meditation on Bhuvaneśvarī.

I worship Bhuvaneśī, whose radiance is like the rising sun, who wears the moon as a crown, whose high breasts are prominent, who is endowed with three eyes, whose face is smiling, and who holds the gestures of granting boons, the goad, the noose, and the gesture of fearlessness in her hands.
(p. 194) Now, the construction of the yantra: One should draw an eight-petalled lotus on the outside, and a circle with sixteen petals;
in the center of the pericarp, one should draw a most beautiful hexagon.
One should draw a mandala that is square and has four doors.
Now follows the extraction of the mantra:
Nakulīśa mounted upon Agni, possessing a left eye and a crescent moon;
this is declared to be her seed-syllable, practiced by those desiring spiritual accomplishments (siddhi).
Now the mantra: Hrīḥ.
Next, the ritual procedure for worship:
having performed the rites beginning with the morning duties and ending with the placement of mantras on the pedestal (pīṭhanyāsa), [one should place them] in the filaments and in the center.
One should place the powers of the seats (*pīṭhaśakti*): *Oṃ jayāyai namaḥ*, likewise *vijayāyai namaḥ*, *ajitāyai*, *aparājitāyai*, *nityāyai*, *vilāsinyai*, *dogdhyai*, *aghorāyai*, *maṅgalāyai*.
In the pericarp (*karṇikā*), [place] *hrīṃ sarvaśaktikamalāsanāya namaḥ*. Then follows the ritual placement of the seers and so forth (*ṛṣyādinyāsa*).

Of this Bhuvaneśvarī mantra, Śakti is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chanda), Bhuvaneśvarī is the deity (devatā), the letter *ha* is the seed-syllable (bīja), the letter *ī* is the power (śakti), and the letter *ra* is the pin (kīlaka). The application (viniyoga) is for the sake of attaining the four aims of human life. [One should perform the assignment: "Salutation to the Seer Śakti on the head; salutation to the Meter Gāyatrī on the mouth; [salutation] to the Deity on the heart."

Salutation to the deity Bhuvaneśvarī. Salutation to the seed-syllable *ha* at the secret place. Salutation to the power (*śakti*) *ī* at the two feet. Salutation to the wedge (*kīlaka*) *ra* on all limbs. Then follows the ritual placement (*nyāsa*):
*Oṃ hṛllekhāyai namaḥ* on the head.

One should assign them to the faces as follows: *e* to Gaganāyā, *namaḥ*, at the mouth; *ū* to Raktāyā, *namaḥ*, at the heart; *i* to Karālikāyā, *namaḥ*, at the secret place; and *a* to Mahocchuṣmāyā, *namaḥ*, at the feet.
One should then assign them to the upward, eastern, southern, northern, and western faces.
One should place Hṛllekhā on the head and face, and Gaganā in the lotus of the heart.

One should place the blood-red Aṅkurālikā on the secret organ and Mahocchuṣmā on the two feet; these should be placed together with the five short vowels beginning with *a* (a-i-u-ṛ-ḷ), endowed with the splendor of the elements. Then follow the placement of the hands and limbs: *hrāṃ* to the two thumbs (*namaḥ*), *hrīṃ* to the two index fingers (*namaḥ*).
*svāhā* *hrūṃ* to the two middle fingers, *vaṣaṭ* *hraiṃ* to the two ring fingers,
*hūṃ* *hrauṃ* to the two little fingers, *vauṣaṭ* *hraḥ* to the palms and backs of the hands, *phaṭ*. In this same manner,
one should perform the ritual of the limbs (*aṅgakriyā*) for the mantra using the seed-syllable (*bīja*) endowed with the six long vowels at the heart and other locations.
In the *Svacchandasaṃgraha*: "Having abandoned the vowels, one should join the seed-syllable with the six long [vowels].

The six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga) are to be applied; this rule is prescribed for all cases. As for the restriction regarding the fingers, it has already been stated previously. This is the sequence for the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the hands and limbs. Then, on the forehead...
Oṃ, salutation to Brahmā accompanied by Gāyatrī—on the right cheek.
Oṃ, salutation to Viṣṇu accompanied by Sāvitrī—on the left cheek.
Oṃ, salutation to Maheśvara accompanied by Vāgīśvarī—on the left ear.
Oṃ, salutation to the Lord of Wealth accompanied by Śrī. At the mouth: Oṃ, salutation to Smara accompanied by Rati.
Above the right ear: Oṃ, salutation to Gaṇapati accompanied by Puṣṭi. Thus one should perform the placement (nyāsa).
Likewise at the base of the throat.

One should install Brāhmī and the other goddesses on the right breast, the left shoulder, the heart, the right shoulder, the right flank, the left flank, and the navel region. This is the installation inseparable from the [seed] syllables, as stated in the Viśvasāra.

One should perform the placement (vinyāsa) beginning with *oṃ* and ending with *namaḥ*, according to the established order. One should perform the entire placement according to the ritual procedure and in accordance with the doctrine of Śaṅkara. Thus it is everywhere. Then, on the forehead: *oṃ brāhmyai namaḥ*. On the left shoulder: *oṃ māheśvaryai namaḥ*. On the left side: *oṃ kaumāryai namaḥ*.

In the stomach: *oṃ vaiṣṇavyai namaḥ*. On the right side: *oṃ vārāhyai namaḥ*. On the right shoulder: *oṃ indrāṇyai namaḥ*. On the hump: *oṃ cāmuṇḍāyai namaḥ*. In the heart: *oṃ mahālakṣmyai namaḥ*. Having thus performed the placement (*vinyāsa*), one should perform the three-fold pervasive application (*vyāpakatraya*) with the root mantra. Then...
Meditative concentration.

I worship Bhuvaneśī, whose face is smiling, who possesses three eyes, whose high breasts are like the moon-crested Lord [Śiva], and whose hands display the gestures of granting boons (*varada*), the goad (*aṅkuśa*), the noose (*pāśa*), and fearlessness (*abhīti*), and who possesses the splendor of the rising sun. 1.
Having meditated thus and performed worship mentally, one should begin the external worship.
The Worship Mandala (pūjāyantra): One should draw an eight-petaled lotus on the outside, followed by a circle with sixteen petals;
in the center of the pericarp, one should draw a most beautiful hexagon.
One should draw a maṇḍala that is square and has four doors.
Then, having performed the worship of the *pīṭha* (seat) as described in the *Dīkṣāpaddhati*, one should worship the *pīṭha-śaktis*. It is as follows:
on the filaments starting from the east, [one worships] Jayā, Vijayā, Ajitā, Aparājitā, and Nityā.

One should worship [the goddesses] beginning with Vilāsinī, then Dogdhṛī, then Aghorā; in the center, one should worship Maṅgalā, using the syllable *Oṃ* at the beginning and *namaḥ* at the end. Above that, [one should worship] with: *hrīṃ sarvaśaktikamalāsanāya namaḥ*.
In the Nibandha: "Then one should fully worship the throne (pīṭha) endowed with various śaktis, [beginning with] the one named Jayā."

[Venerate] Vijayā, Ajitā, Aparājitā, Nityā, Vilāsinī, Dogdhrī, Aghorā, and Maṅgalā. Having offered the seed-syllables and so forth as the seat, one should then conceive of the Form (Mūrti) right there. Then, having meditated as before, perform the invocation (āvāhana) and the other rites.

Having performed the ritual up to the offering of five handfuls of flowers, one should worship with the six limbs beginning with "Hrīṃ, obeisance to the heart" in the filaments— at the northeast corner and so forth, in the center, and in the cardinal directions— and then offer five handfuls of flowers. Then follows the worship of the enclosures (*āvaraṇapūjā*).

In the center of the pericarp: *Oṃ hṛllekhāyai namaḥ*. In the east: *Aiṃ gaganāyai namaḥ*. In the south: *Ūṃ raktāyai namaḥ*. In the north: *Īṃ karālikāyai namaḥ*. In the west: *Hūṃ mahocchuṣmāyai namaḥ*. In the six corners: in the east, *Oṃ gāyatryai namaḥ* and *Oṃ brahmaṇe namaḥ*; in the southwest...

Oṃ, salutation to Sāvitrī; Oṃ, salutation to Viṣṇu. In the northwest: Oṃ, salutation to Sarasvatī; Oṃ, salutation to Rudra. In the southeast: Oṃ, salutation to Śrī; Oṃ, salutation to the Lord of Wealth (Dhanapati). In the west: Oṃ, salutation to Rati; Oṃ, salutation to Smara. In the northeast: Oṃ, salutation to Puṣṭi.
Oṃ, salutation to Gaṇapati. On both sides of the hexagon: Oṃ, salutation to Śaṅkhanidhi;

Oṃ, salutation to Padmanidhi. On the filaments—in the directions of Agni, Nairṛti, Vāyu, Īśāna, and the four cardinal points—one should worship with the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*), beginning with "Hrāḥ, salutation to the heart," and so forth. And likewise, in the *Nibandha*:
One should worship the heart and the other [limbs] on the filaments, beginning from the southeast corner.
The deities of the limbs (aṅgadevatās) should be meditated upon as having their beginning and end in the direction of fire (the southeast), starting from the eye; thus it is everywhere.

However, a specific detail must be stated regarding Bhairavī and the others: [they are worshipped] upon the eight petals in the order beginning with the East. Oṃ, *namaḥ* to Anaṅgakusumā; likewise, *namaḥ* to Anaṅgakusumāturā;
*namaḥ* to Anaṅgakusumāturā; [and] *namaḥ* to Anaṅgamadanā. (p. 197)

To Anaṅgamadanāturā, Bhuvanapālā, Gaganavegā, and Śaśirekhā. In the sixteen petals, starting from the eastern direction, [worship] Oṃkarālinī, likewise Vikarālinī, Umā, Sarasvatī, Śrī, Durgā, Uṣā, Lakṣmī, Śruti, and Smṛti.
To Dhṛti, to Śraddhā, to Medhā, to Mati, to Kānti, and to Āryā. Outside the lotus, in the directions starting from the east, [worship] Anaṅgarūpā, Anaṅgamadanā,
Madanāturā, Bhuvanavegā, Bhuvanapālikā, and Sarvaśiśirā.
One should worship [the goddesses] beginning with Anaṅgavedanā and ending with Anaṅgamekhalā, using mantras beginning with *Oṃ* and ending with *Namaḥ*.
Outside of that, in the house, starting from the east and so forth: *Oṃ lāṃ i* to Indra, the lord of the gods, together with his weapons, and so on;
*Raṃ* to Agni, the lord of splendor, together with his weapons, and so on; *Yaṃ* to Yama, the lord of the pretas.

To Kṣā, for Nirṛti, the lord of the Rākṣasas, equipped with weapons, and so forth; Vāṃ, for Varuṇa, the lord of the waters, equipped with weapons, and so forth; Saṃ, for Soma, the lord of the stars, equipped with weapons, and so forth; Hāṃ.

"To Īśāna, Lord of the Gaṇas, with his weapons," and so forth. Between Indra and Īśāna: "To Brahmā, Lord of Creatures, with his weapons. Between Nirṛti and Varuṇa: "Hrīṃ! To Ananta, Lord of the Nāgas, with his weapons. And likewise: "The World-Guardians (Lokapālas) are to be worshipped on the outside."
All [the deities] are in the square; likewise, they are between Indra and Īśa, as well as between Rakṣas and Varuṇa.
The wise know that Brahmā and Viṣṇu are always to be worshipped, as well as the deities of the directions.

"Those mantras of Indra and the other world-protectors begin with Dhruva (the Pole Star) and so forth; all are joined with their respective seed-syllables (*bīja*), ending in the dative case and followed by *namaḥ*. According to this statement, the syllable *praṇava* (OM) precedes them in every instance. Their seed-syllables are stated in the *Kriyāsāra*:
By means of Earth, Fire, Wind, and the others ending with Varuṇa, Anila, and Śeṣa;

They should be worshipped with [mantras] joined by infinite *bindus* and the noose (*pāśa*) of *māyā*. And so it is stated in the *Yāmala*: "At the conclusion of the sacrifice, one should worship the World-Protectors (*lokapāla*), accompanied by their root-mantras and their attendants (*parivāra*), together with their weapons (*heti*) and their respective classes of beings (*jātyadhipa*), starting from the eastern direction. According to the *Dīpikā*, [the mantra is] "together with their vehicles" (*savāhanāya*). Outside of that, starting from the east, [one worships] "to the Vajra" (*vajrāya*).

One should worship [the weapons] with the mantra beginning with *praṇava* (om) and ending with *namaḥ*: to Śakti, Daṇḍa, Khaḍga, Pāśa, Aṅkuśa, Gadā, Śūla, Padma, and Cakra. Then, one should complete the ritual from the incense offering (*dhūpa*) up to the dismissal (*visarjana*).
For its preliminary rite (*puraścaraṇa*), one should perform thirty-two lakh recitations of the mantra, mentally reciting the mantra thirty-two lakh times.
One should offer oblations with eight substances mixed with the three sweets (*trisvādu*) in a quantity equal to one-tenth [of the recitations]. The eight substances are as follows:

The wise know the eight substances to be: fuel-sticks of *aśvattha*, *udumbara*, *plakṣa*, and *nyagrodha* trees; sesame seeds; white mustard seeds; milk-rice (*pāyasa*); and clarified butter (*ājya*). "Three sweets" refers to clarified butter, honey, and sugar.
Thus ends the ritual manual for the worship of Bhuvaneśvarī.

Now, for the sake of attaining all prosperity, I praise Ambikā, the cause of the universe, who is the embodiment of the hymn, who consists of bliss, and who is the manifest nature of the Word-Brahman (Śabdabrahman). || 1 ||
Having praised with speech that which is the mother of all knowledge, the bestower of the bodies of the lotus-born Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva,
and the cause of the creation, maintenance, and destruction of the three worlds;
O Mother, I purify you.

O Daughter of the Mountain King, you alone are indeed the cause of the possession of power by the God who is the enemy of Manmatha, even though he embodies the earth, water, fire, wind, ether, the sacrificial priest, the moon, and the sun.
O Mother, I understand that very reason for the excellence of the triple-streamed Ganges, who is worshipped by all the gods:
it is her constant rolling about within the matted locks of Śambhu, which are purified by the pollen of your lotus feet.
The lord of the stars (the moon) delights the night-lily, while the sun, the subduer of all others, delights the day-lotus;
yet each is capable of delighting only one. You, however, cause the entire universe to rejoice.
By one's own vision. || 5 ||
Even now you possess the fresh youth of the entire world; though the daughter of the King of Mountains, you are exceedingly tender.
Though the mother of the Triple World, you have not been fully beheld by her; O Gaurī, you are the object of meditation, yet you do not stand within the path of my mind.
Having attained after a long time this birth among humans, so difficult to obtain, and having further acquired proficiency in their own senses,
those who do not worship you, O Mother of the worlds, are like those who, having climbed to the very top of a ladder, fall back down again.
They fall. || 7 ||

O Bhavānī, those who, full of longing, worship you with sandalwood paste mixed with camphor powder and cool water, along with flowers possessing the fragrance of a daughter, indeed become renowned as sovereigns of the entire,
undivided world at the end.
Having entered the central path of the first lotus, she who resembles a *rājasa* [nature] indeed brings forth the universe while sleeping there; then,
bearing the shimmering grace of a circle of lightning-streaks, she bursts open five lotuses.
Attaining equality. || 9 ||

O Mother, Consort of Maheśvara, those whose limbs have been sprinkled by the nectar flowing from that [source] and who have attained dissolution again through that very path— should they ever manifest within your heart, they shall never again be subject to conception in a womb.

O Gaurī, I meditate in my mind upon you, who wear earrings that reach your cheeks, whose face is most beautiful, whose breasts are full and firm, and whose waist is slender and rounded; your hands are adorned with a lotus, a rosary for meditation, and a water-pot.
The embodied form. || 11 ||
Having resorted to yoga, conquered the sixfold group of enemies, and restrained the collection of senses within a serene mind,
they behold the Mistress of the World, whose radiant face is enriched by hands holding the noose, goad, the gesture of fearlessness, and the boon-granting mudrā.
The yogis [meditate upon] you. || 12 ||
Being consecrated by four jars of nectar turned clockwise, which resemble refined gold,
and holding two beautiful lotuses in your two hands, you yourself become Padmā, yet you possess the gesture of granting fearlessness.
Having ascended [the throne] with eight creeper-like arms bearing fierce and diverse weapons—
O Goddess Bhavānī Durgā, you who dwell among the deer and possess the luster of dūrvā grass blades, you surpass the wings of the enemies of the immortals. 14.
I repeatedly bow to you, the primordial forest-dweller maiden, whose face is beautified by the spray of summer water,
who wears a necklace fashioned from *guñjā* berries,
and who is adorned with garments of sapphire-blue luster.
I do not measure. || 15 ||
With their gait followed by swans whose tinkling anklets were visible from afar— as if by the words of their own forms—
and with their heads held high like two lotuses upon erect and well-formed stalks, they bore themselves as the very crown of Śrīkaṇṭha’s consort.
Your two feet. || 16 ||

O Bhavānī, while both your shanks are being gazed upon by the bull-bannered Lord Śiva— who, becoming a vessel of intense passion, has produced two eyes as if never sated by looking at them— may you be victorious.
I bow down to you. || 17 ||
I remember your thighs, which have surpassed the pride of the elephant’s trunk in both girth and softness;
they were fashioned by your youthful body as if they were two pillars to support the weight of your hips.
By means of the middle [path]. || 18 ||

May the waist of the black antelope, whose form is made manifest by the play of the line of hair, shine within me— that waist which, out of childhood, will simultaneously broaden its hips and breasts as it passes into a later age.
In the center of the heart. || 19 ||

O Goddess, I shall never forget that sprout— filled with the waters of beauty by your youth— which, though never having entered your navel, was as if offered by your friend Cupid, who fears the fire of Shiva’s eye;
for even the Lord bears upon his forehead a smile that betrays his home, while you bear the saffron paste upon your lotus-like breasts.
The two frontal globes of the rutting elephant, reddened with vermilion and covered in millions of bubbles arising from his bath, bring to mind the two breasts of a passionate woman.
O Mother, may those two arms of my enemy, beautiful with streams of radiant luster flowing from necks that surpass [the beauty of] yours,
and fashioned like long nooses by the god of love (Makaradhvaja) for the purpose of seizing your neck, not come within the path of my memory.
Let them both feel ashamed. || 22 ||

O Daughter of the Mountain King, when shall I ever attain satisfaction by contemplating your neck, which is neither too long, which steals the splendor of beautiful conch shells, and which shines with a manifold array of ornaments and possesses enchanting qualities?
O Mother, he who has long eyes, a well-born forehead, cheeks slightly blooming with a gentle smile,
lips like the bimba fruit, and a high, long nose— he indeed has been born again. (24)
O Goddess,

for that mortal who here recites this hymn composed by Śruti, which you have entered— being no different from a mass of bees hovering over abundant fragrant flowers— the ancient snare of his mind falls away of its own accord, as he perceives with his heart your braid of hair.
One whose inner self is eternally moist becomes the ground for the attainment of lofty prosperities;
he is the long-enduring abode of the fortune of the crowns of prostrate kings and of auspicious marks.
Thus ends the hymn to Bhuvaneśvarī.
Then the Goddess spoke the armor-mantra (kavaca): "O Lord of Gods, whatever vidyās have been revealed by Bhuvaneśī,"
All these have been heard and understood; now I desire to hear them once more.
The Armor named *Trailokyamaṅgala*. The Lord said:
Listen, O Pārvatī; I shall speak it—attend with careful attention. (2)
O Goddess, this armor named Trailokyamaṅgala is the embodiment of mantra;
it consists of perfected vidyās and bestows all sovereignty.
By reciting and retaining it, a mortal shall become a possessor of sovereignty over the three worlds.
Of this armor (kavaca), which is the auspiciousness of the three worlds, Śiva is the seer (ṛṣi); Virāṭ is the meter; and the goddess Bhuvaneśvarī, the sustainer of the universe, is the deity. (5)
The application [of this mantra] is proclaimed for the sake of dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa.
May the seed-syllable *hrīṃ* protect my head, and may Bhuvaneśī protect my forehead.
Aiṃ may protect my right eye; Hrīṃ may protect my left eye;
Śrīṃ may protect my right ear—may Maheśvarī, whose self consists of these three syllables, protect me.
May Aiṃ always protect my left ear; may Hrīṃ always protect my nose; may the Goddess Aiṃ protect my face; and may Aiṃ protect my tongue.
May Parāmbikā, whose form consists of three letters and who is the vessel of speech, protect my throat.
May Śrīṃ constantly protect my shoulders, and may Hrīṃ always protect my arms. (9)
Klīṃ: May Tripuṭeśānī, the bestower of the sovereignty of the three worlds, protect my two hands. Oṃ: May she protect my heart; Hrīṃ: may she always protect the middle region of my body.
May that three-syllabled Bhuvaneśvarī protect the region of the navel;
may she, the bestower of all seeds and the subduer of all, protect the back.
Hrīṃ, may she protect my anus; salutations to the Blessed One, may Māheśvarī always protect my hips, thighs, and both knees. (12)
May Annapūrṇā always protect [me], svāhā! May she protect the two feet.
May the seventeen-syllable mantra, whose essence is Annapūrṇā, protect [me] from of old. 13.
Tāra, Māyā, Ramā, and Kāma—then follows the sixteen-syllable mantra;
may that supreme mantra, consisting of twenty syllables and residing in the head, protect me always. (14)
"Tāradurge yugaṃ rakṣiṇī svāhā"—this ten-syllable mantra is the protectress.
O Jayadurgā, dark as a rain cloud, may you joyfully protect me from the east! (15)
May this ten-syllabled supreme mantra, beginning with the seed-syllable of Māyā and shining like molten gold, protect the face of Jayadurgā. (16)
The supreme mantra consisting of eight syllables is "Tāraṃ hrīṃ dundurgāyai namaḥ";
may she who holds a conch, a discus, a bow, and arrows in her right hands protect me. 17.
May she who crushes Mahiṣa, who consists of gold and wealth, and who is the destroyer of the demon Mahiṣāsura, protect [me] eternally in the southwest. 18.
*Māyā-padmāvatī-svāhā* is proclaimed as the seven-syllable mantra.
May Padmāvatī, who dwells upon a lotus, always protect me in the west. (19)
O Parameśvarī, may she who consists of thirteen syllables, beginning with *Tāra* (Om), and ending with *pāśāṅkuśapuṭā māye svāhā*, protect the face of the one mounted upon a horse. 20.
May the five-arrowed Sarasvatī, who is eternally moist and flows with intoxication, protect me always with her mantra consisting of eight syllables ending in *svāhā*. 21.
Tārā, Māyā, and Kavacā shall constantly protect the heart and the secret place. Vadhū, Hūṃ, Kṣe, Hrīṃ, Phaṭ—this twelve-syllable Great Vidyā bestows everything. (22)
May Tvaritā, together with the eight serpents, always protect me in the northeast corner;
and may Bālā, [invoked] with "Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ," protect me from the region above.
May Vindvantā, Bhairavī, and Bālā always protect me on the earth.
Thus has been told to you this supreme, meritorious [mantra], which is auspicious for the three worlds. (24)
The essence, the most essential merit, the embodiment of a flood of great vidyās—
even by the recitation of this, Kubera himself instantly became a lord of the earth.
Because of reciting and retaining this, all the gods beginning with Indra became lords of all supernatural powers (siddhis) and attained every form of sovereignty. || 26 ||
Having offered eight handfuls of flowers while reciting the root mantra even once,
one shall obtain the fruit of worship performed throughout an entire year.
Having established mutual affection, Lakṣmī shall dwell immovably in his home, and Vāṇī shall reside in his mouth; this is the truth, the truth—of this there is no doubt. (28)
That meritorious soul who wears this most sacred armor named *Trailokyamaṅgalā* is indeed the best among the virtuous. (29)
Having become endowed with all sovereign powers, one shall be a conqueror of the three worlds;
[this mantra should be placed] on the right arm for a man, and likewise on the left arm for a woman. (30)
Having become possessed of many sons, even a barren woman obtains a son;
weapons such as the Brahmāstra and others do not cut that person at all.
He who recites the mantra of Bhuvaneśvarī without knowing this armor (kavaca) shall encounter extreme poverty and soon meet with death.
Thus ends the *Bhuvaneśvarī-kavaca*, named *Trailokyamaṅgala*, from the *Rudrayāmala*, spoken in the dialogue between the Goddess and the Lord.
Then the Goddess said to Hṛdaya:
"O Blessed One, tell me that hymn which accomplishes all desires."
Merely by hearing it, nothing else is desired to be heard. || 1 ||
If you would show me favor and if you have affection for me, then tell me this, O Brahmin Vimala: what is that which exists upon the surface of the earth?
Īśvara said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim the heart-mantra of Bhuvaneśvarī, which accomplishes all desires and bestows glory. (3)

Oṃ. Of this mantra of the *Śrībhuvaneśvarī-hṛdaya-stotra*, Śakti is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the meter (*chanda*), Bhuvaneśvarī is the deity (*devatā*), the letter *ha* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), the letter *ī* is the power (*śakti*), and the letter *ra* is the pin (*kīlaka*). Its application (*viniyoga*) is for the purpose of attaining the fulfillment of all desires of the mind through its recitation.
Now, the ritual placement of the limbs (aṅganyāsa):
Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to the heart;
Oṃ śrīṃ, svāhā to the head.
Oṃ aiṃ vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock; oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ to the armor; oṃ śrīṃ vauṣaṭ to the three eyes.
Oṃ Aiṃ Astrāya Phaṭ.
Thus is the ritual placement on the hands (kara-nyāsa).
Now, the meditation (dhyāna):

One should meditate upon the Mother who has brought about the birth of Brahmā and the other gods, the Yoginī who is the source of yoga for the deities, the nourisher of life, whose fierce limbs are ablaze with the supreme light of victory,
and who holds the conch, the discus, arrows, and even a bow.
The primordial Māyā, distinguished by the four lotuses of the moon, sustains the earth— the ground for the removal of the burden of existence within the worlds of birth and becoming.

We worship that Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī, by whose command the unborn Lord of Śrī— the very source of the world— creates, sustains, and at the end of time destroys this entire universe as his own legitimate offspring.

We worship that Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī, who brings joy to the people of the world, who is named Jayā, whose fame is illustrious, who is the source of the excellent sacrifice of Yoga, and who has conquered the expansion created by immeasurable enemies.

When Hari was asleep at the end of the three worlds, the Creator, born from the lotus-navel, descended; thereafter, he established his station in the Blind One (Andhakāsurī). We bow to that Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī.
We worship her whose birth is nowhere to be found, whose continuous existence is not perceived here, and for whom no karma remains at the time of cessation. || 8 ||

We worship her whose fierce mind is set upon the casting of side-long glances, who has established the ocean [of compassion], whose heart is softened by pity, and who approaches for the sake of the true devotee’s desired object. 9.
We worship that fierce Kālī, from whose womb the birth of the world arose, who protects it in its midst, and who devours it all at the end. 10.
We worship that Jīva by whom, while people are in deep sleep, one perceives the dream of the world; and who, upon awakening, experiences the waking state. 11.
Who among the perfected ones (siddhas) does not boast of having obtained her side-long glances, which are like buds throbbing with compassion?
We, too, being independent, claim both poetic skill and lordship. 12.
We worship her whose compassionate gaze causes the lotus-face blooming within the heart to blossom forth, radiating light in every direction. 13.
We worship her, by whose presence those who follow her with passion, whose limbs are drenched in ancient love, and who are utterly fearless, rejoice. (14)
We worship her, whose constant favor Hari, Viriñci, Hara, and Īśitāra seek, standing before her with their bodies bowed low. 15.
O Manu, those who chant this [mantra] which resides in the fire of Hara, and which possesses the beauty of the moon and the power of the Veda—they are worshipped by the gods; let us worship them. 16.

May that illustrious Bhuvaneśvarī, whose heart is ever softened by the essence of love, be gracious to me—she by whose compassionate glance those who devote themselves to her feet become like Kubera. (17)
This hymn to Bhuvaneśvarī is always to be joyfully and well-recited by the virtuous;
it is worthy of constant service, bestows happiness, destroys the taints of the Kali age, and is praiseworthy for those who listen or recite it well.
Furthermore, whoever with a concentrated mind recites this Heart-Hymn (Hṛdaya-stotra), [attains the highest goal].
The goddess Bhuvaneśvarī, being pleased, shall become the bestower of his desires. || 19 ||
It bestows wealth, long life, merit, and likewise meritorious intellect;
it grants steadfast devotion to the gods and, in particular, devotion to the guru.
On the full moon day, on the fourteenth day, and especially on a Tuesday,
this hymn should be recited with effort in a temple of the deity.
The fruit of this hymn shall be attained by reciting it anywhere at all;
having purified one's body in every place, one should always recite it for the Goddess of the Gods.
Thus ends the Hṛdaya-stotra of Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī, spoken by the Lord of the Goddess in the Bhuvaneśvarī-paṭala of the Nīlasarasvatī-tantra.
Then, on the beautiful peak of Kailāsa, adorned with various jewels, Pārvatī questioned Śiva for the sake of the welfare of men and women regarding his hundred names. (1)
The Goddess said:
"O Mahādeva, if I am dear to you, then tell me the one hundred and eight names of the Great Knowledge (Mahāvidyā) known as Bhuvaneśvarī."
Īśvara said: Listen, O highly fortunate goddess, to this auspicious king of hymns,
which is superior to the thousand names (Sahasranāma), bestowing success and being the cause of liberation.
Having risen in the morning, those who are pure and composed, endowed with faith, should recite this three times a day; it bestows the fruit of all desires.

Oṃ. Of this hymn of one hundred and eight names of the illustrious Bhuvaneśvarī, Śakti is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandas), Bhuvaneśvarī is the deity (devatā), and its application (viniyoga) is in the recitation for the attainment of the four aims of human life.
Mahāmāyā, Mahāvidyā, Mahāyogā, and Mahotkaṭā; Māheśvarī, Kumārī, Brahmāṇī, and she who has the form of Brahmā. || 5 ||
Vāgīśvarī, whose form is Yoga, served by millions of Yoginīs;
Jayā, Vijayā, Kaumārī, and Sarvamaṅgalā. (6)
Hiṅgulā, Vilāsī, Jvālinī, Jvālarūpiṇī, Īśvarī, Krūrasaṃhārī, and Kulamārgapradāyinī. || 7 ||

She is Vaiṣṇavī, the one who bestows good fortune, belonging to a noble family, and honored by her clan; she has a beautiful left side, moves with a graceful gait, and is likewise beloved by Vāmadeva.
She is the form of the ḍākinīs and yoginīs, the Mistress of Beings, the Leader of Beings;
she is Padmāvatī, the Lotus-eyed One, the Unawakened, and Sarasvatī.
Bhūcarī, Khecarī, Māyā, Mātaṅgī, Bhuvaneśvarī,
Kāntā, Pativratā, Sākṣī, Sucakṣuḥ, and Kuṇḍavāsinī.
Umā, Kumārī, Lokeśī, Sukeśī, Padmarāgiṇī, Indrāṇī, Brahmacāṇḍālī, Caṇḍikā, and Vāyuvallabhā. || 11 ||
Her form consists of all the elements; she is of the nature of water and has a distended belly like a water-jar;
she is of the nature of space and dwells in the battlefield, adorned with human skulls.
The Narmadā is indeed the bestower of liberation, granting desire, dharma, and wealth;
she is Gāyatrī and Sāvitrī, the triple-sandhya who flows through sacred fords.
The eighth, the ninth, the tenth, and likewise the eleventh;
she is the form of the full moon and the new moon, having the nature of the personified lunar days (tithis).
She is the destroyer of the enemy of the gods (Śiva), possesses a fierce form, and is affectionate;
she is like fire, consists of half a mora, is ruddy, and has yellow eyes. || 15 ||
She is modesty, Sarasvatī, knowledge, Bhavānī, and the destroyer of sins;
her form holds the serpent-noose, she is unfathomable, and she wears earrings.
She who brings about the destruction of those in the form of Kṣatriyas, the radiant one with a pure smile;
she who is unmanifest yet manifests the worlds, the wise one whose form is Śambhu. || 17 ||
Mātaṅgī, the intoxicated elephant-woman, who is ever beloved by Mahādeva;
Vārāhī, the slayer of Daityas, auspicious and consisting of all the scriptures. 18.
Whoever recites this with devotion or listens to it with a concentrated mind, one who is childless shall obtain a son, and one who is destitute shall become wealthy. (19)
Even a fool obtains the scriptures, and even a thief finds a refuge;
a Brahmin becomes a reciter of the Vedas, and a Kṣatriya becomes victorious.
The Vaiśya shall become wealthy, and the Śūdra prospers in happiness; this occurs for those of single-minded devotion on the eighth, the fourteenth, and the ninth lunar days. (p. 206) 21.
Those who always recite this with devotion shall indeed never be partakers of suffering—whether once, twice, thrice, or even four times a day. || 22 ||
Those who always recite [this] with devotion are honored in the heavenly world;
they are like the gods upon seeing Rudra, or like the serpents upon seeing Garuḍa. || 23 ||
His enemies flee upon merely beholding his face.
Thus ends the hymn of one hundred and eight names of Bhuvaneśvarī, from the dialogue between the Goddess and Śaṅkara in the venerable Rudrayāmala.
Now, for this *sahasranāma* of the venerable *Śrībhuvaneśvarī*: Sadāśiva is the seer (*ṛṣi*), the *anuṣṭubh* is the meter (*chandaḥ*),
the deity (*devatā*) is Bhuvaneśvarī, the seed-syllable (*bīja*) is *lajjā*, and the power (*śakti*) is Kamalā.
The *vāgbhava* is the *kīlaka*; its application (*viniyoga*) is in the recitation (*japa*) for the accomplishment of all aims.
Bhuvaneśī, worshipful on earth, Bhavānī, destroyer of fear;
she who is the form of existence, the bliss of existence, and the one who carries across the ocean of worldly existence. || 1 ||
She arises from existence, delights in existence, and removes the burden of existence;
she possesses auspicious eyes for the fortunate and an auspicious form—she is the medicine for worldly existence. || 2 ||
She has beautiful limbs, beautiful hair, and releases one from the bonds of worldly existence;
she sits upon a beautiful seat, wears beautiful garments, and is adorned with beautiful ornaments. || 3 ||
She whose form is the *bhaga*, whose bliss is the *bhaga*, the mistress of the *bhaga*, she who is garlanded with *bhagas*;
she who is the knowledge of the *bhaga*, the divine lady (*bhagavatī*), she who is moistened by the *bhaga*, and she who brings forth the *bhaga*.
She whose sprouts are the *bhaga*, she who sports with the *bhaga*, she who is foremost among the *bhagas*, she who is auspicious through the *bhaga*;
she whose play is the *bhaga*, she who is pleased by the *bhaga*, she who is the perfection of the *bhaga*, and the sovereign of the *bhaga*.
She whose abode is the *bhaga*, who is the energy of the *bhaga*, who resides in the *bhaga*, and who nourishes the *bhaga*;
she who is the festival of the *bhaga*, the knowledge of the *bhaga*, the mother of the *bhaga*, and established in the *bhaga*. || 6 ||
She is the power of fortune, the treasure of fortune, the worship of fortune, and the desire for fortune;
she is the mistress of fortune, the sovereign of fortune, the one to be adored through fortune, and the beauty of fortune.
She whose lines are the vulva, whose affection is the vulva, who increases the affection for the vulva;
she who is the sister, who dwells within the seed of the vulva, and who delights in the enjoyment of the vulva. || 8 ||
She whose conduct is the *bhaga*, who is the support of the *bhaga*, whose conduct is the *bhaga*, and who is the refuge of the *bhaga*;
she who has the *bhaga* as her flower, who bestows the glory of the *bhaga*, and who dwells within the flower of the *bhaga*.

She who assumes a beautiful form, who is adorned with the flowers of the worthy and the unworthy, whose grace is auspicious, whose garland is auspicious, whose limbs are auspicious, and who is the beauty of the auspicious. (10)
She whose conduct is auspicious, whose play is auspicious, whose eyes are auspicious, who destroys what is inauspicious;
she whose limbs are auspicious, whose speech is auspicious, whose radiance is auspicious, and who is the possessor of fortune. || 11 ||
She possesses modesty worthy of the noble, she is a river for the noble, she dwells in the enjoyments of the noble;
she has breasts worthy of the noble, a face worthy of the noble, an assembly worthy of the noble, and she is the dispeller of fear.
The Mistress of devotion, the creator of devotion, she who bestows grace upon devotees;
the giver of devotion, the mother of devotion, and the increaser of the bliss of devotees. || 13 ||
She who loves devotion, who delights in devotion, who sports in the state of devotion;
she whose character is devotion, whose play is devotion, who is the mistress of devotion, and who protects devotion. || 14 ||
She is the knowledge of devotion, the knowledge for the devotee, devotion itself, and that which delights in devotion;
she is the way of devotion, the love of devotion, and the accomplisher of the means of devotion.
She who is to be accomplished through devotion, she who is to be accomplished by devotees, the companion of devotion, the sovereign of existence;
the knowledge of warriors, the joy of warriors, abiding in warriors, and having the form of warriors. 16.
She who is honored by warriors, she who resides among warriors, she who dwells in the quarters of warriors;
she who is the lady of warriors, she whose form is that of a warrior, and she who increases the warrior-form. || 17 ||
She who has the appearance of a warrior, the mistress of warriors, the one who possesses the womb, the beauty of existence;
she who acts out of love for warriors, according to the conduct of warriors, and who bestows grace upon warriors.
She is meditated upon by warriors, awakened by warriors, and she delights the awakening of warriors;
she is to be served by warriors, the best of warriors, worshipped by warriors, and the awakener of warriors.
Bhaṭakīrtti, Bhaṭakalā, Bhaṭapā, Bhaṭapālinī, Bhaṭaiśvaryā, Bhaṭādhīśā, Bhaṭekṣā, and Bhaṭatoṣiṇī. || 20 ||
The mistress of warriors, the mother of warriors, the increaser of the fortune of warriors;
she is the liberation of warriors, the union with warriors, and the increaser of the joy of warriors. || 21 ||
She is the mistress of fortune, the progenitor of fortune, the abode of fortune, and the very form of fortune;
she is skilled in the cultivation of devotion, the giver of existence, and the increaser of being.
She whose form is existence, whose essence is existence, who dwells within other states of being;
she is the sprout of existence, the digit of existence, and she resides in the abode of existence. || 23 ||
She is afflicted by existence, sustained by existence, and established in the midst of existence;
she is the prosperity of existence, the accomplishment of existence, the beginning of existence, and that which brings existence into being.
She whose abode is existence, who is intent on existence, and who is devoted to the means of attaining existence;
she is the Mistress of existence, accessible through existence, established in existence, and proud of existence. || 25 ||
She is the future, the delight of existence, the goddess of speech, and the sovereign of the land of Bhārata;
she is the Ganges, the possessor of fortune, and the digit that brings about the dawning of good luck.
She is the refuge of fortune, composed of fortune, fortunate herself, and the bestower of the fruits of fortune;
she is the movement of fortune, the essence of fortune, the stream of fortune, and the giver of fortune.
The mistress of fortune, the treasure-trove of fortune, the fortunate one, the auspicious mother of fortune;
she who beholds fortune, the name of fortune, the giver of fortune and fortune itself, the mother of fortune. || 28 ||
She is the glance of fortune, the mind of fortune, the beginning of fortune, and she who dwells in the midst of fortune.
She is the sovereign of brothers, possessed of brothers, the mother of brothers, and the protector of brothers.
She who abides in her brother, who is well-disposed toward her brother, the bee-like one, the mother of bees;
she who has the form of a Bhilla, who is like a Bhilla, who dwells among the Bhillas, and who protects the Bhillas. || 30 ||
Bhillamātā, Bhilladhātrī, Bhillanī, Bhillakeśvarī, Bhillakīrti, Bhillakalā, and Bhillamandaravāsinī. || 31 ||
She is the sport of the Bhillas, the play of the Bhillas, worshipped by the Bhillas, and beloved by the Bhillas;
she is the daughter-in-law of the Bhillas, the daughter of the Bhillas, the mother of the Bhillas, and the nourisher of the Bhillas. || 35 ||
She is the granddaughter of the Bhillas, the assembly of the Bhillas, and she dwells in the conduct of the Bhillas;
she is worshipped by the Bhillas, the speech of the Bhillas, the mother of the Bhillas, and the destroyer of the enemies of the Bhillas.
She who dwells in fear, the mother of those who fear, fear itself, the destroyer of fear;
she who bestows fear, the remover of fear, and she who sports with forms of fear through fear. || 34 ||
She who is the refuge of the fearful, the pacifier of fear, she who dwells in the abode of the frightened;
she who follows the way of fear, the essence of fear, the witness of fear, and the remover of fear. || 35 ||

The mistress of Bhīma, the mother of Bhīma, the formidable one, the dweller in the terrible; the sovereign of Bhīma, she who delights in Bhīma, the one with formidable limbs, and the protectress of Bhīma. || 36 ||
She whose roar is terrifying, she whose lute is fearsome, she who increases formidable sovereignty;
she whose assembly is awe-inspiring, she who is the nurse of the terrible, she who delights in fearsome knowledge. || 37 ||
She is the bestower of terrible prowess, she who dwells in terrible prowess;
she is the goddess who causes joy to the terrible, and she who sports in terrible joy. || 38 ||
She who constantly instructs Bhīma, she who bestows terrible fortune, she who is the accomplishment of Bhīma, she who is the prosperity of Bhīma, and she who increases devotion to Bhīma. (39)
She who dwells in the formidable, she who grants formidable boons, she who teaches formidable dharma;
the sovereign of Bhīṣma, the sustainer of Bhīṣma, and the awakener of Bhīṣma’s awakening. || 40 ||
She is the glory of Bhīṣma, the mother of Bhīṣma, and the instructor of Bhīṣma’s knowledge;
she abides in Bhīṣma, is attained through Bhīṣma’s austerity, is the sovereign of Bhīṣma, and is the deliverer from Bhīṣma’s distress.

She whose play is formidable, whose character is formidable, who dwells on the banks of the Bhīṣmaroṇī; she who has the formidable as her refuge, who grants formidable boons, and who increases formidable joy. || 42 ||
She is the mistress of the worlds, the one who causes bliss to the worlds;
she dwells upon the earth, her form is the earth, and she is the remover of the earth’s burden.
She who abides in enjoyment, she who bestows enjoyment, she who is enjoyment, she whose form is enjoyment;
she who is the mistress of enjoyment, she who grants enjoyment, she whose form is the very nature of enjoyment. || 44 ||
She who dwells upon serpents, the mistress of serpent-lords, whose form has the shape of a serpent;
she who is a female serpent, whose abode is the serpents, and who bestows joy upon the serpents. || 45 ||
She is the mistress of beings, the mother of beings, abiding in all beings, and possessing the form of all beings;
she is the sovereign of beings, her play is with beings, and she always assumes the guise of beings.
The giver of beings, she whose hair is beings, the sustainer of beings, the Great Sovereign;
she who moves among beings, the consort of beings, and the dweller in the world of beings. || 47 ||

She is the perfection of beings, the supernatural power of beings, and she dwells in the joy of beings; she is the glory of beings, the fortune of beings, and the increaser of the good fortune of beings. || 48 ||
She who is worshipped by the elements, she who delights the elements, she who dispels the ignorance of the elements;
she whose grandsons are the elements, she whose sons are the elements, she who is the sovereign mistress of the wives of the elements.
She who dwells upon the earth, she who is the supreme ornament of the earth, she who is the mistress of kings, she who protects the rulers;
she who is the mother of kings, she who resembles a king, and she who bestows royal sovereignty. || 50 ||
She is the movement of the king, she resides in the king, she increases the majesty of the king;
she is the sister of the king, the mother of the king, as well as the granddaughter and the daughter-in-law of the king. || 51 ||
She is the glory of kings, the policy of kings, and the increaser of the fortune of kings;
she is the action of kings, the sport of kings, and she who dwells upon Mount Mandara.
Worshipped by kings, to be propitiated by kings, increasing the enjoyments of kings, taking refuge with kings, the time of kings, and wielding the scepter of royal curiosity. || 53 ||
She who abides in ornaments, the mistress of ornaments, the ornament itself, she who wears ornaments;
she who is the mistress of the dharma that is the substratum of ornaments, and she whose form is the very shape of ornaments. || 54 ||
She is the abode of the conduct of the lords of the earth, adorned with the conduct of the lords of the earth;
she is the composition of the conduct of the lords of the earth, embellished by the conduct of the lords of the earth. || 55 ||
She is the mistress of the dharma of earthly conduct, she is the performer of earthly conduct;
she is one whose behavior is that of earthly conduct, yet she is devoid of earthly conduct.
She is established in the increase of royal conduct, she bestows the increase of royal conduct;
she is the performer of royal conduct, she is the giver of the fruits of royal conduct. || 57 ||
She is the mistress of the activities of the conduct of kings, the bestower of the activities of the conduct of kings;
she resides within the bodies of those whose conduct is that of kings, and she is the one who performs the actions of the conduct of kings.
Established in the perfection of royal conduct, she bestows the perfection of royal conduct;
she possesses the virtues of royal conduct and maintains royal conduct.
She is the wave of bliss for kings, she whose form is that of the Lord of Kings;
she is established in the policy of kings, and she dwells in the station of a king.
The speech of the gods resides in the position of the lord of the earth, bestowing boons upon that lord of the earth.
The wave of bliss from medicine, whose form is the bliss of medicine;
the queen of the bliss of medicine, whose form is the bliss of medicine. (62)

She who is the mistress of the activity of the joy of medicine, she who bestows the joy of medicine, she who is the physician, she whose root is medicine, and she who dwells in the abode of medicine. || 63 ||
She is the embodiment of Bheṣajeśvara and the bestower of the siddhis of Bheṣajeśvara;
she is the mistress of the dharma of Bheṣajeśvara and the giver of the karma of Bheṣajeśvara. 64.
Bheṣajeśvarakarmeśī, Bheṣajeśvarakarmiṇī;
Bheṣajādhīśajananī, Bheṣajādhīśapālinī. || 65 ||
She is the architect of the Lord of Medicines, auspicious as the Lord of Medicines;
she dwells in the midst of the forest of medicines and is the protectress of the forest of medicines.
She is the science of medicine, the medicine itself, and the bestower of desired medicines;
she abides in medicine, is the mistress of medicine, and increases the joy of medicine. || 67 ||
Bhairavī, whose movement is that of Bhairava, whose form has the appearance of Bhairava, she who is skilled in the conduct of Bhairava, and adorned with the conduct of Bhairava. || 68 ||
Bhairavā, Bhairaveśī, and the bestower of Bhairava-bliss;
the sovereign whose form is Bhairava-bliss, she whose very nature is Bhairava-bliss. || 69 ||
She is skilled in the bliss of Bhairava, she is the temple of the bliss of Bhairava;
she knows the reality of the bliss of Bhairava and is entirely devoted to the bliss of Bhairava.
Skilled in the bliss of Bhairava, she bestows the wisdom of the bliss of Bhairava;
she is the abode of delight in the bliss of Bhairava and the giver of delight in the bliss of Bhairava. || 71 ||
The queen of Bhairavānanda, the garland of Bhairavānanda, the bestower of the intellect of Bhairavānanda, the mother of Bhairavānanda. 72.
She is the mother who gives birth to the support of Bhairava; she is the protector of the support of Bhairava;
she is the sovereign whose form is the support of Bhairava; she is the one whose very nature is the support of Bhairava. || 73 ||
She is the accumulation of the support of Bhairava, the certainty of the support of Bhairava;
she knows the reality of the support of Bhairava and bestows the reality of the support of Bhairava.
She is the mistress of the Bhairavāśraya-tantra, the mantra-practitioner residing in Bhairava;
she is the arrangement of Bhairava’s refuge, colored by the refuge of Bhairava. || 75 ||
She who determines the refuge of Bhairava, she who is filled with the refuge of Bhairava;
she who determines the refuge of Bhairava, she who sustains the refuge of Bhairava. 76.
She is the awakening of Bhairavānanda, the one who awakens Bhairavānanda;
she abides in the awakening of Bhairavānanda and bestows the awakening of Bhairavānanda. 77.

She who bestows the sovereignty and boons of Bhairavī, she who grants the sovereignty of Bhairavī, she who is the manifestation of the sovereignty of Bhairavī, and she who increases the sovereignty of Bhairavī. || 78 ||
Established in the sovereign power and perfection of Bhairavī, she bestows the sovereign power and perfection of Bhairavī;
she is the Mistress of the sovereign power and perfection of Bhairavī, and her very form is the sovereign power and perfection of Bhairavī. || 79 ||

The excellent path of Bhairava’s sovereignty, the radiant splendor of Bhairava’s sovereignty, the abode of the increase of Bhairava’s sovereignty, and the bestower of the increase of Bhairava’s sovereignty. (80)
Skilled in the sovereignty of Bhairavī, she bestows the sovereignty of Bhairavī;
she is easily attained through the sovereignty of Bhairavī, and she is the one who grants the sovereignty of Bhairavī. 81.
She is radiant with the sovereignty of Bhairava, transformed by the sovereignty of Bhairava;
she possesses the discipline of the sovereignty of Bhairava, and is the knower of the sovereignty of Bhairava. || 82 ||
She is the majesty of Bhairava’s sovereignty, she who considers herself the sovereign power of Bhairava;
she is devoted to the sovereignty of Bhairava, and she is fashioned by the sovereignty of Bhairava. || 83 ||
She is the mistress of enjoyments, the mother of enjoyment, the abode of enjoyment, and the protector of enjoyment;
she is the play of enjoyment, the sport of enjoyment, the sovereign of enjoyment, and the increaser of enjoyment. || 84 ||
She whose limbs are enjoyment, she who delights in enjoyment, she who moves within the conduct of enjoyment;
she who is the refuge of enjoyment, she who possesses enjoyment, she who is the enjoyer, and she whose form is enjoyment. || 85 ||
She is the sprout of enjoyment, the means of enjoyment, and she who dwells in the support of enjoyment;
she is the Mother of Enjoyment, devoted to enjoyment, and the bestower of the perfection of enjoyment. || 86 ||
She who dwells in food, who is devoted to food, who bestows the bliss of food;
she who is a wave of the bliss of food, who sports within food. 87.
The greatness of the bliss of eating, the giver of the objects of enjoyment for the bliss of eating, the arrangement of the bliss of eating, and she who is gladdened by the bliss of eating. || 88 ||
She is skilled in the etiquette of eating, adorned by the etiquette of eating;
she practices the etiquette of eating and is refined by the etiquette of eating. || 89 ||
They were perfected in the conduct of eating, endowed with the conduct of eating;
their minds were established in the conduct of eating, and they maintained the manner of eating. 90.
She is the manifestation of the conduct of eating, she is the expansion of the conduct of eating;
she is the delight of the conduct of eating, she is the protector of the conduct of eating. || 91 ||

She who delights in the conduct of eating, she who consumes the conduct of eating, she who bestows happiness through the conduct of eating, and she who has a great longing for the conduct of eating. || 92 ||
She whose essence is food and drink, she who is beautiful through food and drink, she whose conduct consists of food and drink, and she who is restless for food and drink. || 93 ||
She is the abundance of the taste of food, she is fond of the taste of food;
she is satisfied by the taste of food, she is the bestower of the taste of food. 94.
Delighting in the taste of food, relying upon the taste of food, intent on the taste of food, and devoted to the taste of food. || 95 ||
She whose syllable is *bhaukṣara*, she who is the sovereign of *bhaukṣara*, she whose form is the syllable *bhaukāra*;
she who abides in *bhaukṣara*, she who is the beginning of *bhaukṣara*, and she who dwells in the station of *bhaukṣara*. || 96 ||
Bhaṅkārī, Bharmmiṇī, Bharmī, Bhasmeśī, Bhasmarūpiṇī, Bhaṅkārā, Bhañcanā, Bhasmā, Bhasmasthā, and Bhasmavāsinī. || 97 ||
She whose form is the syllable *bhakṣara*, who dwells in the place of *bhakṣara*, who is enriched by *bhakṣara*, the mistress of *bhakṣara*, whose nature is *bha*, and whose form is *bhas*. || 98 ||
She who dwells on the mountain, the mistress of the mountain, the mountain-dweller, the sovereign of the mountain;
she who is the delighter in the bliss of the mountain, and the protector of the bliss of the mountain. || 99 ||
She who generates joy for the mountains, she who dwells in the joy of the mountains, she who delights in the joy of the mountains, and she who is protected by the joy of the mountains. || 100 ||

She whose majesty is the bliss of the mountain-dweller, who is the temple of the bliss of the mountain-dweller, who is the sovereign of all that is the bliss of the mountain-dweller, and who is the mother of all that is the bliss of the mountain-dweller. (101)

The queen of the joy of the mountain-dwellers, the bestower of joy to the mountain-dwellers; the sovereign lady of dharma for the lord of the mountain-dwellers, she whose nature is the joy of the mountain-dwellers. || 102 ||
She is the mistress of the dharma of the lord of mountains, the bestower of success upon the lord of mountains;
she is the mistress of the karma of the lord of mountains, the beloved of the lord of mountains. || 103 ||
Devoted to the Lord of the Mountains, she is ordained by the Lord of the Mountains;
she abides in the policy of the Lord of the Mountains, and she bestows the wisdom of the Lord of the Mountains.
She is the sovereign of fortune for the lord of mountains, the beloved wife of the lord of mountains;
she resides within the intellect of the lord of mountains and bestows wisdom upon the lord of mountains. 105.

She is the bestower of boons upon the lords of the mountains, she is worshipped by the lords of the mountains, she is to be propitiated by the lords of the mountains, and she is praised by the lords of the mountains. || 106 ||
Bhaṅgeśvarī, composed of hemp, residing in hemp, whose form is hemp;
she who is unharmed by hemp, devoted to hemp, worshipped with hemp, and the protectress of hemp. || 107 ||
She who possesses waves, whose play is the wave, who delights in the enjoyment of the wave;
she who resembles the stage of the wave, and who dwells upon the stage of the wave. || 108 ||
She who feeds on hemp, she whose root is hemp, she who ordains the enjoyment of hemp;
she who rests upon hemp, she whose seed is hemp, the sovereign of the sprout from the seed of hemp. 109.
She is the wonder of the mechanism of dissolution, likewise the sovereign of the mechanism of dissolution;
she is the one who causes delusion through the mechanism of dissolution, and she is the one who delights through the mechanism of dissolution. || 110 ||
She who dwells in the contemplation of the mechanism of dissolution, she who contemplates the mechanism of dissolution;
she who finds bliss in the essence of the mechanism of dissolution, she who is the sovereign of the essence of the mechanism of dissolution. 111.

She is the taste of the hemp-press juice, she abides in the taste of the hemp-press juice; she is the support for the taste of the hemp-press juice, she is the refuge of the taste of the hemp-press juice. || 112 ||
She who possesses the form of the Daughter of the Mountain, she whose form is that of the Daughter of the Mountain;
she who is the Mistress of Yoga for the Daughter of the Mountain, she who protects the Daughter of the Mountain. || 113 ||
She whose majesty is that of the Daughter of the Mountain; she who is garlanded by the Daughter of the Mountain;
she who is the mistress of the Lord of Beings, who is the Daughter of the Mountain; she whose form is that of the Daughter of the Mountain. (114)
She who abides in the perfection of the Daughter of the Mountain, she who bestows the perfection of the Daughter of the Mountain;
she who is the mistress of the state of the Daughter of the Mountain, she who brings about the state of the Daughter of the Mountain. 115.

She who dwells in the enjoyment of the Son of the Mountain, she who bestows the enjoyment of the Son of the Mountain, she who is the mistress of the enjoyment of the Son of the Mountain, she who is the enjoyer of the Son of the Mountain. 116.
She is the capable one, the most capable, the one whose capability is non-existent, and the beloved of existence;
she is the state beyond states, known as existence, the radiance of being, and the end of fear.
She whose speech is the limit of speech, who abides in speech, who is the light of speech, who resembles the sun;
she who dwells in the sun, who is the mistress of the sun, and who increases the sovereignty of the sun. || 118 ||
She is the mother who generates the bliss of Bhāskara, the bestower of the bliss of Bhāskara, the majesty of the bliss of Bhāskara, and the source-mother of the bliss of Bhāskara. 119.
Bhāskarānandanaiśvaryā, Bhāskarānandaneśvarā, Bhāskarānandasupathā, and Bhāskarānandasuprabhā. (120)
A mass of bliss from Bhāskarānanda, composed by Bhāskarānanda, abiding in the system of Bhāskarānanda, and bestowing the wisdom of Bhāskarānanda. 121.
She stands in the midst of the rising of the Sun; she dwells within the rising of the Sun;
she abides in the splendor of the rising of the Sun; and by the splendor of the rising of the Sun. || 122 ||
She is the moonlight for the conduct of Bhāskara, expert in the conduct of Bhāskara;
she is the supreme conduct of Bhāskara, the Caṇḍikā of Bhāskara’s conduct. || 123 ||
Supreme in the conduct of Bhāskara, she has mastered the conduct of Bhāskara;
she abides in the liberation of Bhāskara’s conduct and bestows the liberation of Bhāskara’s conduct. 124.
Established in the conduct of Bhāskara, she bestows the perfection of Bhāskara’s conduct;
she is the support for Bhāskara’s feet and rests upon Bhāskara’s feet. || 125 ||
The mistress of Bhāskarācāra’s mantra, the minister of Bhāskarācāra;
the mistress of Bhāskarācāra’s wealth, the artisan of Bhāskarācāra. || 126 ||
She is the Mistress of the Dharma supported by the Sun, she who upholds that which is supported by the Sun;
she is the manifestation of that which is supported by the Sun, and she is protected by that which is supported by the Sun. || 127 ||
She whose actions support the Sun, she who bestows the actions that support the Sun;
she who possesses the form that supports the Sun, she whose very nature is to support the Sun. || 128 ||
She who desires the support of Bhāskara, she who is the beloved of the support of Bhāskara;
she who is the mistress of the portion supported by Bhāskara, she who possesses the portion supported by Bhāskara. || 129 ||
She is the Mistress of the Wheel whose support is the Sun, she whose splendor is the Wheel whose support is the Sun;
she who resides in the Wheel whose support is the Sun, she who possesses the Wheel whose support is the Sun.
The mistress of Bhāskareśvara and Kṣatreśa, the protectress of Bhāskareśvara and Kṣatri;
the mother of Bhāskareśvara, the guardian of Bhāskareśvara. || 131 ||
Bhāskareśvarasarveśī, Bhāskareśvaraśarvarī, Bhāskareśvarasadbhīmā, and Bhāskareśvarasannibhā. || 132 ||
Bhāskareśvarasupathā, Bhāskareśvarasuprabhā, Bhāskareśvarayuvatī, and Bhāskareśvarasundarī. || 133 ||
She is the form of Bhāskareśvara, she is the one whose form is Bhāskareśvara;
she is the mistress of the friend of Bhāskareśvara, and she is the minister of Bhāskareśvara. || 134 ||

She who is full of bliss with Bhāskareśvara, she who has Bhāskareśvara as her refuge, she who resides in the painting of Bhāskareśvara, and she who bestows the wonderful [vision] of Bhāskareśvara. 135.
Bhāskareśvaracitreśī, Bhāskareśvaracitriṇī, she who abides in the fortune of Bhāskareśvara, and she who bestows the fortune of Bhāskareśvara. || 136 ||
She is the mistress of the fortune of Bhāskareśvara, she who brings about the welfare of Bhāskareśvara;
she is the mistress of the glory of Bhāskareśvara, she who is the very glory of Bhāskareśvara.
She whose fame is established by Bhāskareśvara, she who bestows the fame of Bhāskareśvara;
she who is the compassion of Bhāskareśvara, she who acts as Bhāskareśvara. || 138 ||
Bhāskareśvara-gīrvāṇī, Bhāskareśvara-gāruḍī, residing within the body of Bhāskareśvara, she who bestows a body upon Bhāskareśvara. 139.
She who abides in the resonance of Bhāskareśvara, she who resonates as Bhāskareśvara;
she who is the teacher of the resonance of Bhāskareśvara, she who is the resounding one of Bhāskareśvara. 140.

She who dwells in the treasury of Bhāskareśvara, she who bestows the treasury of Bhāskareśvara, she who is the mistress of the treasury of Bhāskareśvara, she who possesses the treasury of Bhāskareśvara. || 141 ||
She who abides in the power of Bhāskareśvara, she who bestows the power of Bhāskareśvara;
she who is the mistress of the satisfaction of Bhāskareśvara, she who brings satisfaction to Bhāskareśvara. || 142 ||
She is the mistress of the field of Bhāskareśvara, the protectress of the field of Bhāskareśvara;
she abides in the yoga of Bhāskareśvara and bestows the yoga of Bhāskareśvara. 143.
Bhāskareśvara-yogeśī, Bhāskareśvara-yoginī;
Bhāskareśvara-padmeśī, Bhāskareśvara-padminī. || 144 ||
She whose heart-seed is Bhāskareśvara, she who is the supreme heart of Bhāskareśvara;
she whose womb is the heart of Bhāskareśvara, she whose splendor is the heart of Bhāskareśvara. || 145 ||

She whose intellect is fixed on Bhāskareśvara, she who possesses the true nature of Bhāskareśvara, she who is the true speech of Bhāskareśvara, and she who is the excellent consort of Bhāskareśvara. 146.
She resides in the kingdom of Bhāskareśvara; she bestows the kingdom of Bhāskareśvara;
she is the sovereign of the kingdom of Bhāskareśvara; she is the nourisher of Bhāskareśvara. || 147 ||
She who abides in the knowledge of Bhāskareśvara, she who bestows the knowledge of Bhāskareśvara;
she who is the Mistress of the knowledge of Bhāskareśvara, she who goes unto Bhāskareśvara. (148)
She is the mistress of Bhāskareśvara-lakṣa, she is washed by Bhāskareśvara, she is marked by Bhāskareśvara, and she is protected by Bhāskareśvara. || 149 ||
Bhāskareśvarakhaḍgasthā, Bhāskareśvarakhaḍgadā, Bhāskareśvarakhaḍgeśī, and Bhāskareśvarakhaḍginī. || 150 ||
She is the active power of Bhāskareśvara, the beloved of Bhāskareśvara;
she resides within the body of Bhāskareśvara and bestows a body upon Bhāskareśvara. 151.
She whose eyes are fixed on Bhāskareśvara, who is beheld by the eye of Bhāskareśvara, who possesses a navel resembling that of Bhāskareśvara, and who is highly honored by Bhāskareśvara. || 152 ||
She is the pacifier of the murder of an embryo, the destroyer of the sin of killing an embryo;
she is the pacifier of the poverty of an embryo and the eradicator of the diseases of an embryo. || 153 ||
She quiets the grief for the fetus, wards off the fault of the fetus, calms the fever of the fetus, and destroys the delusion regarding the fetus. || 154 ||
She dwells in the ocean of existence, she is the mistress of the ocean of existence, she is the destroyer of the fear of the ocean of existence;
she is the one who brings about the crossing of the ocean of existence and the increaser of happiness within the ocean of existence. || 155 ||

She is the one who effects the tasks within the ocean of existence, the treasury of compassion for the ocean of existence, the pacifier of the time of the ocean of existence, and the bestower of boons upon the ocean of existence. || 156 ||
She is the vessel for the ocean of existence, she is situated within the vessel of the ocean of existence;
she has the form of the vessel of the ocean of existence, and she is the activity of the vessel of the ocean of existence. || 157 ||

She whose conduct is the worship of the ocean of existence, she who is the sprout of the worship of the ocean of existence, she who finds bliss in the worship of the ocean of existence, she who is the sovereign of the worship of the ocean of existence. 158.

She is the sovereignty of devotion to the ocean of existence, the mistress of devotion to the ocean of existence, the perfection of devotion to the ocean of existence, and the delight in devotion to the ocean of existence. || 159 ||
Devotion to the ocean of existence is eternal; devotion to the ocean of existence is the night [of ignorance];
devotion to the ocean of existence is the downward slope [toward liberation]; devotion to the ocean of existence removes the fear of birth within the ocean of existence. 160.
The desire to worship the ocean of existence is the essence of worshipping the ocean of existence;
the fame of worshipping the ocean of existence is produced by worshipping the ocean of existence. 161.
She is the eternal bestower of auspiciousness upon the ocean of existence; she is the giver of auspiciousness upon the ocean of existence.
She is the entirety of bliss within the ocean of existence; she is the complete totality of all things within the ocean of existence.
She is the complete accomplishment of the ocean of existence, the treasury of the entire ocean of existence;
she is the essential essence of the whole ocean of existence, and the bestower of all the goals of the ocean of existence. 163.
The form of the abode within the ocean of existence, having the appearance of the abode within the ocean of existence;
it is not to be attained by those unfit for the abode within the ocean of existence, [being submerged] by the waters of the abode within the ocean of existence. 164.
She who takes the form of the intoxication of the ocean of existence, she who is afflicted by the intoxication of the ocean of existence;
she who is the mistress of the intoxication of the ocean of existence, she who is the sovereign of the intoxication of the ocean of existence. (165)
She is the architect of fortune within the ocean of existence, she always bestows the fortune of the ocean of existence;
she is the shore that grants the fortune of the ocean of existence, and she is replete with the fortune of the ocean of existence. 166.

Delighting in the fortune of the ocean of existence, cultivated by the fortune of the ocean of existence, wandering through the fortune of the ocean of existence, and accumulated by the fortune of the ocean of existence. (167)
She is the excellent path for the fortune of crossing the ocean of existence; she is the bestower of the fortune of crossing the ocean of existence;
she knows the ways of the fortune of crossing the ocean of existence; and she grants the wisdom regarding the fortune of crossing the ocean of existence.
She is the manner of fortune within the ocean of existence, she who possesses the manner of fortune within the ocean of existence;
she is skilled in the enjoyments of the ocean of existence, and she is the bestower of those enjoyments.
She is the dense forest of fortune within the ocean of existence, woven with the enjoyments of the ocean of existence;
she is the Gāndhārī of the pleasures of the ocean of existence, interlaced with the delights of the ocean of existence.
She who possesses the divine flavor of the enjoyments of the ocean of existence; she who has a great longing for the enjoyments of the ocean of existence;
she who is the knot of the enjoyments of the ocean of existence; she who is the yoginī of the enjoyments of the ocean of existence. || 171 ||
She whose tongue is the enjoyment of the ocean of existence, who is adorned by the enjoyment of the ocean of existence;
she whose majesty is the enjoyment of the ocean of existence, who is expansive through the enjoyment of the ocean of existence. || 172 ||
Bestower of the enjoyments of the ocean of existence, she is worshipped by the enjoyments of the ocean of existence;
she is skilled in the enjoyments of the ocean of existence, and is adorned by the enjoyments of the ocean of existence. || 173 ||

She is the mother who brings about the destruction of the ocean of existence, the protector of the destruction of the ocean of existence, the architect of the destruction of the ocean of existence, and the guardian of the destruction of the ocean of existence. || 174 ||
She is intent on shattering the ocean of existence, yet free from desire for that shattering;
she is the architect of the destruction of the ocean of existence, and is impassioned by that very destruction. || 175 ||
She who destroys the multitude of distinctions within the ocean of existence, she who delights in the multitude of distinctions within the ocean of existence;
she who is the mistress of the karma that pierces the ocean of existence, she whose very action is to pierce the ocean of existence. || 176 ||
The mistress of auspiciousness, the mother of the auspicious, the auspicious one, she who dwells in the auspicious;
the sovereign of the auspicious, the possessor of the auspicious, she who abides in the auspicious, and the bestower of the auspicious. || 177 ||
She is of auspicious form, consisting of auspiciousness, the giver of auspiciousness, and the speaker of auspicious words;
she has auspicious ears, an auspicious appearance, is the mother of auspiciousness, and her abode is auspicious. || 178 ||
She is auspicious action, the auspicious art, the auspicious one, the increaser of the auspicious;
she is auspicious play, the auspicious portion, and the one who desires auspicious sport. || 179 ||
She whose sprouts are auspicious, who delights in the auspicious, whose limbs are auspicious, and whose counselor is auspicious;
she who possesses auspicious knowledge, who is the auspicious knowledge itself, whose speech is auspicious, and who speaks auspiciously. || 180 ||
She bestows auspiciousness upon kings, she is the king, the creeper-like eyebrow of the earth, and the bearer of the world;
she is the enjoyment of kings, the splendor of kings, the hope of kings, and the giver of royal form. 181.
The form of the earth, the lord of the earth, the glory of the earth, the welfare of the earth;
the policy of the earth, the delight of the earth, and the fear of the earth, which causes terror. (182)
She is the wave of the bliss of existence, beautiful with the bliss of existence;
she is the cause of the bliss of existence and the increaser of the bliss of existence. || 183 ||
She who delights in the bliss of existence, she who bestows the bliss of existence, she who generates the bliss of existence, and she whose very form is the bliss of existence. || 184 ||
Whoever recites this hymn every day, endowed with devotion, being possessed of devotion to the Guru and intent upon service to the Guru; || 185 ||
One who speaks the truth, has conquered his senses, and whose mouth is filled with betel-leaf—whether by day, by night, or at twilight—he shall become the Supreme Lord. (186)
By the mere recitation of this hymn, the king will certainly become submissive;
he becomes a master of all Āgamas and, in all Tantras, is Hara himself.

Having practiced [the mantra] from the mouth of the Guru and remaining in the presence of the Guru, one should [recite it] at the sacred sites of Śiva during the twilight hours, in empty houses, or at crossroads. 188.
Whoever should read or even hear this is a yogi; there is no doubt about this.
One should give away all one's possessions as a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), including wife, sons, and so forth.
Having become one whose mind is free and spontaneous, one should recite this hymn of praise;
O Goddess, one who delights in this hymn is undoubtedly the very form of Hara. 190.
Whoever should always read or even listen with a single-minded focus, he shall be long-lived, happy, and eloquent; of his speech there is no doubt. (191)
O Dear One, by being devoted to the feet of the Guru, one becomes beloved by women;
one becomes wealthy, virtuous, glorious, and wise, just like the Guru himself. 192.
Having become beloved by all, one should always worship this hymn;
O Goddess, for such a person, the accomplishment of the mantra is as if held in the palm of the hand—of this there is no doubt. (193)
He shall become like Kubera, for all supernatural powers (siddhis) are indeed under his control;
and that woman whose sons have died and who is oppressed by misfortune [shall likewise find relief]. || 194 ||
Whether she be barren, or one whose children are only female, or one whose offspring die in infancy; or a woman destitute of wealth and grain, and one who is overwhelmed by disease and grief. (195)
O Great Goddess, one should inscribe this with those [mantras] on birch bark and bind it upon the left arm; thus one shall become possessed of all happiness. || 196 ||
Thus, again and again, she proceeded, tormented by suffering—in the assembly, in calamity, in dispute, and in the peril of enemies. (197)
O auspicious one, in a fourfold battle as well as when afflicted by any kind of calamity, through the recollection of this [mantra], danger goes far away. (198)

O Goddess of the Suras, it should not be given to the disciple of another, nor to one who is lacking in devotion, nor to a wicked person, nor to a hypocrite, nor to one of evil conduct, nor to a miser.
One should bestow [this] upon a disciple who is peaceful, disciplined, self-controlled, devoted, endowed with tranquility, and intent upon recitation and worship. (200)
Even with hundreds of millions of mouths, it would not be possible to describe the majesty of this mere hymn, even over the course of thousands of future births.
O beloved, this was previously told to Viṣṇu by Brahmā;
now, O Supreme Goddess, it has been told to you out of affection for you. 202.
It must be kept secret from the uninitiated, yet it should be revealed in every way to those who are worthy. || 203 ||
Thus ends the hymn of the thousand names beginning with the letter *Bha* of Bhuvaneśvarī, as spoken in the dialogue between Īśvara and Pārvatī within the illustrious Mahātantrārṇava.
Thus ends the Bhuvaneśvarī Tantra within the Śāktapramoda.
Composed and compiled by His Majesty King Śrī Rājādeva Nandana Siṃha Bahādura, the sovereign lord of the capital of Śiva-Hara.
The fifth Tantra of Chinnamastā, contained within the Śāktapramoda.
This has been edited by Paṇḍita Śrī Raghurāja Dubejī, a descendant of the aforementioned royal preceptor.
Printed and published by Khemarāja, son of Śrī Kṛṣṇadāsa,
at his own Śrī Veṅkaṭeśvara Press.
The Chinnamastā Tantra from the Bombay edition;
now, the visualization of Chinnamastā.
Always assuming the *pratyālīḍha* stance, holding a severed head and a chisel, clad in the directions as her garment,
she joyfully drinks the stream of nectar-like blood from her own headless trunk.
One should meditate upon her who has a crest-jewel bound by a serpent, who possesses three eyes, who is adorned with a blue lotus on her heart,
who resembles a dark cloud, and who stands firmly above the God of Love as he is attached to Rati.
In her right hand, she holds a razor with hair as white as snow falling from it, and likewise a skull-bowl;
born of the quality of rajas, she is known by the name Varṇinī,
and she joyfully drinks the stream of blood falling from the severed headless trunk of the Goddess.
She, whose crest-jewel is bound by the Naga, should always be meditated upon by the gods who know the Manu-mantra.
Standing in the *pratyālīḍha* posture, joyfully drinking the blood trickling from the headless trunk— she who is capable of devouring the entire universe at the time of dissolution,
that very *tāmasī* power, the Goddess who is higher than the highest, should be meditated upon by the name of the supreme *Ḍākinī*.
To those devoted to meditation, she always grants with humility the prosperity desired by her devotees.
(p. 222) Now, the extraction of the yantra: First, one should place a triangle; in its center, three mandalas;
and in their center, one should place the womb (yoni), endowed with three openings.
Outside, one should draw an eight-petalled lotus and again three earth-mandalas; in the center, within a triangle, one should write the *kūrca* seed-syllable (*hrīṃ*) accompanied by *phaṭ*.
Now, the extraction of the mantra: Lakṣmī is in the first seed-syllable, and Manobhava is in the seed-syllable of Lajjā.
In this third [kalpa], the Goddess, who destroys great sins, is ever present.
In the fourth [syllable], however, is Guṇātītā, who bestows the knowledge of liberation;
in the letter *va* is Varuṇa himself, and in the letter *ja* is the Lord of the Gods.
In the letter *ra* is the god Hutāśana; in the letter *va* is the lord of the earth;
in the letter *ai* is the goddess Tripurā; and in the letter *ra* is Tripurasundarī.
The goddess Trailokyavijayā is always established in the syllable Oṃ;
the moon-god is in the spoke of the wheel, and Vināyaka is indeed in the syllable Na.
In the letter *ī* is Kamalā herself, and in the letter *ya* is Sarasvatī;
in the pair of *māyās* (the letter *ī*), the Goddess is always united with Prakṛti.
Vaikharī resides in the syllable *phaṭ*, the flower-weaponed god (Kusumāyudha) in the syllable *svā*, and delight (*rati*) in the syllable *hā*; thus it is in this collection of mantras.
Now the mantra:
Śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ aiṃ vajravairocanīye hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.
p. 223) Now, the procedure for worship:
