Having fashioned a garland from the heads of warriors in battle— adorned with weapons and dripping with blood— and having placed it upon your head, you entered the cremation ground with your arms outstretched like a banner.

At night, she was seen by those of great supernatural power— she whose broad hips were girt with a belt of mighty serpents, who held a spear with a piece of raw flesh in her hand, whose eyes were copper-red from constantly drinking sweet blood.

O Goddess, at the time of the end of the world-cycle, when the ocean overflows with human blood and fat and is smoky-grey with the dust of the earth, this entire universe enters within your fierce mouth in half a moment.
You are Kālī, the Kāpālikī, the Yoginī who lies upon a corpse, sealed in the *yogamudrā*, and whose blood-red waters are overflowing.
Seated in the assembly hall, you are Śivā Caṇḍaghaṇṭā, who removes the fear of those who support her. 8.
The eightfold hymn of Dhūmāvatī is meritorious and wards off all calamities;
the practitioner who recites it with devotion attains his desired success.
In times of great calamity, in times of great terror, in the presence of a great disease, or in a great battle;
for the expulsion of enemies, for killing, and likewise for the deluding of living beings.
O Goddess, by reciting this hymn, one shall attain success everywhere;
[one shall overcome] gods, dānavas, gandharvas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and pannagas. || 11 ||
By the mere recollection of this hymn, all beings such as lions and tigers flee to a distance even further than far; how much more so, then, humans and the like? (12)
O Goddess of gods, what on this earth cannot be accomplished by means of this hymn?
O Goddess, there shall be total peace, and in the end, one shall attain nirvāṇa. || 13 ||
Thus ends the Dhūmāvatī Stotra in the Ūrdhvāmnāya.
Then Śrī Pārvatī spoke regarding the armor: "O Śambhu, I have heard in detail the worship of Dhūmāvatī."
O Lord, I wish to hear of her armor; please tell it to me.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Listen, O Goddess, to this supreme secret that must not be revealed in the Kali age—
the armor (*kavaca*) of Dhūmāvatī, which brings about the subjugation of enemies.
O Goddess, it is by her power that Brahmā and the others constantly became destroyers of their enemies; through the influence of meditation upon her, the yogins became slayers of their foes.
Om. Of this Śrī Dhūmāvatī-kavaca, Pippalāda is the seer (ṛṣi), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chandas),
Śrī Dhūmāvatī is the deity (devatā), *dhū* is the seed-syllable (bīja), Svāhā is the power (śakti), Dhūmāvatī is the pin (kīlaka),
and its application (viniyoga) is in the recitation for the destruction of enemies.
Oṃ Dhūḥ—may the seed-syllable protect my head; may Dhūṃ always protect my forehead. May Dhūmā protect the pair of eyes; may Vatī always protect the ears.
May she who is long in the middle of her belly, with a soiled garment at her navel and a winnowing basket in her hand, protect my private parts; may the emaciated one protect my knees.
May she named Bhīmā protect my face, Svāhā protect my nose;
may Sarvavidyā protect my throat, and Vivarṇā my pair of arms.
May Cañcalā protect my heart; may Duṣṭā always protect my sides;
may Dhūmahastā always protect me; and may Bhayāvahā protect my feet.
Her hair bristling intensely, her brows deeply knitted, and her eyes askance, the goddess was afflicted by hunger and thirst; she was terrifying and fond of strife.
"May the Goddess, the destroyer of all enemies, protect all my limbs.
Thus has this meritorious armor been narrated to you, which is difficult to find on earth.
O Great Goddess, it is not to be revealed, not to be revealed, not to be revealed in the Kali age; it should be recited at the three junctions of the day by those intent on meditation.
O Goddess of the gods, malevolent sorcery shall not touch his body at all.
Thus ends the Dhūmāvatī-kavaca within the Dhūmāvatī-tattva, from the Bhairavī-bhairava-saṃvāda.
Now, for the heart [mantra] of Śrī Dhūmāvatī: the seer (ṛṣi) is Pippalāda,
the meter (chandas) is Anuṣṭubh, the deity (devatā) is Śrī Dhūmāvatī, the seed-syllable (bīja) is Dhūm, and the power (śakti) is Hrīṃ.
*Klīm* is the *kīlaka*; its application (*viniyoga*) is in the recitation for the destruction of all enemies.
Now follows the ritual placement on the limbs (aṅganyāsa).
Oṃ dhāḥ, *namaḥ* to the heart; dhīṃ, *svāhā* to the head; dhūḥ, *vaṣaṭ* to the crest-lock; dhaiṃ, *huṃ* to the armor;
dhauṃ, *vauṣaṭ* to the three eyes; dhaḥ, *phaṭ* to the weapon. Thus is the ritual placement upon the hands (*karanyāsa*). (p. 286)

Dhāṃ to the two thumbs, namaḥ; dhīṃ to the two index fingers, svāhā; dhūṃ to the two middle fingers, vaṣaṭ; dhaiṃ to the two ring fingers, hum; dhauṃ to the two little fingers, vauṣaṭ; dhaḥ to the palms and backs of the hands, phaṭ.
Now, as for Dhyānā:
she has a smoky luster and wears smoky garments; her teeth are bared, and she is adorned with loose, tawny-colored raiment.
She stands upon a chariot marked with the sign of a crow, possesses a pair of white hands, and holds a winnowing basket in her hand, appearing exceedingly harsh.

One should meditate upon Dhūmāvatī, whose body is perpetually emaciated by hunger, who is repeatedly and exceedingly crooked, whose mind is distracted by the longing for water, who has a pair of sunken eyes, and whose terrifying face inspires fear.
I worship that Dhūmāvatī who, at the beginning of the kalpa, slew Madhu and Kaiṭabha as Kālikā and others, and who at the end of the kalpa consumes the entire triple world.
I worship that Dhūmāvatī, who carries a skull-topped staff, who is short of stature, who destroys the wicked rākṣasas, and who also holds a shield.

I worship that Dhūmāvatī, who is an abode of virtues, whose qualities are worthy of being sought, and who increases all virtues; she is praised by those who know the true meaning of the Vedas and the Gītā.

I worship that Dhūmāvatī, who whirls her hands in a dizzying dance, who is terrible, whose eyes roll, whose voice is as deep as a thundercloud, and who is the slayer of those who strike her down. || 5 ||
I worship the goddess Dhūmāvatī, who devours fragments of bones, who rends Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, and who possesses a fierce, loud laughter. 6.
I worship Dhūmāvatī, who has severed necks, who is covered with wounds, whose very form is severed heads,
and who cuts down the multitudes of the wicked.
I worship her who has the form of smoke— she who was born when requested by the gods and asuras, she who destroys obstacles, and who speaks much and roars loudly.
I worship the goddess Dhūmāvatī, who utters the sound "jhañjha-jhañjham-ājham," who makes a humming resonance, and who instantly draws [all things] toward her. 9.
I worship Dhūmāvatī, who is joined with the sound of *ṭīpa* and *ṭaṅka*, who produces the twanging sound of a bow, and who is terrible with the massing of thick clouds. 10.
I worship Dhūmāvatī, whose nature is the mantra *ṭhaṃ*, who delights in the path called *ṭha*, and who is the essence of the *ṭha* syllable. 11.
I worship Dhūmāvatī, who is adorned by hosts of Ḍākinīs resounding with the sounds of hand-drums and kettledrums, and who is satisfied by the enjoyments of the Ḍākinīs. 12.
I worship Dhūmāvatī, who is satisfied by the sound of the ḍhakkā drum, who bestows the siddhi of the ḍhakkā-player, and whose mind is as unsteady as the beating of the ḍhakkā. 13.

I worship Dhūmāvatī, who is Tārā in the form of the Savior (Tāra), who delights in the discourse on reality, whose life-force is her beloved, and who enables one to cross the ocean of worldly existence. (14)
I worship Dhūmāvatī, whose nature consists of the syllables *thāṃ, thiṃ, thuṃ, theṃ, thaiṃ, thauṃ, thaṃ, thaḥ*, who is the essence of the letter *tha* and whose form is that very syllable.
I bow to Dhūmāvatī, the goddess whose form is that of the Durgā, the destroyer of wicked dānavas, and the one who brings about the destruction of gods and daityas. 16.
I worship Dhūmāvatī, who destroys the darkness of the form of gloom, who wears the garland of the liberated Dharma, and whose wise splendor resembles a stream of smoke. 17.
I bow to Dhūmāvatī, who delights in the dancing of actresses, who increases the art of drama, who is the lioness among women, and who is worshipped by men. 18.
I bow to Dhūmāvatī, who is to be worshipped by the Lord of Pārvatī, who dwells upon the mountain, whose form is like a lotus, and who is worthy of worship with lotuses. 19.
I worship Dhūmāvatī, who bestows the fruit of the *phaṭ* mantra through breath accompanied by hissing, and who is served by the host of Phetkārīs.
I worship Dhūmāvatī, who is to be honored with offerings, who is propitiated by strength, who takes the form of Bhagalā, who is the supreme knowledge (Vidyā) praised by Brahmā and the other gods. 21.
I worship Goddess Dhūmāvatī, who possesses a beautiful form, who is worthy of adoration, whose very nature is that of Bhuvaneśī, and who bestows prosperity upon her devotees. 22.
I consider Dhūmāvatī to be an illusion, full of sweetness, worthy of honor, esteemed by the god whose banner is a dolphin, and possessing the relish of fish and meat.
I worship Dhūmāvatī, whose face is pleased by the sacrifice of yoga, who is served by yoginīs, who is Yaśodā, and who bestows the fruit of sacrifice. 24.
I take refuge in Dhūmāvatī, whose pair of feet is worshipped by Rāma, who brought about the destruction of Rāvaṇa, and who is worthy of worship by the beloved of the Lord of Ramā (Viṣṇu). || 25 ||
I worship Dhūmāvatī, who is perceived through the arts of a hundred thousand playful gestures, whose lotus feet are venerated by the world, and who is enriched by hanging clusters of seed-pods. 26.
I worship Dhūmāvatī, who is intent on meditating upon the lotus feet of Bakapūjya, and who is to be meditated upon at twilight by Bālāmbakāri. 27.
I take refuge in Dhūmāvatī, the benefactress, whose life-breath is Śaṅkara, who destroys all calamities, who annihilates enemies, and who is pure. (28)
I worship Dhūmāvatī, who destroys the enemy of the six-faced one (Kārttikeya), who assumes sixteen forms, who tastes the six flavors, and who is gentle. 29.
I worship Dhūmāvatī, whose lotus feet are served by the gods, who bestows the happiness of the gods, and who is attended by hosts of beautiful women. 30.
I worship Dhūmāvatī, the mother of Heramba, who is worthy of adoration, who delights in laughter and graceful dance, and who captivates the hosts of enemies. (31)
I worship Dhūmāvatī, who dwells upon the shores of the salt ocean, who is gladdened by the drinking of milk, and whose lotus feet are worshipped by the gods for a moment.
This Heart-Stotra of Dhūmāvatī, composed with the names beginning with each of her thirty-four syllables, bestows excellent accomplishment. (33)
Whoever recites this hymn, which is purifying and destructive of sin, shall attain supreme perfection through the grace of Dhūmāvatī. || 34 ||
Whatever a person desires while reciting this with a one-pointed mind, all that he obtains; this is the truth, the truth—I speak it to you.
Thus ends the Heart of Dhūmāvatī.
Then the Lord Śatanāma said:
Oṃ, Dhūmāvatī, smoke-colored, devoted to the drinking of smoke.
The destroyer of Dhūmrākṣa, the auspicious one, who dwells in the auspicious place.
Content with the Aghora conduct, adorned with the Aghora conduct, delighted by the Aghora mantra, and worshipped with the Aghora mantra. || 2 ||
Delighting in loud, boisterous laughter, wearing soiled garments, she was an old woman, deformed, and widowed; she was a science with few twice-born followers.
Pravṛddhaghoṇā, Kumukhī, Kuṭilā, Kuṭilekṣaṇā, Karālī, Karālāsyā, Kaṅkālī, and Śūrpadhāriṇī. || 4 ||
Mounted upon a chariot with a crow as its banner, she is solitary, harsh, and silent;
she is eternally afflicted by hunger and thirst, with a lolling tongue and naked.
Long-bellied, long-voiced, long-limbed, and long-headed,
with disheveled tresses, she dwells upon Mount Kailāsa through her renown.
She is fierce, the very embodiment of Time, and the one who sets the wheel of time in motion;
she is pale-hued, restless, and formidable, yet the destroyer of all that is evil.
Caṇḍī, whose very nature is fierce, Cāmuṇḍā, with a fierce resonance, possessing fierce speed and fierce gait, the destroyer of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa. || 8 ||
Cāṇḍālinī, Citrarekhā, Citrāṅgī, Citrarūpiṇī, Kṛṣṇā, Kapardinī, Kullā, Kṛṣṇārūpā, and Kriyāvatī. || 9 ||
She has pot-like breasts, is greatly intoxicated, and is overwhelmed by the drinking of wine;
she is four-armed, has a lolling tongue, and is the destroyer of enemies. || 10 ||
Mounted upon a corpse, gone to a corpse, dwelling in the cremation ground;
difficult to propitiate, of evil conduct, she grants favor to the wicked. (11)
She is fleshless and formless, with shaking hands and endowed with excellence;
she is quarrelsome, fond of strife, and the destroyer of the impurities of the Kali age.
She is the very form of Mahākāla, worshipped by Mahākāla;
she is the beloved of Mahādeva, the embodiment of wisdom, and the destroyer of great distress.
She who is dear to her devotees, the refuge of her devotees, the destroyer of the enemies of her devotees;
she who is Bhairavī, Bhuvanā, Bhīmā, Bhāratī, and the soul of the universe. 14.
Bharuṇḍā, with terrifying eyes and three eyes, possessing many forms;
the mistress of the three worlds, the knower of the three times, having a triple nature, and whose body is the triple Veda. || 15 ||
"Trimūrti, Tanvī, Triśakti, and Triśūlinī—thus consists the great hymn to Dhūmā, comprising eight hundred names. (16)
O Goddess, I have told you this which destroys the hosts of enemies,
[to be used] when one is seized by an enemy in prison, during a great portent, or in the face of great fear.
A mortal who recites this hymn is liberated from all perils.
This secret, more secret than the secret, must be guarded with great effort. 18.
It bestows all prosperity upon those who recite its four-line meaning. || 19 ||
Thus ends the hymn of one hundred and eight names of Dhūmāvatī.
Then Śrī Bhairavī spoke the Thousand Names:
"O Maheśvara, tell me [the names] of Dhūmāvatī and Dharmarātrī."
This hymn of a thousand names of mine bestows all spiritual accomplishments. || 1 ||
Śrī Bhairava said:
Listen, O Goddess Mahāmāyā, my beloved, whose nature is my very life-breath; hear this hymn of a thousand names of mine, which destroys the enemy that is worldly existence.

Om. Of this *Śrīdhūmāvatīsahasranāmastotra*, Pippalāda is the seer (*ṛṣi*), the *paṅkti* is the meter (*chanda*), Dhūmāvatī is the deity (*devatā*), and its application (*viniyoga*) is in recitation for the subjugation of enemies.
Dhūmā, Dhūmavatī, Dhūmā, and she who is devoted to the inhalation of smoke; Dhautā, whose speech is purified, Dhāmnī, and she who dwells in Dhūmeśvara. || 3 ||
She is infinite and of infinite forms, having the nature of the letter 'A';
she is the primordial one, the giver of bliss, and has the form of the letter 'Ā', while she is Indra in the form of the letter 'I'.
She bestows wealth, grain, purpose, speech, and gifts; she grants fame, dharma, and what is dear and desired.
She is the abode of fortune, grace, and devotion, residing upon the mountain of the home.
She who causes delusion to Rāma, Rāvaṇa, and Sugrīva; she who is dear to Hanumān;
she who knows the Vedas, Śāstras, and Purāṇas; and she whose very form is astrology and prosody. (6)
She is beautiful with the charm of her cleverness, bestowing delight, love, and satisfaction;
she whose seat is the lotus, whose face is like nectar, who possesses a moon-like smile, and whose countenance is radiant with a gentle laugh.
She is clever, possessed of beautiful hair, the joyful bestower of the four aims of life, an art, the sustainer of time, steadfast, the upholder, and a giver of wealth.
Hīrā possesses the luster of a diamond; she has large, fawn-like eyes;
she is the supreme one who removes hypocrisy, delusion, anger, greed, attachment, and hatred.
She who acts for the welfare of Narada, the beautiful one, who is enchanting with the bliss of Rama,
who removes yoga, enjoyment, anger, and greed, and who is saluted by Hara.
She bestows gifts, honor, knowledge, honor, drink, song, and happiness;
she is the treasury of elephants, cattle, horses, and foot-soldiers; she grants prosperity and destroys all that is unwholesome.
She who is both existence and non-existence, likewise the child-like, the giver of boons, the beloved of Hara;
she who fears the destruction of the *bhaga*, the garland, the jasmine, and she whose heart is struck by the palm-clap.
She who speaks fondly of the net, the tail, the plowshare, and the skull;
she who is rich in the Karañja tree, virtuous conduct, and Guñjā berries; and she who dwells in the mango sprout. || 13 ||
Residing in the jackfruit tree, devoted to the jackfruit tree, the mistress of the household of the Lord of the jackfruit tree;
the purifier, the source of purification, full, with all desires fulfilled. || 14 ||
She is the pure one, the essence of purity, the ancient one, and the beautiful goddess of old;
she is the supreme mistress, the consort of the transcendent, the shoreless, the supreme self, and the supreme enchantress.

She is the illusion of the world, the creator of the world, the glory of the world, and composed of the world; she is the Mother, the Victorious One, the Consort, the Conqueror, and the bestower of victory upon the Jina. 16.
Kīrti bestows knowledge, meditation, and honor; she is the sovereign of charity.
Kāvya possesses the knowledge of grammar and bestows wisdom and insight. (17)
She is consciousness, the giver of victory through wisdom, the wise one, worshipped by the wise;
she is the worshipful one among the high and the low, the bestower of boons, the one who has gone beyond, the autumnal goddess, and the one who removes fear.
Dāriṇī, Devadūtī, Madanā, Madanāmadā, Paramajñānagamyā, Ṣareśī, Paragā, and Parā. (19)
She is sacrifice, the giver of sacrifice, the auspicious one who performs the work of the knowledge of sacrifice;
she is the radiant, the seeker of purity, and the crusher of the demon Niśumbha.
Śāmbhavī, the consort of Śambhu, the wife of Śambhu, the one of auspicious countenance; Śāṅkarī, she who is worshipped by Śaṅkara, Sandhyā, and she whose dharma is as pure as the twilight.
She is the slayer of enemies, the destroyer of foes, the giver of victory over enemies, and the annihilator of adversaries;
she belongs to Śiva, she is absorbed in Śiva, she is the mountain, and she is eternally beloved by the King of Mountains.
She is the night, the Śavarī woman, Śambhu, rich in nectar, and the dweller in the celestial palace;
she possesses qualities, is the embodiment of virtue, is full of dignity, and is Bhairavī whose roar is heroic.

She is fair-limbed, fair-bodied, and Gaurī; she is heavy with dignity, the Guru, and the embodiment of the essence of the cow, Gavya; she is the very nature of bliss arising from the qualities (guṇānanda). || 24 ||
She is the giver of hosts and troops, she who is to be multiplied by virtues, she whose qualities are desired for their weight;
she is the mother of the Gaṇas, worshipped by the Gaṇas, and the destroyer of ten million hosts.
Durgā, the slayer of the wicked, the bestower of joy upon the virtuous, the giver of heaven and liberation, the donor, the humble, and she who is compassionate toward the distressed. (26)
Difficult to look upon, difficult to approach, and difficult to endure, she is the destroyer of all distress; possessing a white, pale, and black luster, she bestows time and destroys time.
She who performs divine play through her actions, she whose nature is playful, she who destroys both dharma and adharma;
she who is fair-complexioned, she who bestows honor, she who grants the Veda, she who bestows the hosts of attendants, and she who is fond of song. || 28 ||
Gangā, Bhāgīrathī, Bhaṅgā, Bhagā, the increaser of good fortune, Bhavānī, the destroyer of worldly existence, Bhairavī, who is equal to Bhairava. (29)
She is Bhīmā, Bhīmaravā, Bhaimī, and the bestower of terrible bliss;
she is the refuge, the protection, the pacifier, the moon-like one, and the destroyer of the Śaṅkha demon. || 30 ||
She is the possessor of qualities, the performer of virtuous deeds, the one who bestows both love and its opposite;
she is the enchantress of people and the giver of joy to the world. || 31 ||
Jitā, Jāyā, Vijayā, and Vijayā who bestows victory;
Kāmā, Kālī, Karālāsyā, Kharvā, Khañjā, Kharā, and Gadā.
Garvā, Garutmatī, Dharmā, Ghargharā, Ghoranādinī, Carācarī, Carārādhyā, Chinā, and Chinnamanorathā. || 33 ||

Chinnamastā, Jayā, Jāpyā, Jagajjāyā, and Jharjharī; she who begins with the letter Jha, the sound Jhīṣkṛti, the commentary (Ṭīkā), the axe (Ṭaṅkā), and she who resounds with the ringing of the axe (Ṭaṅkāra).
She is the firm one, the crest-jewel of the great lords, the sound of the *ṭhaṭhaṭhāṅkāra* and the *ḍhuṇḍhura*;
she is the *ḍhuṇḍhītārā*, the one who has crossed over the ocean, and she who stands upon the palm tree, destroying delusion.
Thakārā, Thakarā, Dātrī, Dīpā, Dīpavināśinī; Dhanyā, Dhanā, Dhanavatī, Narmadā, and Narmamodinī. || 36 ||
Padmā, Padmāvatī, Pītā, Sphāntā, Phūtkārakāriṇī, Phullā, Brahmamayī, Brāhmī, and the bestower of the bliss of Brahman. || 37 ||
She who is to be propitiated by worldly existence, the presiding deity over existence, the one with a skull-mark on her forehead, she who moves slowly, the intoxicating one,
she whose glance is like wine, Yaśodā, and she who is worshipped by Yama.

She who belongs to Yama, she who is delightful, she whose form is Rāma, the enchanting one, the graceful one, the creeper, the mistress of Laṅkā, the bestower of speech, she who is to be spoken of, and she who always dwells in the hermitage. (39)
She is weary and has the form of the letter Śa; she has the letter Ṣa as her harsh vehicle.
She has the form of the Sahya mountain, she is blissful, and she is the female deer who takes the form of Hari. || 40 ||
She who is to be propitiated by Śiva; she who is pleased by the love for Mount Bālavaṅga;
she who brings about the destruction of the night; she whose nature consists of the vowels beginning with 'a'.
Kālikā, Kālamūrti, Kalahā, Kalahapriyā, Śivā, Śandāyinī, Saumyā, and Śatrunigrahakāriṇī. || 42 ||
Bhavānī, Bhavamūrti, Śarvāṇī, Sarvamaṅgalā, Śatruvidrāviṇī, Śaivī, and Śumbhāsuravināśinī. || 43 ||

She whose form is the mantra of the syllable *dhak*, who is gratified by the seed-syllable *dhūm*, who is praised by the Lord of Wealth, who is steadfast, whose form is the earth, and who possesses the earth. || 44 ||
Carviṇī, Candrapūjyā, Chandorūpā, Chaṭāvatī, Chāyā, Chāyāvatī, Svacchā, Chedinī, Medinī, and Kṣamā. || 45 ||
She who causes prosperity, she who increases [fortune], she worthy of worship, the mother of the Vedas, praised by the wise;
she who is the stream, the possessor of streams, the blessed one, and devoted to the gift of dharma. || 46 ||
She is proud, worthy of worship by her gurus, a bestower of knowledge, and endowed with virtues;
she is righteous, the very embodiment of dharma, and devoted to the sound of the bell.
She resounds with the ringing of bells, she is whirling, she is the one who has whirled, and she possesses a terrible form;
she is the destroyer of the Kali age, the messenger of Kali, the one worshipped by Kali, and the beloved of Kali.
She who destroys Time, the Black One, the giver of poetic inspiration, she whose form is Time;
she who rains, the giver of rain, the rain itself, and the one who wards off excessive rain. || 49 ||
The destroyer, the slayer, the ghoṇṭā fruit, the killer, she of solid form;
she whose seed-syllable is *dhūm*, she who rejoices in the recitation of *dhūm*, she who is gratified by the recitation of the *dhūm* seed-syllable. || 50 ||
She is intent on the recitation of the seed-syllable *dhūṃ*, devoted to the seed-syllable *dhūṃ*;
she rejoices in the sound *dhūṃ*, she is the smoke-colored one, the giver of wealth, and proud of her riches.
Padmāvatī, Padmamālā, she who is worshipped by the one born from a lotus; the boundless, the fulfiller, the full, she who is saluted by the Full Moon. || 52 ||

She is the giver of fruit, the enjoyer of fruit, the one possessing fruit, and the bestower of fruit; she is the one who utters the sound "phūt," the attainer of fruit, the enjoyer of fruit, and she is endowed with fruit.
Delighting in obstructions, she is the one who crosses to the further shore of the ocean of waters;
she is pale-hued, with smoky eyes, possessing smoke-colored eyes, and having a smoke-colored form.
She is policy and the very nature of policy; she knows policy and is skilled in statesmanship.
She is the Savior and the form of salvation, devoted to the knowledge of ultimate reality.
She is the gross one, the one whose lower lip is gross, the sustainer, the dweller in the highest station; (p.
293) she is the gross one stationed on the lotus-foot, she who has fallen from her place, yet remains established in the dry land.
She who withers, she who is beautiful, she who is cool, she who drinks cold water;
she who moves like a parrot, she who possesses a conch, she who is pure, and she who is the destroyer of the demon Śaṅkha. || 57 ||
She who is the night, she who is worshiped by the night, she who is fully adored by the Lord of Night;
she who is awakened during the night, she who is worthy, the Yoginī, saluted by the yogis. || 58 ||
She is served by the host of Yoginīs; she is a Yoginī perfected through yoga;
she is devoted to and intent upon the path of yoga; she follows the path of yoga. || 59 ||
She is the embodiment of yoga, united with yoga, and saluted by the Lord of the Night;
she is beyond the reach of the unqualified, a female yoginī, a warrior, and skilled in the art of battle.
She who delights in the path of battle, she who dwells in the field of combat;
she who is perfected, the sovereign of the perfected, perfection itself, and she who resides in the abode of perfection.
She is the way of the Siddhas, the delight of the Siddhas, the perfected one, and the bringer of the final goal;
she is accessible to the Siddhas, worshipped by the Siddhas, saluted by the Siddhas, and the bestower of perfect success.
She is the accomplisher, she who delights in accomplishment, she who is to be accomplished, and she who effects accomplishment;
she is that which is to be accomplished, she who accomplishes what is to be accomplished, and she who shines beautifully amidst the assembly of those to be accomplished.
She is virtuous, of a virtuous nature, and the bestower of a lineage of the virtuous;
she is worthy of worship by the virtuous, worthy of salutation by the virtuous, and ever intent upon beholding the virtuous.
She is well-beheld by the virtuous, well-inquired after by the virtuous, and intent upon nourishing the virtuous;
she is characterized by purity, perfected through purity, to be cultivated by those of pure nature, and the source of happiness.

She who increases the strength of beings, she who is peaceful, whose mind gladdens beings, she who possesses the knowledge of beings, she who is the science of beings, and she who effects the spiritual realization of beings. 66.
She increases the strength of beings, she brings about the success of beings, and her mind is perfected by the power of beings;
she is of beautiful form, of lovely body, and with charming, flickering eyes.
She is the one who conceals, whose resolve is concealment, whose discourse is concealment;
she is fond of forbearance, stubborn, delighted by force, her discourse is forceful, and her exertion is through force.
She whose actions are forceful, whose nature is forceful, who is devoted to forceful deeds, who delights in forceful enjoyment, and who loves the pleasure of forceful compulsion. (69)
She who pierces through force, she who is dear to the heart, she whose news is pleasant to the heart, she who is beloved by Hari;
she who is golden-hued, she with the eyes of a doe, and she who devours the flesh of the deer.
She has eyes like a deer's, feet like a deer's, and she bestows joy upon the herds of does;
she is the destroyer of the herds of does and the nourisher of the does.

She is devoted to the hunt for the deer, yet she is the foremost bestower of honor upon the deer; she is the distressed one, appearing in a wretched form, the scorched one, the one who drives away [evil], and the giver of wealth. (72)
She dwells on Mount Draviṇa, she is the one who causes things to flow, she is endowed with wealth;
she is long, she has long strides, she is visible, she is beautiful to behold, and her form is firm. || 73 ||
Firm, with a mind free from hatred, she is the destroyer of the wicked, the hater, and those who harbor enmity;
she is faultless, yet she is joined with the destruction of faults and the eradication of evil enemies.
She is the remover of the distress of the gods, the destroyer of the hosts of wicked daityas, the slayer of evil dānavas, and the annihilator of malevolent daityas. || 75 ||
The goddess who bestows life upon the deities, the destroyer of the gods' misfortune;
she is to be served by the leader of actors, the dancer, and the beloved of dancers. 76.
She is the science of drama, the creator of drama, the soundless one, and the producer of sound;
she is ever-new, ever-fresh, the novel one, and the wearer of new garments.
Adorned with new garments, new garlands, and new ornaments;
she who speaks the syllable "Na," she who is to be bowed to, and she who is decorated with fresh finery. || 78 ||
She is the lowly path, the low ground, and the destination of those who travel the lowly path;
she is to be served by the Lord, devoted to the Lord, and the bestower of bliss upon the Lord. || 79 ||
Bowing with a graceful gait, she was the leader who spoke words of cause;
though a woman situated among women, she was a woman who stood apart from women, O sinless one.
She is the delight of women, worthy of being propitiated by men, and she reveals the name of Nara.
She is Rati, beloved of Rati, delightful, full of love for Rati, and the bestower of Rati. || 81 ||
She is to be worshipped as abiding in the locus of delight, bestowing the joy of passion;
she is the embodiment of delight, whose meditation is delight, and who sustains the nectar of the path of delight.
She is the great delight of the ocean of passion, she who sports in the ocean of passion;
she is praised by Rati and Kānta, the sovereign, and the protector of the lunar mansions. || 83 ||
She is formless and pure form; she is beautiful and proud of her beauty; endowed with beauty and youth, Ramāvatī is a mass of loveliness. || 84 ||
She who obstructs, she who is wrathful, she who is enraged, she who is hindered by anger, she who bestows essence;
she who gladdens, she who is pleased with passion, she who is intoxicated by honey, she who bestows honey. 85.

She who drinks intoxicants, she who is meditated upon by those who drink intoxicants, she who protects the lives of those who drink intoxicants, she who bestows the bliss of drinking intoxicants, and she who is gratified by the love of those who drink intoxicants. || 86 ||

Delighting in the drinking of wine, intoxicated, and habituated to the practice of drinking wine; she is intoxication itself, impassioned by intoxication, and gladdened by the drinking of wine. || 87 ||
She is satisfied by the drinking of wine, she is enchanted by the drinking of wine;
she is the innocent one whose mind is wine, she is the drinker of honey-wine, and the giver of wine. 88.
She whose constant bliss is the gift of honey-wine, who delights in drinking honey-wine, who is intoxicating, who bestows joy, who is joyful, and whose mind is full of delight. (89)
She is the maker of sweetmeats, the giver of joy, and the bringer of auspicious delight;
she is satisfied by the offering of sweetmeats and capable of receiving them.
Enraged by the loss of sweetmeats, yet delighted by the acquisition of sweetmeats;
a consumer of flesh, a devourer of flesh, and one who rejoices in the eating of flesh. || 91 ||
She who delights supremely in the cooking of meat, who dwells in the kitchen for cooking meat, who tastes fish and meat, and who is endowed with the five things beginning with the letter 'ma'. (92)
Mudrā is accompanied by Mudrā; she is the Mother, possessed of great delusion, and high-minded.
She is Mudrikā, joined with Mudrikā, and characterized by the form of Mudrikā. || 93 ||
Adorned with a seal-ring, Mādrī dwells upon Mount Mandara;
she is to be served by Mount Mandara and resides on Mount Mandara. || 94 ||
She whose lotus feet are to be meditated upon by Indra, who dwells in the Mandara forest, who resides in the stable,
who is gentle, the destroyer of death, and the immeasurable slayer of Māra.
The Great Plague, the pacifier of the Great Plague, she who dwells upon corpses;
she whose food consists of the flesh of corpses, and who resides in the cremation ground as her abode. || 96 ||
Delighted by the accomplishment in the cremation ground, she dwells in a cremation ground abode;
her bedchamber is the cremation ground, and she is smeared with the ashes of the cremation ground. || 97 ||
Her body is formidable with the ashes of the cremation ground; she makes her dwelling in the cremation ground.
She is the pacifier, worshipped by Yama, and praised by the hymns of Yama. || 98 ||
Content with the conduct of tranquility, dwelling in the house of tranquility, the mistress of tranquility, peace itself, she is worshipped by peaceful and virtuous people. || 99 ||
She is devoted to peaceful worship, she is peaceful, she delights in the light of the peaceful abode;
she is to be worshipped peacefully, she is to be venerated peacefully, and she sustains the nectar of the peaceful planets.
She is of peaceful form, endowed with peace, possessing the pure radiance of a tranquil moon;
she is stainless, immaculate, yet withered, a jasmine flower dwelling in a thicket. 101.

She who delights in the *mālatī* flower, she who is worshipped with the *mālatī* flower; she who is most fierce, she who is great, she who is of middle stature, and she who dwells in the Middle Country. 102.
Delighting in the middle path, she is the creator of the middle path;
she is the middle one, whose joy is centered, and who is filled with middling love.
Clad in variegated garments upon her middle limbs, she is weary at the waist yet exceedingly exalted;
she is worshipped by Mahendra and saluted by Mahendra. || 104 ||
She is endowed with the skill of Indra’s net, she is the creator of Indra’s net;
she is honored by Mahendra, yet she is free from pride, standing in the midst of a multitude of proud women.

She who delights the minds of proud women, she who brings about the destruction of pride, she who attracts the proud, she who is liberation, she who bestows liberation, and she who grants perfect liberation. (106)
She who causes aversion to liberation, she who creates value, she who takes away value;
she who is stainless, she who is joined with the root, she who possesses roots, and she who is the mantra of the root.

She who is worthy of worship through the root mantra, she who delights in the offering of the root mantra, she who establishes the root mantra, and she who brings great joy to the root mantra. || 108 ||
She whose face is pleased by the root mantra, who is worshipped with the root mantra, who is the bringer of the root mantra, and who has performed worship with the root mantra. (109)
Her soul delighted by the root-mantra, she is the root-vidyā that removes impurity;
she is both knowledge and ignorance, residing in the banyan tree and dwelling within the banyan tree.
She made her dwelling in the banyan tree, was devoted to the worship of the banyan, was deeply pleased by the worship of the banyan, and longed for the sight of the banyan. || 111 ||

She is the joy arising from the worship of the banyan tree, she who increases the worship of the banyan tree; she is the self-controlled one, she who is worshipped by those who lack self-control, and she who possesses the mantras for subjugation.
She who is delighted by subjugation, she who bestows the siddhi of subjugation;
she who is the child-like (baṭuka), she who is worshipped by children, and she who gives food to children. || 113 ||
She is devoted to the worship of Baṭuka, she is worthy of worship, she is the one who increases the worship of Baṭuka;
she is the creator of bliss for Baṭuka and the protector of Baṭuka’s life-force. || 114 ||
She bestows the worship of Baṭuka, she is boundless, she is the wife of Pāriṇa, and she is dear to Pārvatī;
she has made her dwelling on a mountain peak and is worshipped by the Lord of Mountains.

She is worthy of worship by the Lord of Pārvatī, she bestows joy upon the Lord of Pārvatī, she resides within the intellect of the Lord of Pārvatī, and she is the enchantress of the Lord of Pārvatī. || 116 ||
She is to be worshipped by the twice-born of the mountains, she who dwells on the mountain, the one who carries across;
she is Padmalā, Padminī, Padmā, adorned with a garland of lotuses.
She whose feet are marked by the lotus-born [Brahmā], whose head is adorned with a garland of lotuses,
whose pair of feet is worshipped by the lotus-born, and who is the daughter of the ocean holding a lotus in her hand.
She who goes to the further shore of the ocean of milk is celebrated as Pāthodhi;
she is purified by crossing the ocean of milk, yet she is nourished by the water of a mere puddle.
Her movement is like that of the purifying wind, submerged in the waters within a pond;
she drinks the milk, bestows the clouds, and longs for water to drink. 120.
Adorned with garlands of lotuses and decorated with garlands of severed heads;
she who possesses a shaven head, the slayer of those with shaven heads, she who is herself shaven-headed, and she who is beautified by severed heads. || 121 ||
Adorned with jewels, with a jeweled neck, and resplendent with a garland of gems;
she is great delusion, great wrath, great illusion, and the great battle. (122)
She is human, worthy of worship by humans, and the increaser of Manu’s lineage;
she is the destroyer of monasteries, the shatterer of monasteries, and the one who takes away the wealth of monasteries.
Possessing great wrath, she is the deluded one who destroys the enemies of the deluded;
she is the eater of pāṭhīna fish, the full one, who sports with a complete necklace.
Her radiance is like the fire of universal destruction; she has the form of the fire of universal destruction.
She is submerged in the ocean of universal destruction and sports within the ocean of universal destruction.
Born from the great dissolution, she is the cause of the great dissolution;
she delights in the great dissolution and accomplishes the great dissolution.
She is the great sacrifice of the great dissolution, she who delights in the great dissolution;
she is the cutter, the fierce one with severed heads, the severed one, and she who seeks the welfare of those who have grown anew from what was severed.
She who cuts down enemies, she who is concealed, she who grinds, she who causes grinding;
she who is the mark, she who is worshipped by hundreds of thousands, she who is perceived, and she who is endowed with auspicious marks.
She is endowed with a hundred thousand weapons, the discharger of a hundred thousand arrows;
she is devoted to the worship of a hundred thousand, herself unperceivable, and the shatterer of a hundred thousand bows.
She is endowed with a hundred thousand bows, she is the bearer of a hundred thousand bows;
she is the abode of a hundred thousand divine sports, she is unattainable [by the unworthy], and she dwells in the house of lac.
She who is intent on the desire for the *lakṣa*, she who is fickle, she who is worshipped with offerings of a *lakṣa*;
she who perceives the worlds, she who is honored by the world, and she who effects the protection of the world. || 131 ||
She whose lotus feet are worshipped by the world, she who causes delusion to the world, Lalitā, she who is cherished by her attendants, and she who effects the destruction of the world. 132.

She who performs the divine play in this world, she who causes the manifestation of the light of the worlds, she who effects the purification of the elements, she who protects the elements, and she who gratifies the elements. || 133 ||
She is joined with the army of spirits (bhūta), surrounded by a host of spirits;
she is the mistress of bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, and others, and is worshipped by the bhūtas. || 134 ||
She is the Ḍākinī and Śākinī who causes the sound of the ḍiṇḍima drum;
she is satisfied by the ḍamaru drum and other instruments, and she performs with the ḍamaru drum and other such sounds. || 135 ||
She who utters the sound *huṃ*, the Hotṛ priestess, the one who causes lamentation, she who seeks the sacrificial offering;
she who laughs, she who causes laughter, she who delights in laughter, and she who speaks with force. || 136 ||
She who laughs with a loud, piercing laugh; she who creates commentaries;
she who possesses a spear; she who is pierced by a spear; she who is a coin; and she who bestows gold equal in weight to a single coin.
She is the wielder of the ṭaṅka-weapon, enriched with the letter ṭa, the one who effects the destruction of enemies;
she is the severed, the form of the moment (truṭi), and the one who causes doubt regarding the moment. || 138 ||
Thirsty, exhausted by thirst, emaciated by hunger, overwhelmed by hunger, she who carves out eyes, seeking alms, and devouring her enemies. (139)
The longing one, the procuress, the cruel one, she who dwells in the house of the procuress;
she who is worshipped by ten million procuresses, she who follows the path of the procuress-lineage. || 140 ||
She is the protector of the guild of courtesans, the guardian of the lineage of courtesans; she is the maiden enveloped by the noose of Time, and she is fond of the worship of Kumārī. 141.
Kaumudī, delighted by the moonlight, endowed with a compassionate gaze, skilled in the performance of festive rites, she dwells in the chamber of wonder. || 142 ||
Wearing the feathers of a crow, guarding like a crow, surrounded by crows;
having the form of a chariot marked with a crow, she is stationed upon a chariot marked with a crow. || 143 ||
Kākinī, who has the gaze of a crow and bestows the eating of crows;
the mother of crows, born from the womb of a crow, adorned by the circle of crows. || 144 ||
Constantly habituated to the sight of crows, her dwelling crowded with crows, her body and other limbs fixed in the meditation on crows, she was covered in filth. 145.
The wealthy one, worthy of being served by the lord of wealth, the one who effects the cutting off of wealth;
the one who is free from worldly toil, whose form is free from toil, and the slayer of Dhūmralocana. || 146 ||
She who utters the sound "dhūṃ," she who is worshipped with the smoke-mantra, the destroyer of unrighteousness;
she who is smoke-colored, smoke-eyed, and the slayer of the demon Dhūmrākṣa. || 147 ||

Satisfied by the recitation of the *dhūm* seed-syllable, with her mind intent on the recitation of the *dhūm* seed-syllable, worthy of worship through the recitation of the *dhūm* seed-syllable, she is the performer of the recitation of the *dhūm* seed-syllable. || 148 ||
She who draws in the seed of the dust, she who is bold, she who is the subduer, she whose mind is courageous;
she who scatters dust, and she who wears her braided hair enveloped in dust. || 149 ||
She who is enriched by the rosary of the *dhūm* seed-syllable, she who is the ender of those who revile the *dhūm* syllable;
she who hates unrighteousness, she who protects righteousness, and she who is gratified by righteousness. || 150 ||
She who causes the pillar of streams, the clever one, she who sports in the flow of waters;
she whose mantra-syllables are *dhāṃ dhīṃ dhūṃ dhaiṃ*, she whose very form is *dhauṃ dhaḥ svāhā*.
She who is worshipped by the earth, the invincible, she who effects the cutting of grain,
she who censures [the wicked], she who is honored by the wise, and she who dwells in the garden of the celestial abode.
She is the giver of the garden of celestial abodes, she is profusely covered with the pollen of those abodes,
she possesses a great sound, she is fragrant with incense, and she rejoices in the aroma of incense.
Exceedingly delighted by the offering of incense, she who delights in the gift of incense;
she who is worshipped by the hosts of fisherwomen, and she who bestows boons upon the fisherwomen. || 154 ||
She stands in the midst of the assembly of fisherwomen; she dwells in the abode of the fisherwomen;
she is the protector of the assembly of fisherwomen; and she is gratified by the assembly of fisherwomen. || 155 ||
She is the giver of wealth to the fisherwoman and the protector of the fisherwoman’s life;
she is the nurse of the Lord, worshipped by the Creator, and she has her abode in the dhātrī tree.
She is the one who honors the *dhātrī* tree and the one who causes the planting of the *dhātrī*;
she is devoted to the practice of smoking incense and bestows what is desired upon those devoted to smoking incense. (157)
She who delights in the act of inhaling smoke, she who causes the raining down of smoke,
she who is pleased by hearing the word "dhanya," and she who cuts through the people who utter the sound "dhundhu."
She who bestows the desired [boons] upon Dhundhukārin, she who grants supreme liberation to Dhundhukārin;
she whose form is worshipped by Dhundhukārin, she who dwells within the mind of Dhundhukārin. || 159 ||
She who desires the welfare of Dhundhukārin, she who seeks what is beneficial for Dhundhukārin;
she who utters the sound "dhindhi-māra," she who meditates, she who is attainable through meditation, and she who seeks wealth. || 160 ||
The cow, fond of her calf; the sustainer; she of terrible form;
the goddess who protects the earth; the one who causes the dissolution of the earth. || 161 ||
She possesses a splendor equal to that of all the clouds and the daughter of the mountain (Pārvatī);
she is the presiding deity of wealth, the attainment of riches, and the increaser of both wealth and grain.
She is the attractor of wealth, the bringer of wealth,
the cutter away of wealth, devoid of wealth, and yet dear to wealth.
Endowed with an abundance of increasing wealth, they were devoted to the giving of riches. || 164 ||
Delighted by wealth, nourished by wealth, she performs acts of charity and study;
she is the protector of wealth, whose very life is wealth, and who always brings joy through wealth. 165.
The slayer of enemies, mounted upon a corpse, the performer of the destruction of foes;
she who delights in the injury of the enemy faction, and the destroyer of the enemy faction. || 166 ||
She is the shadow that severs the necks of enemies, the one who shatters the tracks of foes;
she is the irresistible taker of the lives of enemies and the one who effects their total uprooting.

She is the frustrator of the enemy's undertakings, the destroyer of the enemy along with his followers, the cutter down of the enemy's lineage together with its branches, and the giver of dwellings to her foes. || 168 ||

She is the destroyer of all enemies, along with their limbs, weapons, and all their prosperity; she is the burner of the bodies and dwellings of all enemies, together with their limbs and weapons. || 169 ||
Thus, this thousand-name hymn of the one whose form is smoke—whosoever should recite it in a deserted dwelling during deep darkness with a restrained mind, [attains success]. (170)
Indeed, one who is filled with the fragrance of wine and devoted to the meditation upon the Goddess—his enemy goes to destruction, even if that enemy is equal to Śakra himself. || 171 ||
This great hymn called the Thousand Names, which removes the bonds of existence, is meritorious and dear to Dhūmāvatī; it has issued forth from my mouth. (172)
Whether one recites it or even hears it, one shall become a slayer of enemies;
however, O beloved of my life, this should not be given to the disciple of another nor to one who lacks devotion.
This supreme secret, which is very difficult for those of wicked mind to obtain, should be given to a devoted disciple who is intent on devotion to the Goddess. (174)
Thus ends the complete *Dhūmāvatīsahasranāmastotra*.
Thus ends the Dhūmāvatī Tantra within the Śāktapramoda.
Composed and compiled by the sovereign King Śrī Rājādeva-nandana Siṃha Bahādura, the lord of the capital of Śiva-Hara and the possessor of glory.
The eighth Tantra, the Bagalāmukhī-tantra, contained within the Śāktapramoda.
This has been edited by Paṇḍita Śrī Raghurāja Dubejī, a descendant of the aforementioned royal preceptor.
Printed and published by Śrī Kṛṣṇadāsātmaja Khemarāja at his own Śrī Veṅkaṭeśvara Press.
Bombei. Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa.
The Delight of the Śāktas.
Now, the Bagalāmukhī Tantra; now, the meditation on Bagalāmukhī:
Seated upon a lion-throne atop a jeweled altar in a pavilion of gems within the middle of the ocean of nectar, she is of a deep yellow complexion.
I bow to the Goddess whose limbs are adorned with yellow garments, ornaments, and garlands, who holds a mallet and has swallowed her enemies. || 1 ||

I bow to the goddess who, with her left hand, seizes the tip of her tongue and crushes her enemies, while with her right hand she strikes them with a mace; she is adorned with yellow garments and possesses two arms. (2)
(p. 304) Now, the extraction of the yantra:
a triangle, a hexagon, a circle, an eight-petaled lotus, accompanied by a city of walls (bhūpura).
Now, the extraction of the mantra:
The Praṇava, then Sthiramāyā, and thereafter Bagalāmukhi.
At the end of that, [one should utter] the word "vācāmukha" for the sake of all wicked beings.
Then, the two words "stambhaya" (paralyze) and "jihvām kīlaya" (nail the tongue) [should be recited].
Having first destroyed the intellect, one should then draw a firm illusion.
And one should write the syllable Oṃ again, with the word Svāhā at the end.
The thirty-six-syllable vidyā is considered to be the bestower of all prosperity.
Now the mantra: Oṃ hlīṃ, O Bagalāmukhī, paralyze the speech and mouths of all the wicked; pin the tongue, pin it! Destroy the intellect! Hlīṃ oṃ svāhā.
Now, regarding the procedure for worship:
having performed the morning rites up to the regulation of breath (*prāṇāyāma*), one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the seers and other elements.
For example: "Salutation to Nārada, the seer (*ṛṣi*), on the head; salutation to the *triṣṭubh* meter (*chandas*), on the mouth; [salutation] to [the deity], on the heart."
Salutation to the deity Bagalāmukhī at the secret place; salutation to the seed-syllable *hlīṃ* at the genitals;

salutation to the power (*śakti*) *svāhā* at the two feet. Then, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*): Nārada as the seer (*ṛṣi*) on the head, the *triṣṭubh* meter in the mouth, and the goddess Śrī-Bagalāmukhī in the heart.
The seed-syllable *hlīṃ* is in the secret place, while the power *svāhā* is in the two feet. Then follow the ritual assignments (*nyāsa*) for the hands and the limbs.
Oṃ hlīṃ, salutation to the two thumbs; (p. 305) Bagalāmukhī, svāhā to the two index fingers;
vaṣaṭ to the two middle fingers for all the wicked; paralyze speech and the mouth!
With the two ring fingers: *hūṃ*. With the two little fingers: *jihvāṃ kīlaya kīlaya vauṣaṭ*.
With the palms and backs of the hands: *oṃ svāhā buddhiṃ nāśaya hlī phaṭ*.
Thus [it is applied] to the heart and other [limbs]. And likewise in the *Divyatantra*: "In the case of the twin arrows, [the mantra is formed] with the seven special syllables."
Born from Manu, one should perform the *karāṅganyāsa* (hand and limb assignment) on the tips of the fingers and the palms. Then, at the end of the root mantra:

"I worship the *śrīpādukā* of Bagalāmukhī, the pervader of the *ātmatattva*," [one worships] in the *mūlādhāra*; at the end of the root mantra: "Bagalāmukhī, the pervader of the *vidyātattva*... [and so forth].

I worship the Śrīpādukā on the head; at the end of the root mantra, "Śivatattvavyāpinī Bagalāmukhī, I worship the Śrīpādukā on all limbs. And then: on the crown of the head, the forehead, the two eyes, the two ears, the two cheeks, the two nostrils, the two lips, the perimeter of the mouth, and the right shoulder.
One should then place [the mantras] on the left elbow, the wrist, the base of the fingers, the throat, the two breasts, the heart,
the navel, the hips, the region of the genitals, the left shoulder, the elbow, the wrist, and the base of the fingers;
and likewise on the right and left thighs, the knees, the ankles, and the bases of the toes.
Having sequentially assigned the syllables of the mantra according to the ritual rule, one should meditate; next is the meditation.
In the center,
seated upon a lion-throne on a jeweled altar within a gem-studded pavilion in the midst of the ocean of wine,
I meditate upon the Goddess, whose complexion is deep yellow, her limbs adorned with yellow garments, ornaments, and garlands.

I bow to the two-armed goddess, who wears yellow garments, who holds the tongue of her enemy with a mallet in her hand, who seizes the tip of the tongue with her left hand while crushing her foes, and who strikes them with a mace in her right hand. Having meditated thus and worshipped her mentally, [one should proceed].
One should begin the external worship (*bāhyapūjā*). In that regard, first is the placement of the *arghya* water. As follows:

Having fashioned a square measuring eight finger-breadths, one should worship the elephant-faced [deity] in the corners starting from the northeast and in the directions starting from the east, using flowers, unbroken grains (*akṣata*), and red sandalwood, with the mantra "Oṃ Gaṇapataye Namaḥ. Then, one should fill the *arghya* vessel with that [liquid] or with honey. Thereafter, three times...

Having worshipped with the *vidyā*, one should perform the placement of the limbs (*aṅganyāsa*). Then, having displayed the cow-mudrā (*dhenumudrā*) and the womb-mudrā (*yonimudrā*), one should sprinkle oneself and the articles of worship with that water. Then, reciting the root mantra: "Oṃ, obeisance to the lotus-seat of the foundational power (*ādhāraśakti-kamalāsana*). Likewise: "Obeisance to the lotus-seat of power (*śakti-padmāsana*)."
Having meditated as before and having invoked [the deity] upon the seat, one should perform the six-limbed assignment (*ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*).

Then, having displayed the mudrās, one should worship the maṇḍala in front with the six-limbed [mantra]. Then, having consecrated it with the root mantra and having displayed the *dhenu* and *yoni* mudrās—

Having cast the three *bindus* upon the face with the principles (*tattvas*) of the Self, Knowledge, and Śiva, one should satisfy Gaṅgāmukhī, together with her limbs and attendants, by means of the union of the index finger and the thumb. Then, having worshipped her with offerings as available, one should begin the worship of the enclosure (*āvaraṇa-pūjā*). In the six corners, in the east: *oṃ subhagāyai namaḥ*.
Thus, in the southeast, [offerings] to Bhagasarpiṇī; in the northeast, to Bhagavāhā; in the west, to Bhagasiddhā; in the southwest, to Bhagapātinī; and in the northwest, to Bhagamālinī.
Then, on the petals of the eight-petaled lotus, Brāhmī and the others are to be worshipped. At the tips of the petals: *Oṃ jayāyai namaḥ*.

...to Vijayā, Ajitā, Aparājitā, Stambhinī, Jambhinī, Mohinī, and Ākarṣiṇī. Then, at the doors, [one should offer] "Oṃ, obeisance to Bhairava. Outside of that, one should worship Indra and the others, as well as the vajra and the other weapons. Then, having offered incense and other articles with the root mantra, one should perform recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity.

Having formed the *triśūla-mudrā* and offered three handfuls of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*), one should display the *yoni-mudrā* to the Goddess. Then, one should offer the sacrificial oblation (*bali*) to Bhairava. Thereafter, one should complete the ritual up to the dismissal (*visarjana*). For this [mantra], the preliminary practice (*puraścaraṇa*) consists of one hundred thousand recitations (*lakṣajapa*). And so it is said:
Having put on yellow garments, he stood facing the eastern direction.

One should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times with a rosary of turmeric knots, remaining constantly devoted to celibacy, pure, and intent on meditation. One should also perform the fire-oblation (*homa*) with *priyaṅgu* flowers and yellow flowers.
Now, the hymn of praise (*stotra*).

Oṃ. Of this *Śrī-Bagalāmukhī-stotra*, Nārada is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Śrī-Bagalāmukhī is the deity (*devatā*), and the application (*viniyoga*) is for the purpose of paralyzing the speech, mouths, feet, and intellects of those who are hostile toward me.
In the center, seated upon a lion-throne on a jeweled altar within a pavilion of gems over an ocean of nectar, she is of a deep yellow complexion,
her limbs adorned with yellow garments, ornaments, and garlands.
I worship the Goddess, who holds the tongue of her enemy like a mallet.
I worship the Goddess who, with her left hand, holds the tip of her tongue and crushes her enemies, and with her right hand, strikes them with a mace;
she is adorned in yellow garments and possesses two arms.
I meditate upon Bagalāmukhī, whose beautiful cheeks are radiant with swinging golden earrings,
whose face possesses a moon-like orb with the luster of a shimmering golden campaka flower,
and whose tip of the tongue flickers as she seizes the throats of her enemies struck down by her mace.
Which paralyzes speech, mind, and face. || 3 ||
Seated upon a corpse-throne atop a lion-throne set within a pavilion of beautiful, shimmering red lotuses in the midst of the ocean of nectar;
her golden-hued body crushes the tongues of her enemies, while her mace whirls about.
For one who meditates thus upon the dissolution of delusions, all calamities immediately go to their destruction. || 4 ||

O Goddess, the practitioner who, for the sake of worshipping Your lotus feet, places handfuls of yellow flowers with devotion in his left hand while reciting the mantra of beautiful syllables, and then,
intent on meditation upon the pedestal, [projects] the seed-syllable by means of breath-retention (kumbhaka);
A king should remember this [mantra] against one who has an enemy’s face; by its power, there shall arise instantly a paralysis of speech and heart.
The disputant becomes mute, the king becomes a pauper, the fire becomes cold, the angry man becomes pacified, the wicked man becomes virtuous, and the swift follower becomes lame.

O Śrī Nityā Vagalāmukhī, you who are ever auspicious, homage be to you daily: by being constrained by your discipline, the proud are humbled and the all-knowing are rendered as if dull-witted. || 6 ||
Your mantra is indeed the destroyer of adversaries; your hymn is purifying; your yantra is the restrainer of disputants and the victorious, wondrous [weapon] over the three worlds.
O Mother Śrī Bagalāmukhī, for that person who possesses your charming name upon their lips, by the utterance of your name—
In the assembly, there shall be a paralysis of speech for the disputants. || 7 ||
It is the subduer of the wicked, the pacifier of fierce obstacles, the dispeller of poverty, the destroyer of the fear of kings, and the attractor of the hearts of fawn-eyed women;
it is the sole abode of good fortune for those who possess equal vision.
O Mother, may your form, which is filled with compassion and is the nectar that slays death, manifest before me. 8.
O Mother, shatter the faces of my adversaries and pierce their tongues; O Brāhmī, destroy their intellect quickly and paralyze their fierce movements.
O fair-limbed Goddess clad in yellow garments, crush the enemies with your sharp mace.
O Goddess whose eyes are filled with compassion for those who bow before you, remove the flood of obstacles from our throats. || 9 ||
O Mother Bhairavī, Bhadrakālī, Vijayā, Vārāhī, O refuge of the universe! O Śrīvidyā, Samayā, Maheśī, Bagalā, Kāmeśī, Rāmā, Ramā!
O Mātaṅgī, O Tripurā, O you who are higher than the highest, O bestower of heaven and liberation; I am your servant, come for refuge—O Sovereign of the Universe, protect me with compassion! (10)

In a violent encounter with a band of thieves, at the time of striking with weapons, in captivity, in the midst of water, in a debate on spells, in a dispute, when the king is enraged, at the time of a divine ordeal, or during the night;
whether for subjugation, for paralyzing, at the time of slaying an enemy, or in a solitary forest—(p. 308).
Whether walking or standing, if a wise person recites this at the three times of day, they shall swiftly attain Śiva. || 11 ||
Whoever constantly recites this purifying hymn of the Goddess here with devotion, having likewise worn this yantra upon their arm, hand, or neck— whether in battle or at home—
even hostile kings, elephants blinded by rut, serpents, lions, and the like shall surely flee from them.
The hosts of enemies are utterly deluded; Fortune is stable and the supernatural powers are perfected.

O Tvaritā! You are supreme knowledge, the mother of the three worlds, the destroyer of the flood of obstacles, the one who effects the attraction of women, and the increaser of the bliss of the three realms.
You are the one who performs the eradication of the wicked, the bestower of delusion upon the minds of men, and the Bhairavī who pins down the tongue.
Just as the mantra beginning with "Brahma" is victorious. || 13 ||

O Supreme Goddess, whatever has been performed as the armor of recitation (japa-sannāha) for the sake of subduing the wicked— by that man on this earth, knowledge, fortune, all prosperity, longevity, sons, grandsons, the attainment of universal sovereignty, honor, enjoyment, mastery, health, and happiness have been obtained. || 14 || Whatever has been performed as the armor of recitation, O Supreme Goddess, it is for the purpose of suppressing the wicked.
Therefore, accept it; salutations be unto you. || 15 ||
This is renowned as the Brahmāstra, famous throughout the three worlds;
it should be given to one devoted to the guru, but must not be given to just anyone.
One should meditate upon her whose face is like that of a tawny cow, who wears yellow garments, has two arms and three eyes, whose body is radiant, and who holds a stone and a mallet in her hands.
Thus ends the Bagalāmukhī Stotra from the Rudrayāmala.

Then Girijā, having bowed to Śiva— the abode of the Kailāsa mountain, the purifier of the city [of the senses], the tranquil one with three eyes, who bestows prosperity, and whose armor rests upon his left side— questions him regarding that armor.
O Goddess Śrī Bagalāmukhī, who are like a forest fire to the grove of enemy hosts, please now tell me with affection the mantra released from Your bow.
Śrī Śaṅkara said:
O Goddess, beloved of Śiva, listen to this great mantra of the Goddess which bestows prosperity,
is endowed with armor, grants all happiness, confers sovereignty, and bestows liberation.
O Tārā, O consort of Rudra; O Virañci’s wife, O beloved of Viṣṇu; O Kāmayuk, O beautiful-faced Śrī Bagalāmukhī—grant me a pair [of success] for the destruction of my enemies. || 2 ||

"Grant me sovereign powers and the [highest] state; quickly accomplish the task desired by my mind. This is the mantra ending with the Consort of Śiva (Umā), the Beloved of Fire (Svāhā), and the Couple (Yugma).
Kaṃsāri’s son (Kṛṣṇa) is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), Aparā is the power (*śakti*), and Vāṇī is likewise the bolt (*kīla*) in this glorious [mantra].
The meter is Virāṭ, accompanied by the Bhairava year. || 3 ||
For the certain attainment of one's own desired goal or that of another,
for the certain destruction of various incurable great diseases, and for the acquisition of valor—
one should meditate upon the venerable Bagalānanā and recite the excellent mantra a thousand times with long breaths.
With the seed-syllables honored by Rudra, joined with the six groups, [one should perform] the dissolution of the limbs. [Meditation:]
Seated upon a golden throne, three-eyed, radiant with yellow garments,
her body possessing a golden luster, wearing a crown of the moon and adorned with a garland of *campaka* flowers;
she holds in her hands a mallet, a noose, and a bound tongue.

I meditate upon her who bears [the severed head], whose limbs are covered with ornaments, who has the face of Bagalāmukhī, and who paralyzes the three worlds. Oṃ. Of this *kavaca* (armour) mantra of the venerable *Brahmāstra* of Śrī Bagalāmukhī, Bhairava is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Virāṭ is the metre (*chandas*), Śrī Bagalāmukhī is the deity (*devatā*), *klīṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), and *aiṃ* is the power (*śakti*).
Śrīṃ is the *kīlaka*; the *viniyoga* is for the sake of accomplishing the desired and cherished goals of both myself and others.

Salutation to the sage Bhairava on the head; salutation to the Virāṭ meter on the mouth; salutation to the deity Bagalāmukhī on the heart; salutation to the seed-syllable *klīṃ* on the private parts; salutation to the power (*śakti*) *aiṃ* on the feet;
salutation to the pin (*kīlaka*) *śrīṃ* on all limbs; *oṃ hrāḥ*.

Oṃ, *namaḥ* to the two thumbs; Oṃ *hrīṃ*, *namaḥ* to the two index fingers; Oṃ *hrūṃ*, *namaḥ* to the two middle fingers; Oṃ *hraim*, *namaḥ* to the two ring fingers; Oṃ *hrauṃ*, *namaḥ* to the two little fingers; Oṃ *hraḥ*, *namaḥ* to the palms and backs of the hands.
Oṃ hrāḥ, homage to the heart; Oṃ hrīṃ, svāhā to the head; Oṃ hrūḥ, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock; Oṃ hraiṃ, huṃ to the armor; Oṃ hrauṃ, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes; Oṃ hraḥ, phaṭ to the weapon.

The extraction of the mantra (mantroddhāra) is as follows: Oṃ hrāḥ aiṃ śrīṃ klīṃ, O Śrī Bagalāmukhī, destroy my enemies, destroy them; grant me sovereign powers, grant them; quickly accomplish the work desired by my mind, accomplish it, accomplish it; hrīṃ svāhā.
May *oṃ hrīṃ aiṃ śrīṃ klīṃ* protect my head;
may the vocative address protect the forehead, O Śrī Bagalānanā! (1)
May Śruti protect my two enemies; may Nāśā destroy the pair [of my foes].
May she always protect my cheeks, and may Aiśvaryā protect the extremity, my head. (2)
May He grant us freedom from duality; may He always protect my tongue; may He quickly protect my speech; may He protect the region of our throat; and may He protect our desired root of the arms. (3)
May she who accomplishes all tasks protect my two hands;
likewise, may Svāhā, joined with Māyā, protect my heart at all times. (4)
May Bagalāmukhī, who possesses forty-eight additional staffs, always grant me protection everywhere—in my home and in the forest. 5.
May the mantra known as the Brahmāstra protect me in all limbs and at all joints;
may the King of Mantras always provide protection for me at all times. (6)
Oṃ Hrīṃ! May she protect my navel region; may Bagalā protect my waist. May Mukhī protect my two hips, and may she protect my genitals and pair of testicles.
May the five-syllabled [mantra] protect my knees from all malevolent beings;
likewise, may the supreme goddess of six syllables protect my speech, my face, and my feet.
May Bagalā, the deluder of enemies, always protect my pair of shanks;
may the three syllables of the word "stambhaya" (paralyze) protect my back.
May the tongue protect me; may the two syllables protect my ankles with the mantra "kīlaya";
may [the syllable] always protect the upper part of my feet, and may [the syllable] protect the soles of my feet.
May the word *vināśaya* protect my feet, and may the nails of my toes protect me;
may the seed-syllable *hrīṃ* always protect my intellect, senses, and speech. (11)
May the Praṇava protect my entire body; may Svāhā protect my body hairs.
May Brāhmī protect the eastern petal, and Viṣṇuvallabhā the southeast.
May Māheśī protect [me] in the south; may Cāmuṇḍā protect in the southwest;
may Kaumārī protect in the west; and may Aparājitā protect in the northwest. || 13 ||
May Vārāhī protect me in the north; may Nārasiṃhī protect me in the northeast. May Mahālakṣmī protect me above, and may Śāradā protect me in the netherworld.
Thus may the eight Śaktis, equipped with weapons and their respective vehicles, protect [me];
may the Lord of the Fort (Gaṇanāyaka) protect me at the royal gate and in the great fortress. || 15 ||
May Bhairava always protect [us] in the cremation ground and in the midst of water;
[they are] two-armed, clad in red garments, and adorned with all ornaments. (16)
"May the Yoginīs always protect me in the great forest.
Thus, O Goddess, this most wonderful armor has been told to you. (17)
The one named Śrīviśvavijaya bestows the glory of fame and victory; a sonless man obtains a son who is wise, heroic, and long-lived for a hundred years. (18)
By reciting this armor, one who is destitute obtains wealth;
having muttered the king of mantras and meditated upon Śrī Bagalāmukhī. (19)
For he who recites this armor-mantra at night according to the rule, whatever desire he may wish for—whether it be achievable or unachievable on this earth—[shall be attained]. (20)
Accompanied by a Śakti, having meditated upon the Guru and drunk wine at night, one who belongs to the lineage of Śaṅkara attains each respective desire within seven nights. || 21 ||
O Goddess, for one who recites this armor (*kavaca*), nothing remains unattainable. Having meditated upon it, one should mutter the mantra a thousand times and then recite the armor.
Within three nights, one brings [the enemy] under control; death follows—of this there is no doubt.
Having drawn the image of the enemy with turmeric on a board measuring one hundred tālas, || 23 ||
Having written that name on the heart and meditated upon it, one should recite the mantra a thousand times every day for twenty-one days. 24.
Having recited [the mantra], one should chant the armor-verse (*kavaca*) twenty-four times; the enemy will be paralyzed—of this there is no doubt.
In dispute one shall achieve victory over Vijayanta, and in battle one shall obtain triumph;
moreover, there is no fear in the cremation ground by the power of this armor. (26)
O Maheśvarī, having consecrated fresh butter with mantras, one should give it to women;
even a barren woman shall give birth to a son endowed with the power of knowledge.
Having taken charcoal from a cremation ground on a Tuesday night during the transit of Saturn,
and having touched it with water used for washing the feet, one should draw [the diagram] with an iron stylus.
One should draw the form of the enemy on the ground and write his name in one's heart;
placing one's hand upon his heart, one should employ the armor-mantra (kavaca) according to the lunar day and the weekday.
Having meditated, O King of Mantras, one should recite [the mantra] diligently for nine nights;
he will die from the burning fever on the tenth day, without a doubt.
One should write this hymn with the eight fragrant substances on birch bark;
a woman should wear it on her right arm, and likewise, a man on his left arm.
In battle one attains victory, and a woman shall become the mother of sons;
even weapons such as the Brahmāstra cannot harm that person.
By constantly worshipping the armor-mantra (kavaca), one obtains the fruit of worship;
one becomes equal to Bṛhaspati in wisdom or like Kubera in wealth.
To women he is like the god of love, and to his enemies he is like Yama;
the wave of his poetry shall flow like the current of the Ganges. (34)
By the grace of the Goddess, one's speech shall consist of both prose and verse;
this is said to be the *puraścaraṇa* for one thousand and eleven [recitations]. || 35 ||
If devoid of the preliminary rite (puraścaryā), this [mantra] does not bestow its fruit;
it must not be given to the disciples of others, and especially not to the wicked.
This should be given to a devoted disciple; otherwise, one may meet with death.
He who worships Bagalāmukhī without knowing this protective mantra (kavaca) [shall likewise suffer].
Even after reciting it a hundred million times, success does not arise for him.

A man endowed with a wife attains supreme perfection through one hundred thousand recitations of this mantra. O Hero, he likewise obtains the Śrīvijayā-vidyā, as well as the excellent and well-restrained Brahmāstra-mantra.
Having written it clearly upon birch bark with the finest fragrant substances, those who wear it and travel toward the city of kings indeed achieve their purpose.
The king is their slave. || 38 ||
Thus ends the Bagalāmukhī-kavaca, spoken in the dialogue between Pārvatī and Īśvara within the Viśvasāroddhāra-tantra.
Now, the Heart [Mantra]:

Oṃ. Of this Śrī Bagalāmukhī Hṛdaya Mālā Mantra, Nārada is the seer (ṛṣi), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chandas), Śrī Bagalāmukhī is the deity (devatā), Hlīṃ is the seed-syllable (bīja), Klīṃ is the power (śakti), and Ai is the kīlaka.
The ritual application (viniyoga) for the recitation is for the sake of attaining the grace and accomplishment of the auspicious Bagalāmukhī through this stake (kīlaka).
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa).

Oṃ, salutation to the sage Nārada on the head; Oṃ, salutation to the Anuṣṭubh metre on the face; Oṃ, salutation to the deity Śrī Bagalāmukhī on the heart; Oṃ, salutation to the seed-syllable Hlīṃ on the private parts; Oṃ, salutation to the power (Śakti) Klīṃ on the feet; Oṃ, salutation to the pin (Kīlaka) Aiṃ on all limbs.
Now, for the ritual placement on the hands and limbs (*karāṅganyāsa*):
*oṃ hlīṃ* to the two thumbs, *namaḥ*; *oṃ klīṃ* to the two index fingers, *namaḥ*; *oṃ aiṃ* to the two middle fingers, *namaḥ*; *oṃ hlīṃ* to the two ring fingers, *namaḥ*.
Oṃ klīṃ, salutation to the two little fingers; Oṃ aiṃ, salutation to the palms and backs of the hands.
Oṃ hlīṃ, salutation to the heart; Oṃ klīṃ, svāhā to the head; Oṃ aiṃ, vaṣaṭ to the tuft of hair.
Oṃ hlīṃ, hūṃ to the armor; Oṃ klīṃ, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes; Oṃ aiṃ, phaṭ to the weapon.
Oṃ hlīṃ klīṃ aiṃ—this is the binding of the directions.
I meditate incessantly upon her who wears yellow garments, yellow garlands, and is adorned with yellow ornaments,
whose two lotus feet and throat possess a yellow luster.
Having meditated thus and performed worship.
O Bagalā, who holds a yellow conch and mace in your hands, who are anointed with yellow sandalwood paste,
grant me a boon— you who rend the hosts of enemies!
Having thus addressed [him].
Oṃ hlīṃ klīṃ aiṃ, svāhā to Bagalāmukhī, who wields a mace and sits upon a corpse-throne.
Having thus recited the mantra, one should again perform the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) of the heart and so forth as before,
and then recite the hymn of praise.
It is as follows:
I bow to the goddess Ambāgalā, adorned with yellow ornaments, the goddess whose form is composed of splendor, whose very nature is yellow radiance. || 1 ||
I worship her whose face is terrifying with a frown that shatters clouds as she whirls her mace,
who strikes fear into her formidable enemies, and who bestows auspicious fortune upon her devotee.
I take refuge in her whose face is like the full moon, who is anointed with yellow perfumes and ointments,
who is clad in yellow garments, and who is pure.
Beholding her upon the surface of the earth protecting those devotees who are intent on the yellow ritual (pītācāra) and free from obstacles, I worship Bhavānī. 4.
I salute the supreme goddess, who is worshipped by Brahmā, whose pair of feet are like yellow lotuses, who plants herself in the groves of campaka trees, and who wears a yellow crest-ornament. 5.
I worship the one whose lotus-feet are praised by Brahmā and others, whose face is adorned with golden earrings that tinkle beautifully as she moves,
and whose yellow moon-like countenance is radiant; those who recite the pure mantra while holding a bright yellow garland of safety (abhaya) attain victory.
In battle, against enemies drenched in passion and rage, you struck down those who created enmity through force in dispute; O Mother,
you are the most venerable one, whose armlets mock the pride of foes and whose splendor eclipses the sun with its radiant light.
I take refuge in her who is most venerable, rich in the qualities of a temple of virtues, whose limbs are adorned with excellence, who is accessible to the lords of the quarters and others,
and who is enriched by the absence of worldly attributes.
Those people who, remembering their own true nature, daily recite this supreme and fierce seed-mantra throughout the worlds—
whether they be disputants, there shall be a paralysis of the mouth for their opponents, and victory quickly arises for those who speak.
Established in the perfection of meditation and devoted with love to the worship of the lotus feet of those endowed with self-knowledge,
kings— whether commoners or scholars— become like servants, filled with clarity and intent upon the Purāṇas and other sacred texts.
O Mother, we bow to you, whose lotus-feet are as lovely as gold,
who dispels the dense darkness with a body the color of blazing lightning,
and who effects the crossing over for those souls submerged in the ocean of existence.
O Mother Bagalā, you who are the refuge for all who have sought shelter, you are the subduer of suffering in this world. 11.
I remember your abode, which is a mine of blazing moonlight and jewels, its walls adorned with gems,
and which is clearly visible morning and night as it is brought forth by the foremost of the gods— Smara, Hara, Hari, Indra, and the Moon.
He is of a supremely yellow form, dwelling on the island of jewels that has been thoroughly cultivated. || 12 ||
O Mother, we address you by that charming name which brings delight to the ears—“Bagalā,” as it is widely known in the world, with its radiant measures and syllables.
Whether moving, standing, sitting, or even lying down, we have no fear; may that which is the highest good [be attained] in heaven.
Difficult for even the gods to obtain. || 13 ||

O Mother, may a fresh delight in the worship of Your feet arise within us every day, such that we who bow down must look toward Your grace at every moment; O Mother, may this not be in vain through our overflowing devotion, but rather, may You grant us true devotion upon this earth.
The Blessed One has bestowed abundant [blessings] upon us.
O Blessed One, quickly paralyze the speech of all my enemies; O you who are like a wedge, nail their tongues. Quickly destroy the resolute intellects of the wicked and make my many tasks successful.
O Mother, you who possess true compassion, be gracious! 15.
May Bagalā, holding a mace in her hand, go to the abode of my enemies as a female ghost; having swiftly slain them there out of rage,
she shall again burn their wealth, clothing, grain, and dwellings.
May you return quickly to your own abode. || 16 ||
With her hand busy pressing down the tongues of her enemies, again striking them with her mace, protecting her sons,
surrounded by hosts of prostrate gods, and clad in yellow garments— Please perform the ritual service (sevā) of that Goddess Durgā, who is the protector of those who have surrendered.
We bow to her who has the luster of a blue lotus, who wears yellow garments, and who is the end of the power of the many. || 17 ||
To those who offer a mass of devotion through mind, speech, and body— [the Goddess], moist with manifested compassion,
speaks thus as she pleases: "Wealth, then abundant grain, the increase of sons, grandsons, and so forth— what is there that is not obtained from these?"
It must certainly be given in this manner. || 18 ||
