She is firmly established in the Vedas, she ordains the rites according to the rules,
she possesses a conch, she wears bracelets of conchs, she is adorned with a garland of conchs, and she is the bringer of peace.
Śaṅkhapātrā, Śinī, she whose voice is like a conch and whose throat is a conch,
Śaśī, Śabarī, Śambarī, Śambhu, she whose hair is like that of Śambhu, and she who wields arrows and swords.
She who dwells among corpses, who possesses hawks, who is dark-complexioned, whose limbs are dark, and whose eyes are dark;
she who stays in the cremation ground, who is the cremation ground itself, and who adorns the site of the cremation ground.
She is tranquility and the destroyer of tranquility; she who possesses the conch, she who is the essence of the conch;
she is peace and the bestower of peace; she is the Residue, she who is called the Residue, and she who reclines upon the Residue (Śeṣa).
She is the intellect that withers the serpent Śeṣa, the embodiment of valor, the arrow of valor,
the one who bestows curses, the remover of curses, the path for those whose hopes for curses have perished, and she is Sadāśivā.
She who possesses horns, she who feeds on the flesh of horned animals, the benefactress, the daughter of Śaṅkara, the auspicious one;
she who dwells in corpses, she who devours corpses, the peaceful one, she whose ears are like a corpse, and she whose belly is a corpse.
She who possesses the splendor of a corpse-like *śiṃśapā* tree, she who lies upon a corpse, she who dwells in the cremation ground,
she who has a corpse as her ear-ring, she who is the nourishment for the devotees of Śiva, and she who is cooled by the one who consumes cold things (the Moon).
She whose girdle is a corpse, whose beauty is a corpse, who wears a garland of corpses, whose form is that of a corpse;
she who flows, who is constricted, who is power, who is Śantanu, and who bestows a corpse.
She is the river Sindhu, the Sarasvatī, the beauty of the Sindhu, and the one with a beautiful countenance;
she is the virtuous one, the bestower of perfection, the perfected one, and the Siddha-Sarasvatī.
The perfection of continuity bestows the attainment of all desires;
she is a rival wife to the nectar of immortality, full of flavor, essential, the producer of Sarasvatī, and like ambrosia.
She who eats wine and meat, she who is to be propitiated at all times,
she who possesses equanimity, she who bestows peace, she who is the boundary, she who causes delusion, and she who has equal vision.
She is the essence of tranquility, the boundary of the self, the mother of the Vedas, endowed with all methods, and the ever-present reality;
she is the sacrificial rite, the essence of the sacrifice, the supreme light, the source of all sounds, and the one who dwells within all things.
She is ever-pure, virtuous, harmonious, and accompanied by her attendants;
she is a female swan with the gait of a swan, a female swan radiant as a swan, and clad in a shimmering robe white as a swan.
Halinī, Hālinī, Hālā, Halaśrī, Haravallabhā; she is indeed Halā, Halavatī, Helā, and the increaser of joy.
She is the slayer, the destroyer, the one who eats the horses, the one who has slain the "hā-hā" sounds, and she who causes the end of destruction.
She is the maker of the sound "haṃ," the utterance of "haṃ," the sound "haṅ," and she who is both the "hī-hī-hā-hā" and the non-beneficial as well as the beneficial.
Hīti, Hemapradā, Hārārāviṇī, Harirasammatā,
Horā, Hotrī, Holikā, Homā, Homahavir, and Haviḥ.
She is tawny, with tawny eyes, a dweller on the Himālaya;
she has a protruding belly, long ears, a hanging tongue, and a pendulous body.
She is Līlā, Līlāvatī, Lolā, Lalanā, Lalitā, and Latā;
she has beautiful eyes, is alluring, possesses tremulous glances, and is the abode of the noble lineage.
Lapatnī, lapatī, lampā, lopāmudrā, lalantikā,
latikā, laṅghinī, laṅghā, lālimā, and laghumadhyamā.
Laghīyasī, Laghūdaryā, Lūtā, Lūtāvināśinī,
Lomaśā, Lomalambī, Lulantī, and Lulumpatī.
She who dwells upon the elephant, who steals away strength, the sovereign of the city of Laṅkā;
she who is Lakṣmī, the bestower of fortune, who is attainable, whose eyes are like lac-dye, and whose radiance is shimmering.
She is the moment, the destroyer of moments, the patient one, the forbearance itself, and the possessor of patience;
she is emaciated, slender-waisted, the source of security, and the noble lady who wears linen garments.
She is destruction, the cause of destruction, milk, the giver of milk, the ocean of milk;
she is the bringer of security, the destroyer of decay, the maker of decay, the night, and the wound.
Kṣudrikā, Kṣudrikākṣudrā, Kṣutkṣamā, and Kṣīṇapātakā—
this is the thousand names of the Mother Sumukhī, which bestows spiritual accomplishments (siddhi).
Whoever recites this constantly with a disciplined mind shall indeed become Maheśvara;
even one who recites it daily despite improper conduct shall, if poor, become wealthy.
O Goddess, one who is mute shall become a lord of speech; one who is diseased shall attain freedom from disease;
and one desiring a son shall obtain a son, renowned throughout the three worlds.
May even a barren woman give birth to a son who resembles a learned teacher;
may truth prevail in many ways, and may cows yield abundant milk.
Kings will bow at his feet like manifest smiles;
his enemies perish even when merely remembered in his mind.
By the mere sight [of him], men and women alike become subject to his power;
he himself becomes a hero, the creator and destroyer—of this there is no doubt.
Whatever desire one may wish for, that one certainly attains;
for such a person there is no misfortune, nor is there any sorrow whatsoever.
The supreme practitioner, a fearless hero, who recites this excellent hymn ten times while alone at a crossroads at midnight, [attains success].
Whatever task is contemplated by the mind, its accomplishment is certain;
provided that one never recites a mantra without the Thousand Names.
Success does not arise for him even through hundreds of ritual manuals (kalpas),
if he always recites [the mantra] on a Tuesday, in a cremation ground, or at midday.

He who, seated upon his seat, recites this at midnight while afflicted by disease, shall become one who has accomplished all his tasks, and he shall be the creator and the remover of the ailments of men in this world.
If one is free from fear, one immediately attains freedom from disease.
At midnight or in a cremation ground on a Saturday, one should chant the mantra;
one should then perform the recitation ten times, each time one thousand and eight times.
For then Śivā herself indeed proceeds with this Thousand Names.
In the form of a great wind, she howls with the terrifying cry of a jackal;
if there should be no fear from that, then the words "Give [me]! will arise.
Then Caṇḍikā herself accepts the animal sacrifice;
having granted a boon as desired, the auspicious Śivā departs with a gracious countenance.
Having written [the mantra] on a birch-bark leaf with yellow pigment, agallochum, musk, camphor, sandalwood, and saffron on an excellent day;

When there is an auspicious conjunction of stars, having performed the ritual involving the movement of air and having carried out the procedure for the descent [of the deity], one should hold [the vessel] in the right hand.
When the practitioner, having conquered his senses, recites the Thousand Names while holding gold on his neck,
that man who is angry shall die at that moment.
No fear of wicked beasts of prey arises anywhere;
this is protection for children and even for pregnant women, O beloved.
Delusion, paralysis, attraction, killing, and expulsion—
these indeed arise for the practitioner through the wearing of the yantra.
If [the deity] stands upon a banner painted with blue cloth,
then even a fierce enemy army is surely destroyed.
If one should wear this great ash, consecrated by mantra, upon the forehead,
living beings will become his servants merely by the sight of it.
If even the wives of kings are rendered helpless, what need be said of other city women?
By drinking water consecrated with this mantra for one month, one shall become a great poet.
He becomes a wise and great debater; of this there is no doubt.
One should recite the hymn ten thousand times for the sake of accomplishing the preliminary rite (puraścaraṇa).
Having offered oblations according to the prescribed rite with lotuses smeared with the three sweets and numbering one-tenth [of the total], Kamalā herself comes to that abode accompanied by Vāṇī.
The mantra becomes unbarred, the fair-faced one becomes truly fair-faced;
merit becomes infinite, and demerit shall go to destruction.
Whatever fruit may arise from bathing at sacred fords such as Puṣkara,
a living being obtains that same fruit by reciting the hymn of Sumukhī.
(349) This has been told to you in secret, O fair-faced one, as my very own essence; O Goddess, do not reveal it, if you wish to attain accomplishment.
Through its manifestation, success is attained; she who was angry becomes gracious-faced.
There is nothing superior to this in the world for bestowing success upon living beings here.
I bow to the illustrious Sumukhī, whose face is gracious, whose countenance is like the orb of the full moon,
whose head is marked with vermilion, and who wears a pearl necklace shimmering with the intoxication of honey;
she is teaching the dark-complexioned Śyāmāṅka, who holds the tips of his hands joined in reverence.
Adorned with clusters of Śuka and Guñjā flowers, she was compassionate, her braid-like creeper left unbound.
Thus ends the hymn of the thousand names of Mātaṅgī in the Uttarakhaṇḍa of the venerable Nandyāvartatantra.
Thus ends the Mātaṅgītantra within the Śāktapramoda.
Composed and compiled by His Majesty King Śrī Rājā Deva Nandana Siṃha Bahādura, the Lord of the Sovereign Capital of Śiva-Hara.
The tenth tantra within the Śāktapramoda, titled the Kamalātmikā-tantra.
This has been edited by the learned Śrī Raghurāja Dubejī, a descendant of the aforementioned royal preceptor.
Printed and published by Khemarāja, son of Śrī Kṛṣṇadāsa,
at his own Śrī Veṅkaṭeśvara Press.
Bombei.
Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa. Now begins the Śāktapramoda.
Now, the *Kamalātmikā-tantra*.
Now, the meditation on Kamalātmikā:
[one should meditate on her] resembling gold in luster, borne by four elephants that resemble the Snowy Mountain (Himavat).

I worship her who dwells upon the lotus, resplendent with a crown, her hips graced by a silken garment, and bearing in her hands a boon-bestowing gesture and a pair of lotuses; she who is being sprinkled by golden jars of nectar uplifted by the gods. || 1 ||
(p. 354) Now, regarding the extraction of the yantra:
one should draw a lotus mandala with eight petals for a yantra whose ritual procedure has not been previously described.
Therein is a six-cornered pericarp, adorned with four gates.

Now follows the extraction of the mantra: having first written "Tāram" (Om), followed by "Paramalamamalam" (the supremely stainless), then another seed-syllable, "Vāgbhavam" (Aiṃ), preceded by the seed-syllables of "Lajjā" (Hrīṃ) and "Śrī" (Śrīṃ), and finally, after that, the "Aṅkāma-bīja" (the seed-syllable of the desire that subjugates).

The mantra of Ramā is declared as follows: first the syllable *hsauḥ*, then the word *yojanīyam* well joined, then the word *jagat* preceded by *prasūtyā*, ending in the suffix *ṅe*; this entire sequence is uttered with the *anuvidas*.
Now the mantra:
Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ hsauḥ, obeisance to the Mother of the Universe.
Now, the procedure for worship:

having performed the rites beginning with the morning duties up to the placement of the throne (pīṭhanyāsa), one should place the powers of the throne (pīṭhaśaktis) and the mantra of the throne upon the eastern filaments and the center of the heart-lotus.

Oṃ, obeisance to Vibhūti; likewise, obeisance to Unnati, Kānti, Sṛṣṭi, Kīrti, Sannati, Vyuṣṭi, Utkṛṣṭi, and Ṛddhi. Then, having assigned the seat with "Obeisance to the venerable Kamalāsana," one should perform the assignment of the seers (*ṛṣi*) and so forth: "Obeisance to Bhṛgu, the seer, on the head"; [on the] mouth...
Salutation to the *nicṛt* metre; salutation to the deity Śrī in the heart. Then one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) on the hands and limbs:
*śrāṃ* to the two thumbs, *namaḥ*; *śrīṃ* to the two index fingers, *svāhā*;
*śrūṃ* to the two middle fingers, *vaṣaṭ*, and so forth.
In this manner, one should perform the placement [of mantras] with "śrī-hṛdayāya namaḥ" and so forth; and likewise, it is stated in the Nibandha:
One should fashion the limbs with the seed-syllable of Ramā joined with a long vowel. Then follows the meditation.
In her splendor resembling gold,
she bears the Goddess Śrī— who is being sprinkled by four elephants like the Himālaya mountains with golden jars of nectar lifted by their trunks—
and who holds in her hands a boon-bestowing lotus pair and the gesture of fearlessness.
I bow to her who dwells upon the lotus, whose limbs are radiant with a crown and whose hips are graced by a silken garment.
Having meditated thus and worshipped with mental offerings, one should perform the installation of the conch (*śaṅkhasthāpana*).

Then, having performed the worship of the pedestal (*pīṭhapūjā*), one should perform the worship of the pedestal-mantra (*pīṭhamantra*) and its end, beginning with *vibhūti* (ashes) and so forth, upon the filaments and in the center. Having meditated again, [one performs] the invocation (*āvāhana*) and the subsequent rites.
Having performed the rites up to the offering of five handfuls of flowers, one should begin the worship of the protective enclosures (āvaraṇapūjā).

Having worshipped with "Oṃ *śrīṃ* hṛdayāya namaḥ" and so forth at the filaments starting from the fire-quarter (Agni), in the center, and in the cardinal directions; then, in the petals of the directions starting from the east: "Oṃ vāsudevāya namaḥ," likewise "saṅkarṣaṇāya," "pradyumnāya," and "aniruddhāya. In the intermediate petals: "Oṃ damakāya."

Oṃ salilāya, Oṃ guggulāya, Oṃ kuraṇṭakāya. Then, to the right of the Goddess: Oṃ śaṅkhanidhaye namaḥ; likewise, Oṃ vasudhāyai namaḥ. To the left: Oṃ padmanidhaye, Oṃ vasumatyai. On the tips of the petals, starting from the east: Oṃ balākāyai namaḥ; likewise, Oṃ vimalāyai.
One should worship Vanamālikā and Bibhīṣikā, and outside of that, Indra and the other deities, as well as the thunderbolt and the other weapons.
Then one should complete the ritual actions from the offering of incense up to the dismissal.

The preliminary practice (*puraścaraṇa*) for this consists of twelve hundred thousand recitations. Likewise, one who has received initiation and has conquered the senses should recite the mantra one million times, and [then] one thousand times more.

One should offer oblations with lotuses soaked in honey. At the conclusion of the recitation, the practitioner should offer oblations with sesame seeds soaked in honey, or the best of practitioners should offer oblations with bilva fruits, or with all three together. Thus concludes the procedure for worship.
Now, O Goddess worshipped by the three worlds, O Kamalā, beloved of Viṣṇu:
just as you are steadfast, O Kṛṣṇā, so may you be firm toward me. (1)
The Sovereign, Kamalā, Lakṣmī, the Unsteady One, Bhūti, the Beloved of Hari, Padmā, Padmālayā, she who perfectly and loftily bears the lotus, Śrī. (2)
Whoever recites these twelve names after having fully worshipped Lakṣmī, for him prosperity shall become stable, together with sons, wife, and so forth. (3)
Thus ends the Śrī Kamalātmikā Stotra.
Now, O Maheśānī, I shall proclaim the armor (*kavaca*), which grants all desires;
by the mere knowledge of which one becomes Sadāśiva himself. (1)
O Goddess of the gods, a man who merely recites the mantra of this [deity] without performing worship shall become a son of Pārvatī, proficient in all the scriptures. || 2 ||
Knowledge is always the best giver of wealth to those seeking learning; likewise, Kamalā, the beloved of Viṣṇu, should always be served by those desiring merit and wealth.

Of this armor (*kavaca*) of the four-syllabled mantra beloved of Viṣṇu, the Lord is the seer (*ṛṣi*), the *anuṣṭubh* is the meter (*chandaḥ*), Vāgbhavī is the power (*śakti*), the deity is Vāgbhavī, the seed-syllable (*bīja*) is Vāgbhava, the pin (*kīlaka*) is Lajjāramā, and the armor consists of the Kāma-bīja; may it grant me great scholarship and poetic skill.
The application is for the sake of the complete attainment of all siddhis.
May the syllable Aiṃ protect my head; may Vāgbhavī, the bestower of all accomplishments, protect me.
May Hrīṃ protect the space between my eyes, and may Śāṅkarī protect my pair of eyes.
In the tongue, in the perimeter of the mouth, in the ears, in the teeth, in the nose, in the upper and lower lips, in the row of teeth, at the root of the palate, and again in the jaw; || 5 ||
May Lakṣmī, the beloved of Viṣṇu, who is the very form of Śrī-Viṣṇu, protect me! ||6||
Pārvatī [is to be worshipped] on the pair of ears, the pair of arms, and the pair of breasts;
furthermore, in the heart, at the wrists, in the neck, and on the two sides.
Likewise on the back, in the private parts, on the left and the right,
as well as in the genitals, the hips, the navel, and again in the two shanks.
In the wheel of the knees, in the pair of feet, in the kneecaps, at the base of the toes, in the self-element, the vital breath, the power, the self, and again at the crown of the head; || 9 ||
May Vijayā protect me in my home; may Jayā always protect me;
may the Great Goddess Kāmeśī protect all my limbs, and may Sarasvatī protect me. 10.
May Tuṣṭi protect; may Mahāmāyā protect; may Utkṛṣṭi protect at all times;
may Ṛddhi, the great goddess beloved of Śambhu, protect everywhere.
May Vāgbhavī protect me always; may the consort of Hara protect me;
may the goddess Ramā protect me always; and may Māyā herself, the self-sovereign, protect me.
May Lakṣmī, the illusory power of Viṣṇu and sovereign of the gods, protect me in all my limbs;
may Śivadūtī always protect me, and may Sundarī protect me at all times. (13)
May Bhairavī protect me everywhere; may Bheruṇḍā protect me at all times. May Tvaritā protect me constantly; may Ugratārā protect me always. (14)
May Āṅkālikā protect me always; may Kālarātri protect me forever.
May Navadurgā protect me always; may Kāmākṣī protect me at all times. (15)
May the Yoginīs protect me always; may the Mudrās protect me always. May the Mothers and the hosts of Yoginīs stationed in the circle protect me always. (16)
May the Goddess of gods, Lakṣmī, the bestower of all prosperity, protect me everywhere, in all undertakings, in all actions, and at all times. (17)
Thus has this divine kavaca been told to you for the sake of all accomplishments;
it must not be spoken of here or there if one desires one's own welfare.
The Great Goddess should never reveal herself to one who is deceitful, devoid of devotion, or a slanderer; nor to one with missing limbs or with redundant limbs.
One should not show the divine [icon] to those who do not offer praise; by showing it to such, one becomes a slayer of Śiva.
However, one may show it to one of noble birth, great aspiration, and who is devoted to Durgā. (20)
One should bestow this supreme armor upon a Vaiṣṇava who is pure,
as well as upon one's own disciple who is peaceful, wealthy, and possessed of knowledge.
One should bestow the armor (kavaca), as it is said, which is endowed with all the tantras;
likewise on Saturdays and Tuesdays, using red sandalwood.
One should write the mantra, complete with all its constituent parts, using barley-meal;
having written it, one should apply the divine armor (kavaca) with auspicious, self-arisen flowers.
With one's own semen or the semen of another, combined with various fragrances, or with gorocanā, saffron, or red sandalwood; || 24 ||
On an auspicious lunar day, during a favorable yoga, on the day of the sun [Sunday], or under the asterisms of Śravaṇā, Aśvinī, Kṛttikā, Phalgunī, or Maghā; || 25 ||
On the day of Tuesday, during the conjunction of the asterism Pūrvabhādrapadā and the nakṣatra Svātī,
one should write out and recite this hymn in a temple at an auspicious moment.
And especially during the conjunction of the venerable Prīti, the Brahma-yoga, the auspicious Indrayoga, and likewise the Śukra-yoga. || 27 ||
In Kaulava, Bālava, and Vaṇija, O best of men, [one should practice] especially in an empty house, a cremation ground, or a secluded place. || 28 ||
Having first worshipped the maiden, one should worship the eternal Goddess;
one should worship the Supreme Deity with fish, meat, vegetables, and soups.
Having fed the Brāhmaṇas with ghee and other offerings, along with various utensils, and especially with cakes and soups, one should worship the Supreme Goddess. (30)
There, he should spend three days in the narrative of Akheṭaka, while reciting that Great Vidyā which was proclaimed by Śaṅkara. (31)
He obtains powers such as killing and inciting hatred; of this there is no doubt.
He shall become a son of Pārvatī, honored by all the scriptures. (32)
The Guru is the god Hara himself, and his wife is the beloved of Hara;
for him who worships them without making any distinction between them, spiritual perfection is not far off.
The mortal who here recites this with a perpetually moist inner self shall obtain whatever is ordained as the fruit of recitation;
he becomes such a one.

May that state, which for a long time was the fortune upon the crowns of kings who bowed before him due to his exalted prosperity, and the very mark of his auspicious characteristics, [attain its fulfillment]. 34.
Thus ends the Kamalātmikā-kavaca in the Viśvasāra-tantra.
Now, for the Hṛdaya [section] of the Ādyādi-Śrī-Mahālakṣmī-Hṛdaya-Mālā-Mantra: Bhārgava is the seer (ṛṣi);
Ādyādi-Śrī-Mahālakṣmī is the deity; Anuṣṭubh and various other meters are the meters; Śrī is the seed-syllable.

*Bīja* is *hrīṃ*, the *śakti* is [the same], and *aiṃ* is the *kīlaka*. The application (*viniyoga*) is for the purpose of attaining the grace and perfection of the primordial Mahālakṣmī during the recitation (*japa*).
Now, the ritual placement (*nyāsa*):
*Oṃ*, salutation to the sage Bhārgava on the head; salutation to the various meters beginning with Anuṣṭubh on the mouth;
salutation to the deity, the primordial Śrī Mahālakṣmī, on the heart; salutation to the seed-syllable *Śrīṃ*.
At the secret place: *hrīṃ śaktyai namaḥ*. At the feet: *aiṃ kīlakāya namaḥ*. On all limbs: *namaḥ*.
Now, the ritual assignment of the limbs (karanyāsa): Oṃ Śrīṃ, salutation to the two thumbs; Oṃ Hrīṃ, salutation to the two index fingers;
Oṃ Aiṃ, salutation to the two middle fingers; Oṃ Śrīṃ, salutation to the two ring fingers.
Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to the two little fingers (kaniṣṭhikā). Oṃ aiṃ, salutation to the palms and backs of the hands (karatalakarapṛṣṭha).

Oṃ śrīṃ, salutation to the heart (hṛdaya). Oṃ hrīṃ, svāhā to the head (śiras). Oṃ aiṃ, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock (śikhā). Oṃ śrīṃ, hūṃ to the armor (kavaca). Oṃ hrīṃ, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes (netratraya). Oṃ aiṃ, phaṭ to the weapon (astra).
Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ—this is the binding of the directions (digbandha).
Then, I shall meditate upon Goddess Lakṣmī, who holds two lotuses in her hands with graceful ease, and who is adorned with necklaces and anklets.
Having meditated thus and performed worship, ||

"O Lakṣmī, who holds the conch, discus, and mace in your hands, who is of radiant white complexion, and who is beautifully adorned—O bestower of all perfections, grant me boons! Having thus prayed, [one should recite]: "Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ mahālakṣmyai kamaladhāriṇyai..."
Having recited the mantra "siṃhavāhinyai svāhā" and again performed the six-limbed assignment (ṣaḍaṅganyāsa) of the heart and so forth as before, one should recite the hymn of praise.
Thus it is.
I bow to Lakṣmī, who is identical with the Supreme Śiva,
whose form is the splendor of pure gold, who is adorned with golden garments and whose limbs shine with every ornament.
I salute the primordial Śakti, the mother of all beings, who rests upon the left lap of Viṣṇu and holds a citron, a golden pitcher, and a golden lotus.
I praise the eternal Lakṣmī, the auspicious mother of good fortune,
who brings about the singular happiness that is the means for attaining the fruits of all desires.
O Goddess of gods, I remember that my mind is always impelled by you;
bearing your command upon my head, I worship the Supreme Goddess. (3)

I worship the Great Glory that bestows all prosperity and happiness, the Great Glory that brings about all auspicious fortune, the Great Glory that effects all well-being, and the Great Glory that grants wisdom. || 4 ||

I bow to the beloved of Hari, who bestows the perfection of consciousness, grants eternal happiness, produces various forms of speech and prosperity, is captivating to the mind, and bestows infinite, fragrant bliss. || 5 ||
O Sovereign of universal form, you abide within all beings as their inner witness and are the enjoyer of all;
there is no entity whatsoever that exists apart from you. O Śrī, I bow down to your lotus feet.
O Śrī, may your lotus feet, which destroy the darkness of the flood of the suffering of poverty, be present within me;
sprinkle me with your compassionate glances, which are the cause for severing the afflictions of the wretched and the distressed.
O Mother, be gracious; with a gaze moistened by the nectar of compassion, make me a dwelling for the wealth of your mercy.
O Destroyer of the sorrow within the hearts of those who bow before you, look upon me; I prostrate myself at your pair of lotus feet.
Śrīḥ || 8 ||
Salutations to Śānti, who grants refuge to those who have sought it; salutations to Kānti, the abode of desirable virtues;
salutations to Kṣānti, the cause of the destruction of misdeeds; salutations to Dhātrī.
To the bestower of abundance in wealth and grain. || 9 ||
Salutations to Śakti, who is praised by the moon-crested Lord; salutations to Rati, who is like the sister of the moon;
salutations to Bhakti, who delivers one from the ocean of worldly existence; salutations to Mati.
To the beloved of Madhusūdana. || 10 ||

Salutations to Lakṣmī, who is marked with auspicious signs; salutations to Siddhi, who is well-worshipped by Śiva and the Siddhas. Salutations to Dhṛti, the shatterer of immeasurable misfortunes; salutations to Gati.
To her who bestows the supreme state and the excellent destinies. || 11 ||
Salutations to the Goddess, who is worshipped by the hosts of gods in heaven; salutations to Bhūti (Prosperity), who destroys the afflictions of the world.
Salutations to the Giver, the beloved of the Supporter of the Earth; salutations to Puṣṭi (Nourishment).
To her who is beloved by Puruṣottama. || 12 ||
Salutations to you, the destroyer of the intense suffering of poverty; salutations to you, the remover of all fears;
salutations again and again to her who dwells upon the sacred ground of the tree of Śrī Viṣṇu; salutations to the bestower of all prosperity. 13.
Victory, victory to Lakṣmī, whose limbs are adorned with auspicious marks! Victory, victory to Padmā, who dwells in the lotus and is worthy of worship!
Victory, victory to Vidyā, who resides upon the left lap of Viṣṇu! Victory, victory!
Śrī is that which brings about all perfect prosperity. || 14 ||
Victory, victory to the Goddess, worshipped by the hosts of gods! Victory, victory to the auspicious Bhārgavī, whose form is fortune!
Victory, victory to the eternal one, to be known through stainless wisdom! Victory, victory to the Truth!
She dwells within all beings. || 15 ||
Victory, victory to the beautiful one dwelling within the womb of jewels! Victory, victory to the pure one with the luster of refined gold!
Victory, victory to the lovely one whose limbs are illuminated by radiance! Victory, victory to the peaceful one!
Come quickly, O gentle one! || 16 ||

From whom the Kalās and others, the lotus-born [Brahmā] and others, the Rudras, and the gods headed by Śakra derive their life—all those powers live only because they have attained their sovereignty from you; may that supreme life-force be yours. 17.
The Creator has inscribed this decree upon my forehead: "Having cast it within, you must write this [other thing] for the sake of attaining its fruit.
Therefore, O Goddess dwelling in the lotus, clearly bestow upon me this seal-ring which yields that inner fruit.
[She is] the indicator of all auspicious portions. || 18 ||
O Goddess Lakṣmī, granter of prosperity, just as all beings, both moving and unmoving, live by a fraction of Your power, so may You always be gracious toward me.
Just as Viṣṇu eternally established his own portion within Dhruva,
even so, O Lakṣmī, properly entrust your own portion to me.
O Goddess who bestows all happiness upon your devotees, O granter of fearlessness, make this digit placed within me firm through your effort. 21.
May the manifest digit of the splendor of the supreme state rest joyfully upon my forehead; may the beauty of Vaikuṇṭha always dwell as a digit within my two eyes;
may the digit of the fortune of Lakṣmī’s husband reside in my speech in the world of Satya; and may the glory of Śrī reside in Śvetadvīpa.
May my artistic skill dwell within my own hands. || 22 ||
May the digit of Śrī dwell eternally upon my limbs within the ocean of milk for as long as the sun and moon exist, and for as long as the Lord of Lakṣmī remains endowed with his splendor.
O primordial Śrī Mahālakṣmī, who is complete with all auspiciousness and endowed with all sovereignty, may a portion of you abide within me. (24)
May that digit of yours, which dispels the darkness of ignorance, illuminates pure knowledge, and bestows all sovereignty, abide within me. 25.
May it swiftly remove misfortune, just as the light of the sun dispels darkness;
may that digit of yours, established within me, extend my spiritual welfare.
Since the source of sovereignty and auspiciousness, which is Your own power, is deposited within me, I have therefore achieved my purpose; I am a worthy vessel for Your abiding presence.
O daughter of Bhṛgu, I am fortunate, being worthy of the fortune of your possession; through your grace I have become purified. O Mother of the World, salutations be to you! (28)
Since you purify me with your very glance, therefore come before me;
O Śrī, become my supreme state, be well-pleased with me, and enter me as Acyuta, O primordial Lakṣmī.
O Lakṣmī residing in Śrī Vaikuṇṭha, come before me;
together with Nārāyaṇa, look upon me with a glance of compassion. 30.
O Lakṣmī, residing in Satyaloka, come into my presence;
together with Vāsudeva, be gracious and become the bestower of boons. || 31 ||
O Lakṣmī dwelling on Śvetadvīpa, come quickly, O lady of virtuous vows;
O Goddess, mother of the world, accompanied by Viṣṇu, be gracious to me. 32.
O Lakṣmī, who dwells in the ocean of milk, come together with Mādhava;
look upon me constantly with the nectar of your compassionate glance. 33.
O Lakṣmī, who dwells within the womb of jewels and who consists of perfect gold, come, come hither; stay quickly before me! 34.
Be firm, O Mahālakṣmī; be immovable, O stainless one.
O Goddess Kamalā, be gracious and be of a joyful heart. (35)
O Śrīdhara, O you who are the great embodiment of prosperity, quickly extract the great treasure situated within you, display it before me, and offer it to me.
O Vasundharā, O Śrīvasudhā, O milch-cow of the earth, O you who are full of compassion!
Quickly reveal to me all that which is contained within your womb. (37)
O beloved of Viṣṇu, O you who contain jewels within, O auspicious one who bestows all fruits! Reveal, reveal the gold and other treasures situated within your womb. (38)
"O Lakṣmī, who have gone to the netherworld, come quickly before me!
I do not know your supreme form; show it to me. (39)
"Manifest yourself through the speed of the mind and come quickly before me!
O child, do not fear; protect me as Kāmaṇḍalū protects Gaurī," he said. (40)
"O Goddess dwelling within the womb of the earth, come quickly!
O Mother, I am a servant of your servants; I seek you out out of curiosity. (41)
Arise, wake up; rise up for me and awaken well!
[I give you] inexhaustible golden jars, beautifully filled with gold.
Having drawn forth my deposits and extracted them from within the earth, stand with your face uplifted before me and bring them forth from the depths of the ground.
Come into my presence out of the essence of the compassion bestowed by me;
be gracious, O Lakṣmī, who milks forth all blessings, and appear before my eyes.
Sit here, O Lakṣmī; be firm, O golden one!
Be well-established with great affection, be gracious, and be a bestower of boons.
O Goddess, having brought them here, likewise reveal the treasures to me;
today, having suddenly granted them in an instant, protect me forever.
Abide in me eternally, just as you abide in Indra and the other gods;
O Goddess Mahālakṣmī, grant me fearlessness; salutations be to you! 47.
Come hither, O Mahālakṣmī, you who possess the luster of pure gold!
Be gracious; standing before me, look upon me as I bow down. 48.
O Lakṣmī, wherever you appear as golden upon the surface of the earth, there you are present; reveal your form to me. (49)
You play in many ways upon the earth, which is filled with gold;
place your hand without delay upon my head. (50)
O Lakṣmī, who dwells in all cities, may the rise of my fortune bear fruit;
O Mahālakṣmī, be gracious to me whose desires are fulfilled. (51)
While [the king] was established in all the cities, beginning with Ayodhyā,
come forth endowed with various splendors and accompanied by an army.
Come together, come together; be well-established before me, you who are radiant with the two eyes that overflow with the essence of compassion. 53.
Abide here, O Mahālakṣmī; place your hand upon my head.
With the nectar of your compassion, sprinkle me and make me firm. (54)
O Lakṣmī, come joyfully to the entire city of Rājagṛha;
standing quickly before me today, grant me fearlessness through your grace. (55)
Out of compassion, please respectfully place your hand upon my head;
O Lakṣmī, may a portion of yourself abide within me in every royal palace.
O primordial Śrī Mahālakṣmī, who dwells upon the left lap of Viṣṇu, manifest Your form before my eyes; protect me, who have come to You for refuge. (57)
Be gracious to me, O Mahālakṣmī; be well-pleased, O Mahāśivā!
Be immovable through your affection, and remain firmly established in my home.
As long as the Vedas endure, as long as your name remains,
and as long as Viṣṇu exists— so long, O Lord, show mercy toward me.
Just as the digit of the moon increases day by day during the bright fortnight,
so may your compassion for me alone increase and grow ever greater.
Just as in the city of Vaikuṇṭha and just as in the Ocean of Milk,
so may you remain steadfastly in my abode together with Śrī Viṣṇu.
Just as you always abide in the hearts of yogis together with Viṣṇu,
so may you abide permanently in my abode together with Śrī Viṣṇu.
Just as you abide in the heart of Nārāyaṇa, and just as Nārāyaṇa abides in the lotus of your heart, so may both you and Nārāyaṇa eternally remain in my heart as well, O compassionate Śrī.
O Śrī, increase wisdom in my heart; O Śrī, increase prosperity and good fortune in my home;
O Śrī, may compassion greatly increase within me; O Śrī, increase the abundance of gold in my home.
(64) O you who are like a wish-fulfilling tree to those who take refuge in you, a cintāmaṇi gem for true devotees, and a cow of plenty—do not abandon me.
O Mother of the Universe, be well-pleased in my home, among my wives, and within the circle of my sons.
O primordial Māyā, you are the seed of the cosmic egg; you alone possess both form and formlessness.
By you are sustained the multitudes of Brahmā’s eggs; O Goddess, the conduct of Viṣṇu is wondrously yours.
Even the gods, beginning with Brahmā and Rudra, as well as the Vedas themselves, would not be able to praise your infinite majesty; how then could I, who am dull-witted, be capable of it? (67)
O Mother, O Omniscient One, please graciously accept with compassion all the words spoken by your son, whether they be well-spoken or ill-spoken. (68)
"Having gone for refuge to you, the ancients attained their goals.
Thinking thus in my mind, I go to you for refuge. (69)
"O Goddess, according to the authority of the Vedas, those who are devoted to You, who have You as their supreme goal, are infinite and eternally blissful; therefore, I go to You for refuge. (70)
Reflecting again and again upon your promise that "those devoted to me do not perish," even in some [difficult] circumstance, I sustain my life-breaths.
O Mother, I am dependent on you; your grace is upon me. O Treasure of Compassion, grant this until my desires are fully satisfied.
I am unable to live for even a single moment without your compassion;
for here, water-born creatures do not survive once they have been deprived of water.
For just as a mother, out of affection for her child, with milk flowing from her breasts, comes quickly when her calf has arrived and satisfies it with love; (74)
If I am your son and you are my mother,
then sprinkle me with the nectar from the breasts of your compassionate clouds.
Not even a trace of virtue is to be sought in me, who am an abode solely of faults;
there is no measure for my heaps of dust, my drops of rain, and my defects. (76)
I alone am the foremost among sinners, and you are the leader among the compassionate;
who else in these three worlds besides me is worthy of your mercy? (77)
If you had not been created by the Ordainer, there would be no compassion in you;
or if disease had not been created, the emergence of medicine would be in vain. (78)
"Is my elder brother compassionate toward me, or am I his elder?
Having reflected upon this, O Goddess, treasury of mercy, grant me wealth. (79)
O Mother, Father, Teacher, and auspicious destiny; you alone are the cause of my very life.
O Goddess, sole Mistress of the world, I consider nothing else to exist; you alone are everything for me, truly.

O primordial Lakṣmī, be well-pleased; you who are the sole milch-cow of pure wisdom and bliss, the destroyer of ignorance, transcending the three qualities (guṇas), and the leader of discernment—be well-pleased! 81.

May you, who remove the impurity of all dullness of speech and bestow ever-new, clear, and eloquent words, become a celestial dancer upon the tip of my tongue; and may the Goddess of Fortune dwell in my mouth. 82.
Shining amidst all prosperity, resplendent with a mass of all splendors, O beloved of Viṣṇu, may you be radiant; may the Goddess of Speech be gracious toward my eyes. (83)

O you who reveal everything, O you who bestow all purposes, O you who possess radiant beauty and are the milch-cow of compassion, O giver of gold, be gracious-faced; may the golden Śrī be pleased with my eyes. (84)
Bestower of all aims, the source of the entire world, sovereign of all, and remover of all fears;
you who are supreme over all, be gracious-faced; may the golden Śrī be pleased with my eyes. 85.
The destroyer of the entire flood of obstacles, expert in uplifting all devotees, and the bestower of infinite good fortune and happiness—may she, the golden one, be gracious before my eyes. (86)
O Goddess, be gracious to me, who am most worthy of compassion; O Sovereign of the Gods, become the protector of the hosts of deities, you who are worshipped by them!
O Mother, likewise remain ever present before my eyes, and appear together with my husband within my sight.
Suprasannā || 87 ||
"O child, do not fear; I, who grant fearlessness, have placed myself upon your head"—thus spoke she out of compassion for the wretched.
"O Mother, bestow upon me with joy your merciful glance; create here for us the auspicious seed."
O Mother, [this is] birth. || 88 ||
O Indirā, your sidelong glance here is the cow of plenty, your mind is the wish-fulfilling gem, your hand is the celestial tree, and you yourself are ever a fresh treasure-trove.
May the essence of your compassion be my elixir, and may your joy be mine every day.
The treasury of arts, which bestows the objects of various desires. || 89 ||
Just as even iron may attain the state of gold through contact with mercury, so too, O Lotus-faced One,
you bring auspiciousness even to those who are inauspicious through the touch of your sidelong glances.
Fearing the words "give" and "there is not" that enter [my ears], I delight in seeking refuge in you;
therefore, O Bestower of Fearlessness, always remain present with your husband within me.
May Your most beautiful splendor, accompanied by the wish-fulfilling jewel, remain with me through the essence of aesthetic delight and the elixir of nectar;
for thereby all moving and non-moving beings, touched by my eyes, head, hands, and feet, shall become possessed of golden bodies. (92)
O primordial Viṣṇu, you alone are the wife of the eternal Dharma; through your husband, please be present within me.
O primordial Lakṣmī, by your grace, may there be the sight of treasures for me at every step.
Whoever recites the *Ādyādilakṣmīhṛdaya* attains the sovereignty of fortune that remains unshaken until the end;
even one who is greatly impoverished becomes wealthy, and prosperity becomes firmly established within his lineage. (94)
Merely by remembering him, the beloved of Viṣṇu becomes pleased;
she swiftly grants his desires and protects him like a son.
This secret heart-mantra bestows the fruit of all desires;
a recitation of five thousand times is said to constitute the preliminary rite (puraścaraṇa). || 96 ||
Whether three times a day or at a single time, the person who, endowed with devotion, either recites or even listens to this, attains supreme glory. (97)
Having recited this Śrī-hṛdaya five times at night on a Friday dedicated to Mahālakṣmī, one shall become wealthy. (98)
If one gives food consecrated with this heart-mantra to a woman who is not pregnant, a son who is himself a lord of fortune will be born in her family. (99)
Whether by a man or a woman, when the *lakṣmī-hṛdaya-mantra* has been consecrated and water is drunk, no one of that lineage shall be born unfortunate. (100)
Whoever, with singular devotion, recites this during the festival of Rāma in the bright fortnight of the month of Āśvina,
shall obtain a golden rain by increasing the number of recitations by one each day.

He who, with a purified intellect, eats but one meal a day for one year while chanting [the mantra] seventy times, even if he be of meager fortune, shall—by the side-glance of Ramā—possess a splendor exceeding that of a hundred thousand-eyed gods. [This applies to one who has devotion to the feet of the Lord of Śrī. 102. Devotion to the feet of the Lord of Śrī...
O Mother Śrī, grant me the service of Haridāsa, unwavering single-minded devotion to the meaning of the propitious mantra, remembrance of the Guru, and an intellect characterized by pure awakening;
O Abode of Prosperity, grant sovereignty over the earth, the status of Puruṣottama, various supernatural powers, and the accomplishment of diverse goals. 103.
O Lakṣmī, grant me again and again complete fame and the enjoyment of many years.

O daughter of Bhṛgu, grant me in birth after birth the accomplishment of the goals of debate, mastery over many people, stability of youth, excellent enjoyment with women, the attainment of sons and grandsons, and the fulfillment of all aims.
O Śrī, bring about an increase of gold in my home; O Śrī, bring about an increase of prosperity and power in my home.
Now, the seed-syllable of the head.
Oṃ yaṃ haṃ kaṃ laṃ paṃ.
One should meditate upon Śrī Lakṣmī with a smiling face, possessing the brilliance of ten million rising suns,
wearing garments the color of lightning, and adorned with magnificent ornaments.
May Acyutaśrī, who holds a citron, a pair of lotuses, and a golden vessel, and who, joined by her husband, repeatedly grants me fearlessness—[protect me]. 107.
You are the guardian of the most secret of secrets; accept this recitation performed by us.
O Goddess, may accomplishment be mine, abiding within me through your grace. 108.
Thus ends the Lakṣmīhṛdayastotra in the Śrī Atharvaṇa-rahasya.
Now, the Upaniṣad:
Then Sanatkumāra, wandering through the worlds, reached the world of Puṇyacitta; having transcended those worlds, he arrived at the divine abode of Viṣṇu, accompanied by celestial hosts.
She reached a place adorned with coral railings and clusters of gems and pearls;

there she beheld Mahāmāyā, seated upon a couch, wearing garments, ornaments, and upper cloths of supreme excellence, moving through the air. And having seen the Blessed One, the Supreme Lord, the Primordial God—
With his voice faltering and his hair standing on end, he began to offer praise.
May the Goddess Śrī grant me speech; may Vaiṣṇavī grant me the mind.
May vigor, splendor, strength, and keenness of sight be mine, and may there be for me the majesty of wisdom.
"O Blessed One, by Your grace may certain wisdom arise within me.
May the divine Śrī, the primordial power of Viṣṇu and the Great Māyā, grant us auspiciousness— she,
having attained whom the Lord Ādideva himself, the knower of the high and the low, became divided threefold."
He creates, protects, and devours the three worlds;

for by attaining the power of his mere brow-glance, the lotus-born Brahmā and the other principal deities became the directors of the wheel of creation. She who is indeed the giver of boons, through her own means, is well-pleased.
Those worlds which constantly bow their heads and hearts to a thousand men bring happiness; yet not even one among them goes to an evil rebirth, for they are honored by the world.
Furthermore, he shall dwell upon the surface of the earth accompanied by great prosperity, sovereignty, sons, and grandsons.

Having worshipped the gods, the ancestors, and human beings for a hundred years with sacrifices and abundant sacrificial fees, even those great royal sages and brahmin sages go, by your grace, O Vaiṣṇava,
to the world from which there is no rebirth.
Having previously treated you with disrespect, they now consider themselves happy; yet there is no other path for one’s journey.
How much more so here, where the Blessed Lord Nārāyaṇa, the primordial God, makes you the presiding deity over all? How shall I describe you?
A thousand times I bow to you, who recite these verses upon rising early in the morning;
for those who give abundant gifts, whatever remains here of their sovereignty— which is indeed difficult for living beings to attain— [shall be theirs].
Thus ends the Kamalātmikopaniṣad.
(p. 368) Now, the Śrīsūkta:
Oṃ. O Jātavedas, bring unto me Lakṣmī, who is golden-hued, tawny, adorned with garlands of gold and silver, moon-like, and made of gold. 1.
O Jātavedas, bring to me that imperishable Lakṣmī,
in whom I may find gold, cattle, horses, and men.
I invoke the goddess Śrī, who is filled with horses, whose center is chariots, and who rejoices in the trumpeting of elephants; may the goddess Śrī be pleased with me. 3.
I invoke here Śrī, who is golden-hued, seated upon a lotus, dwelling within a golden rampart—moist, blazing, satisfied, and satisfying others. 4.
I take refuge in that Padmanemi, who is radiant with moon-like splendor, blazing with glory, the noble fortune cherished by the gods in this world; may misfortune perish for me, as I choose you. 5.
O you who possess the luster of the sun, born from asceticism, the bilva tree is your forest-king;
may its fruits, through the power of austerity, dispel all misfortune—both that which is internal and that which is external.
May the friend of the gods approach me, along with fame and this jewel;
you have appeared in this kingdom—may you grant me an increase in fame. (7)
I destroy the impurities of hunger and thirst, the eldest form of misfortune; drive away all lack of fortune and lack of prosperity from my home.

I invoke here Śrī, the mistress of all beings, who has the fragrance as her door, who is difficult to overcome, who is ever-nourished, and who bestows prosperity. May we obtain the desire of the mind and the truth of speech.
May the form of the six kinds of grain, the nourishment of food, prosperity, and glory rest within me. 10.
O Kardama, from whom all creatures have come into being, O you who are like a whirlpool of passion,
establish Śrī, my mother Padmālinī, in my family.
May the waters create unguents; O Śrī, mother of the gods, cling to me and dwell in my house. Dwell in my family, O goddess! 12.
O Jātavedas, bring to me Lakṣmī— Ārdrā, Puṣpakariṇī, Puṣṭi, Suvarṇā, Hemamālinī, Sūryā, and Hiraṇmayī.
O Jātavedas, bring to me Lakṣmī, who is Ārdrā, Yyaḥkaraṇī, Yyaṣṭī, Piṅgalā, Padmamālinī, Candrā, and Hiraṇmayī.
O Jātavedas, bring to me that imperishable Lakṣmī,
by whom I may obtain abundant gold, cattle, female slaves, horses, and male servants. (15)
One who desires prosperity, having become pure and self-restrained, should offer clarified butter daily; and one desiring prosperity should constantly recite the fifteen verses of the Śrīsūkta.
Thus ends the Śrīsūkta.
Now, the hymn of one hundred and eight names.
Śrī Śiva said:
"O fair-faced one, [herein lies] the hymn of one hundred and eight names of Kamalā."
I shall proclaim that which is indeed extremely secret; one should never reveal it.
Mahāmāyā, Mahālakṣmī, Mahāvāṇī, Maheśvarī, Mahādevī, Mahārātri, and Mahiṣāsuramardinī. || 2 ||
Kālarātri, Kuhū, Pūrṇā, Nandā and the others, Bhadrikā, Niśā, Jayā, Riktā, Mahāśakti, Devamātā, and Kṛśodarī. (3)
She is Śacī, Indrāṇī, the one praised by Śakra, the beloved of Śaṅkara,
the mother of Mahāvarāha, the destroyer of Madana, and the Earth.
The beloved of the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, who dwells upon the chest of Viṣṇu;
the sovereign of the universe, the mother of the universe, the bestower of boons, the dispeller of fear, the auspicious one.
She who holds the trident, she who holds the discus, she who holds the noose, and she who bears the conch;
she who wields the mace, she who wears a garland of severed heads, she who is Kamalā, and the abode of compassion.
Indeed, Mother Padmākṣadhāriṇī is the one who brings delight to Mahāviṣṇu;
she is the beloved of the Lord of Goloka and is worshipped by the Lord of Goloka.
The Gaṅgā at Gayā, the Yamunā, the Gomatī, the Garuḍāsanā, the Gaṇḍakī, the Sarayū, the Tāpī, the Revā, and the Payasvinī; || 8 ||
Narmadā, Kāverī, she who dwells in the region of Kedāra, Kiśorī, she who is praised by Keśava, and she who is saluted by Mahendra. || 9 ||
She is the creator of the gods beginning with Brahmā, worshipped by the Vedas;
she dwells within the midst of millions of cosmic eggs and is the creator of millions of cosmic eggs.
She whose form is the Veda, who causes the Veda to be heard, who is devoted to the Śruti and Smṛti;
she is Indirā, the daughter of the Ocean, Mātaṅgī, and the Mother of the World.
The mother of the three worlds, the embodiment of Tantra and Mantra, youthful, the destroyer of darkness, auspicious, and the refuge of all that is auspicious. || 12 ||
She is the crusher of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, the destroyer of the demon Śumbha, the remover of Niśumbha and others, the Mother worshipped by Hari and Śaṅkara. (13)
She consists of all the gods, she is everything, the protector of those who have come for refuge;
she is the worthy refuge, the consort of Śambhu, and the dweller on the banks of the Sindhu.
Delighting in the songs of the Gandharvas, she is the beloved of Govinda;
she protects the three worlds and is filled with the youthfulness that is the very essence of reality. (15)
Candrāvalī, Candramukhī, Candrikā, Candrapūjitā, Candrā, Śaśāṅkabhaginī, and Gītavādyaparāyaṇā. || 16 ||
She is the form of creation, the creator of creation, and the performer of the dissolution of creation.
Thus, O Goddess, these one hundred and eight names of Ramā have been told to you.
Having become purified at the three junctions of the day, one who recites this with a concentrated mind shall undoubtedly obtain whatever desire he may wish for. || 18 ||

The mortal who recites this hymn to the consort of Vaikuṇṭha here with supreme devotion shall be honored by the Lord of Wealth and others, and at the time of death, he will proceed to the abode of Śrī.
Thus ends the hymn of one hundred and eight names of Kamalā.
Now, the Thousand Names: Om! I invoke that auspicious Lakṣmī, who is worshipped by the three worlds. Come, come, O Goddess with lotus-eyes, whose abode is made in the lotus lake! (1)
Come, come, O Giver of Boons; behold me with your own eye!
Come, come, O Auspicious One, who consists of dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa! || 2 ||
Thus, with these true words of praise, the illustrious younger sister was extolled for her truthful nature by Candra, the Supreme Self. (3)
And Niśākara— that goddess and her brother— those two sons of the Ocean,
as soon as they were born, took refuge in Śiva and Keśava respectively.
Having addressed that ancient sage, Sanatkumāra related this history, the unsurpassed hymn of praise to Lakṣmī.
Now, how can there be liberation from such a most terrible hell of poverty in this world, so that poverty may be reduced to ashes? (6)
Sanatkumāra said: In the former Kṛta age, the blessed Brahmā, the creator of all worlds,
having performed various kinds of creation, subsequently fell into reflection.
What shall be the food of these creatures on the surface of the earth?
And how, in this state of poverty, shall their deliverance come about? (8)
Reflecting in his mind that death is better than poverty,
the Lotus-born One went to the northern shore of the Ocean of Milk.
There, having performed intense austerities, he once beheld the Supreme Lord, the lotus-eyed Vāsudeva, the teacher of the world. (10)
To the omniscient one, the abode of all powers, the eternal dwelling of all, the Lord of all, Vāsudeva, Viṣṇu, the Lord and husband of Lakṣmī. || 11 ||
Resembling ten million moons, resting upon the bed of Ananta’s coils in the waters as pure as the Ocean of Milk, it is the abode of Śrī.
Resembling ten million suns, the Lord of the Great Lords of Yoga,
delighting in yogic sleep, the illustrious Lord, the abode of all, and the Sovereign of the Gods.
The cause of the causes for the creation, destruction, and maintenance of the world; the source of powers such as Lakṣmī and others; adorned by the circle of those born [from him]. 14.
Surrounded by weapons and embodied beings such as the discus and others,
it was difficult to behold even for the gods, the Siddhas, and hundreds of great yogis.
Seeing the awakened Lord Īśāna, the source of all powers and a splendor difficult to endure, the lotus-born Brahmā [approached]. || 16 ||
Placing his joined palms upon his head, he first spoke this hymn:
"O Maheśvara, fulfill the desires of my mind! (17)
Victory to you, O lotus-eyed one; salutations to you, O creator of the universe!
Salutations to you, O Hṛṣīkeśa, the primordial source of the Great Puruṣa. 18.
O Lord of All, O Joy of Victory, O Abode of All, O Supreme beyond the supreme!
Be gracious to me, your devotee, and cut away the darkness of my doubt.
Thus praised by Brahmā, whose birth is unmanifest,
the Blessed Lord Hari, with eyes resting in tranquility, spoke while facing the palace.
The Blessed Lord said: "O Hiraṇyagarbha, I am pleased; tell me what you desire.
I shall grant it to you without a doubt, for you are my devotee, O observer of noble vows."
Having heard the words from Keśava, his heart filled with compassion,
the one of great intelligence replied to the Blessed Janārdana.
O Keśava, for the sake of my protection, tell me the most wonderful secret concerning this fourfold existence and the creation of beings. (23)
O Lord of All, O Greatly Wise One, your own nature is a supreme majesty—auspicious, delightful, purifying, and the ultimate alleviator of poverty. 24.
O Acyuta, [tell me] likewise of the eternal knowledge of Śrī, who lies upon all suffering,
as well as her principal names and those that are secondary.
"I wish to hear, in accordance with reality, those [teachings] arising from the lotus of your mouth.
Having heard these words of his, he spoke this reply. (26)
Endowed with great majesty, she is eternally inseparable from the Blessed Lord Vāsudeva, whose body consists of the six divine attributes. 27.
She exists as one alone, yet appears divided like the moonlight of the cold-rayed moon;
she is the essence of all powers, pervading and abiding throughout the universe. || 28 ||
Endowed with all sovereign qualities and eternally pure in nature, she is indeed this supreme vital energy (prāṇa-śakti) of all living beings on earth. (29)
The supreme power (kalā), which is the source of all powers, is beyond destruction;
this is the most excellent thousand names of her who flows forth. 30.
Listen with focused attention to this which bestows supreme sovereignty and prosperity;
by the mere remembrance of the name of the Goddess, poverty is reduced to ashes. (31)
The Blessed Lord said: Śrī is Padmā, Prakṛti, Sattvā, Śāntā, the imperishable power of consciousness (cicchakti);
she is absolute, partless, pure, all-pervading, and has the sky as her form.

She whose support is formed by the lotus of space, who is supreme, born from the immeasurable space, who is beyond space, who dwells in the midst of space, and who rests upon the five planes of space. || 33 ||
She is infallible, dwelling in the celestial firmament, whose nature is supreme bliss;
she is eternally pure, eternally satisfied, changeless, and all-seeing.
The power of knowledge, the power of agency, the power of experience, and that which carries the crest;
it is characterized by oiliness and radiance, devoid of bliss, pure, and unshakable. (35)
She is indeed infinite, belonging to Viṣṇu, manifest, the bliss of the universe, and radiant;
she is the power that dispels all afflictions and brings satisfaction to the ocean.
The eternal form is within the heart, waveless and free from affliction;
it is both knowledge and the object of knowledge, accessible through knowledge, and the illuminator of knowledge and its objects. || 37 ||
She is profound with the power of her own will, possessing unwavering radiance and perfect purity;
she is beautiful in form, omnipresent, boundless, the source of nourishment, and exalted by her excellent qualities.
Stainless, supportless, free from conceptual construction, and without dependence;
unmixed, perfectly tranquil, eternal, and abiding in luminosity. || 39 ||
The speech of the sky-farer (Vaikharī) is incomparable, free from conceptual construction, unrestrained yet moving by means of constraint;
it is indivisible, yet it divides, and though divided, it is the very essence of the world. 40.
Ungraspable, the grasper, hidden, profound, the protector of the universe;
indefinable, unimpeded, seedless, purifying, supreme. (41)
Inconceivable, immeasurable, and the destroyer of the wandering in existence, she is the Sovereign of the Gods—single, dual-formed, threefold, and innumerable. (42)
Supratiṣṭhā, Mahādhātrī, Sthiti, Vṛddhi, Dhruvā, Gati, Īśvarī, Mahimā, Ṛddhi, Pramodā, and Ujjvalodyamā. (43)
Akṣayā, Vardhamānā, Suprakāśā, Vihaṅgamā, Nirajā, Jananī, Nityā, Jayā, Rociṣmatī, and Śubhā. || 44 ||
She is Taponudā, Jvālā, Sudīpti, Aṃśumālinī, Aprameyā, Tridhā, Sūkṣmā, Parā, and Nirvāṇadāyinī. || 45 ||
She is white and perfectly pure, the lineage known as Amoghā;
she is Sandhānakī, the Pure Knowledge (Śuddhavidyā), the Great Sovereign of all beings. 46.
She is Lakṣmī, Tuṣṭi, Mahādhīrā, Śānti, and the ever-new Āpūraṇī;
she is the primordial power of grace, the eldest in the world, and the creator of the universe. || 47 ||
The [first] is the denial of truth; the [second] is capable of action and is delightful; the [third] is auspicious and characterized by surrender;
the [fourth] is perfectly delightful and pure; the [fifth] is luminous and brings about the state beyond thought.
Rajovatī, Arkapratibhā, Karṣiṇī, Rasā, Parā, Vasumatī, Devikānti, Śānti, Mati, and Kalā— (49).
The digit (kalā) is free from blemish, vast, illuminating, delightful, awakening, captivating, powerful, and the bestower of worldly prosperity. (50)
Amṛtasyandinī, Jīvā, Jananī, Khaṇḍikā, Sthirā, Dhūmā, Kalāvatī, Pūrṇā, Bhāsurā, Sumatī, and Rasā. (51)
She is the pure path, the course, the creation, the transformation, and the very drawing forth;
she is the one who leads forward, the giver of life, the humble, and she whose garment is as white as the universe.
The earth, the adamantine tube, the variegated one, the dweller in the cosmic egg;
she who has infinite forms, whose self is infinite, who abides in the infinite, and from whom the infinite originates. (53)
She is the great power, the vital energy, the giver of life, and full of delight;
she is the entire great multitude, the support of will, and the bringer of happiness.
She is the unshakable splendor of direct perception, the sprout within the range of the intellect;
she possesses various bodies, is the great whirlpool, and manifests in many forms.
She is the foremost among thousands, illuminating the principles of logic;
she fulfills all desires, she is everything, and she speaks of every purpose.
She is the sustainer of consciousness in its various forms, preceded by sound, ancient,
manifest and unmanifest, the hair upon the head of the individual soul (jīva), and the fulfiller of all desires.
Accomplished through volition, she is beyond calculation, containing the essence of reality, and bringing forth radiance.
She is the form of the elements, the nature of consciousness, possessed of the three qualities, and proud of those qualities. (58)

The sovereign of Prajāpati, the fierce goddess, the support of all, the bringer of happiness, the carrier of auspiciousness, the cosmic eon, and the destroyer of the impurities of the Kali age. || 59 ||

She whose continuum is manifested from the formless, who is well-restrained, the abode of the three qualities, the Great Illusion (Mahāmāyā), the Illusion of Yoga (Yogamāyā), and the beloved of the Great Lord of Yogins (Mahāyogeśvarī). || 60 ||
She is the Great Woman, the stainless Fame, Victory, Fortune, and the Untainted One;
she is Primordial Nature, O Lord, the power of Māyā, Sleep, and the Bringer of Glory.
Cintābuddhi, Yaśas, Prājñā, Śānti, and Āprītivardhanī;
she is the virtuous mother of Pradyumna, the bestower of happiness, good fortune, and spiritual accomplishment.
She is the ultimate limit, the final goal, and the firm foundation; she is the eldest, the most excellent, and the bringer of victory.
She is the delight that transcends all, the power of the universe, and possesses great strength.
She is the most excellent, the victorious, the heroic, the triumphant, and the bestower of victory;
she dwells in the heart, the protectress, the secret one, served by hosts of Gaṇas and Gandharvas.
The mistress of yogis, the power of yoga (yogamāyā), the female yogi, the bestower of the perfection of yoga;
she is surrounded by the great lords of yoga and is beloved by the lord of yoga and yoga.
She is bowed to by Brahmā, Indra, and Rudra; she is the bestower of boons upon gods and demons;
she moves along the three paths; she dwells within the three worlds; and she has arisen from the foot of Trivikrama.
Sutārā, Tāriṇī, Tārā, Durgā, Santāraṇī, Parā, Sutāraṇī, Tārayantī, and she who possesses the splendor of the Lord of Many Stars (Bhūritāreśvara). 67.
She is the secret knowledge, the sacrificial knowledge, the great knowledge, and the beautifully adorned one;
she is the inner spiritual knowledge, the mistress of obstacles, seated upon a lotus, and the supreme sovereign.
She is Ānvīkṣikī, Trayī, Vārttā, and Daṇḍanīti whose essence is policy;
she is Gaurī, Vāgīśvarī, Goptrī, Gāyatrī, and Kamalodbhavā. 69.
The sustainer of the universe, the universal-formed, the mother of the universe, the bestower of wealth;
she is accomplishment, the sacrificial exclamation *svāhā*, the ancestral offering *svadhā*, well-being, the nectar of immortality, and the achiever of all aims. (70)
She is the creation of desire, splendor, prosperity, fame, faith, compassion, and intellect;
she is sacred learning, wisdom, fortitude, modesty, and fortune—Vidyā, who is worshipped by the wise. (71)

She is Anasūyā (free from envy), Ghṛṇā (compassion), Nīti (right conduct), and Nivṛti (cessation); she is the cow of plenty (Kāmadhukkarā), the continuity of vows (Pratijñāsantati), Bhūti (prosperity), Dyaus (the sky), and Prajñā who considers herself the universe.

Sarasvatī is memory, the mother of all speech, the Visionary (Paśyantī), the Intermediate (Madhyamā), and the Equal (Samā); she is the Twilight (Sandhyā), intelligence, radiance, the Terrible (Bhīmā), and she who possesses every form. (73)
Kāṅkṣā, Māyā, Mahāmāyā, Mohinī, Mādhavapriyā; Saumyā, Bhogā, Mahābhogā, Bhaginī, and Bhogadāyikā. || 74 ||
She resembles well-polished gold; she has a golden lotus as her seat;
she is the womb of gold (Hiraṇyagarbha); she possesses beautiful hips; she is the captivating one; she is the delightful one; she is Ramā. || 75 ||
She is the moon, golden-hued, the delightful moonlight, the beautiful splendor that brings auspiciousness;
she is the woman who adorns the three worlds and is honored by the best of lords of men. (76)
The beautiful woman who is the most lovely in the three worlds, who possesses great majesty, who dwells upon a lotus, whose abode is the lotus, and who is adorned with a garland of lotuses. (77)
The beloved one holds a pair of lotuses, adorned with divine ornaments,
wearing a crown of various jewels and decorated with variegated garments.
Rich with various garlands and fragrances, possessing diverse weapons and vehicles, she is the goddess Mahānārāyaṇī, the Vaiṣṇavī praised by heroes. (79)

She is the terrible Kālasaṅkarṣaṇī, the digit (kalā) that withdraws the principles (tattvasaṅkarṣaṇī); she is the all-pervading Viśvā who fills the universe and is adorned with great majesty. || 80 ||
She is Vāruṇī, the giver of boons, she who is explained [in the scriptures], and she who is adorned by Ghaṇṭākarṇa;
she is Nṛsiṃhī, Bhairavī, Brāhmī, Bhāskarī, and the one who moves through the sky.

She is the power of Indra, the wish-fulfilling cow, the creation, the source of desire, and of great splendor; she is the one who grants all desires when seen, the universal energy, and the vision of the Self through the movement of the seed-syllable.
Śrī Cāndrī has Garuḍa mounted upon her heart; she is sweet-faced, Mahograrūpā, Vārāhī, and Nārasiṃhī, who has slain the asuras. 83.
She is the terrifying, tawny digit like the flame of the fire at the end of an eon;
she is the ornament of the three worlds, the formidable, the dark-hued one who fascinates the three worlds.
Mahotkaṭā, Mahāraktā, Mahācaṇḍā, Mahāsanā, Śaṅkhinī, Lekhinī, Svasthā, Likhinī, and Khecareśvarī. || 85 ||
Bhadrakālī, Ekavīrā, Kaumārī, Bhavamālinī, Kalyāṇī, Kāmadhuk, Jvālāmukhī, and Utpalamālikā. (86)
Bālikā, Dhanadā, Sūryā, Hṛdayotpalamālikā, Ajitā, Varṣaṇī, Rīti, Bharuṇḍā, and Garuḍāsanā. || 87 ||
Vaiśvānarī, Mahāmāyā, Mahākālī, Vibhīṣaṇā, Mahāmandāravibhavā, Śivānandā, and Ratipriyā. || 88 ||
Udrīti, Padmamālā, Dhūmavegā, Vibhāvanī, Satkriyā, Devasenā, and Hiraṇyarajatāśrayā. (89)
Sahasāvartamānā, Hastinādaprabodhinī, Hiraṇyapadmavarṇā, Haribhadrā, and Sudurddharā. (90)
Sūryā resembles the brilliance of gold, wears a golden garland, has a lotus-like face, is eternally nourished, is the mother of the gods, and was born from the nectar of immortality. || 91 ||
She who possesses great wealth, who has prominent horns, whose skin is like mud, and whose neck is like a conch shell;
she who has the color of the sun, the luster of the moon, whose gateway is fragrance, and who is difficult to approach. (92)
Worshipped by the best, possessing excellent limbs, most worthy of praise, the beloved of Viṣṇu;
auspicious, the giver of boons, the beautiful one, the mistress of the beautiful, she who dwells in the Vindhya mountains.
Yoganidrā, she who delights in yoga, Devakī, she who can assume any form at will; the dispeller of Kaṃsa, Durgā, Kaumārī, Kauśikī, and Kṣamā. || 94 ||
Kātyāyanī, Kālarātri, the eternally satisfied, the invincible, the one with deformed eyes, the large-eyed one, the protector of her devotees. || 95 ||
She is multiform, she is her own true form, she is deformed, and she is devoid of form;
she abounds in the resonance of bells and possesses the sound of the thundering clouds.
The crusher of the great lord of the asuras, her face curved with a frown, she is the sole one honored by truthful means; she belongs to Kubera and observes the vow of celibacy.
The Noble Yaśodā is the giver of sons, the bestower of the wealth of Dharma, the pacifier of the suffering of poverty, and the destroyer of the pain of terrible misfortune. (98)
She is the alleviator of the distress of her devotees, the auspicious one, the remover of the fear of worldly existence;
she is the daughter of the Ocean of Milk, Padmā, Kamalā, Dharaṇī, and Dharā. 99.
Rukmiṇī, Rohiṇī, Sītā, Satyabhāmā, Yaśasvinī, Prajñādhārā, Mitābuddhi, Vedamātā, and Yaśovatī. (100)
Concentration is her cultivation; loving-kindness and compassion are her affection for devotees; the inner altar is her sacrificial fee, and the supreme goal is her devotion to celibacy. || 101 ||
She is initiation, vision, examination, and discernment; she is affectionate toward heroes; she is Ambikā, Surabhī, and Siddhā; she is worshipped by the Siddhas and Vidyādharas. (102)
The intensely radiant, the licking, the formidable, the filler of the universe, the sustainer of the universe, the light, the burner, and the lover of the *tāṇḍava* dance. || 103 ||
Udbhavā, Virajā, Rājñī, Tāpanī, Bindumālinī, Kṣīradhārā, Suprabhāvā, Lokamātā, and Suvarcasā. (104)
Containing the oblation and containing the clarified butter, she is born of sacrifice when it is being offered;
she is the nourisher, the purifier, the burner, and that which has fire as her refuge. 105.
Mātṛkā, Mādhavī, Mucyā, Mokṣalakṣmī, the bestower of great supernatural power, the granter of all desires, Bhadrā, Subhadrā, and Sarvamaṅgalā. || 106 ||
She is white, dressed in very bright white garments, adorned with white garlands and unguents;
she is the swan, the one who removes [defilements], the female swan, the heart-pleasing one, whose abode is the lotus of the heart.
She who possesses a white parasol, she of beautiful hips, whose eyes are as long as lotus petals;
she is Sāvitrī, whose resolve is truth, the granter of desires, and she who fulfills every wish.
The excellent woman is beautiful to behold, visible yet beyond the reach of sight, tangible and worthy of service;
she delights in enjoyment, possesses all enjoyments, and has her bed and seat upon the king of serpents.
Ārdrī, Puṣkariṇī, Puṇyā, Pāvanī, Pāpasūdanī, Śrīmatī, and Śubhākārā bestow supreme sovereignty and prosperity. (110)
She possesses inconceivable and infinite power; she is the destroyer of existence and its manifestations.
She is the ladder situated within all bodies, and she is saluted by all living beings. 111.
She who possesses superior strength and power, the divine one, the daughter of Gautama, whose abode is Gokula;
she who is to be propitiated, who has the luster of the full moon, who is singular bliss, and who has a hundred faces.
Kūṣmāṇḍī dwells in gardens, city gates, palaces, and groves; she is Dāruṇī, Caṇḍā, Kirātī, and has her abode in the Nandana grove.
Kālāyanī, attainable through time, the giver of fear and the destroyer of fear;
Saudāminī, with the roar of clouds, the crusher of Daityas and Dānavas. || 114 ||
The Mother of the World, the Terrifier, the Sustainer of Beings, she who is very difficult to attain;
the Daughter of Kaśyapa, the Bestower of Auspiciousness, the One with the Forest Garland, the Most Excellent and Auspicious One. 115.
Dhanyā, Dhanyeśvarī, Dhanyā, Ratnadā, Vasuvardhinī, Gandharvī, Revatī, Gaṅgā, Śakunī, and Vimalānanā. || 116 ||
Iḍā is indeed the bringer of peace, the dark one (tāmasī) whose abode is the lotus;
Ājyapā is Vajrakaumārī, and Somapā has her refuge in the flower. 117.
She is beloved by the world, accompanied by her charioteer, invincible, and borne by a bird;
she is born of the mind, moves at will, and is served by the Siddhas and Cāraṇas.
She is the Fortune of the Sky, the Great Fortune, the Fortune of Splendor who blazes brightly;
she is the Fortune of Taste, the Source of the World, and the Fortune of Fragrance who dwells in the forest.

She is the one to be heard, the cause of hearing, the leader, the tongue, and the mover within the vital breath; she is the mother of Viriñci, the all-pervading power, and she whose vehicle is the excellent lotus.
Vīryā, Vīreśvarī, the venerable one, free from sorrow, the increaser of wealth; (p. 378) Anāhatā, Kuṇḍalinī, Nalinī, and Vanavāsinī. || 121 ||
Gāndhārī, saluted by Indra, saluted by the lord of the gods, the virtuous one, the most auspicious of all auspicious things, the bestower of the fulfillment of all desires. || 122 ||
Sarvānandā, Mahānandā, Satkīrti, Siddhasevitā, Sinīvālī, Kuhū, Rākā, Amā, Anumati, and Dyuti. || 123 ||
Arundhatī, Vasumatī, Bhārgavī, Vāstudevatā, Māyūrī, Vajravetālī, Vajrahastā, and Varānanā. || 124 ||
She is the sinless Earth, steadfast, the vital channel adorned with jewels;
she possesses the form of royal splendor and is the glory of Brahman, saluted by the knowers of Brahman. || 125 ||
She is to be known as the glory of victory who bestows victory; she is the glory of creation and the heavenly path for the virtuous;
she is the beautiful flower, the abode of blossoms, the glory of fruit, and the beloved of the stainless.
Dhanurlakṣmī, Tvamilitā, Parakrodhanivāriṇī, Kadrū, Dhanāyu, Kapilā, Surasā, and Suramohinī. (127)
Mahāśvetā, Mahānīlā, Mahāmūrtti, Viṣāpahā, Suprabhā, Jvālinī, Dīpti, Tṛpti, Vyāpti, and Prabhākarī. (128)
Tejovatī, Padmabodhā, Madalekhā, Aruṇāvatī; Ratnā, who has become a string of jewels, Śatadhāmā, and Śatopahā.
She who possesses the three qualities, she who resounds with a proclamation, she who protects, she who roars, she who is devoid of sound;
she who is to be attained, the mother Aditi, the goddess Diti, she whose vehicle is a deer, and she who dwells upon the moon. 130.
Seated upon a variegated blue lotus, resting on the foundation of a treasury of jewels,
she possesses pairs of gold and silver and is established upon a conch and an auspicious throne.
She has cow-urine, cow-dung, milk, curd, ghee, and water as her abodes;
she is clad in bark garments and possesses the full moon and sun as her seats. 132.
Susūkṣmā, Nirvṛti, Sthūlā, Nirvṛtā, Atirā, Mārīci, Jvālinī, Dhūmrā, Havyavāhā, and Hiraṇyadā. (133)
The bestower, the black one, the accomplishment, the witherer, the awakener, the radiant, the unassailable, the sharp, and the blazing with fierce fire. 134.
She is endowed with her limbs (Sāṅgā), Pracaṇḍā, Dīptā, Vaidyuti, Sumahādyuti,
Kapilā, Nīlaraktā, Suṣumnā, and Visphuliṅginī.
Radiant, destroying enemies, long, a column of smoke, old age;
full-orbed like the sun, falling away, yet most enchanting. (136)
Jayā is the nourishing shadow, mental and heart-illuminating;
she is the excellent maker of gold and the reviver of the dead in battle. (137)
Viśalyakaraṇī, Śubhrā, Sandhinī, Paramauṣadhī, Brahmiṣṭhā, Brahmasahitā, Aindavī, and Ratnasambhavā. (138)
Vidyutprabhā, Bindumatī, the Mother who possesses the qualities of the three natures;
she is eternally arisen, eternally joyful, and the eternal fulfiller of desires. 139.
Marked with a lotus and bearing the sign of a vajra, Vakradaṇḍā is resplendent;
she is the maiden worshipped by Videha, Māyā, who carries victory. 140.
The proud one, the auspicious, the venerable, the woman of pride, the bestower of honor;
the sovereign of the universe, the possessor of hosts, the circle, and the mistress of the circle. 141.
Haripriyā, Bhaumasutā, Manojñā, Matidāyinī, Pratyaṅgirā, Somaguptā, Manobhijñā, and Vadanmati. (142)
Yaśodharī, Ratnamālā, Kṛṣṇā, Trailokyabandhanī, Amṛtā, Ādhāraṇī, Harṣā, Vinatā, Vallakī, and Śacī. (143)
Saṅkalpā, Bhāminī, Miśrā, Kādambaryāmṛtaprabhā, Āgatā, Nirgatā, Vajrā, Suhitā, Sahitā, and Akṣatā—[these are the goddesses]. 144.
She who accomplishes all aims, the stainless upholder of the elements, born from the source of compassion, the lotus-eyed one beloved by the moon. 145.
She is of gentle form, greatly radiant, and possessing a vast expansion of flames;
she wears a garland and a golden necklace, with the constant luster of vajra-gold.
The supreme Prakriyā, the eloquent one, the agitating one, the source of the mouth; the blossoming one, the one called Vajra, the chain, and the lotus-eyed one. (147)
She is Jayaṅkarī, Madhumatī, Haritā, Śaśinī, and Śivā;
she is Mūlaprakṛti, Īśānī, Yogamātā, and Manojavā. (148)

The Source of Phenomena (Dharmodayā), the Radiant One (Bhānumatī), the All-Illuminating (Sarvābhāsā), the Bringer of Bliss (Sukhāvahā), the Sustainer (Dhurandharā), the Youthful (Bālā), the One to be Served by Dharma (Dharmasevyā), and the Tathāgatā. 149.
She is delicate, with a gentle face, and supreme in her gentle address;
she is auspicious, beneficial in every way, the secret power, and whose abode is the cave. || 150 ||
Halāyudhā, Kāvīrā, who upholds the nectar of all scriptures; Vyomaśakti, Mahādehā, Vyomagā, and Magumanmayī. (151)
The Gaṅgā, Vitastā, Yamunā, Candrabhāgā, and Sarasvatī; Tilottamā, Urvaśī, Rambhā, Svāminī, and Surasundarī. (152)

The young woman who has arrows as her weapons, whose lips are like the bimba fruit, who possesses a beautiful smile, who is preeminent and has a lovely back, bestows the fruits of both seen and unseen [merit]. (153)
She who acts according to desire and is herself desirable, who sports in the conduct of desire;
she resembles the lord of the snowy mountains and has the best of elephant-kings as her vehicle. (154)
She is the supreme source of the perfection of all happiness and good fortune;
she is the most excellent, consisting of all things, all-encompassing, and beloved by the Lord of All. 155.
She is the source of all limbs, the unmanifested one, the sovereign of the lords of the primary principles;
she resides upon the chest of Viṣṇu—what more than this could be said? (156)
The supreme Goddess of great majesty, who rests upon the chest of Hari—that Goddess, the destroyer of sins, may she grant her presence to me. (157)

Thus, this thousand names of Lakṣmī, which brings auspiciousness, has been proclaimed according to the distinction between the supreme and the inferior, and through their primary and secondary aspects. 158.
And whoever, O Lotus-born One, should constantly recite this or even listen to it, having become pure and composed, endowed with devotion and faith; || 159 ||
Having worshipped Śrīnivāsa, the teacher of the world, with flowers, incense, ointments, and enjoyments such as the honey-mixture (madhuparka) according to one's capacity.
Having worshipped the goddess Śrī, the beloved of Śrīdhara, who stands at his side,
he should then satisfy the Supreme Goddess with the Thousand Names.
Whoever constantly recites this *Nāmaratnāvalīstotra*, Lakṣmī, being well-disposed toward him, bestows everything upon him. (162)
From that Lakṣmī, powers that pervade the universe have always arisen;
yet, due to her being the ultimate cause, they do not remain as independent agents within this world of moving and unmoving beings.
Therefore, the Mother of the World, Śrī, who is the beloved of Acyuta, is pleased with him;
and when she is well-pleased, her powers indeed bestow upon him his desired perfections.
The Lord Acyuta alone is the sovereign of the world and possesses power;
