Oṃ, salutation to Kṛṣṇā; Oṃ, salutation to Dhūmrā;
Oṃ, salutation to Tīvrā.
Oṃ, obeisance to Sphuliṅginī; Oṃ, obeisance to Rudhirā; Oṃ, obeisance to Jvālinī.
Then: *namaḥ* to the seat of the fire of passion (*rāgāgni*). Then:
Vāgīśvarī, who has bathed after her menses, with eyes like blue lotuses.
He was joined by Vāgīśvara, who was endowed with a state of playful sport.
Having meditated thus.

Having worshipped with the five offerings using the mantra "Oṃ hrīṃ vāgīśvarāya namaḥ, oṃ vāgīśvaryai namaḥ," one should bring forth the fire produced from a sun-crystal or obtained from the house of a learned Brahmin (śrotriya).
In the case of Sundarī, however, one should worship Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī.
In the Gautamīya [Tantra]: "Whether it be fire produced from stone or that which arises from a fire-drill..."
Or he may take from one born in the family of Vedic scholars, or from a forest-dweller.
Even if he is content with whatever comes by chance, he is unfit for the performance of sacrifice.
For what is obtained from a Brahmin who maintains no sacred fires yields only half the benefit.
The Fire-god shall grant a fourth-part of the fruit to the kṣatrabandhu.
From a Vaiśya and a Śūdra, the rite of burnt offering (homa) becomes fruitless.
Therefore, with every effort, one should collect [the substance] freed from fire. As stated in another Tantra:
Or else, the practitioner, having brought fire from the house of a twice-born man, [should proceed].
One should gaze [at it] after it has been consecrated with the root mantra ending in *vauṣaṭ*.
Immediately after that, one should invoke Agni with the Astra mantra.
One should cause the flesh-eaters to depart by means of the root mantra ending in *hūṃ phaṭ*.
Then: Oṃ, salutation to the yoga-pīṭha of Vahni.

In the four directions: Oṃ, obeisance to Vāmā; likewise, obeisance to Jyeṣṭhā, obeisance to Raudrī, obeisance to Ambikā. Then, having recited the root mantra: obeisance to the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) of the deity [Name].
Having thus worshipped the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), [one should worship] Vāgīśvarī beneath it.

Having meditated upon her as the form of that respective deity while she is in her menses, having brought the fire as previously described and consecrated it with the rites of inspection (*vīkṣaṇa*) and so forth, one should extract the fire from that [fire-pot] with the syllable *raṃ*. Then,
reciting the root mantra followed by *hūṃ phaṭ kravyādebhyaḥ svāhā*, one should discard the portion belonging to the flesh-eaters (*kravyāda*).

Having protected it with the fire-mantra (vahnimantra), veiled it with the syllable *hūṃ*, rendered it nectar-like with the cow-mudrā (*dhenumudrā*), lifted it up with both arms, and whirled it three times over the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*), one should, with knees touching the ground, [place it] facing oneself upon the womb of the Goddess, perceiving it as the seed-syllable of Śiva.
One should cast this [into the fire].

Then, having worshipped with "Hrīṃ, obeisance to the form of fire," and having joined the consciousness there with "Raṃ, obeisance to the consciousness of fire," one should kindle the flame with: "O Voci Piṅgala, slay, slay! Burn, burn! Cook, cook! Make all known, make known! Svāhā!"
Then: "I revere Agni, the blazing one, Jātavedas, the consumer of oblations."
"Golden-hued, stainless, kindled, with faces on all sides"—with these words, one should perform the ritual worship (upasthāna).
Then, having assigned the name, "O Agni, you are [Name]," he recites: "Om, O Vaiśvānara, Jātavedas, bring [the gods] here;
O red-eyed one, accomplish all rites, Svāhā!"

Having worshipped [Agni] with this [mantra] and with water for honor (*arghya*) and other offerings, [one should recite]: *Oṃ agnihiraṇyādisaptajihvābhyo namaḥ* (Oṃ, salutation to the seven tongues beginning with Hiraṇyā),
*Oṃ sahasrārcciṣe hṛdayāya namaḥ* (Oṃ, salutation to the heart, the thousand-rayed one),
and *Oṃ ityādyagniṣaḍaṅgebhyo namaḥ* (Oṃ, salutation to the six limbs of Agni beginning with the aforementioned).
Oṃ, obeisance to the eight forms beginning with Agni Jātavedas;
outside of that, Oṃ, obeisance to the eight Śaktis beginning with Brāhmī;
further outside, Oṃ, obeisance to the eight treasures (nidhis) beginning with Padma.
Outside of that: Oṃ, salutation to Indra and the other guardians of the world-quarters (lokapālas).

Outside of that, [one should say] "Oṃ, salutation to the weapons beginning with the Vajra. Then, having placed two *kuśa* leaves, each a span (*prādeśa*) long, in the middle of the clarified butter, one should meditate upon the *iḍā*, *piṅgalā*, and *suṣumnā* in the left, right, and central parts respectively.
One should perform the *homa*.

Having taken clarified butter (*ājya*) from the southern part with the *sruva* ladle, one should offer it into the right eye of the fire with the mantra: *oṃ agnaye svāhā*. Likewise, having taken clarified butter from the northern part, *oṃ...* [one should offer it into the left eye].
One should offer oblation into the left eye with the mantra "Somāya svāhā."
Then, having taken clarified butter from the middle portion, one should offer it into the forehead-eye of the fire with the mantra: *oṃ agnīṣomābhyāṃ svāhā*.
Again, from the south, having taken clarified butter with the word "namaḥ," [one offers it] into the mouth of the fire with the mantra: *oṃ agnaye sviṣṭakṛte svāhā*.
Then follows the oblation of the Great Utterances (mahāvyāhṛti).
One should offer oblations three times with this mantra: "Oṃ bhūḥ svāhā, Oṃ bhuvaḥ svāhā, Oṃ vaiśvānara jātaveda ihāvaha lohitākṣa sarvakarmāṇi sādhaya svāhā."
Then, having worshipped the deity upon the pedestal in the fire with the root mantra, one should offer oblations twenty-five times into its mouth with clarified butter while reciting the root mantra.
Having meditated upon the identity of the fire and the deity with one's own self, one should offer eleven oblations with the root mantra.
Then, from the root mantra, [one offers] svāhā to the deities of the limbs.
If one is capable, one should offer one oblation for each [deity] individually.
Then, having formed the formal resolve (saṅkalpa), one should perform the fire-oblation (homa) with the specific substances prescribed for each respective ritual manual (kalpa).

Then, having offered the final oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*) with the root mantra, one should bring the chosen deity into one's own heart by means of the withdrawal mudrā (*saṃhāramudrā*), dismiss them with the words "Forgive me," give the sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*), and perform the rite for ensuring the ritual is complete and without defects (*acchidrāvadhāraṇa*).
Thus ends the section on the abbreviated fire offering (saṃkṣepahoma).
Composed and compiled by His Majesty King Śrī Rājā Deva Nandana Siṃha Bahādur, the Lord of the Sovereign Capital of Śiva-Hara.
The Thirteenth Durgā Tantra, contained within the Śāktapramoda.
This has been edited by Paṇḍita Śrī Raghurāja Dubejī, a descendant of the aforementioned royal preceptor.
Printed and published by Śrī Kṛṣṇadāsātmaja Khemarāja at his own Śrī Veṅkaṭeśvara Press.
Mumbai: Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa. Śāktapramoda.
Now follows the Durgā-tantra; now follows the meditation on Durgā: [one should meditate on her] mounted upon the shoulders of a lion and adorned with various ornaments.
The great goddess has four arms and wears a serpent as her sacred thread.
Clad in red garments, with a body resembling the rising sun.
The consort of Śambhu, who is served by hosts of sages such as Nārada and others.
She was beautifully adorned with a navel-stalk encircled by three folds.
On the great island of Ratnadvīpa, which is furnished with lion-thrones.
One should meditate on her who dwells in the lotus, seated upon a fully blossomed lotus.
(p. 420) Now, regarding the extraction of the yantra: O beloved of Hara, listen as I proclaim the Durgā-yantra.
One should first arrange a triangle provided with nine corners.
All [of these] are accompanied by the three images and provided with eight petals.
The vajra is accompanied by three lines and joined with two earth-fortresses (bhūpura).
Having leveled it, one should draw [the mandala] according to the aforementioned method by this following rite.
One should draw a wheel joined with various weapons and adorned with mantras.
There, one should worship that Goddess, who is the form of the primordial nature (mūlaprakṛti).
Now follows the extraction of the mantra; next, I shall declare the mantra of Durgā, which bestows both seen and unseen fruits.
This [world], beginning with Māyā and enriched by the piercing of the ear-cavity, shall again possess further creation.
And Cāntaka is established, with Māruta as his seat and Bhautika as his foundation.
This mantra, beginning with *Tārā* and ending with *hṛdaya*, consists of eight syllables.
Now the mantra:
Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Duṇḍurgā. Now the procedure for worship.

Having performed the morning rites and so forth, up to the *pīṭhanyāsa*, one should install the powers of the seat (*pīṭhaśakti*) upon the filaments and in the center. As follows: *Āṃ* salutation to Prabhā;
*Īṃ* salutation to Māyā; *Ūṃ* salutation to Jayā; *Ṝṃ* salutation to Sūkṣmā.
Salutation to Viśuddhā; salutation to Nandinī.
Oṃ, obeisance to Suprabhā; aṃ, obeisance to Vijayā; aḥ, obeisance to Sarvasiddhidā.
Above that.
One should worship with: Oṃ, to the one whose weapons are adamantine claws and fangs, to the great lion-throne, hūṃ phaṭ namaḥ.
p. 241) Next is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the seers (*ṛṣi*) and so forth: *Namaḥ* to Nārada, the seer, on the head.
Salutation to Gāyatrī, the metre, in the mouth; salutation to the goddess Durgā in the heart.
Then, the placement of mantras on the hands and limbs (*karāṅganyāsa*): *hrāṃ oṃ hrīṃ dundurgāyai aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ*;
*hrīṃ oṃ hrīṃ dundurgāyai tarjjanībhyāṃ svāhā*; *hrūṃ oṃ hrīṃ dundurgāyai madhyamābhyāṃ vaṣaṭ*; *hrauṃ oṃ hrīṃ dundurgāyai*.
HŪM with the two ring fingers; HRAUṂ OṂ HRĪṂ DUṂ DURGĀYAI VAUṢAṬ with the two little fingers; HRAḤ OṂ HRĪṂ DUṂ DURGĀYAI PHAṬ with the palms and backs of the hands.
In this same way, [the mantras for] the heart and so forth [are to be understood].
HĀṂ OṂ HRĪṂ DUNDURGĀYAI HRDAYĀYA NAMAḤ, HRĪṂ OṂ HRĪṂ DUNDURGĀYAI ŚIRASE SVĀHĀ,
HRŪṂ OṂ HRĪṂ DUNDURGĀYAI ŚIKHĀYAI VAṢAṬ.
Hraiṃ Oṃ Hrīṃ Dundurgāyai Netratrayāya Vauṣaṭ;
Hrauṃ Oṃ Hrīṃ Dundurgāyai Kavacāya Hūṃ;
Hraḥ Oṃ Hrīṃ Dundurgāyai Astrāya Phaṭ—thus is the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the six limbs and so forth.
And so it is stated in the Nibandha:
"The preceptor, by means of the root mantra joined with the salutation..."
One should perform the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga) together with Hrīṃ and the other syllables according to the prescribed rule.
Now, meditation.
Seated upon a lion, crowned with the moon, and adorned with three eyes, she holds a conch, a discus, a bow, and arrows in her four arms which resemble emeralds.
With armlets, necklaces, bracelets, jingling girdles, and tinkling anklets,
and with earrings radiant with jewels— may she who removes even the most difficult misfortunes be our protection.
Having meditated thus, one should perform the ritual installation of the conch with mental offerings.
Then one should perform the worship of the pedestal (pīṭhapūjā).
On the filaments and in the center: *āṃ prabhāyai namaḥ*, *īṃ māyāyai namaḥ*, *ūṃ jayāyai namaḥ*, *ṝṃ sūkṣmāyai namaḥ*.
Oṃ ḷṃ, salutation to Viśuddhā; oṃ aiṃ, salutation to Nandinī.
Oṃ, obeisance to Suprabhā. Aṃ, obeisance to Vijayā.
AḤ, homage to the giver of all accomplishments! Above that, HŪM PHAṬ, homage to the great lion throne whose weapons are diamond claws and fangs!
One should offer a seat with this [mantra] and fashion the form with the root-mantra.
Then, having again meditated and performed the rites from the invocation up to the offering of five handfuls of flowers,
one should begin the worship of the deities of the enclosure (*āvaraṇapūjā*).
In the southeast, southwest, northwest, northeast, the center, and the cardinal directions.
Hrāḥ / Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to the heart of Durgā.
One should worship with these and other [mantras].

Then, on the petals starting from the east [and proceeding clockwise]: *jaṃ* to Jayā, *viṃ* to Vijayā, *kiṃ* to Kīrti, *paṃ* to Prīti, *paṃ* to Prabhā, *śuṃ* to Śuddhā, *maṃ* to Medhā, and *śaṃ* to Śruti. *Namaḥ* is to be added after each.

On the tips of the petals, one should worship: *laṃ* to the sword, *vaṃ* to the shield, *śaṃ* to the arrow, *ṣaṃ* to the bow, *saṃ* to the trident, and *haṃ* to the index finger; outside of that, one should worship Indra and the others, as well as the thunderbolt and the other weapons.
Then, one should complete the ritual actions ending with the dismissal of the incense and other offerings. The mantra for its bali-offering is as follows:
"Come, come! O Queen of the Asuras, accomplish my pair of feet and the pair of feet of the buffalo;
say 'the second,' and eat the second again!"
The word *sarvasiddhipada* followed by the goddess [name] and then the word *svāhā* constitutes this mantra for the offering of the *bali*,
as proclaimed by the Mantrinī.
The preliminary rite (puraścaraṇa) for this consists of eight hundred thousand recitations; the fire oblation (homa) is performed with eight thousand sesame seeds.
And so it is said:
"One should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times along with a thousand sesame seeds," and so forth, according to such scriptural statements.
Now, I know neither the hymn nor the mantra, nor even the ritual diagram; I do not know the praise, O Great One, nor the invocation, nor even the meditation, nor the words of praise.
I do not know those mudrās, nor do I know that [other] lamentation; O Mother, I know only this: taking refuge in you removes all afflictions. || 1 ||
The fall from your feet that occurred was due to ignorance of the ritual injunctions, lack of wealth, laziness, or the impossibility of performing the prescribed act.
Therefore, O Mother Śivā, who delivers all beings, this must be forgiven;
for while a bad son may occasionally be born, a bad mother never exists. || 2 ||
O Mother, there are many upright sons of yours upon this earth;
yet among them all, your son is exceedingly rare.
O Śivā, this transgression of mine is not worthy of you;
for while a bad son may be born somewhere, a bad mother never exists. || 3 ||
O Mother of the World, O Mother, service at your feet has not been performed by me, nor has even abundant wealth been offered to you, O Goddess.
Nevertheless, you display incomparable affection toward me;
for while a bad son might occasionally be born, a bad mother never exists. || 4 ||
Having abandoned the gods due to the agitation caused by the performance of various rituals,
I have reached an age exceeding eighty-five years.
O Mother, if at this moment you have no compassion for me, O Mother of Lambodara, I shall go to [another] refuge, being without support. || 5 ||
The outcaste becomes a chatterer with a voice like that of a honey-drinking bee;
free from fear, though wretched, he dwells with long-coiled golden ornaments.
O Aparṇā, when the syllable *manu* enters your ear, O Mother, who among people knows this fruit of that which is to be recited during the rite of recitation? 6.
Smeared with funeral ashes, consuming poison, wearing a garment of human skin,
bearing matted locks, and having the lord of serpents as a necklace— such is Paśupati.
O Bhavānī, even Kapālī, the Lord of Beings, attains the singular status of the Lord of the Universe;
this is the fruit of the ritual of taking your hand in marriage.
O moon-faced one, I have no longing for liberation, nor do I desire worldly power, nor do I seek higher knowledge, nor even the desire for pleasure.
Therefore, O Mother, I entreat you: may my clay [image] indeed become Mṛḍānī, Rudrāṇī, Śivā, Śivā, and Bhavānī—so let him mutter. || 8 ||
Were you not propitiated according to the prescribed rites with various services?
Was it not done through words that were devoid of dry contemplation?
O Śyāmā, if you alone show even a little compassion toward me, who am without a protector, then that is indeed fitting for you, O Mother.
O Durgā, O Mistress of the ocean of compassion, when submerged in calamities I remember you;
do not consider this to be deceit on my part, for those afflicted by hunger and thirst remember their mother.
O Mother of the World, what is so strange in this? If you possess perfect compassion for me, then surely a mother does not neglect her son, even when he is shrouded in a succession of offenses. 11.
"There is no sinner equal to me, and indeed there is no destroyer of sins equal to you.
Knowing this, O Great Goddess, act as is appropriate."
Thus ends the hymn of praise.
Now listen, O Goddess, to the armor; I shall proclaim the armor that grants all accomplishments.
By reciting it and by causing others to recite it, a person shall be liberated from distress.
O Goddess, he who recites the Durgā mantra without knowing the armor-mantra (kavaca) does not obtain its fruit and shall go to the supreme hell.
May Umādevī protect my head; may Śūladhāriṇī protect my forehead;
may Khecarī protect my eyes; and may Catvaravāsinī protect my ears.
May Sugandhā protect the nose; may Sarvadhāriṇī protect the face; may the goddess Caṇḍikā protect the tongue, and likewise Saubhadrikā protect the neck;
may Aśokavāsinī protect the heart, and Vajradhāriṇī protect the two arms.
The goddess Lalitā is the heart; Siṃhavāhinī is the belly.
The goddess Kaṭimbhagavatī is the two thighs, Vindhyavāsinī is the two shanks, Mahābalā is the two calves, and Bhūtalavāsinī is the two feet.
Thus you abide, O Goddess; you whose nature is the protection of the three worlds, protect me in all my limbs, O Durgā; salutations be unto you!
Thus [ends] the armor;
now follows the Upaniṣad: all the gods approached the Goddess and asked, "Who are you, O Great Goddess?"
She said: "I am the very nature of Brahman; from me proceeds the universe consisting of Prakṛti and Puruṣa;
I am both the void and the non-void; I am bliss and the absence of bliss."
"Indeed, there is consciousness and unconsciousness;
'I am Brahman, and the Vedas are Brahman—that which is to be known,' so says the Atharvaṇa Śruti."
I am the five elements; I am the five subtle essences.
I am the entire world; I am the Veda and I am that which is not the Veda; I am knowledge and I am ignorance; I am the born and I am the unborn; I am below, above, and across.
I move with the Rudras and the Vasus; I move with the Ādityas and the Viśvedevas.
I support both Mitra and Varuṇa; I [support] Indra and Agni; I [support] both the Aśvins.
I join together Soma, Tvaṣṭṛ, Pūṣan, and Bhaga;
I establish Viṣṇu of the wide stride, as well as Brahmā and Prajāpati.
Bestow wealth upon the one who offers oblations, the sacrificer of noble progeny who presses the soma.
I am the sovereign ruler, the gatherer of treasures, the wise one, the first among those worthy of sacrifice.
I am the wise one; upon his head is my father; my source is within the waters, in the ocean.
He who knows this attains the state of the Goddess. Those gods said:
"Obeisance to the Goddess, to the Great Goddess; obeisance forever to the Auspicious One."
Homage to Prakṛti, the auspicious one; we are self-restrained and bow down before her.
Her, who is fire-colored, blazing with ascetic fervor, the daughter of Virocana, who enjoys the fruits of her own actions.
I take refuge in Goddess Durgā, who utterly destroys darkness.
The gods begot the goddess Ambā; her, the multiform creatures speak. May she, the cow Speech, yielding us joy, refreshment, and strength, come to us with well-spoken hymns.
I bow to Kālarātri, Vāpastutā, Anantā, Vaiṣṇavī, Skandamātṛ, Sarasvatī, Aditi, the daughter of Dakṣa, and the purifying Śivā.
And may we know Mahālakṣmī, and may we meditate upon Sarvaśakti.
May the Goddess inspire us. Aditi was indeed born as your daughter, O Dakṣa.
The gods, auspicious kinsmen of immortality, were born after them.

In the realm of desire (kāma), the womb (yoni) is the lotus; the hand of the reed-bearer (vetrapāṇi) is the cave (guhā); Mātariśvan (the wind-god) is the arrow; Indra is the bow; again, the house (geha) is the fruit; and by means of illusion (māyā), together with A-pṛthuka (Aghora), this is the primordial knowledge (vidyā) of the Mother of the Universe (Viśvamātṛ). This is the Self (Ātman) as Power (Śakti). She is the enchantress of the universe. She is the bearer of the noose, the goad, the bow, and the arrows.
O Śrī Mahāvidyā, whoever knows her thus crosses over sorrow. Homage to you, O Blessed Mother; protect us from all sides. She is these eight Vasus; she is these eleven Rudras;
she is these twelve Ādityas; she is these Viśvedevas; she is both the Soma-drinkers and the non-Soma-drinkers.
The Yātudhānas, Asuras, Rakṣasas, Piśācas, Yakṣas, and Siddhas—she is these; she is the qualities of sattva, rajas, and tamas; she is this in the forms of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra;
she is these as Prajāpati, Indra, and Manu; she is these as the planets, lunar mansions, luminaries, and the divisions of time such as kalās and kāṣṭhās.
I bow down to her who has the form of ashes.
The Goddess, who eternally removes all sins and bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
[She is] infinite, victorious, pure, worthy of refuge, bestowing auspiciousness, and beautiful;
she is joined with the form of the sky and endowed with the sacrificial fire.
The seed-syllable of the Goddess, shining like a half-moon, accomplishes all aims.
In this way, those of pure mind performed sacrifices with the single-syllable mantra.
Those who are oceans of the water of knowledge, consisting of supreme bliss, meditate.
The left [hand] belongs to that which has become Brahman, endowed with eight faces.
The Sun (R) is the bindu of the left ear; it is joined with the third of the eighth group.
He is equal to Nārāyaṇa, endowed with friends, and possessed of speech and lower faculties.
O Vidhi, the nine-syllabled [mantra] should have nine corners; it bestows great bliss.
She who dwells in the center of the heart-lotus, possessing a radiance like the morning sun.
Holding a noose and a goad, with gentle hands displaying the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness.
I worship her who has three eyes, who wears red garments, and who is the cow of plenty for her devotees.
I worship you, O Great Goddess, the destroyer of great fear.
She who pacifies great poverty, and who possesses both great beauty and the formless nature.

Because her true nature is not known even by Brahmā and the other gods, she is called Anantā (the Infinite). Because no abode of hers is perceived, she is called Alakṣya (the Unperceivable). Because no birth of hers is found, she is called Ajā (the Unborn). Because she alone exists everywhere, she is called Ekā (the One). She alone possesses every universal form.
Therefore, she is manifold.

The Goddess Mātṛkā is the mother of infinite mantras—mantras that are expressed by infinite ascetic practices, whose objects of knowledge are infinite, and which are characterized by both unity and multiplicity; she is the embodiment of the knowledge of all words.
She transcends the consciousness of cognitions and is the witness of emptiness within all that is empty.
She beyond whom there is nothing higher is proclaimed as Durgā;
she is the Goddess who makes even those difficult places inaccessible and who ordains difficult conduct.
Fearing worldly existence, I bow to her who carries one across the ocean of saṃsāra.
Whoever studies this Atharvaśīrṣa obtains the fruit of the five Atharvaśīrṣas.
He who installs an image without knowing this Atharvaśīrṣa, even if he has recited it a hundred lakhs of times, [obtains no merit].
Nor does he obtain purity through ritual worship. One hundred and eight recitations are prescribed as his preliminary rite (*puraścaryā*).
He who recites it ten times is immediately liberated from sins; by the grace of the Great Goddess, he crosses over great difficulties. Reciting it in the evening...
It destroys the sins committed during the day. By practicing it in the morning and evening, one becomes sinless.

By reciting it at midnight or during the fourth twilight (turīyasandhyā), mastery over speech (*vāksiddhi*) is attained. By reciting it in the presence of a newly consecrated image, the presence of the deity (*devatāsānnidhya*) is established.
Having recited the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* [mantra], one becomes the deity.

Having recited [this] in the presence of Mahādevī on an Aśvinī day under the Bhauma (Mars) asterism, one crosses over great death; he who knows this indeed crosses over great death. Thus ends the Devyatharvaśīrṣopaniṣad.
Then the Lord spoke the Eightfold Hundred Names:
"I shall proclaim the hundred names; listen, O lotus-faced one!"
By the mere grace of whom Durgā shall always remain pleased. || 1 ||
She is Satī, the virtuous one, the beloved of Bhava, Bhavānī, the liberator from worldly existence;
she is Āryā, Durgā, Jayā, the primordial one, the three-eyed goddess, and the bearer of the trident.
She who bears the Pināka bow, the multiformed one, the one with the moon-bell, the one of great asceticism;
she who is mind, intellect, ego, and the form of consciousness; she who is the accumulated and the act of accumulating. || 3 ||
She consists of all mantras, she is the truth, whose nature is the bliss of truth;
she is infinite, the bringer of existence, that which is to be meditated upon, existence itself, that which is to be attained, and the eternal goal.
She is the consort of Śambhu, the mother of the gods, ever fond of her son Cintāmaṇi;
she is all-knowing, the daughter of Dakṣa, and the destroyer of Dakṣa’s sacrifice. || 5 ||
Aparṇā and Parṇā, Pāṭalā and Paṭalāvatī,
were dressed in fine silken garments and adorned with the tinkling of anklets.
Immeasurable in valor, Krūrā, Sundarī, Kulasundarī, Navadurgā, and Mātaṅgī, who is worshipped by the sage Mataṅga. (p. 427) || 7 ||
Brāhmī, Māheśvarī, Aindrī, Kaumārī, Vaiṣṇavī, as well as Cāmuṇḍā, Vārāhī, and Lakṣmī in human form. || 8 ||
She is Vimalotkarṣiṇī, the knowledge and action that bestows truth through speech;
she is Bahulā, possessed of abundant love, and she who rides upon all vehicles.
She is the slayer of Niśumbha and Śumbha, the crusher of the demon Mahiṣāsura,
the destroyer of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, and the annihilator of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa.
She is the destroyer of all asuras, the slayer of all dānavas;
she is the knowledge consisting of all scriptures and likewise the wielder of all weapons.
With many weapons in her hands and bearing various missiles,
she is the maiden, the girl, the youthful maiden, the young woman, and the ascetic.
Both the immature and the mature—the aged mother who bestows strength—he who recites this hymn, the "One Hundred and Eight Names of Durgā," [attains his desire]. (13)
O Goddess Pārvatī, there exists nothing unattainable in the three worlds—be it wealth, grain, sons, a wife, horses, or even elephants. (14)
Likewise, at the end, he shall obtain the fourfold goals and eternal liberation, having worshipped the maidens and meditated upon the Goddess, the sovereign of the gods. || 15 ||
One should worship with supreme devotion and recite the hundred-and-eight names;
O Goddess, for such a person, even by all the foremost of gods, success shall be attained.
Kings shall become his servants, and he shall obtain the glory of a kingdom. (16)

Having drawn the yantra according to the prescribed rite with gorocanā, lac, saffron, vermilion, camphor, and the three kinds of honey, the knower of the ritual shall always become Śiva himself for one who wears it. 17.
On the night of the new moon day of the month of Bhādra, when the moon has entered the asterism Śatabhiṣaj, one should write down and recite this hymn; he shall become a vessel for all prosperity.
Thus ends the one hundred and eight names.
Then the illustrious Goddess spoke the Thousand Names:
"The thousand names of mine were indeed fashioned by Śiva in the past."
Let that be recited according to the prescribed rule; then everything will come to pass. || 1 ||
Having spoken thus, the goddess Pārvatī caused them to hear that very same thousand names beginning with "Kārā," O lady of beautiful countenance.
The name of the deity Śrī Durgā is honored by all as the destroyer of disease, poverty, misfortune, grief, and suffering. (p. 428) 3.
One's own seed-syllable (bīja) shall be the seed; it is called the mantra-pin (kīlaka).
O Goddess, its application (viniyoga) is proclaimed for the fulfillment of all desires. || 4 ||
Dundurgā, the remover of misfortune, who dwells within the waters of Durgā. || 5 ||
She has entered the difficult path, she is one who enters the difficult path;
she makes her dwelling on the difficult path, and she is fond of conquering the difficult path.
Her form is grasped upon the difficult path; her very nature resides on the difficult path;
she is intent on praising the difficult path; she is intent on the recollection of the difficult path. || 7 ||
She is the eternal abode on the difficult path, she who delights in the difficult path,
she whose station is upon the ground of the difficult path, and she who sports upon the difficult path.
She who has cast off her garments on the difficult path, she who traverses the difficult path, the slayer of the demon Durga, and the destroyer of the demon Durga. || 9 ||
The messenger of Hara who removes the demon Durga; the destroyer of the demon Durga;
intoxicated by the slaying of the demon Durga; eager for the slaughter of the demon Durga. || 10 ||
She was enthusiastic about the slaying of the demon Durgāsura, intent upon the slaughter of the demon Durgāsura,
desirous of killing the demon Durgāsura, and the one who brought an end to the sacrifice of the demon Durgāsura.

She who is pleased by the destruction of the asura Durga, she who tears apart the dānava Durga, she who causes the difficult-to-conquer to flee, and she who is eternally the one who puts the unassailable to flight. 12.
She who causes the agitation of fortresses, she who cuts down the summits of fortresses;
she who brings about the destruction of fortresses, she who slays the Daityas within fortresses. || 13 ||
She who takes the life of the demon Durga, she who brings about the end of the demon Durga,
she who is the protector who removes the demon Durga, and she who is intoxicated by the blood of the demon Durga.

She is the devourer of the Daityas who are difficult to overcome, she is clothed in the hide of Durga, she causes the festival of battle with the invincible, and she is highly skilled in battle with the invincible. || 15 ||
She who delights in the battle for the fortress, she who crushes the battle for the fortress;
she who delights in laughter during the battle for the fortress, she who utters loud shouts of laughter during the battle for the fortress. || 16 ||

Greatly intoxicated by the battle for the fortress, following the course of the siege of the fortress, enthusiastic for the festival of the fortress-battle, she dwells in the region of the fortress. || 17 ||
She delights in dwelling in difficult places; she sports in difficult places;
she is intent on worshipping in difficult places; she is beloved by the people of difficult regions. || 18 ||

She resides in inaccessible places, she is the means for conquering inaccessible regions; she is difficult to attain, she dwells within the inaccessible, and her own essential nature is that of the inaccessible.
She is the connection between difficult paths, she is praised by those who traverse difficult paths;
she is difficult to understand for those on difficult paths, and she is esteemed by the sacred scriptures that are difficult to master. || 20 ||
She who is honored by the difficult-to-attain Vedas, she who is worshipped by the difficult-to-attain Vedas;
she who is well-pleased by the difficult-to-attain Vedas, and she who bestows joy upon the difficult-to-attain Vedas. (21)

She whose form is established in the difficult-to-attain Vedas, who takes pride in the difficult-to-attain Vedas, who is satisfied by difficult conduct, and who is pleased by difficult conduct. || 22 ||
She is perfected through difficult conduct, honored by difficult conduct, adorned with difficult conduct, and the bestower of difficult stations. || 23 ||
She is devoted to love that is difficult to attain, she bestows wealth that is difficult to obtain;
she dwells in the center of a lotus that is difficult to reach, and she resides within a lotus that is difficult to enter.
She whose movement is along the path of the difficult channels, who courses through the difficult channels;
she who delights in the lotuses of the difficult channels, who resides in the lotuses of the difficult channels. || 25 ||
She who has come from the difficult channel, she who has made her abode in the difficult channel,
she who delights in the difficult channel, and she who is praised by the Lord of the difficult channel.

Delighting in the Lord of the difficult channel, kissed by the Lord of the difficult channel, seated upon the lap of the Lord of the difficult channel, and longing for that which arises from the difficult channel. || 27 ||
She who ascends the difficult channel, she who frequents the difficult channels,
she who dwells in mountain caves and in places of refuge, she who brings an end to the demons.
She made her ascetic penance a mere cave, she made her worship of Hara a mere cave;
she made her desired objects a mere cave, and she made the act of love a mere cave. || 29 ||
She is worthy of being made into a cave by Hara; she is a doll played with in caves;
she delights in beholding caves; and she has had scorpions grown within her caves.
Abounding in caves, secret chambers, and wonders; intent on wandering through mountain clefts;
the destroyer of the demons; the one who rends asunder the lineage of the wretched Danujas. || 31 ||
The destroyer of the Danujas, the distressed one, the annihilator of the lords of the Danujas; the goddess who destroys the Dānavas and brings fear to the Dānavas. || 32 ||
She is the giver of gifts, worshipped by the Dānavas, the bestower of boons upon the lords of the Dānavas;
she is the slayer of the lords of the Dānavas and the virtuous one who hates the Dānavas.
She who delights in love for the enemy of Dānavas, she who is worshipped by the enemy of Dānavas,
she whose worship is performed by the enemy of Dānavas, and she who bestows prosperity upon the enemy of Dānavas.
She is the great bliss of the enemy of the Dānavas, she is dear to the beloved of the enemy of the Dānavas;
she delights in giving to the enemy of the Dānavas, and she has made her abode in the enemy of the Dānavas.
She delights in praising the ocean of nectar; she is fond of remembering the ocean of nectar; she rejoices in consuming the noble nectar of the Dānavas; she awakens the ocean of nectar. || 36 ||
She who holds love for the Dānavas, who liberates from suffering and grief, who destroys suffering, who bestows suffering, and who acts as the uprooter of suffering. || 37 ||
She who uproots suffering, she who destroys the enemy that is the ocean of suffering;
she who removes suffering, she who annihilates suffering, she who is difficult to approach for the multitude of sufferings. (38)
Free from suffering, yet a stream of sorrow; bestowing wealth and proper conduct;
satisfied by the relinquishing of wealth; and finding delight in the renunciation of riches. || 39 ||
She is satisfied by the touch of wealth; she bestows the honor of the touch of wealth;
she is rich with the joy of the touch of wealth; and she grants the satisfaction of the touch of wealth.
She who causes the touch of wealth, she who is intent on the touch of wealth, she who exerts herself for the touch of wealth, and she who is accomplished through the touch of wealth. 41.
She is known as Draviṇasparśanā, the daughter of Draviṇasparśa;
she is the protector of Draviṇasparśa and the bestower of heaps of wealth. || 42 ||
She who attracts wealth, she who bestows floods of riches,
she who is rich in the granting of mountains of gold, and she who dwells upon the mountain of wealth.
She is the mother of the distressed, the kinswoman of the wretched, and the destroyer of the obstacles of the lowly;
she is to be served by the destitute, perfected by the poor, and attainable by the humble—she who is clad in the directions as her garment.

She brings joy to the homes of the wretched; she is the playful mistress of the homes of the wretched; she delights in love for those in a state of misery; she dispels the sorrows of those in a state of misery. || 45 ||
Residing in the hearts of humble men, she bestows joy upon those lowly people;
she desires the destruction of the wretchedness of the distressed and grants wealth to the poor.
She is satisfied with meager means, she bestows a vision of the wretched, she grants sons and other blessings to the destitute, and she ordains prosperity for the lowly. || 47 ||
She is devoted to the meditation on Dattātreya, she is worshipped by Dattātreya, she has attained perfection through the sage Dattātreya, and she is manifested by Dattātreya. || 48 ||
She is worthy of worship by Dattātreya, she is adorned by Dattātreya, she bestows joy upon Dattātreya, and she grants happiness to Dattātreya. || 49 ||
She was always praised by Dattātreya, constantly honored by Dattātreya, devoted to love for Dattātreya, and esteemed by Dattātreya. || 50 ||
She is the one praised by Dattātreya, the wife of Dattātreya;
she is equal to the life-breath of Dattātreya and is the very embodiment of Dattātreya. || 51 ||
She who brings joy through Dattātreya, she who is born from a portion of Dattātreya, she who abides as the manifestation of Dattātreya, and she who follows Dattātreya. || 52 ||
She who delights in the songs of Dattātreya, who bestows the wealth of Dattātreya, who removes the suffering of Dattātreya, and who grants the boons of Dattātreya. || 53 ||
She is the giver of knowledge to Dattātreya, the remover of fear from Dattātreya;
she is the daughter of the gods, honored by the gods, and the destroyer of the suffering of the gods.
She is accomplished by the gods, worshipped by the gods, the object of sacrifice for the gods, and saluted by the gods;
she is honored by the gods, the source of prosperity for the gods, and the destroyer of the obstacles of the gods. (55)
Delightful to the gods, devoted to the gods, intent on the wonders of the gods;
the play of the gods, the modesty of the gods, and the destroyer of the enemies of the gods. || 56 ||
She who desires the gods, who is the beloved of the gods, who destroys those who hate the gods, the Goddess who is dear to the God of gods, and who is worshipped by gods and dānavas. || 57 ||

She who delights in the joy of the God of Gods, she who is eager for the excellence of the God of Gods, she who is devoted to love for the God of Gods, and she who speaks what is dear to the God of Gods. 58.
Equal in life-force to the God of gods, she is the lady of the God of gods;
her mind is captivated by the God of gods, and she brings happiness to the God of gods. || 59 ||
She who delights in the lap of the God of gods, she who bestows happiness upon the God of gods, she who is the great bliss of the God of gods, and she who is kissed by the God of gods. || 60 ||
She is enjoyed by the God of gods and served by the God of gods;
her life-breaths have gone to the God of gods, and her very self has gone to the God of gods.
She who bestows joy upon the God of gods, she who grants happiness to the God of gods, she who is the great bliss of the God of gods, and she who is the playful consort of the God of gods. || 62 ||
She is the lawful wife of the God of gods, she whose mind is fixed on the God of gods;
she is the consort of the God of gods, and she who delights in the worship of the God of gods.
She whose abode is the body of the God of Gods; she who reclines upon the body of the God of Gods;
she who finds bliss in the body of the God of Gods; she who dwells within the body of the God of Gods. 64.
She is the ornament upon the body of the God of Gods, and she is the adornment of the God of Gods’ own limbs;
she brings joy to the God of Gods and brings an end to that which is displeasing to the God of Gods.
She whose life-breath is dear to the God of gods; she whose very self is dear to the God of gods;
she whose life-breath is the worshipper of the God of gods; she who is dear to the worshipper of the God of gods. || 66 ||
She is the zeal for the worship of the God of gods, she is dear to the worshiper of the God of gods;
she is the obstacles to the worshiper of the God of gods, and she is also the mother of the God of gods.
The mother of the God of Gods, the creator of the God of Gods;
the beloved of the God of Gods, whose heart is the refuge of the God of Gods. (68)
The beloved goddess of the gods of gods, she who causes the falling away of gods and ascetics;
she who is satisfied by the state of divinity, and gratified by the state of divinity. || 69 ||
She is the bestower of the state of divinity and the granting of boons; she is the giver of the accomplishment of the state of divinity;
she is fully perfected as the state of divinity and originates from the state of divinity.
Happy through the state of divinity, she is saluted by those who possess the state of divinity;
well-pleased by the state of divinity, she bestows joy upon the state of divinity.
She is the destroyer of obstacles for the deities, the annihilator of those hostile to the deities;
her feet are worshipped by the deities, and she is pleased by the love of the deities. || 72 ||
She whose abode is the temple of the deities, who bestows the happiness of the deities, whose own nature is that of the deities, and whose mind is captivated by the deities. (73)
She whose feet are worshipped by the deities, who receives devotion from the deities, who stands amidst the pride of the deities, and who is the deity of the deities. (74)
Salutations to Dundurgā, whose name is Namonāmnī; she is the embodiment of the mantra *dūṃ phaṭ*, the form of the mantra *dūṃ namo*, and her very self is the manifestation of *dūṃ namo*.
She is beloved by those who see afar; she is frequented by both the wicked and the virtuous;
she delights in the love of those who see afar; and she is the speech dear to those who see afar.
She who bestows the siddhi of far-sightedness, she who is gratified by those with far-sighted vision, she who resides upon the neck of Dūradarśin, and she who is gladdened by Dūradarśin. || 77 ||

She who accepts worship from those with far-reaching vision, she who gratifies those with far-reaching vision, she who is equal to the very life-breath of those with far-reaching vision, and she who bestows happiness upon those with far-reaching vision. || 78 ||
She removes the delusions of those who see afar; she is the abode of the hearts of those who see afar;
she possesses the state of being an enemy to those who see afar; and she brings joy to those who possess long-range vision.
Equal to long-sighted beings, she is the bestower of boons upon the long-sighted;
she grants joy to the long-sighted and is herself delighted by those of far-reaching vision. || 80 ||
She is the great joy of the far-sighted, the dwelling-place for the far-sighted,
she whose worship is accepted by the far-sighted, and she who receives the offerings of the far-sighted.
She is compassion itself, possessing generosity, the giver, merciful, and affectionate toward the distressed;
she is moistened by compassion, compassionate by nature, rich in compassion, and whose very essence is compassion.
She is an ocean of compassion, the essence of compassion, one who has reached the further shore of the sea of compassion;
she is a river of compassion, the burden of compassion, the compassionate one, and the source of mercy.
The Goddess is compassionate and affectionate, always delighting in mercy and charity; she finds happiness in devotion to the merciful and is fully satisfied by those who possess compassion. 84.

She is devoted to compassion and affection; she is the one who manifests compassion; she is the one who provides protection through compassion; and she is the one who bestows liberation through compassion. || 85 ||
She is satisfied by the state of being compassionate, gratified by compassion;
she is intent on rescuing through compassion and bestows the attainment of success through compassion.
She whose disposition is like that of a compassionate son, she who takes the form of a compassionate son;
she whose abode is the body of the compassionate, she who is the kinsman of compassion, and she who is the refuge of compassion. || 87 ||

She who acts with compassion and affection, she who bestows the perfection of compassion, she who is devoted to those who seek refuge in the compassionate, and she whose temple is the body of the compassionate. 88.

She abides in the state of compassionate devotion; she is the very life-breath of the merciful; she is the deceptive form that bestows happiness upon the compassionate; she showers the rain of love for those who are kind. || 89 ||
She was under the sway of compassion; she was tall, with long limbs, long eyes, long eyelashes, and long vision, her body consisting of long, vine-like arms.
She has long hair, a long face, and a long nose; she is formidable.
She is the slayer of dreadful asuras and the tearer of dreadful asuras. || 91 ||
She who performs the terrible battle, she who rejoices in the terrible battle, she who is rich in the oblations of the terrible battle, and she who destroys the terrible mountain. || 92 ||
Devoted to fierce conduct, delighted by fierce festivals,
possessing a form intent on fierceness, she is the warder-off of fierce enemies.
Endowed with a fierce gaze, she is adorned with four arms;
she possesses ten eyes and ten hands, resplendent with ten arms. (94)
The Goddess who bears ten weapons, whose prowess is renowned in the ten directions, whose feet are worshipped by Daśaratha, and who is forever beloved by the son of Daśaratha. 95.
Satisfied by her love for the son of Daśaratha, she is most dear to the son of Daśaratha;
she acts for the welfare of the son of Daśaratha and is the beloved of the son of Daśaratha. 96.

She who bestows what is desired by the son of Daśaratha, she who is the deity worshipped by the son of Daśaratha, she who destroys those who hate the son of Daśaratha, and she who grants favor to the descendants of Daśaratha. 97.
The most beloved of the son of Daśaratha, worshipped by the son of Daśaratha;
she who is to be honored by the enemy of the ten-faced Rāvaṇa, and the deity of the enemy of the ten-faced one. 98.

She is the consort of the enemy of the ten-faced one, the birthplace of the enemy of the ten-faced one, the bestower of delight upon the enemy of the ten-faced one, and she who is served by the enemy of the ten-faced one. 99.
She who bestows happiness upon the enemy of the ten-faced one, she who was taken by the enemy of the enemy of the ten-faced one;
she who is the chosen deity of the women of the ten-faced one, she who is saluted by the enemy of the ten-necked one. 100.
She is the mother of the ten-headed enemy of Arjuna, she is the one who brings about the destruction of the ten-headed enemy,
she is united with the enemy of the ten-headed one, and she is honored by the assembly of the ten-headed one.
She is the beloved of the enemy of the ten-headed one, and also the daughter-in-law of the ten-headed one;
she is the destroyer of the ten-headed one, and the bestower of boons upon the ten-headed one.
She resides before the Ten-necked One, she is eager for the slaying of the Ten-necked One, she is the giver of joy to the Ten-necked One, and she is the destroyer of the Ten-necked One. || 103 ||
She who causes the battle with the Ten-necked one, she who never departs from the Ten-necked one,
she who is dear to the Ten-necked one, she who is worthy of worship, and likewise she who was carried away by the Ten-necked one.

She who brings about the destruction of the Ten-necked one, she who is beloved by the Lord of the Ten-necked one, she who is the very life-breath of the Lord of the Ten-necked one, and she who bestows boons upon the Ten-necked one. (105)
The mistress of the Ten-Necked One is delighted with ten-year-old maidens;
she is fond of ten-year-old girls and dwells among those who are ten years old. (106)
She who removes the ten sins, who is to be tamed, who is adorned with ten hands, whose ten weapons gleam with brilliance, and who is worshipped by the guardians of the ten directions. || 107 ||
She possesses the forms of the ten incarnations and is embodied as the ten incarnations;
she is the Goddess distinct from the ten sciences and is the very nature of the ten vital breaths.
She is the embodiment of the ten sciences and likewise consists of the ten sciences;
she is the nature of vision, the bestower of vision, the form of vision, and the illuminator of vision.

She who dwells in the furthest reaches of every direction, she who is the celestial nymph of the sky-clad ones, she who resides within the assembly of the sky-clad ones, and she who is worshipped by the sky-clad ones. (110)
She is the companion of the sky-clad (Digambara), she has made her abode in the sky-clad, her mind is captivated by the sky-clad, and she is fond of the stories of the sky-clad. || 111 ||
She who delights in the virtues of the sky-clad, she whose very nature is the sky-clad,
she who is to be borne upon the heads of the sky-clad, and she who has taken refuge in the hearts of the sky-clad.
She is devoted to love for the Digambara, she is intensely longing for the Digambara, she possesses the very nature of a Digambarī, and she is worshipped by the hosts of Digambarīs. || 113 ||

She whose life is the host of Digambara women, she who is dear to the host of Digambara women, she who is worshipped by the host of Digambara women, she who is the sovereign of the host of Digambara women. || 114 ||
She is intoxicated by the drinking of wine from the touch of the host of naked women;
she is surrounded by ten million naked women and encompassed by the multitude of naked women. || 115 ||
She who brings an end to existence, who removes evil deeds, who is difficult to contemplate, and who is hard to overcome;
she who hates the wicked Dānavas and brings about the destruction of the evil Danujas. 116.
She is the destroyer of enduring evil, the one who effects the deliverance of the Aśvins;
she resides within the minds of the Aśvins and increases the wisdom of the Aśvins. || 117 ||
She who generates the enjoyment of the Aśvins, she who bestows the enjoyment of the Aśvins;
she whose abode is the enjoyment of the Aśvins, she who ordains the knowledge of the Aśvins. || 118 ||

She who removes the distress of the Dasras, the mother of the Dasras, beautiful as the Dasras; she whose command is the knowledge for the performance of devotion to the Dasras, and she who destroys those hostile to the Dasras. || 119 ||

She who subdues those who harm the Dasras, she who bestows the accomplishments (siddhis) of the Dasras, she who is propitiated by the star Dasra, and she who is worshipped by the mother of the Dasras. || 120 ||

She who removes the distress of the Aśvins, she who is served by the sons of the Aśvins, she whose splendor is equal to hundreds of fathers of the Aśvins, and she who bestows the skill of the Aśvins. || 121 ||
She who is accompanied by the enemy of the ten-headed one, she who is the beloved of the enemy of the ten-headed one;
she who is the goddess of the city of the ten-headed one, she who is honored by the ten-headed one.
She who is well-pleased with the enemy of the ten-headed one, she who is dear to the wife of the ten-headed one;
she who is the cutter-off of the heads of the ten-headed one, she who possesses hips like those of the ten-headed one.
She whose life-force is the destroyer of the ten-headed one; she whose very essence is the destroyer of the ten-headed one;
she who is to be propitiated by the destroyer of the ten-headed one; she who is saluted by the enemies of the ten-headed one. 124.
She who bestows happiness upon the enemy of the ten-headed one, she who holds the skull of the ten-headed one;
she who grants the knowledge of the ten-headed one, she who has taken the body of the enemy of the ten-headed one. 125.
She who has assumed the form of Śrī Rāmacandra through the slaying of the ten-headed one;
she who is the sovereign goddess of the kingdom of the ten-headed one; she who is the destroyer of the enemies of the ten-headed one. || 126 ||

She who delights in the brother with ten heads, she who is dear to the wife of the ten-headed one; she whose life is the wife of the ten-headed one, she who is devoted to the wife of the ten-headed one. (127)
She who is devoted to the preceptor of the Daityas, the virtuous one; she who is worshipped by the preceptor of the Daityas;
she who is the instructor of the preceptor of the Daityas; and she who is served by the preceptor of the Daityas. || 128 ||
She whose life-breath is centered in the preceptor of the Daityas; she who destroys the torment of the preceptor of the Daityas;
she who pacifies insurmountable suffering; she who subdues the wicked. 129.
She who pacifies endless sorrow, she who destroys endless disease, she who subdues endless enemies, and she who annihilates endless demons. || 130 ||
She is the destroyer of long-standing impurities and the annihilator of the multitude of evil deeds;
she is difficult of intent, difficult to support, invincible, and the subduer of the wicked who lust after her. || 131 ||
She is beautiful to behold, visible, and within the range of vision;
she is fond of the messenger-sacrifice (*dūtīyāga*), she is the messenger (*dūtī*), and she is fond of performing the messenger-sacrifice. || 132 ||
She who brings bliss through the sacrifice of the messenger (dūtī), she who bestows the happiness of the messenger-sacrifice;
she who has come for the sake of the messenger-sacrifice, she who rejoices in the messenger-sacrifice. || 133 ||
She who is worshipped by Durvāsas, who is the Dūrvā grass, who is meditated upon by the sages, whose feet are honored by Durvāsas, and who is the one contemplated by the sage Durvāsas. || 134 ||

She who is worshipped by the sage Durvāsas, she whose deity is the sage Durvāsas, she who is the mother of the sage Durvāsas, and she who bestows the spiritual perfections (siddhi) upon the sage Durvāsas. || 135 ||
Abiding in the state of the sage Durvāsas, served by the sage Durvāsas, residing in the mind of the sage Durvāsas, and adorned by the sage Durvāsas. || 136 ||
She is frequented by the sage Durvāsas; she is dear to the heart of Durvāsas; she is to be propitiated by the heart of Durvāsas; she dwells in the lotus-heart of Durvāsas. 137.
She is worshipped by the ascetic Durvāsas, she is the refuge of the ascetic Durvāsas,
she delights in the ascetic Durvāsas, and she is the sovereign of the ascetic Durvāsas.
She is the daughter of the sage Durvāsas, the bestower of siddhis born from Durvāsas;
she is the night of dissolution, the destroyer of fear, endowed with compassion, and the remover of terror.
She is the one who strikes, the destroyer, she who is joined with fear, and she who is the refuge from fear. || 140 ||
She is of gentle smile, with slightly sidelong glances; she is the giver of compassion and the abode of mercy.
She is worshipped by the Aśvins, the mother of the Aśvins, the goddess of the Aśvins, and she is intoxicated by her own splendor.
She is perfected by the Dasras, established in the Dasras, the liberator from the afflictions of the Dasras;
she eternally removes the agitation of the Dasras, and her essence has reached the world of the Dasras. || 142 ||
She is worshipped by the wives of the preceptor of the Daityas; she is beloved by the wives of the preceptor of the Daityas;
she is perfected by the wives of the preceptor of the Daityas; she is eager for the wives of the preceptor of the Daityas. || 143 ||
She is the most beloved of the preceptor of the Daityas and is served by the preceptor of the Daityas;
she has the form of the mother of the preceptor of the gods and is honored by the preceptor of the gods. (144)
Endowed with love for the divine teacher, honored by the divine teacher, knowing the power of the divine teacher, she bestows happiness upon the divine teacher. 145.
She who bestows knowledge upon the preceptor of the gods, she who delights the preceptor of the gods;
she who is worshipped by the hosts of Daitya women, she who is honored by the hosts of Daitya women. || 146 ||
She assumes the forms of hosts of Daitya women and captivates the hearts of the Daitya women;
she is worshipped by hosts of celestial women and saluted by hosts of celestial women. || 147 ||
She dwells in the hearts of the hosts of celestial women; she is adorned by the hosts of celestial women;
she is perfected by the hosts of celestial women; she is gratified by the hosts of celestial women. || 148 ||
Fanned by beautiful whisks held in the hands of hosts of celestial women, and anointed with lovely perfumes held in the hands of hosts of celestial women. (149)
The moon-like face was gazed upon by the goddesses as they held up mirrors,
while it was filled with longing for the betel leaves offered by the celestial nymphs.
She beholds the garlands of lamps held in the hands of the hosts of celestial women; she is delighted by the scent of incense held in the hands of the hosts of celestial women. (151)
She drinks the *vāsaka* and *āsave* held in the hands of celestial women;
she cleanses the hair that has been shaved by the combs of celestial women. 152.
Her limbs were thrilled by the celestial nymphs; she was filled with longing for the celestial nymphs;
and she was adorned with flower garlands fashioned by the celestial nymphs. || 153 ||
Her limbs were adorned with celestial women; she was fed by the wives of the gods;
she was sung to by the throngs of celestial women; and she was eager for the songs of the celestial women. || 154 ||
She finds delight in the dance of the celestial women, she displays the dance of the celestial women, and her lotus-like feet are adorned with shimmering jewels set by the celestial women. 155.
Seated upon a beautiful couch spread out by hosts of celestial women, her body and limbs were touched by the graceful hands of divine damsels. 156.
Pleasant with the breeze from palm-leaf fans held in the hands of celestial women, and its mind filled with longing for the sounds of the flutes and lutes of the celestial women. || 157 ||
Praised by ten million gods, honored by ten million gods, her virtues sung by ten million gods, and lauded by ten million gods. || 158 ||
With the result of agitation caused by the biting of teeth, she is filled with the clamor of divine beings;
she is entirely abandoned by hatred and passion, being devoid of both hatred and passion. || 159 ||
She who is worshipful with a rope, whose ornament is a rope, who sports with Dāmodara, who delights in love for Dāmodara, and who is also the sister of Dāmodara. || 160 ||
The mother of Dāmodara, the wife of Dāmodara, devoted to her husband, whose body was non-different from Dāmodara, and who was dear to the pleasure of Dāmodara. || 161 ||
Her body is non-different from Dāmodara; she has made her abode in Dāmodara;
her life-breaths are established in Dāmodara; her very self is centered in Dāmodara. (162)
Rich with the curiosity for Dāmodara, she is the essence of the arts of Dāmodara;
her limbs are embraced by Dāmodara, and she is full of wonder for Dāmodara. || 163 ||
She who brings delight to Dāmodara, she who is beautifully kissed by Dāmodara, she who is drawn toward Dāmodara, and she who bestows happiness upon Dāmodara. || 164 ||
She is enriched by the companionship of Dāmodara, she is the consort of Dāmodara, she knows the virtues of Dāmodara, and she is the bestower of boons upon Dāmodara. || 165 ||
She is favorable to Dāmodara, the broad-hipped consort of Dāmodara, skilled in the water-sports of Dāmodara, and fond of being beheld. 166.
She who has abandoned affection for her own kin through her childhood play with Dāmodara, and likewise she who delights in the curiosity of the playful dance with the smiling Dāmodara. 167.
She has Dāmodara as her brother, she is devoted to Dāmodara, she bears Dāmodara, and she is the destroyer of Dāmodara’s enemies. || 168 ||
She is the wife of Dāmodara, invited by Dāmodara, surpassed by Dāmodara, and conquered by Dāmodara. || 169 ||
She is embraced by Dāmodara; she has destroyed the inauspiciousness of Dāmodara;
she delights in the festival of Dāmodara; and she brings about the festival of Dāmodara. 170.
She is the giver of breast-milk to Dāmodara, she who is sought after by Dāmodara;
she is the bestower of success upon Damayantī, and she who is adorned by Damayantī. || 171 ||
She is the beloved deity of Damayantī, she possesses the very form of Damayantī,
she is the object of Damayantī’s worship, and she was manifested by the sage Dama.
Equal in life-force to the sage Damanarṣi, she possesses the very form of the sage Damanarṣi;
she is the embodiment of the sage Damanarṣi, yet her physical form is filled with pride.
The destroyer of hypocrisy, the giver of hypocrisy, the deluder of the world through hypocrisy;
she whose nature is hypocrisy, the remover of hypocrisy, and the one who utterly crushes those possessed by hypocrisy. || 174 ||
She is the embodiment of hypocrisy, the creator of hypocrisy, and the one who tears asunder the lineage of hypocrisy;
she is the giver of liberation, the giver of wealth, the giver of health, and yet she is also the hypocritical one.
She whose sons were given away, whose wife was given away, and whose necklace was given away;
she whose enjoyments were given away, whose grief was given away, and whose elephants and other mounts were given away. (176)

She who bestows a wife not previously given, she who provides understanding of the scriptures, she who grants drink, she who bestows gifts, and she who destroys the poverty of those to whom she has been given. || 177 ||
She has bestowed dwellings and lands, she has granted heaven, and she is the giver of servants;
she is pleased by service, she removes servitude, and she bestows hundreds of male and female slaves. (178)
She whose form is wood, who dwells in wood, whose heart-abode is in wood;
she who is worshipped by the people dwelling in wood, and who is beloved by the people dwelling in wood. (179)
She is brought forth by Dāravāsin, she is worshipped by Dāravāsin;
her life-breaths were taken away by Dāravāsin, and she is the destroyer of Dāravāsin’s enemies. || 180 ||
She is the remover of obstacles dwelling in the home, the bestower of liberation from those dwelling in the home;
she is the form of the fire of the household, the wife, and the destroyer of enemies in the form of children. || 181 ||
She was beloved by couples, the very life-breath of her husband, devoted to the love between husband and wife, and fond of the means for strengthening the marital bond. || 182 ||
She was an army of conjugal bliss, bestowing the happiness of marriage;
she was devoted to the conduct of a married couple and delighted in the joy of husband and wife. (183)
She who finds happiness in the fragrance of the couple, she who brings delight to the husband and wife;
she whose lotus feet are cherished by couples, and she who is the very embodiment of conjugal love. || 184 ||
She is the abode of conjugal enjoyment, she who eats pomegranate fruit,
she who is content with pomegranate fruit, and she whose mind is fixed on the pomegranate fruit.
She has the form of a pomegranate tree, she dwells in a pomegranate tree, she has the appearance of a pomegranate tree, and she resides in a grove of pomegranate trees. || 186 ||
Devoid of breasts that resemble pomegranate fruits, she is Dakṣiṇā, whose form is the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), and who assumes the form of the sacrificial fee. || 187 ||
She is the daughter of Dakṣa, the progeny of Dakṣa, the mother of Dakṣa, and the offspring of Dakṣa;
she belongs to the lineage of Dakṣa, is the daughter of Dakṣa, and is the destroyer of Dakṣa’s sacrifice. || 188 ||
She is the destroyer of Dakṣa’s sacrifice, the bringer of an end to Dakṣa’s sacrifice;
she is the progeny of Dakṣa, the object of Dakṣa’s worship, and the sole purifier of Dakṣa’s lineage.
She is the daughter of Dakṣa, the son of Dakṣa, born of Dakṣa, and belonging to the lineage of Dakṣa;
she is born from Dakṣa, has Dakṣa as her progenitor, and is produced from the body of Dakṣa.
Born of Dakṣa, she is the destroyer of Dakṣa’s sacrifice;
she is the daughter of Dakṣa, devoted to right conduct, and the bestower of satisfaction through right conduct. || 191 ||
She is perfected through right conduct, cultivated by right conduct, happy through right conduct, and accomplished by right conduct. || 192 ||

She who attains liberation through the practice of the right-hand path, she who is praised by those of the right-hand practice, she who takes refuge in the right-hand practice, and she who rejoices in the right-hand practice. || 193 ||
She is the beloved of the door-keepers, the dweller at the gate, she who stands at the gateway;
she is the form of the door, established at the door, and the inhabitant of the region of the door. || 194 ||
She is the maker of the gateway, the sustainer of the gate, and entirely devoid of faults;
she is the creator of defects, the remover of defects, and the destroyer of the mass of defects.
Richly adorned with the ornaments of the moon, she who bears the skull of the moon;
possessing the luster of a thousand moons, her face is like the moon. (196)
Divine, with a face like the moon, born from the tips of the rays of the moon,
possessing a luster equal to the moon, and as cool as the moon.
She whose side-glances resemble the moon, she who is the beloved deity of the moon, and she who is served by the moon.

She whose form is the life-force of the moon (the mine of defects), who is a mirage of the moon (the mine of defects), whose forehead shines with the moon (the mine of defects), and who brings great joy to the moon (the mine of defects). || 199 ||
She is the head-ornament of the moon; she is dear to the wife of the moon; she is the life-breath of the wife of the moon; she is considered the beloved of the wife of the moon. 200.
She who delights in the consort of the moon (the night), she who is the consort of the moon;
she who is worshipped at night, as well as she who is worshipped by the night; she who removes all defects. || 201 ||
She is the great bliss born from the recitation of faults, devoted to the recitation of faults;
she delights in the preliminary rites of faults and possesses sons who worship the faults.
The Mother of the World, who shows affection to those who worship at dusk, who slays the enemies of those who worship at dusk, and who removes the obstacles of those who worship at dusk. || 203 ||
She is satisfied by those who worship faults; she grants liberation to those who worship faults.
She is to be worshipped with the flowers of self-restraint and always delights in the flowers of self-restraint.
She is worshipped by Duryodhana, honored by Duḥśāsana, beloved by Daṇḍapāṇi, the mother of Daṇḍapāṇi, and a treasure-house of compassion. (205)
She who is to be propitiated by Daṇḍapāṇi, she who is worshipped by Daṇḍapāṇi,
she who is attached to the home of Daṇḍapāṇi, and she who speaks what is dear to Daṇḍapāṇi.
She is beloved by Daṇḍapāṇi, she is charming to Daṇḍapāṇi;
she has taken the life of Daṇḍapāṇi, and she bestows excellent siddhi upon Daṇḍapāṇi.
She is touched by Daṇḍapāṇi, delighted by Daṇḍapāṇi, the remover of obstacles for Daṇḍapāṇi, and held upon the head of Daṇḍapāṇi. || 208 ||
She who has reached the hand that holds the staff, she who is ever intent upon the one who holds the staff;
she whose feet have reached the one who holds the staff, she who is intent upon the boon-granting one who holds the staff. || 209 ||
She who holds a staff in her hand, whose hand wields a staff, whose arm is a staff, the end-maker of the terrible;
she who bestows punishment, whose hands are instruments of punishment, and whose abode is made by a mind intent on punishment. 210.
She is the science of the staff, the mother of the staff-bearer, the destroyer of those who break the staff;
she is dear to the staff-bearer, worthy of worship by the staff-bearer, and the bestower of satisfaction upon the staff-bearer. || 211 ||
She is worshipped by the Dasyus, she possesses the nature of a Dasyu, she bestows wealth upon the Dasyus;
she is worthy of honor by the host of Dasyus, and she is the destroyer of the host of Dasyus. || 212 ||
The destroyer of bandits, likewise the annihilator of the race of bandits;
she who acts for the benefit of bandits, and she who is intent upon witnessing the dance of bandits. (213)
She who inflicts punishment upon the wicked, she who puts to flight the hosts of the evil, she who is worthy of subduing the wicked, and she who destroys the lives of those who corrupt. || 214 ||
She generates remorse in the corrupter, she brings about misfortune for the corrupter;
she causes hatred toward the corrupter, she is burning, and her nature is that of fire. || 215 ||
She is the slayer of Dārakāri, worshipped by Dārukeśvara;
she is the mother of Dārakeśvara and is saluted by Dārukeśvara. || 216 ||
She holds darbha grass in her hand, she is endowed with darbha grass, she is free from the ritual acts involving darbha grass;
she consists of darbha grass, her body is made of darbha grass, and she is the embodiment of the totality of all that is darbha grass.
She is devoted to the practice of darbha-grass rites; she offers worship with darbha-grass in her hand;
she is favorable to darbha-grass; she possesses the splendor of darbha-grass; and she is adorned with a luster like that of a sacrificial ladle.
She is the one to be worshipped by Damaghoṣa, the bestower of boons upon Damaghoṣa,
she who is propitiated by Damaghoṣa, and likewise she who has the form of a forest fire.
She has the form of a forest fire, by which the great strength of the forest fire is destroyed;
she possesses the power of the teeth and fangs of a demon, and her hands are smeared with ivory.

She whose chariot is her tusks and fangs, by whom the Asuras were destroyed with her tusks, she who is to be worshipped with curds, who is delighted by curds, and who granted boons to Dadhīci. || 221 ||
She is the chosen deity of Dadhīci, the bestower of liberation upon Dadhīci, the slayer of Dainya, and the renter of Dadhīci’s ribs. || 222 ||
She who finds happiness in devotion to Dadhīci, she who is served by the sage Dadhīci, she who bestows the knowledge of Dadhīci, and she who grants the virtues of Dadhīci. || 223 ||
She is the ornament of the lineage of Dadhīci, the bestower of enjoyment and liberation to Dadhīci, the goddess of the lineage of Dadhīci, and the deity of the lineage of Dadhīci. || 224 ||
She is approachable by the lineage of Dadhīci, she is worshipped by the lineage of Dadhīci, she is the bestower of happiness upon Dadhīci, and she is the remover of the distress of Dadhīci. || 225 ||
She is the destroyer of Dadhīci’s sorrow, the beauty of Dadhīci’s lineage, born of Dadhīci’s family, and the protectress of Dadhīci’s clan. || 226 ||

She who is to be approached through the gift of Dadhīci, she who considers herself worthy of the gift of Dadhīci, she who is satisfied by the gift of Dadhīci, and she who is the deity of the gift of Dadhīci. || 227 ||

She who is well-pleased by the recitation of Dadhīci, whose mind is intent on the recitation of Dadhīci, who is enriched by the worship and recitation of Dadhīci, and who wears a rosary for the recitation of Dadhīci. || 228 ||
Satisfied by the recitations of Dadhīci, she who is pleased by the recitations of Dadhīci;
she who is propitiated by the penance of Dadhīci, she who bestows auspiciousness upon Dadhīci. || 229 ||
Dūrvā is dark-green like a blade of dūrvā grass, possessing a luster equal to a blade of dūrvā;
thus is the thousand names of Durgā, beginning with "Dā," proclaimed. (230)
The sovereign of practitioners who recites this, being self-controlled and pure at dawn, midday, and twilight, shall obtain all supernatural powers (siddhis). || 231 ||
Likewise, at the time of midnight, like another Maheśa,
that great hero, joined with his Śakti, should perform worship during the deep night.
One who possesses the nature of perfection should recite this hymn of praise to Mahādevī with the five supreme substances beginning with the letter *ma*. 233.
In a temple, in a cremation ground, on the bank of the Gaṅgā, in one's own home,
in the house of a courtesan, and even in the presence of the venerable Guru— 234.
One should always recite this hymn on a mountain, in a wilderness, or in a terrible place;
for by means of the Thousand Names of Durgā, one beholds Durgā with one's own eyes.
A hundred recitations of this is said to be the preliminary rite (puraścaraṇa).
This essence of praise has been declared; what more do you wish to hear? 236.
Thus ends the *Sahasranāmastotra* of Durgā, beginning with the letter ‘A’, in the venerable *Kulārṇava*.
Thus ends the *Durgātantra* in the *Śāktapramoda*.
Composed and compiled by the sovereign King Śrī Rājā Deva Nandana Siṃha Bāhādura, the lord of the capital city of Śiva-Hara and the possessor of prosperity.
The fourteenth Śivatantra, contained within the Śāktapramoda.
This has been edited by Paṇḍita Śrī Raghurāja Dubejī, a descendant of the aforementioned royal preceptor.
Printed and published by Śrī Kṛṣṇadāsātmaja Khemarāja at his own Śrī Veṅkaṭeśvara Press.
Mumbai. Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa. Now begins the Śāktapramoda.
Now follows the Śiva-tantra; now follows the meditation on Śiva:
one should constantly meditate upon Maheśa, who resembles a mountain of silver and is adorned with the beautiful crescent moon.
I bow to the one whose limbs are radiant with ornaments of jewels, who holds in his hands the axe, the deer, the boon-granting gesture,

and the gesture of fearlessness; who is gracious, seated upon a lotus, praised on all sides by hosts of gods, clad in a tiger skin, the primordial source of the universe, the seed of the universe, the remover of all fears, five-faced, and three-eyed.
(p. 446) Now, regarding the extraction of the diagram (*yantra*): one should draw a diagram with eight lotus petals even when no specific ritual procedure (*kalpa*) has been stated.
Therein is a six-cornered pericarp, adorned with four gates.
Now, the extraction of the mantra:
Having extracted the word of salutation (namas), followed by the letter *va* joined with the eye (*i*),
then the letter of Varuṇa (*va*) with the face-circle (*u*), and the letter of Vāyu (*ya*) joined with the forehead (*ma*).
O Goddess, when this five-syllabled mantra, which bestows the fruit of the five desires,
begins with the *praṇava* (Om), then it becomes a six-syllabled mantra.
Now the mantra: Oṃ namaśśivāya. Now the procedure for worship.

Having performed the morning rites and other duties, having gone to the house of worship, having sat upon a seat, and having lit the lamp, one should worship the lamp with "Oṃ dīṃ, obeisance to Dīpanātha," and then, having performed the expulsion of obstructing spirits (*bhūtāpasarpaṇa*), one should begin the worship. It is as follows: Now, the meditation (*dhyāna*).
The god who resembles the bandhūka flower, who has three eyes and the moon as his crest-jewel,
who wields the trident, who possesses a beautiful smile, and who is perfectly pure.
One should always meditate upon Śambhu, the Lord of Soma, who holds a skull, whose hands grant boons and fearlessness, and who is accompanied by Umā. Thus is the meditation.
Now, the invocation.
"Come, O Blessed One, O Śambhu, O Śarva, O Lord of the Daughter of the Mountain!
Be gracious, O Lord of Gods; salutations indeed unto you, O Śaṅkara! Thus is the invocation.
Now, the seat.
"O Viśveśvara, Mahādeva, beloved of the Rājarājeśvara! O Īśāna, O Īśvara, I offer this divine seat to you. Thus is the seat.
Now, the water for the feet:
"O Mahādeva, O Maheśāna, O Mahādeva, O Supreme beyond the supreme!
O Lord, together with Pārvatī, accept this water for the feet offered by me. Thus ends the water for the feet.
Now, for the *arghya*:
"O Lord Tryambaka, you who are the embodiment of eternal conduct and the creator of the beginning of the world;
O God, together with Ambā, bestower of all goals, please accept this *arghya*. Thus ends the *arghya*.
Now, the water for sipping: O Destroyer of Tripura, Dispeller of the Suffering of the Distressed, Śrīkaṇṭha, Eternal One! Accept this water for sipping, prepared with pure water.
Thus ends the water for sipping. Now follows the bath with cow’s milk.
O Lord of the gods, O Supreme Lord, accept this auspicious milk from the Madhuranga cow, purified by a cloth and presented before you for the purpose of your bath.
Thus ends the milk bath. Now follows the curd bath.
O Lord of Pārvatī, please accept this most rare, delicious curd, which is supremely dear to all, for the purpose of your bath.
Thus ends the bath with curd. Now follows the bath with ghee.
O Lord of the Daughter of the Mountain, O Moon-crested One, accept this pure, unctuous cow’s ghee, which is most worthy of use for those desiring nourishment, for the purpose of your bath.
Thus ends the bath with clarified butter. Now follows the bath with honey.
Sweet, gentle, destroying delusion, and removing hoarseness of voice.
"O Mahādeva, O Śaṅkara, this has been released for your bath."
Thus concludes the honey bath. Now follows the sugar bath.
O Lord of the Gods of gods, this sugar, which pacifies heat, is cool, and endowed with a sweet taste, is offered for the purpose of bathing.
Thus concludes the bath with sugar. Now follows the bath with pure water.
May the Gaṅgā, Godāvarī, Revā, Payoṣṇī,
Yamunā, Sarasvatī, and other sacred fords (tīrthas) accept [this] for the purpose of bathing.
Now, the ritual bath with the Śatarudrīya. Its procedure is as follows:
The *namaste rudra* hymn and again the sixteenth [hymn], as well as "eṣa te" twice, "namaste" twice, and "natavid" twice.
One should recite "mīḍhuṣṭama," "aṣṭa," and "catvāri" as the four [sections], and one should mutter the eighth.

Oṃ! Salutations to you, O Rudra, for your wrath, and also salutations to your arrow; salutations also to your two arms. (1) O Rudra, that auspicious form of yours which is non-terrible and free from the appearance of evil—with that most peaceful form, O Lord of the Mountain, look upon us with favor. (2)
O Girisha, you carry that arrow in your hand for the purpose of hurling it.
O Śivāṅgiras, act thus; do not harm the person or the world. || 3 ||
With auspicious speech, O Lord of the Mountain, we address you, so that this entire world of ours may be free from disease and well-disposed toward us. 4.
The first divine physician, the Adhivaktṛ, has spoken in favor [of us]. Subduing all serpents and all sorceresses, drive them downward and away.
This one who is copper-colored, ruddy, and tawny, the most auspicious;
and those Rudras who dwell around him in the various directions by the thousands—we seek freedom from their wrath.
He who creeps along, blue-necked and deep red—him the cowherds have seen, him the water-carriers have seen; seen, may he be gracious to us. (7)
Homage be to the blue-necked one, the thousand-eyed, the bountiful;
and also to those who are his attendants—to them I have paid homage. (8)
Unstring the bow from both ends;
O Blessed One, cast away those arrows that are in your hand. 9.
