His arrows have vanished; his quiver has become powerless. || 10 ||
O most bountiful one, with that missile which was in your hand and that bow which was yours—with those, protect us on every side from disease. 11.
May the missile of your bow avoid us on every side;
and as for that quiver of yours, O Lord, place it far away from us.
O thousand-eyed one, wielder of the hundred quivers, having drawn back your bow and blunted the points of your arrows, be auspicious and well-disposed toward us. (13)
Salutations to you, the armed one who is unassailed and bold;
salutations to both your arms, and salutations to your bow. 14.
Do not [harm] our great ones, nor our small ones; do not [harm] our growing ones, nor those already grown.
Do not slay our father, nor our mother; O Rudra, do not harm our dear bodies.
Do not harm us in our children, nor in our grandchildren, nor in our life-span; do not harm us in our cattle, nor in our horses.
Do not slay our heroic men, O wrathful Rudra! Bearing oblations, we invoke you at all times.
Salutations to the one with the golden arms, the leader of armies, and the lord of the quarters; salutations, salutations to the trees!

Homage again and again to Harikeśa, the Lord of Animals; homage again and again to Śaṣpiñjara, the radiant one, the Lord of Paths; homage to Harikeśa, the wearer of the sacred thread, the Lord of Prosperity.

Homage to Babhluśa, the hunter, the lord of foods; homage, homage to the weapon of Bhava, the lord of moving beings; homage, homage to Rudra, the archer, the lord of fields; homage, homage to Sūta, the unassailable one, the lord of the forests. || 18 ||

Homage to Rohita, the carpenter, the lord of trees; homage, homage! Homage to Bhuvantya, the maker of room, the lord of herbs; homage, homage! Homage to Mantrin, the merchant, the lord of thickets; homage, homage! Homage to Uccairghoṣa, the one who cries out, the lord of foot-soldiers; homage, homage!
Homage! 19.
Homage to him who runs with his full array, the lord of beings; homage, homage to the victorious one, the piercer, the lord of those who pierce;
homage, homage to the quiver-bearer, the towering one, the lord of thieves;
homage, homage to the prowler, the wanderer, the lord of the forests. 20.

Homage to the deceiver, to the over-deceiver, to the lord of thieves, homage! Homage to the one armed with a sword and a quiver, to the lord of robbers, homage! Homage to those who carry slings, to those who seek to kill, to the lord of plunderers, homage! Homage to those who bear swords, to those who roam by night, to the lord of those who cut down, homage!
Homage! 21.
Homage to the one with the uṣṇīṣa, who wanders the mountains, the lord of the Kuluñcas; homage again and again to you who possess arrows and to you who carry bows;
homage to you who are drawing [the bow] and to you who are fixing [the arrow];
homage to you who are drawing [the string] and to you who are shooting. || 22 ||

Homage to you who are emitting [semen] and to you who are piercing; homage, homage to you! Homage to you who are sleeping and to you who are waking; homage, homage to you! Homage to you who are lying down and to you who are sitting; homage, homage to you! Homage to you who are standing and to you who are running; homage, homage to you! || 23 ||

Homage to the assemblies and to you, the lords of the assemblies; homage, homage! Homage to the horses and to you, the masters of the horses; homage, homage! Homage to the unstruck and to those who pierce through;
homage, homage! Homage to the fierce hosts and to those who crush; homage, homage! 24.

Homage to you, the hosts and to you, the lords of hosts; homage to you, the troops and to you, the lords of troops; homage to you, the clever ones and to you, the lords of the clever; homage to you, the multiformed and to you, the all-formed. 25.

Homage to you, the armies, and homage to you, the commanders of armies; homage to you, those who ride in chariots, and homage to you, those who do not ride in chariots; homage to you, the charioteers, and homage to you, the drivers; homage to you, the great ones, and homage to you, the small ones. || 26 ||

Salutations to the carpenters and to you, the chariot-makers; salutations to the potters and to you, the smiths; salutations to the Niṣādas and to you, the Puñjiṣṭhas; salutations to the dog-keepers and to you, the hunters. || 27 ||
Homage to the dogs and to the masters of dogs; homage, homage to Bhava and to Rudra;
homage to Śarva and to Paśupati; homage to the blue-necked one and to the white-throated one. 28.
Homage to him with matted hair and to him with shorn hair; homage to the thousand-eyed one and to the wielder of the hundred-bowed bow;
homage to the dweller on the mountain and to Śipiviṣṭa; homage to the most bountiful giver and to the possessor of arrows. || 29 ||
Homage to the short and to the dwarf; homage to the great and to the more extensive; homage to the aged and to the increaser; homage to the foremost and to the first. || 30 ||
Homage to the swift and to the one who runs on the race-course; homage to the rapid and to the quick;
homage to the one of the waves and to the one who dwells in the water; homage to the one of the rivers and to the one who dwells on an island. || 31 ||
Homage to the eldest and to the youngest; homage to the first-born and to the later-born; homage to the middlemost and to the immature; homage to the last-born and to the wise. || 32 ||
Homage to Sobhya and to Pratisarya; homage to Yamya and to Kshemmya; homage to Shlokya and to Avasanya; homage to Urvarya and to Khallya. || 33 ||
Homage to Vanya and to Kakṣya; homage to Śrava and to Pratiśrava; homage to Āśuṣeṇa and to Āśuratha; homage to Śūra and to Avabhedin. || 34 ||

Homage to the one clad in felt and to the one clad in armor; homage to the one wearing mail and to the one possessing a protective shield; homage to the famous one and to him whose army is famous; homage to the one belonging to the drum and to the one who strikes it. || 35 ||
Homage to the bold one and to the one who reaches out; homage to the one who carries a quiver and to the one who possesses a bow-case;
homage to the one with sharp arrows and to the one armed with weapons; homage to the one with excellent weapons and to the one with a fine bow. 36.

Homage to the one who flows and to the one who is beneficial; homage to the one who flows through a ravine and to the one who flows through a canal; homage to the one who flows through a stream and to the one who dwells in a lake; homage to the one who flows in a river and to the one who dwells in a pool. || 37 ||
Homage to the one who is in the well and to the one who is in the pit; homage to the one who is in the depth and to the one who is in the heat;
homage to the one who is in the cloud and to the one who is in the lightning; homage to the one who is in the rain and to the one who is in the drought. || 38 ||
Homage to Vātya and to Reṣmya; homage to Vāstavya and to Vāstupā;
homage to Soma and to Rudra; homage to Tāmra and to Aruṇa. || 39 ||

Salutations to Śaṅgu and to Paśupati; salutations to the Fierce and to the Terrible; salutations to the One who strikes nearby and to the One who strikes from afar; salutations to the Slayer and to the More-Than-Slayer; salutations to the trees with golden hair; salutations to Tāra. 40.
Homage to Śambhu and to Mayobhava; homage to Śaṅkara and to Mayaskara; homage to Śiva and to Śivatarā. || 41 ||
Homage to the one who has reached the further shore and to the one who has not yet reached it; homage to the one who enables crossing and to the one who enables emerging;
homage to the one who dwells on the ford and to the one who dwells on the bank; homage to the one who is like young grass and to the one who is like foam. || 42 ||
Homage to the one who dwells in the sand and to the one who flows along; homage to the one on the *kiṃśila* stone and to the one who causes destruction;
homage to the one with matted hair and to Pulasti; homage to the one of the saline waste and to the one who is encountered on the road. 43.

Homage to him who is in the wandering and to him who is in the cow-pen; homage to him who is on the couch and to him who is in the house; homage to him who is in the heart and to him who is in the dwelling; homage to him who is in the thicket and to him who dwells in the abyss. || 44 ||

Homage to the one who is withered and to the one who is green; homage to the one who is dusty and to the one who is in the atmosphere; homage to the one who is to be dissolved and to the one who is to be washed away; homage to the one who is wide and to the one who is all-pervading. || 45 ||

Homage to Parṇa and to Parṇaśada; homage to him who raises [the weapon] and to him who strikes down; homage to him who draws out and to him who pierces; homage to those who make arrows and to those who make bows;
homage to you, the Kirikas, the hearts of the gods; homage to those who sift and search.
Homage to those who have destroyed [their enemies] and to those who are unassailable. || 46 ||
O wearer of the mantle, Lord of the foodless ones, O Daridra, blue-and-red one!
May there be no fear for these conscious animals; may they not suffer, and may we have no affliction whatsoever.
We offer these prayers to Rudra, the powerful one with matted hair, the lord of heroes who dwells among men.
Just as there is peace among bipeds and quadrupeds, may this entire village be nourished and free from disease.
O Rudra, that auspicious form of yours which is propitious and a healing balm for all days, the auspicious healing balm of the roar—with that, be gracious to us so that we may live. || 49 ||
May the missile of Rudra pass us by, and may the ill-will of the impetuous, malevolent one avoid us.
O Bounteous One, relax your firm [bow] for the sake of our patrons; O Gracious One, be merciful toward our children and progeny. 50.
O most bountiful one, O most auspicious one, be gracious and well-disposed toward us.
Having set aside your weapon upon the highest tree and wearing your skin, come hither bearing your Pināka bow. 51.
O you who scatter and are blood-red, homage be unto you, O Blessed One!
May those thousand missiles of yours strike down someone other than us. || 52 ||
Thousands upon thousands are the weapons in your arms;
O Blessed One, as their lord, turn their points away from us.
Those thousands of Rudras who are upon the earth—in a thousand yojanas away from them, we unbend our bows. (54)
O Bhava, you who exist above this great ocean in the intermediate space;
we stretch out their bows over a distance of a thousand yojanas. 55.
The blue-necked, white-throated Rudras have taken refuge in heaven;
we bow down to their bows at a distance of a thousand yojanas. 56.
Those who have blue necks and dark throats, the Sharvas who roam the earth below—far away, at a distance of a thousand yojanas, we unbend our bows for them. (57)
Those who are the lords of beings, with shaven heads or matted locks—
may we unstring our bows at a distance of a thousand yojanas from them.
Those who are tawny like young grass upon the trees, with blue necks and red bodies—for them we bend our bows even at a distance of a thousand yojanas. 59.
Those who are the protectors of the paths on the journey, the increasers of prosperity, and the warriors for life— for them, we unstring our bows at a distance of a thousand yojanas.
Those who roam among the sacred fords, carrying spears in their hands and wearing quivers—we bend our bows against them at a distance of a thousand yojanas. 61.
Those who pierce the food and the vessels of people as they drink—to them we stretch our bows a thousand yojanas away. 62.
Those Rudras who have spread out through these many directions and even beyond—may we unstring their bows at a distance of a thousand yojanas. (63)
Homage be to the Rudras who are in heaven, whose arrows are the rain;

to them—ten to the east, ten to the south, ten to the west, ten to the north, and ten upward—let there be homage. May they protect us; may they be gracious to us. Whomever we hate, and whoever hates us—[may they overcome him].
We place him whom he hates within the jaws of these. || 64 ||
Homage be to the Rudras who are in the intermediate space, whose arrows are the wind;
to them [be] ten in the east, ten in the south, ten in the west, ten in the north, and ten above.
Homage be to them! May they protect us; may they be gracious to us. Whomever we hate and whoever hates us—[may they strike him].
We place him whom he hates within the jaws of these. || 65 ||
Homage be to the Rudras who are upon the earth, whose arrows are food.

To them—ten to the east, ten to the south, ten to the west, ten to the north, and ten upward—let there be homage. May they protect us; may they be gracious to us. Whomever we hate and whoever hates us—[may they strike him].
We place him whom he hates within the jaws of these. || 66 ||
Salutations to you, O Rudra, for your wrath; and salutations also to your arrow.
Or rather, homage to you with both arms. || 67 ||
O Rudra, that auspicious form of yours which is non-terrible and free from the appearance of evil—with that most peaceful form, O Lord of the Mountain, look upon us with favor. 68.
O Girisha, that arrow which you carry in your hand to hurl—O Agni, make it auspicious;
do not harm the person or the world.
With auspicious speech, O Lord of the Mountain, we address you, so that this entire world of ours may be free from disease and well-disposed toward us. 70.
The first divine physician, the Adhivaktṛ, has spoken in our favor;
subduing all serpents and all sorceresses, drive them away downward.
That one who is copper-colored, ruddy, and brown, the most auspicious;
and those Rudras who dwell around him by the thousands in every direction—to them we pray for freedom from wrath.
He who creeps along, blue-necked and deep red—him the cowherds have seen, him the water-carriers have seen;
seen, may he be gracious to us. (73)
Homage be to the blue-necked one, the thousand-eyed, the bountiful;
and also to those who are his attendants—to them I have rendered homage. (74)
Unstring the bow from both ends;
O Blessed One, cast away those arrows that are in your hand.
The bowstring of the matted-hair god has been removed; he is without arrows, yet still carries his quiver. His arrows have vanished, and his scabbard has become empty.
That missile which was in your hand, O most bountiful one, and that bow of yours—
With that [power] which is free from disease on all sides, protect us completely.
May the missile from your bow avoid us on every side;
and as for that quiver of yours, O Arrow, place it far away from us.
Having bent your bow, O thousand-eyed one, wielder of a hundred arrows, and having blunted the points of your shafts, be auspicious and well-disposed toward us. (79)
Salutations to you, the one armed with weapons, the unstrung, the bold;
salutations to both your arms and to your bow. 80.
Do not harm our great ones, nor our small ones; do not harm our growing ones, nor those already grown. Do not slay our father, nor our mother; O Rudra, do not injure our dear bodies.
Do not harm us in our children or grandchildren, nor in our life-span; do not harm us in our cattle or our horses.
Do not slay our heroic men, O wrathful Rudra; bearing oblations, we invoke you forever. 82.
This, O Rudra, is your portion, together with your sister Ambikā; accept it, Svāhā! This, O Rudra, is your portion; this animal is offered unto you. 83.
We propitiate Rudra, we propitiate the three-eyed Lord of Creatures, so that he may make us more prosperous, so that he may make us better, and so that he may inspire us with resolve. 84.
Salutations to you, O Hara, to your radiant heat; salutations to you, to your splendor! May your other weapons burn others than us; O Purifier, be auspicious toward us. 85.
Homage be to you, O lightning; homage be to you, O thunder;
homage be to you, O Blessed One, from whom you desire heaven.
You do not perceive Him who generated these [beings]; indeed, another thing has come between you.
Enveloped by mist and idle chatter, insatiable for breath, they go about as mere reciters of hymns. 87.
For Viśvakarman was born as the first god; the Gandharva became the second.
The third father, having generated the plants, deposited their embryo in many places within the waters.
O most bountiful, O most auspicious one, be gracious and well-disposed toward us.
Having set aside your weapon upon the highest tree and wearing a skin, come hither bearing your Pināka bow. 89.
O you who scatter and drench in blood, homage be unto you, O Blessed One!
May those thousand missiles of yours strike down someone other than us. (90)
Thousands upon thousands are the weapons in your arms;
O Blessed One, as their master, turn their points away from us.
Those Rudras who are innumerable thousands upon the earth—
for them we unstring our bows at a distance of a thousand yojanas.
O Soma, bearing our minds within our bodies according to your law, may we, possessed of progeny, abide in harmony with you. || 93 ||
This, O Rudra, is your portion, together with your sister Ambikā; accept it, Svāhā! This, O Rudra, is your portion; this goat is your animal sacrifice.
We have propitiated Rudra, we have propitiated the divine Tryambaka, so that he may make us more prosperous, so that he may make us better, and so that he may inspire us with resolve. 95.
You are medicine; you are medicine for the cow, for the horse, and medicine for man; [grant] happiness to the ram and the ewe. 96.
We worship Tryambaka, the fragrant, the increaser of prosperity.
May he deliver us from death as a cucumber is released from its stem, yet not from immortality.
We worship Tryambaka, the fragrant, the bestower of wealth.
May he release me from this world as one releases a cucumber from its stalk—yet not from that [higher] world. 97.
O Rudra, go beyond the Mūjavat mountains by this path that leads downward.
The triple life-span of Jamadagni, the triple life-span of Kaśyapa;
that triple life-span which is among the gods—may that triple life-span be ours. 99.
Thou art named Śiva; the axe is thy father; homage be unto thee, do not harm me.
I turn [thee] back for the sake of long life, for the sake of food, for procreation, for the increase of wealth, for good offspring, and for great heroism. 100.
Thus concludes the ritual bath with pure water.
Now, the garment.
O Lord of Gods, I have brought various new garments made of fine silk; O Śaṅkara, be pleased with me.
Thus ends the section on clothing.
Now, this sacred thread made of gold, silver, copper, or likewise cotton,
has been given by me as an act of affection; please accept it.
Thus [is described] the sacred thread; now, the perfume.
"O Lord of All, worshiped by the world, seated upon the divine throne;
O Lord of Gods, accept this fragrance—let the sandalwood be accepted. Thus [is offered] the fragrance.
Then the unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*): white *akṣata* grains upon the fragrance.
(p. 456) "O best of gods, these *akṣata* grains are pure, bright, shaken [cleaned], and stainless."
"O Supreme Lord, accept these which have been offered by me with devotion"— thus [he offers] the unbroken grains (akṣata).
Then, O Lord, [he offers] flowers, garlands, and other fragrant blossoms such as the jasmine (mālatī).
"May these flowers, gathered by me for the purpose of worship, be accepted. Thus [the offering of] flowers. Now, the bilva leaves:
"The bilva leaf, fashioned in the shape of a trident with gold..."
O Mahādeva, accept this bilva leaf offered by me.
Thus [are described] the bilva leaves.
Now, the incense:
"Born from the essence of the lord of the forest, rich in fragrance, the most excellent scent;
to be inhaled by all the gods—may this incense be accepted. Thus, the incense.
Then, as for the lamp: "O Lord, accept this lamp, which is provided with a wick soaked in ghee and ignited by fire;
O Dispeller of the Darkness of the Three Worlds. Thus [is the offering of] the lamp.
Now, for the food offering (*naivedya*):
"May the food offering—cakes, cooked pastries, *maṇḍakas*, and *vaṭakas*, as well as milk-rice (*pāyasa*), soup, and rice—be accepted. Thus ends the food offering.
Next is the water for sipping.
"O Lord of Pārvatī, please accept this great and supreme water, cool and pure, originating from the Gaṅgā, prepared for your pleasure. Thus is the *ācamanīya*.
Then, for the hand-rubbing (*karodvarttana*):
"O Maheśvara, O Lord of the world, accept these fragrant substances such as camphor and the like for the purpose of hand-rubbing. Thus ends the hand-rubbing.
Now, the fruits:
"O beloved of Pārvatī, O Śaṅkara, whose crest is the moon, please accept these fruits—the kūṣmāṇḍa, the mātuliṅga, and coconut fruits. Thus, the fruits.
Now, regarding betel nuts, betel leaves, and so forth.

"O Lord of the gods, accept this great and divine betel nut (*pūgīphala*) together with betel leaves (*nāgavallīdala*); O Lord of the gods, [accept] the grapes and other fruits. Thus [ends the section on] the betel nut and other items.
Now, as for substance (dravya).

"O Bull-bannered One, please accept this which is situated within the womb of Hiraṇyagarbha, endowed with the golden seed, and given by me consisting of the five jewels. Thus ends the section on the materials.
Now follows the lustration ceremony (nīrājana).
"Agni is light, the sun is light, the all-pervading Nārāyaṇa is light;
O Lord of Gods, O Sovereign of the Suras, I perform the lustration with five lamps. Thus ends the lustration (nīrājana).
Now, the offering of a handful of flowers (puṣpāñjali).
O Hara, support of the entire universe, without support, without refuge;
O Lord, Someśvara, accept this handful of flowers; salutations be unto you! Thus, the offering of a handful of flowers.
p. 457) Now, the mantra for prostration:
Homage to the Guru, who is the cause of the worlds themselves, the bridge across the ocean of saṃsāra, the source of all sciences, and Śambhu.
This is the mantra for prostration.

At the end of every mantra, one should append: "Obeisance to [the deity] together with his limbs, together with his weapons, together with his vehicle, together with his retinue, and together with his enclosures."
Now, regarding the *Śivasahasranāmāvalī*:

for this *Śrīsadāśivasahasranāmastotra-mantra*, Nārāyaṇa is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Śrīsadāśiva is the deity (*devatā*), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (*chandaḥ*), Sadāśiva is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), and Gaurī is the power (*śakti*).
This is the application for the offering of such-and-such a substance with these thousand divine names, for the sake of pleasing Śrī Sadāśiva.
Then, one should constantly meditate upon Maheśa in dhyāna— resembling a mountain of silver, adorned with the beautiful crescent moon,
his limbs radiant with jeweled ornaments, holding in his hands the axe, the deer, the boon-granting gesture, and the gesture of fearlessness, and full of grace.

Seated upon a lotus, praised on all sides by hosts of immortals, wearing a tiger skin, the primordial source of the universe, worthy of universal homage, the remover of all fears, five-faced and three-eyed. || 1 ||
Salutation to Sthirāyana. || 1 || Salutation to Sthāṇu. || 2 || Salutation to Prabhava. || 3 ||
Salutation to Bhīmāya. || 4 || Salutation to Pravarāya. || 5 || Salutation to Varadāya. || 6 ||
Salutation to the Excellent One. || 7 || Salutation to the Soul of All. || 8 || Salutation to the Universally Renowned One. || 9 ||
Salutation to Sarvasma. 10. Salutation to Sarvakara. 11. Salutation to Bhava. 12.
Salutation to Jaṭin. || 13 || Salutation to Carmin. || 14 || Salutation to Śikhaṇḍin. || 15 ||
Salutation to the one whose limbs are all-pervading. 16. Salutation to the one whose nature is all-encompassing. 17.
Salutation to the one who takes away [sins]. || 18 || Salutation to the deer-eyed one. || 19 || Salutation to the one who seizes all beings.
|| 20 || Salutation to the source of manifestation. || 21 || Salutation to the one engaged in worldly activity. || 22 || Salutation to the one withdrawn from worldly activity. || 23 ||
Salutation to the one of fixed course. || 24 || Salutation to the eternal one. || 25 || Salutation to the steadfast one. || 26 ||
Homage to the dweller in the cremation ground. (27) Homage to the Blessed One. (28) Homage to the sky-walker. (29)

By this offering of arghya, may the Blessed Lord Śrī Bhavānīśaṅkara Mahārudra be pleased.
Thus concludes the offering of the *arghya*.
Now, the Mahimnaḥstotra.
Homage to Śrī Gaṇeśa.

If hymns even by Brahmā and the other gods are inadequate to describe the limits of the greatness of You, the supreme knower, then all my words fail when addressing You; yet, O Hara, since everyone is beyond description when speaking according to the reach of their own intellect, let this be my praise as well.
The retinue is beyond reproach. || 1 ||
The path has passed away and Your majesty transcends both speech and mind; even the Veda expresses You only by negating what You are not.
To whom can You be praised? Of how many kinds are Your qualities? And who is the subject for Your domain?
But when it falls upon a base word, whose mind or speech does it not affect? || 2 ||
O Brahmin, for you who have fashioned speech so abundant with honey as the supreme nectar, even the speech of the Preceptor of the Gods is a source of wonder;
yet these words of mine are [only] by virtue of the merit gained from recounting your qualities.
O Destroyer of Cities, my intellect is firmly resolved upon this purpose of purifying [myself]. || 3 ||

O Giver of Boons, that sovereignty of yours which effects the creation, preservation, and dissolution of the universe through your three bodies— distinguished by the [three] qualities and corresponding to the objects of the three Vedas— is, in this world,
a beautiful celestial maiden for the unfortunate.
Some of dull intellect here utter insults in order to dispel it. || 4 ||
With what purpose, with what body, by what means, and with what support does the Creator create the three worlds, and what is his material cause?
Such questions are misplaced and ill-founded when directed toward You, whose sovereignty is inconceivable; they are the products of impaired intellects.
This fallacious reasoning merely makes certain people talkative for the delusion of the world. || 5 ||
Are the worlds unborn, even though they possess constituent parts?
Does the creator of the worlds exist by disregarding the laws of existence? Or, being powerless, could he bring about the birth of the universe; for what apparatus could he possibly have?
For this reason, O best of immortals, these dull-witted ones have doubts regarding you.

The triple Veda, Sāṃkhya, Yoga, the doctrine of Paśupati, and the Vaiṣṇava system— these are the various divergent paths; yet for men who follow these straight, crooked, and manifold ways, each thinking "this is supreme" or "that is the right path," you alone are the one goal to be reached because of the diversity of their inclinations.
Like an ocean of milk. || 7 ||
O Giver of Boons, your ritual implements consist of nothing more than a great bull, a skull-topped staff, an axe, a deer skin, ashes, serpents, and a human skull;
yet the gods possess such various powers because they are directed by the movement of your eyebrows.
The mirage of sense-objects deludes one who finds delight in their own self. || 8 ||
O Destroyer of Cities, some declare that everything is eternal, another that all this is impermanent, and yet another speaks of both eternity and impermanence regarding distinct objects;
yet when these two views are combined, O Puramathana, I am as if struck with wonder by them.
I praise you with my tongue; indeed, is boldness of speech not truly audacious?

O Lord Giriśa, when Viriñca and Hari, despite their efforts, were unable to fully measure the extent of your sovereignty— Virīñca above and Hari below— you, whose body is a mass of fire, [spoke] to them as they praised you with voices heavy with the weight of devotion and faith.
Since these two reside within you yourself, why does your conformity to them not bear fruit? 10.
Having effortlessly brought the three worlds under his sway without the occurrence of enmity, he bore arms that were overcome by the itch for battle—
arms upon which rested the power of the lotus-feet of Śiva, who was adorned with a multitude of lotuses in the form of [severed] heads.
O Destroyer of Tripura, this is the manifestation of your steadfast devotion.
For him whose arm has acquired strength through service to you, even as he exerts his prowess upon Kailāsa— the very abode of you—
there is nothing unattainable, even in the netherworld where the tip of his thumb remains motionless.
Your foundation is indeed firm; the wicked man, however, becomes deluded when he prospers.
O Giver of Boons, it is not surprising that Bāṇa, who was subservient to his attendants and ruled over the three worlds, brought down even the exceedingly lofty supernatural power of Sutrāman;
for he served Your feet.
For the elevation of someone else, there is the bowing of your head. || 13 ||
When you, moved by compassion for the gods and asuras who were terrified at the untimely destruction of the universe, swallowed the poison of the three-eyed Lord Śiva,
that dark stain upon your throat— alas!— does it not actually enhance your splendor?
Even a transformation is praiseworthy for one who is devoted to dispelling the fears of the world. || 14 ||
O Lord, since the arrows of him whose shafts are eternally victorious in this world never fail their aim— never failing their purpose among gods, asuras, or men anywhere— he, Smara,
upon seeing you who are no different from any other god, became one whose very self is now merely a memory; for he is no longer a reality.
In those who have self-mastery, humiliation is salutary. || 15 ||
The earth suddenly falls into a state of peril from the blow of Viṣṇu’s foot; the host of planets is shattered by his whirling, mace-like arms;
and for a moment, the sky suffers distress as its surface is struck by his unrestrained matted locks.
Indeed, for the protection of the world, you perform your dance; surely your sovereign power is wondrous.
The stream of water that pervades the sky, possessing the luster of foam multiplied by the clusters of stars,
which is seen upon your head as a mere spray—
by this very fact it is to be inferred that the ocean, acting as a girdle for the island-like world, has been held up by you of vast majesty.
Your body is divine. || 17 ||
The earth is the chariot, Śatadhṛti (Brahmā) the driver, the Lord of Mountains the bow, the sun and moon the two wheels, and the wielder of the discus (Viṣṇu) the arrow—
for you who desire to burn the triple city, what need is there for this elaborate display of straw? Indeed, those who sport with their subordinates do not employ such grandeur.
Those whose intellects are dependent on a master are subject to others. || 18 ||
Having offered a thousand-petaled lotus as an oblation at the feet of Hari, when one was missing from that number,
he offered his own lotus-eye; thus,
the intensity of his devotion reached its full fruition in the form of the Cakravartin.
O Destroyer of Tripura, you remain awake for the protection of the three worlds.

When the sacrifice is asleep, you remain awake; when the fruit is to be joined, it is the action of the sacrificer that bears fruit, for ritual action perishes without the propitiation of the Supreme Person.
Therefore, I behold you as the guarantor who bestows the fruits of sacrifices.
Having bound his faith to the sacred revelation, a person becomes firmly girded for ritual actions.
Skilled in action, Dakṣa is the lord of sacrifices and the sovereign of embodied beings; the ṛṣis perform the office of officiating priests, the hosts of gods are the members of the assembly,
and the failure of the sacrifice comes from you, O you who are devoted to the bestowal of the fruits of sacrifice.
For sacrifices performed by one devoid of faith are certainly intended for malevolent magic.
O Protector of Creatures, O Lord, even today that arrow— discharged with force by you toward your own daughter who had become a deer,
desiring to sport with her in the form of a Rishi,
and which pursued her even into heaven while you held your bow in hand— does not yet leave her, having pierced her through and through.
Impetuous in the hunt for deer. || 22 ||

O Giver of Boons, when even the Flower-Armed God, whose bow was instantly reduced to mere straw before him upon seeing your own beauty, was regarded by the Goddess as a mere man among women—simply because of his union with half the body of the one who delights in sacrifice—then alas for you! *(Note: The term "straiṇa" refers to that which pertains to women; "puṣpāyudha" is the Flower-Armed One, i.e., Kāmadeva; "puramathana" is the Destroyer of Cities, i.e., Śiva; "yamanirata" refers to Yama, the god of death, whose body is half-composed of the Goddess Umā.)*
The young women are innocent. || 23 ||
O Destroyer of Smara, your playgrounds are cremation grounds; your companions are Piśācas; your body is smeared with the ashes of funeral pyres;
even your garland is a human skull;
and your attire is such—let all these unpropitious things indeed be yours, yet, O Granter of Boons, they are so for those who remember you.
You are the supreme auspiciousness. || 24 ||
When, having fixed their minds within their own inner consciousness and restrained their breath, they experience a thrill of joy with hair standing on end and eyes overflowing with tears of rapture—
upon beholding that [bliss], they sink as if into a lake of nectar.
For you, it is said, bestow upon the self-restrained some ineffable inner reality.
"You are the sun, you are the moon, you are the wind, you are the fire, you are the waters,
you are the sky, you are the earth, and you are the Self"— thus do people utter words that, though limited in scope, find their fulfillment within You.
We know those various principles, but here we do not know that which you are not.
Salutations to Him who, through the three letters beginning with 'A', denotes the three Vedas, the three modes of conduct, the three worlds, and even the three gods—
transcending all modification— and who attains the fourth state, the ultimate abode, by means of subtle sounds.
Whether taken as a whole or individually, O Giver of Refuge, one recites the word "Om."
Bhava, Śarva, Rudra, Paśupati, Ugra, Mahat, Bhīma, and Īśāna—
O God, even the Veda itself investigates each of these eight names one by one within Him.
I offer my salutations to you, who have been directed toward this beloved abode. || 28 ||
Salutations to the nearest and to the dearest, and salutations, salutations to the most distant;
salutations to the smallest, O destroyer of Smara, and salutations to the greatest;
salutations to the oldest, O three-eyed one, and salutations, salutations to the youngest.
"To you who are all this, and to you who are the All, [I offer] salutation. (29)

Salutations again and again to Bhava, who is characterized by intense rajas during the creation of the universe; salutations again and again to Hara, who is characterized by powerful tamas during its dissolution;
salutations again and again to Mrda, who increases the quality of sattva for the sake of the happiness of living beings.
Salutations again and again to Śiva, the state of supreme splendor, which is beyond the three qualities (guṇas). || 30 ||
Where is this mind, emaciated in its development and subject to the afflictions, and where is your constant growth that transcends the limits of all virtues?
Thus, O Giver of Boons, having intensified my trembling with devotion, may I offer this floral tribute of words at Your feet. 31.

Even if Śāradā were to take up ink equal to the Black Mountain in the vessel of the ocean, with a pen made from the branch of the best of celestial trees, and the earth as paper, and were to write for all eternity— nevertheless, [the virtues of the Buddha would remain inexhaustible].
O Lord, the limit of your virtues cannot be reached.

Of the Lord (Īśvara), who is worshipped by Asuras, Suras, and the lords of Munis; who wears the moon upon his crest; whose great majesty is woven from attributes, yet who is himself beyond all attributes (nirguṇa); there is one named Puṣpadanta, the most eminent among the entire host of Gaṇas.
He composed this hymn in charming, flawless, and light meters. || 33 ||
That person of pure mind who recites this hymn to Dhūrjaṭi every day with supreme devotion becomes equal to Rudra in the world of Śiva, and likewise here on earth.
He will possess abundant wealth and long life, as well as sons and fame. || 34 ||
There is no god other than Maheśa; there is no hymn of praise greater than Mahiman;
there is no mantra other than Aghora; and there is no reality higher than that of the Guru. (35)
Initiation, charity, austerity, pilgrimage, knowledge, and rituals such as sacrifice—these do not equal even a sixteenth part of the merit of reciting the *Mahimnaḥ Stava*. (36)
This entire hymn, which extols the Lord until its conclusion, is incomparable, captivating, meritorious, and spoken by a Gandharva. (37)
The king of all Gandharvas named Kusumadaśana is indeed a servant of the God of Gods, who bears the moon upon his excellent crest;
yet he has truly fallen from his own greatness because of him.
Out of anger, he uttered this praise of his own divine and supreme majesty.
If a person, with palms joined in reverence and a mind focused on nothing else, recites [this work] which is worshiped by the best of gods and sages and is the sole cause for heaven and liberation,
he goes into the presence of Śiva while being praised by the *kiṃnaras*.
This unfailing hymn was composed by Puṣpadanta. || 39 ||
He who is well-pleased by this hymn— which issues from the lotus-like mouth of Śrī Puṣpadanta, which removes all sins, and is beloved by Hara—
when it is held in the throat, recited, and chanted with a concentrated mind.
He becomes Maheśa, the Lord of Beings. || 40 ||
Thus ends the hymn known as the Śivamahimnaḥ Stotra, composed by the venerable Puṣpadanta.
Now follows the hymn to Śiva composed by Rāvaṇa:
Upon whose head shines a creeper-like wave, restless and surging from the mountain torrents that tumble down the mass of his matted locks;
My devotion is at every moment fixed upon Him whose crest is the young moon, and upon the fire blazing "dhaga-dhaga-dhag" on His forehead. || 1 ||
To her whose mind rejoices in the continuous flow of sidelong glances— charming as the playful companion of the daughter of the mountain king—
and who has warded off insurmountable calamities with the stream of her compassionate side-long looks.
In some instances, let the mind find diversion in the subject of the sky-clad (Digambara). || 2 ||
In this world where the faces of the women of the quarters are anointed with the saffron paste of the mass of radiance from the jewels of the throbbing hoods of the serpents in his matted locks;
and which is made lush by the upper garment of the shimmering skin of an elephant blinded by rut.
May he, the sustainer of all beings, bear a wondrous delight for the mind. || 3 ||
I bow to the Lord of Nīlīmā, who has swallowed the five-arrowed god of love with the sparks of the blazing Dhananjaya fire on the courtyard of his forehead,
and whose crest is resplendent with a streak of nectar-like moonlight.
May there be for us the splendor of Mahākapālin, with his matted locks streaming like a river. || 4 ||
The base of his footstool is greyed by the showers of floral pollen from the crowns of all the gods, beginning with the thousand-eyed Indra;
his mass of matted locks is bound by the garland of the king of serpents.
May he whose crest is the friend of the cakora bird (the moon) be born for the long-lasting prosperity of Śrī. || 5 ||
Upon the fierce five-arrowed god, who offered the five arrows as oblations into the fire of the *dhanañjaya* blazing with a *dhagaddhag* sound upon his formidable forehead-plate,
[there appeared] the variegated leaf-designs on the tips of the breasts of the daughter of the mountain king.
My devotion is fixed upon the Three-eyed One, whose sole craft is creative imagination.

May the Lord, beautiful in his elephant hide, who bears the streams of the celestial Ganges, whose neck is encircled by the dense mass of darkness of the night of the new moon— darkness as irresistible and shimmering as it is obstructed by a fresh circle of clouds— grant us prosperity.
Charming as a treasury of the arts, he is the bearer of prosperity and the sustainer of the world.
p. 481) Whose neck is radiant with the beauty of a throat-stalk supporting the luster of a multitude of blossoming blue lotuses;
who destroys Smara, who destroyed the cities [of the demons], who cuts off worldly existence, and who severs the elephant-god [Kāma].
I worship Him who destroyed Makhacchid, who destroyed Andhaka, and who destroyed Antaka.
To him who is the bee to the blossoming sweetness of the flowing nectar of the cluster of all auspicious arts that are not small;
to the ender of Smara, the ender of cities, the ender of sins, and the ender of worldly existence.
I bow to the one who was worshipped by the destroyer of Gaja, the destroyer of Andhaka, and the destroyer of Antaka.
Victorious is the fierce sacrificial fire upon the forehead, flashing with the rhythmic emergence of the hissing serpents that writhe in abundant agitation;
accompanied by the lofty auspicious sounds of *dhimindhimindhi* drumbeats.
Śiva performs a fierce tāṇḍava dance set in motion by the succession of sounds. || 10 ||

To him for whom a speckled carpet and a bed of snakes were equal; for whom a pearl necklace and a string of beads were alike; for whom a precious gem and a clod of earth were the same; for whom a friend and an enemy faction were indistinguishable;
and for whom a blade of grass and the lotus-eyed Goddess of Fortune were one and the same—as were a common subject and a great lord of the earth.
When shall I worship Sadāśiva with equanimity? || 11 ||
When, dwelling in the hollow of a bower by the stream of the celestial river Nilañjanā,
forever freed from evil thoughts, bearing my joined palms upon my head,
and gazing at that which is fixed upon the forehead of her whose eyes are tremulous and lovely—
Uttering the mantra "Śiva," I am always happy.
May she, who is enchanting with the flowing *madhūlikā* honey profusely exuding from the jasmine flowers atop the *kadamba* tree that is the head of Lord Nīlīnātha,
grant us the joy of delight day and night.
The mass of light from the rays produced by his body is the supreme state of the highest glory. || 13 ||
Moving with the auspicious radiance of the fierce submarine fire, her chatter was carried away by the women desiring the eight great supernatural powers;
she was like the sound of a wedding ceremony for those who have cast off their beautiful eyes.
May she, adorned with the mantra "Śiveti," arise for the conquest of the world. || 14 ||
Thus ends the hymn to Śiva composed by Rāvaṇa.

Now, for this Śivakavaca, the mantra of the Śrīśivakavacastotra: Brahmā is the seer (ṛṣi), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chandas), the venerable Sadāśiva-Rudra is the deity (devatā), Hrīṃ is the power (śakti), and Raṃ is the pin (kīlaka).
Śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ is the seed-syllable (bīja). This is the application (viniyoga) for the recitation of the Śivakavaca Stotra for the sake of pleasing Śrī Sadāśiva.

Now, the ritual placement on the hands (karanyāsa): Oṃ, salutation to the Blessed One who wears a garland of blazing flames; Oṃ Rāṃ, to the abode of all powers, the Īśāna-self, salutation to both thumbs.

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One garlanded with blazing flames! Oṃ na/rīṃ, homage to the two index fingers, who are the abode of eternal satisfaction and whose nature is that of Tatpuruṣa. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One garlanded with blazing flames! Oṃ ma/rū/, homage to the two middle fingers, who are the abode of primordial power and whose nature is that of Aghora. Oṃ, homage...
To the Blessed One garlanded with blazing flames, *oṃ śiṃraiṃ*, to the abode of the independent power (*svatantra-śakti*),
whose self is Vāmadeva— to these two ring fingers (*anāmikā*) be salutation.
To the Blessed One garlanded with blazing flames, *oṃ vā rauṃ*, to the abode of the incomparable power (*atulya-śakti*), whose self is Sadyojāta— [to these two little fingers be salutation].

To the two little fingers, *namaḥ*. *Oṃ namo bhagavate jvalajjvālāmāline oṃ ya raḥ*, to the abode of primordial power, the self of all, to the palms and the backs of the hands, *namaḥ*. In the same manner for the heart and the other limbs.
Now, for the meditation:
I pay homage to Śambhu, the Lord of Umā, who possesses adamantine fangs and three eyes, whose throat is dark blue, who subdues his enemies, and who has a thousand most fierce arms. (1)

Now, furthermore, for your benefit, I shall declare the Śaiva armor (*kavaca*), which is the secret of all Purāṇas, the purifier that removes the entire flood of sins without exception, the bestower of victory, and the liberator from all calamities.
Ṛṣabha said:
Having paid homage to Mahādeva, the Lord who pervades the universe, I shall proclaim the armor consisting of Śiva, which provides protection for all human beings. (3)
Seated in a clean place upon a properly prepared seat,
with senses conquered and vital breaths subdued, one should meditate upon the imperishable Śiva.

One should meditate upon the Great Lord, who consists of supreme bliss, seated within the lotus of the heart, pervading the expanse of the sky with his own splendor, beyond the senses, subtle, infinite, and primordial.
Having shaken off all bonds of karma through meditation, with his mind long immersed in the bliss of consciousness,
and with his self composed by the placement of the six-syllable mantra, he should perform protection with the armor of Śiva.
May the Lord, the soul of all deities, protect me who have fallen into this fathomless well of saṃsāra;
may His divine name, the root of the most excellent mantra, shake off every sin residing within my heart.
May the one whose form is the universe, the mass of light and bliss, the conscious self, protect me everywhere;
may that Lord, who is subtler than the subtle and possesses vast power, protect me from every fear. 8.
May Giriśa, who possesses eight forms, protect me from the earth—he who sustains the universe by means of the nature of the earth;
may he who brings life to men by means of the nature of the waters protect me from the waters.

May that Kālarudra, who at the end of the aeon dances with manifold sports after burning all the worlds, protect me from the fear of the submarine fire, the wind, and other such calamities, and from every form of suffering. (10)

Shining with the luster of blazing lightning and gold, holding in his hands the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness along with a battle-axe, four-faced, three-eyed, and known as Tatpuruṣa—may he protect me perpetually while stationed in the east. 11.
Wielding an axe, a shield, a goad, a noose, a trident, a skull-bowl, a drum, and a rosary;
four-faced, blue-hued, and three-eyed—may Aghora protect in the southern direction. 12.
Resplendent like jasmine, the moon, a conch, and crystal; marked with a Veda, a rosary, and the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness;
three-eyed, four-faced, and of vast power—may Sadyojāta protect me in the west. 13.

May Vāmadeva protect me in the northern direction—he who holds a rosary, a gesture of fearlessness, and an axe in his hands; whose complexion is like the filaments of a lotus; who possesses three eyes and four beautiful faces. 14.

May Īśāna—who holds in his hands the Vedas, the shield, the goad, the noose, the horn, the skull-bowl, the drum, the eye, and the trident; who possesses white radiance, five faces, and is the supreme light above—protect me.
May he whose head is the moon protect my head, and may he who has an eye in his forehead protect my forehead.
May he who stole the eyes of Bhaga protect my eyes; may Viśvanātha always protect my nose. 16.
May he whose fame is sung by the Vedas protect my ears; may the one who wears the crescent moon on his head always protect my cheeks;
may the five-faced one always protect my face; and may he whose tongue is the Veda always protect my tongue. (17)
May Girīśa protect my throat, may Nīlakaṇṭha protect both my hands,
may Dharmabāhu protect the roots of my arms, and may Dakṣamakhāntaka protect the region of my chest.

May the one whose bow is the king of mountains protect my belly; may the destroyer of Madana protect my waist. May the father of Heramba protect my navel; may the three-locked Lord Īśvara protect my hips.
May the friend of Kubera protect my two thighs; may the Lord of the World protect my two knees;
may he whose banner is the bull protect the pair of my shanks; and may he whose feet are worshipped by the gods protect my feet.
May Maheśvara protect me during the first watch of the day; may Vāmadeva protect me during the middle watch;
may Tryambaka protect me during the third watch; and may the Bull-bannered Lord protect me during the final watch of the day. (21)
May the moon-crested Lord protect me at the beginning of the night; may the bearer of the Gaṅgā protect me at midnight;
may the husband of Gaurī protect me at the end of the night; and may the Conqueror of Death protect me at all times. (22)

May Śaṅkara protect me while I am inside; may Sthāṇu always protect me while I am outside; may the Lord of Beings (Paśupati) protect me in between those two; and may Sadāśiva protect me on all sides. || 23 ||

May the sole Lord of the universe protect me while standing; may the Lord of the Pramathas protect me while walking. May He who is known through the Vedāntas protect me while sitting; may the imperishable Śiva protect me while lying down.
May the Blue-throated One protect me on the paths; may the Foe of the Three Cities protect me in mountains and other difficult terrains.
May the noble-powered Mṛgavyādha protect [us] during great journeys such as dwelling in the forest. || 25 ||

May Vīrabhadra protect [us] from the terrible and insurmountable great fear of the ocean of enemies, he whose laughter is a loud, piercing roar that causes the cosmic egg to tremble through his fierce anger, as intense as the cataclysm at the end of an aeon.

May Mṛḍa, with the edge of his terrible axe, cut through a hundred akṣauhiṇīs of assailants— terrifying with thousands, lakhs, ayutas, and koṭis of foot-soldiers, horses, elephants, chariots, and protective enclosures.
May the trident of the Destroyer of Tripura, blazing with flames like the fire of universal dissolution, slay the demons;
may the Pināka bow of the Lord terrify the predators such as tigers, lions, bears, and wolves.
May it destroy for me bad dreams, ill omens, miserable rebirths, dejection, famine, misfortunes, unbearable infamy,
portents, afflictions, fear of poison, the distress of malevolent planets, and diseases.
The supreme lord of the worlds. || 29 ||
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Sadāśiva, who consists of all principles, whose form is all mantras,
who is presided over by all yantras, whose form is all tantras, who is far beyond all principles,
the incarnation of Brahmā and Rudra, the blue-throated one, the beloved of the heart-stealing Pārvatī.
To him whose eyes are the moon, the sun, and fire; whose body is smeared with ashes;
who wears a crown of great jewels; who is adorned with rubies;
who is the fierce descent of Rudra at the time of creation, preservation, and dissolution; and who is the destroyer of Dakṣa’s sacrifice.
To the one who shatters Mahākāla, whose sole abode is the root-stream, who has transcended reality, the bearer of the Gaṅgā,
the supreme god of all gods, the refuge of the six, and the essence of Vedānta.

To the one who accomplishes the three aims of human life, the leader of infinite millions of cosmic eggs (brahmāṇḍas), adorned by the eight great families of nāgas— Ananta, Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Karkkoṭaka, Śaṅkha, Kulika, Padma, and Mahāpadma— and whose very nature is the syllable Om (praṇava).

Salutations to Him whose nature is the space of consciousness and the directions of the sky; who is garlanded by the planets and constellations; who is the whole yet free from all blemish; the sole creator of all worlds, the sole destroyer of all worlds, the sole teacher of all worlds, and the sole witness of all worlds.
To the one who is the secret of all the *nigamas*, who has reached the further shore of all the *vedāntas*, who is the sole bestower of boons upon all the worlds,
who is the sole benefactor (*śaṅkara*) of all the worlds; to the one whose crest is the moon, whose own abode is eternal,
who is without appearance, free from disease, stainless, devoid of greed, free from pride, and beyond care.
To the one who is without ego, unrestrained, stainless, devoid of qualities, free from desire, undisturbed, blameless, uninterrupted, causeless, free from fear,
beyond conceptual proliferation, unattached, free from dualities, without support, and passionless.
To the one free from anger, stainless, sinless, fearless, free from conceptual construction, undivided, actionless, incomparable, beyond doubt, untainted, possessed of matchless glory,
the eternally pure, awakened, perfect, non-dual Being-Consciousness-Bliss, whose very nature is supreme peace.

Victory, victory to you, O Rudra, whose form is light, who consists of light! O Great Raudra, great incarnation, Mahābhairava, Kālabhairava, Bhairava of the end of the aeon; wearer of the garland of skulls, armed with the *khaṭvāṅga*, sword, shield, noose, goad, hand-drum, trident, bow, arrow, mace, and spear!
With a thousand hands terrifying with weapons such as the *nandīpāla*, *tomara*, *musala*, *mudgara*, noose, iron club, *bhuśuṇḍī*, *śataghnī*, and discus; with a face made formidable by fangs;
with a wide, boisterous laugh that causes the circle of the universe to tremble; and adorned with earrings of lordly serpents.
O wearer of the serpent-king’s necklace, O wearer of the serpent-king’s armlets, O wearer of the serpent-king’s skin;

O conqueror of death, O three-eyed one, O destroyer of Tripura, O universal form, O odd-eyed one, O Lord of the universe, O you whose vehicle is the bull, O you whose face is everywhere—protect me, protect me from all sides! Blaze, blaze!

Destroy, destroy the fear of great death and untimely death! Eradicate, eradicate the fear of thieves! Pacify, pacify the fear of venomous serpents! Kill, kill the thieves! Expel, expel my enemies! Tear asunder, tear asunder with the trident! Split them with the axe!

Pierce! Cut, cut with the sword! Pound, pound with the khaṭvāṅga staff! Crush, crush with the mace! Strike, strike with arrows! Terrify, terrify the rākṣasas! Put to flight, put to flight all beings without exception!
Terrify, terrify the hosts of *kūṣmāṇḍas*, *vetālas*, *mārīs*, and *brahmarākṣasas*;
grant me fearlessness, grant it; comfort me who am terrified, comfort me.

Lift me up, lift me up from the great terror of hell; revive me, revive me! Satisfy me, satisfy me with hunger and thirst! Gladden me, gladden me, who am afflicted by suffering, with the armor of Śiva.
Cover me, cover me! O conqueror of death, three-eyed one, eternal Śiva, salutations to you!
Ṛṣabha said:
"O Śiva, O bestower of boons, this armor has been proclaimed by me;
it is a secret for all embodied beings that pacifies every affliction. (30)
That mortal who always wears this supreme armor of Śiva shall never experience fear anywhere, by virtue of the grace of Śambhu.
Whether one's life-span is exhausted, death has arrived, or one is afflicted by a great disease, such a person immediately attains happiness and gains a long life. (32)
He who wears this armor of Śiva, which pacifies all poverty and increases auspiciousness, is honored even by the gods. (33)
One is liberated from the multitude of great sins (mahāpātaka) as well as the minor sins (upapātaka);
at the end of the body, one attains liberation through the power of the armor of Śiva (śivavarma). || 34 ||
You too, my child, should wear with faith this supreme armor of Śiva given by me; you shall indeed swiftly attain the highest good. (35)
Sūta said:
Having spoken thus to that son of the king, the yogin Ṛṣabha gave him a conch of great sound and a sword that destroys enemies.
Furthermore, having consecrated the ashes with mantras, he touched his limbs all around;
he bestowed the strength of twelve thousand elephants upon him.
Having attained strength, sovereignty, fortitude, and mindfulness through the power of his grandfather’s spiritual influence,
that prince shone with splendor like the autumnal sun.
Having joined his palms in reverence, that yogi spoke again to the prince:
"This sword, empowered by the influence of asceticism and mantras, has been given to you by me. (39)
To whomever you clearly show this sharp-edged sword, that enemy shall die instantly, even if he were Death himself in person. (40)
Those enemies who hear the sound of this conch shell shall fall down unconscious, their weapons cast aside and deprived of sense. || 41 ||
These two divine objects, the sword and the conch, destroy the enemy forces and increase the valor and splendor of one's own army and partisans. (42)
And by the power of these two, as well as by the Śaiva armor and even by the great strength of twelve thousand nāgas, [he was protected].
By the power of wearing the sacred ash (bhasma), you shall conquer the enemy armies;
having attained your father’s throne, you shall protect this earth. || 44 ||
Having thus properly instructed Bhadrāyus along with his mother,
the yogi, honored by them both, then departed at his own will.
Thus ends the Śivakavaca in its entirety.

Now the Upaniṣad: Oṃ, obeisance to Śiva. Oṃ, obeisance to you, O Śambhu, the three-eyed one of beautiful limbs, Lord of the three worlds, Consort of Umā, destroyer of Dakṣa’s sacrifice, and annihilator of the bodies of lustful women.
O destroyer of terrible sins, Great Being of most fierce form, bringer of destruction to all beings,
maker of auspiciousness, Maheśvara, wielder of the trident, enemy of Smara, abode of Guha, sky-clad one,
you whose crest is the great conch, wearer of matted locks, whose body is adorned with a garland of skulls.
O Lord who agitated the gods and the progenitors with Your left eye; O destroyer of Bhaga’s eyes;
O Lord Bhīmasena; O Paśupati; O burner of Kama’s body; O dweller in the crossroads; O Śiva, Mahādeva, Īśāna, Śaṅkara, Bhīmabhava, Vṛṣadhvaja, Kaiṭabha, Prauḍha, and Mahānātheśvara!

O Bhūtirata, Avimuktaka, Rudra, Rudreśvara, Sthāṇu, Ekaliṅga, Kālindīpriya, Śrīkaṇṭha, Nīlakaṇṭha, Aparājita, Ripubhayaṅkara, Santoṣapati, Vāmadeva, Aghora, Tatpuruṣa, Mahāghora, Aghoramūrti, Śānta, Sarasvatīkānta!

O thousand-formed one, O great source, O all-pervading Lord, O Kālāgni, O Rudra, O fierce Hara, O beloved of the mountain, O you who dwell at all sacred fords, O Haṃsa, O Kāmeśvara, O Kedāra, O Sovereign,
O Paripūrṇa, O Mucukunda, O dweller in Madhu, O sword-handed one, O terrifying one, O King of Knowledge, O King of the Moon!
O Kāmarāja, who dwells in the heart-lotus of the daughter of the King of Mountains; O You who recline upon the ocean;
O Gayāmukha, Gokarṇa, and Brahma-yoni; O Sahasravaktra, Akṣicaraṇa, and Hāṭakeśvara—salutations to You, salutations to You! Thus ends the Upaniṣad.
Now, Śiva has a hundred names: Maheśvara, Śambhu, Pinākin, Śaśiśekhara, Vāmadeva, Virūpākṣa, Kapardin, and Nīlalohita. (1)
Śaṅkara, the trident-bearer, the wielder of the khaṭvāṅga staff, the beloved of Viṣṇu, Śipiviṣṭa, the Lord of Ambikā, Śrīkaṇṭha, and the one who is affectionate toward his devotees. || 2 ||
Bhava is the lord of all the three worlds, the blue-throated one, the beloved of Śivā;
he is the fierce one, the bearer of the skull, the enemy of Kāma, and the slayer of the demon Andhaka. || 3 ||
The bearer of the Gaṅgā, whose eye is on his forehead, the death of Death, the ocean of compassion;
Bhīma, with axe in hand, with a deer in his palm, and wearing matted locks.
Dwelling on Kailāsa, clad in armor, and fierce, he is the destroyer of Tripura;
marked by the bull, mounted upon the bull, his body is smeared with ashes.
He who loves the Sāman chants, who consists of the musical notes, whose form is the three Vedas, and who is without a superior lord;
he who is omniscient, the supreme self, and whose eyes are the moon, the sun, and fire.
Soma consists of the Havis-sacrifices; he is Sadāśiva with five faces, the Lord of the Universe, Vīrabhadra, the Lord of the Gaṇas, and Prajāpati. || 7 ||
Hiraṇyaretas, Durddharṣa, Girīśa, Giriśa, Anagha, Bhujaṅgabhūṣaṇa, Bharga, Giridhanvan, and Giripriya. || 8 ||
Clad in an elephant hide, the enemy of the Triple City, the Blessed Lord, the sovereign of the Pramathas;
the conqueror of death, subtle-bodied, pervading the universe, the preceptor of the world. (9)
Vyomakeśa, Mahāsena-janaka, Cāruvikrama, Rudra, Bhūtapati, Sthāṇu, Ahirbudhnya, and Digambara. || 10 ||
He who possesses eight forms, whose nature is manifold, who is composed of sattva, whose body is pure, who is eternal, the wielder of the broken axe, the unborn, and the liberator from bonds.
He is Mṛḍa, Paśupati, the God, Mahādeva, the Imperishable Lord;
he is Pūṣadantabhida, the Unperturbed, the Destroyer of Dakṣa’s sacrifice, and Hara.
He who pierced the eyes of Bhaga, the unmanifest, the thousand-eyed, the thousand-footed, the bestower of liberation, the infinite, the savior, the Supreme Lord. || 13 ||
These divine names are always recited by me;
this Name-Kalpalatā (Wish-fulfilling Creeper of Names) bestows all desired objects.
O fortunate one, these names undoubtedly bestow auspiciousness;
in reality, these names constitute the very essence of the Vedas. (15)
These names, which bestow all goals, are recited by me daily with devotion and according to the prescribed rules. (16)
O fortunate one, within the various Vedas there exist infinite names of Śiva that are most excellent and destroyers of sin. (17)
Having collected their names from them, Maheśvara formerly taught the one thousand and eight names to the Kumāra.
Thus ends the hymn of one hundred and eight names of Śivā.
(p. 489) Now, regarding the Thousand Names, Sūta said: "Listen, O best of sages; I shall relate it just as I have heard it."
By him the Supreme Lord was entreated by Viṣṇu and was thereby satisfied.
Therefore, I shall now recite this auspicious thousand names.
Śrī Viṣṇu said:
Śiva, Hara, Mṛḍa, Rudra, Puṣkara, and Puṣpalocana. (2)

He who is to be approached by those seeking his grace, the embodiment of righteous conduct, the all-pervading Śambhu, the Great Lord (Maheśvara), he whose crest is the moon (Candrāpīḍa), the moon-crested one (Candramauli), the origin of the universe (Viśvādi), and the Lord of the immortals (Amareśvara). || 3 ||
He is the essence of the Vedānta, the bearer of the skull, the blue-and-red one; he is to be discerned through the support of meditation, the husband of Gaurī, and the Lord of the Gaṇas. || 4 ||

He who possesses eight forms and is the form of the universe; he who is the threefold aim of life and the means to attain heaven; he who is accessible through knowledge and possesses firm wisdom; the God of gods, the three-eyed one.
Vāmadeva, Mahādeva, Paṭu, Parivṛḍha, Dṛḍha, Viśvarūpī, Virūpākṣa, Vāgīśa, and Śucimattara. || 6 ||
He is the one who speaks with all means of valid cognition, the bull-bannered, the one whose vehicle is the bull,
the Lord, the wielder of the Pināka bow, the bearer of the skull-topped staff (khaṭvāṅga), the one of variegated attire, and the eternal one.

The dispeller of darkness, the great yogi, the protector, the one whose matted locks are the heart of the universe; the death of Death, the wearer of the elephant hide, the fortunate one, whose very self is bowed in devotion. (8)

He who wears the triple mark (tripuṇḍra), the protector of sight, Durvāsas, the subduer of cities, the wielder of divine weapons, the preceptor of Skanda, the supreme lord, higher than the highest. || 9 ||
He is without beginning, middle, or end; the Lord of the Mountains; the Kinsman of the Mountain; the Friend of Kubera; Śrīkaṇṭha; the most excellent among the classes of beings; and the Gentle One.

He who is to be known through meditative concentration, the wielder of the bow, the blue-throated one, the bearer of the battle-axe, the large-eyed one, the hunter of the deer, the lord of the gods, and the scorcher like the sun. || 11 ||

The abode of Dharma, the field of forbearance, the Blessed One who pierced the eyes of Bhaga, the fierce one, the Lord of Creatures, Tārkṣya, the lover of his devotees, and the speaker of pleasant words. 12.

The giver, the compassionate one, the skillful, the one with matted hair, the subduer of desire, whose abode is the cremation ground, the subtle, who dwells in the cremation ground—Maheśvara. || 13 ||
The creator of the world, the lord of beasts, the great creator, the great medicinal herbs;
the northern one, the lord of rays, the protector, accessible through knowledge, the ancient one.
He is policy, excellent policy, and the pure-souled one; he is Soma, the lover of Soma, and the blissful one;
he is the drinker of Soma, the drinker of nectar, the gentle one, the great light, and the one of great splendor. || 15 ||
Consisting of splendor, consisting of nectar, and consisting of food, he is the Lord of Ambrosia;
he is the one whose enemy is unborn, who is to be perceived through light, and the bearer of oblations. (16)
The creator of the world, the creator of the Vedas, the author of the Sūtras, the eternal one; the great seer, the teacher Kapila, the light of the universe, the all-seeing. || 17 ||
The wielder of the Pināka bow, subject to the will of the god of gods, the bestower of well-being, the wise one;
the abode of the Creator, the maker of light, the giver of all, whose range is universal. || 18 ||

The creator of Brahmā, the creator of the universe, the all-encompassing, the lover of the *karṇikāra* flower, the wise poet, the one with branches, the branchless, the one with cow-branches, the auspicious, and the unsurpassed physician. || 19 ||
Gaṅgāpplavodaka, Bhavya, Puṣkala, Sthapati, and Sthira;
Vijitātman, Vidheyātman, and Bhūtavāhanasārathi. || 20 ||
Sagaṇa, Gaṇavarya, Sukīrti whose doubts were severed, Kāmadeva, and Kāmapāla, his body smeared with ashes; || 21 ||

He who loves ashes, who lies upon ashes, the lover, the beloved, the author of the sacred scriptures, the one of even whorls, the one whose self is withdrawn, the mass of dharma, the ever-auspicious Śiva. || 22 ||
Stainless, four-armed, difficult to approach, and hard to assail;
rare to attain, difficult to traverse, and impregnable; he is skilled in all weapons. || 23 ||
He is the abode of internal yoga, the excellent thread, the increaser of the thread;
he is the one with auspicious limbs, the essence of the world, the Lord of the universe, and the agitator of men.
He who effects purification through ashes, who is Mount Meru, who is full of vital energy, whose form is pure;
he who accomplishes the impossible and makes the virtuous attainable, and who assumes the forms of a servant and a monkey.
He is the ancient one whose essence is fire, the immovable destroyer of the lives of his enemies;
he is the great lake, the great abyss, and he is praised by hosts of perfected beings and gods.
Clad in tiger-skin garments, the serpent, the great being, the great treasure, the experience of immortality, the glorious one, the Pāñcajanya conch, and the wind-god. || 27 ||

Established in the twenty-five principles, he is the Pārijāta tree, higher than the highest; he is easily attained, firm in his vows, heroic, the treasury of all that consists of speech, and the ultimate treasure.
The teacher of the castes and stages of life, the student, the conqueror of enemies, the scorcher of foes;
the hermitage, the destroyer, the emaciated, the possessor of knowledge, and the Lord of the immovable. || 29 ||
He is the embodiment of valid cognition, difficult to comprehend, the well-winged one whose vehicle is the wind;
he is the wielder of the bow, the science of archery, the quality itself, and the source of the moon’s qualities.
He is truth, devoted to truth, humble, the limb of dharma, and the means for accomplishing dharma;
he possesses infinite vision, is bliss, the rod of punishment, the subduer, and self-restraint itself.
He is the performer of miracles, the master of great illusion, the architect of all, and the fearless one;
he is free from passion, self-disciplined, an ascetic, and the rider of living beings.
Wearing the garb of a madman, having conquered desire, and honored by his beloved;
possessing the nature of the end of the aeon, yet himself the perfect one, he is the Lord of Progeny for all the worlds. (33)
He is the swift one, the deliverer, the wise, the preeminent, the lord, the imperishable;
he is the guardian of the worlds, the one whose self is hidden, the beginning of the eon, and the lotus-eyed one.
He knows the true meaning of the Vedas and the Shastras; he is the restraint and the refuge of all restraints; he is the moon, the sun, Saturn, and Ketu; he is dispassion and has the luster of coral.
The Supreme Brahman who is subdued by devotion; the policy that strikes down the deer;
the mountain whose abode is the mountain; the beloved; the Supreme Self; the Teacher of the World. (36)
He is the abode of all desires, contented, auspicious, and surrounded by auspiciousness;
he is of great austerity, long-practiced asceticism, most ancient, venerable, and like a tree.
He is the day, the year, pervasiveness, the supreme authority, and the highest austerity; he is the mantra that creates the year, the means of realization, and the all-seeing one.
The unborn one, the Lord of all, the perfected, possessing great seed and great strength;
the yoga, the fit one, of great splendor, whose body is the perfected form of all the primordial deities. || 39 ||
He is the Vasu, the benevolent-minded, the Truth, the remover of all sins, Hara;
he is of auspicious fame, the adorned, the one who makes others hear, and indeed beyond the reach of speech and mind.
He is immortal, eternal, and tranquil; he holds a droṇa-measure in his hand and is full of majesty.
He carries a water-pot, is a wielder of the bow, is the limbs of the Vedas, a knower of the Vedas, and a sage.
Resplendent, the enjoyer of food, the Lord of the World, the invincible;
beyond the senses, possessed of great illusion, the abode of all, the crossroads. || 42 ||
The Yogi of Time, the Great Sound, the Great Zeal, the Great Strength, the Great Intelligence, the Great Prowess, the Wanderer among Beings, the Destroyer of Cities. || 43 ||
A night-stalker who moves at will, possessing great power and great splendor, with an indescribable form, glorious, and one whose mind moves as fast as that of all teachers. || 44 ||
He is the one of great learning, the master of great illusion, self-controlled, the eternal, and the non-eternal;
he is the bearer of splendor and the radiance of splendor, the hellish one, and the teacher of all.
Fond of dance, constantly dancing, the luminous self, the illuminator;
clear, cruel, wise, the mantra, equal, the flood of essence. || 46 ||
The creator of the beginning of the ages, the one who causes the ages to revolve, the profound, the one whose vehicle is the bull;
the beloved, the most distinguished, the one desired by the learned, the Śarabha, and the one whose bow is the Śarabha.
He who is the form of the sacred ford (*tīrtha*), whose name is the sacred ford, who is invisible even to the sacred fords, and who bestows excellent fords;
he is the treasure-house of waters, the foundation, victory, and the knower of the time of triumph. (48)
Established, the knower of the means of valid cognition, the golden-armored Hari;
the liberator, the host of gods, the Lord of Knowledge, who rests upon the point (bindu). || 49 ||
Appearing as a child, intoxicated by strength, the transformer, the impenetrable, Guha;
the instrument, the cause, the agent, and the liberator from all bonds. || 50 ||
He is resolve, he is steadfastness, the bestower of stations, and the source of the world’s beginning;
he is the giver of teachers, the graceful one, the distinction, and he is established within the self as the abode. || 51 ||
Vīreśvara, Vīrabhadra, Viśvarūpa, Vidhi, Virāṭ, Vīracandra, Maṇidhartṛ, Tīvrānanda, and Nadīśvara. || 52 ||
The support of fire, the trident-bearer, Śipiviṣṭa, the abode of Śiva, Vālakhilya, the one of great heroism, the sun-rayed, the deaf, and the sky-goer. || 53 ||
He is delightful, the excellent refuge, the one of noble Vedic invocation, the treasure-house of nectar;
He is Maghavan, Kauśika, the possessor of cows, the cessation, and the means for accomplishing all things. || 54 ||
Born from the forehead, possessing a universal body, he sustains the wheel of the essential cycle of existence;
infallible, situated in the midst of the staff, he is the deer-marked one, endowed with the splendor of Brahman.
The ultimate reality, the supreme illusionist, the self-restraining one, the fire for the tiger;
the radiant one, the most excellent Ruci, the venerable one, the Lord of Speech, and the Lord of Day.
Ravi, Virocana, Skanda, Śāstṛ, Vaivasvata, Amara, Yuktikṛt, Mattakīrti, Sānuga, and Purañjaya. (57)
The beloved lord of Kailāsa, whose eye is the sun, the most excellent in the universe, free from fear, the sustainer of the universe, and unimpeded. || 58 ||
He is eternal, of constant auspiciousness, whose hearing and chanting are meritorious;
he is heard from afar, the sustainer of the universe, the object of meditation, and the destroyer of suffering.

He is the deliverer, the destroyer of evil deeds, the one to be known, the invincible Bhava; he is the beginningless source of the worlds Bhūḥ and Bhuvaḥ, the Goddess Lakṣmī, the wearer of the crown, and the lord of the thirty gods.

The protector of the universe, the creator of the universe, the one of noble heroism, he whose armlets are radiant; the progenitor, the source of birth for all beings, the one full of love, the one possessed of wisdom, and the kinsman.
Vasiṣṭha, Kaśyapa, Bhānu, Bhīma, and Bhīmaparākrama; Praṇava, Satpathācāra, Mahākāśa, and Mahādhana. || 62 ||
The lord of birth is Mahādeva, who has reached the further shore of all the Āgamas;
he is the one self-knower of reality and the essence, the all-pervading Viṣṇu, whose ornament is splendor.
The seer, the Brahmin, the sovereign, who has transcended birth, death, and old age;
the source of the five sacrifices, the Lord of the Universe, whose arising is stainless. (64)
Without beginning or end, self-born, affectionate, the sustainer of the world of devotees, the beloved of Gāyatrī, lofty, full of trust, and the maker of light. || 65 ||

The Child, the Delighter of the Mountain, the Sovereign, the One with a Fair Army, the Slayer of the Enemies of the Gods, the One with No Rim, the One with a Desired Rim, the Bestower of Liberation, and the One Free from Fever.
He is self-luminous, the light of austerity, the supreme light, and immovable;
he is tawny, golden-hued, bearded, with an eye in his forehead, and has the three Vedas as his body.
He is the mass of knowledge, great policy, the origin of the universe, and the source of worldly affliction;
he is the enjoyer, the reality of the sun, the master of yoga, and the lord of the day.
Named for his auspicious virtues, he was the destroyer of evil, one whose sight brought merit;
he possessed noble fame, was diligent, highly honored, and a protector of living beings.
Nakṣa, Malinakeśa, Svādhiṣṭhāna, Madāśraya, Pavitra, Pāpanāśa, Maṇipūra, and Nabhogati. (70)
Seated upon the lotus of the heart is Śakra, the peaceful Vṛṣākapi;
he is Kṛṣṇa, the lord of the planets, the dark one who is all-powerful and the destroyer of the worthless.
He is the enemy of unrighteousness, unknowable, invoked by many, and renowned by many;
he is the womb of Brahman, the womb of the vast, the cow of dharma, and the source of wealth.
The Sugata, who desires the welfare of the world, the Youth, the source of virtue;
he is golden-hued, radiant, delighting in various manifestations, and the Resonant Sound. (73)
Ārogya, Nayanādhyakṣa, Viśvāmitra, Dhaneśvara, Brahmajyoti, Vasurdhāmā, and Mahājyotis the unsurpassed. (74)
Mātāmaha, Mātariśvan, Nabhasvat, Nāgahāradhṛk, Pulastya, Pulaha, Agastya, Jātūkarṇya, and Parāśara. || 75 ||
He is free from obscuration and beyond destruction; he is Vairañcya, Viṣṭaraśravas, the Self-born, Aniruddha, Atri, the embodiment of knowledge, and the one of great fame. || 76 ||
The foremost hero of the world, the heroic Candra, whose valor is truth; who is like a serpent, the Great Kalpa, the wish-fulfilling tree, and the bearer of all arts. || 77 ||
He who adorns himself, the immovable one, the radiant, the valorous, the sky-clad, the swift, the lord of sound, the leaper, the one whose vehicle is fire. || 78 ||
The Lord of Non-transmigration, Śakra, the seat of negligence, Vasuśravas, Kavyavāha, the Radiant One, and Viśvabhojana. || 79 ||
He is the one to be recited, the enemy of old age, the pacifier, the red-horsed Tanūnapāt;
he is born from the sky, perfectly accomplished, fragrant, and of a cooling nature. (80)
Vasanta, Mādhava, Grīṣma, Nabhasstha, Bījavāhana, Aṅgiras, Guru, Ātreya, Vimala, and Viśvavāhana. || 81 ||
The Purifier, the one of vast conquest, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the knower of the three Vedas, the elephant among men;
the mind, the intellect, the ego, the Knower of the Field, and the Protector of the Field. || 82 ||
Jamadagni, the ocean, Vigola, Viśvagolaka, Aghora, Anuttara, Yajña, Śreṣṭha, and the abode of the highest bliss (niḥśreyasa). || 83 ||
Śaila, who resembles a jasmine flower in the sky, the enemy of the foes of the Dānavas, the life-sustainer of Cāmuṇḍā, the beautiful one free from thorns, and the upholder of the world’s destiny. 84.
He is the four Vedas, the four states of being, the fourfold, and the beloved of the four;
he is the sacred tradition, the compendium of tradition, the Veda of the holy fords, and the abode of Śiva.
He is of many forms, of great form, and the form of all things, both moving and unmoving; he is the creator of eyes and illusions, the principle of justice, accessible through logic, and untainted.
The thousand-headed lord of gods, the destroyer of all scriptures, shaven-headed, deformed, valorous, staff-bearing, and supreme in the qualities of Tāṇḍa. || 87 ||
He has tawny eyes, a horse's neck, and a blue throat; he is free from all affliction.
He possesses a thousand arms, is the Lord of all, the refuge, and the sustainer of all worlds.
He who is seated upon the lotus, the supreme light, the highest shore, and the ultimate fruit;
he who is the womb of the lotus, the great womb, the womb of the universe, and the all-seeing. || 89 ||
The knower of the moving and the unmoving, the bestower of boons, the Lord of boons, the one of great sound;
the god who is the preceptor of gods and asuras, and who is saluted by gods and asuras. || 90 ||
The great friend of gods and asuras, the great ascetic of gods and asuras, the god who is the primordial god of gods, the divine fire, the bestower of boons upon gods and asuras. || 91 ||
The divine lord of gods and asuras, the great lord of gods and asuras; the god of gods, the great object of meditation, the self of all deities, born of the Self. || 92 ||
The lion among gods, the sun, who instantly destroyed the tiger of his own life-force;
